title: Report: Nick Bosa out for a few weeks with pulled calf
summary: The 49ers are evaluating whether or not to place Bosa on injured reserve.
full_text: '' On Thursday, Nick Bosa was added to the injury report with an issue to his knee and calf. It's now clear that Bosa suffered a significant injury. According to a joint report from ESPN and NFL Network, Bosa pulled his calf during Thursday's practice and is expected to miss a few weeks — beginning with Sunday's matchup against the Cardinals. San Francisco is evaluating whether or not to place Bosa on injured reserve. Bosa did not practice on Wednesday, but that was a scheduled rest day. The team added knee and calf injuries to his listing on Thursday. Bosa was able to play just three games last year due to an ACL tear. In the first two contests this season, Bosa registered seven total tackles with two tackles for loss and one QB hit.
author: Myles Simmons

title: ManningCast dips to 661,000 viewers for Week 2
summary: Week 1 was bad.
full_text: Week 1 was bad. Week 2 was worse. The ManningCast audience keeps shrinking. For the Broncos-Chiefs game to start the season, 705,000 of 23.2 million viewers watched the alternate broadcast on ESPN featuring Peyton and Eli Manning. Via Andrew Marchand of The Athletic , the Giants-Rams Week 2 audience dipped to 661,000 . The total broadcast generated 19.4 million . The only good news is that the percentage of ManningCast viewership moved from three percent in Week 1 to 3.4 percent in Week 2. No ManningCast is on the docket for the Eagles-Bears game in Week 3. The possibility of a Pat McAfee alternate broadcast has been mentioned , subject to league approval. There has been no further word on whether it will happen. If it does, the bar has been set. If a McAfeeFest gets to seven figures (which the ManningCast once did, consistently), that will be a bad look for the Peyton and Eli show, which continues to experience a disconnect between the industry's view of it and the audience's response to it.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kyle Juszczyk fined for offensive demonstration for "imitation of chugging a beer"
summary: There are plenty of beers being sold at NFL stadiums and advertisements for them being shown during games, but the NFL has apparently drawn the line at players pretending to drink them on the field.
full_text: '' There are plenty of beers being sold at NFL stadiums and advertisements for them being shown during games, but the NFL has apparently drawn the line at players pretending to drink them on the field. Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk has been fined $14,926 for engaging in an offensive demonstration during the team's Week 2 win over the Dolphins. According to the fine letter that Juszczyk received, it was for a celebration that involved him pretending to chug a beverage. “Your imitation of chugging a beer constituted an offensive demonstration and could reasonably be construed as being in poor taste,” the league said in the letter. Juszczyk has done the celebration in the past — it's related to his nickname "Juice" — without drawing the notice of the league and is appealing the fine.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins fined for celebrations the league deemed obscene
summary: The NFL is sometimes called the No Fun League.
full_text: '' The NFL is sometimes called the No Fun League. Apparently, it's also the No Phallus League. Yes, I've now seen everything. (Not literally.) The league fined Bengals receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins for a celebration that was deemed to be obscene. From Jonathan Jones of The Athletic : "On multiple occasions last week, Chase and Higgins each did a gesture that can be interpreted as resembling a phallus ." In a session with reporters, Chase explained that the gesture is a variation of "the people's elbow," a move made popular by Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson. "Bro, at the end of the day, I can't say what something we made up, and then everybody else saying what it is ," Chase said, via Pat Brennan of the Cincinnati Enquirer. "I can't sit there and say that. "Everybody gonna have their opinion on what it look like, what it is. They had many people talking about what it looked like, what it is but I can't really sit here and say, 'That's what it is.' You know? Obviously, that's not what it is, but it is what it is." Some people other than the powers-that-be at 345 Park Avenue did indeed interpret the celebration as referring to the display of a body part other than an elbow . Chase displayed a potentially acceptable alternative during his Wednesday press conference. The disclosure comes on the same day that news emerged of a fine imposed on 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk for, in the league's view, miming the chugging of a beer . Chase suggested that the league's "superstars" should work with the NFL Players Association and " fight for our money ." While it makes no sense to fine Juszczyk for pretending to do what thousands of fans literally do while attending NFL games, the Chase and Higgins fines become the logical extension of the punishment, since that's where the chugged beer quickly ends up.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jaxson Dart to undergo meniscus surgery on Friday
summary: While Dart's meniscus is the primary concern, Dart's MCL and PCL will be addressed in the procedure if necessary.
full_text: '' Jaxson Dart is going under the knife. Per Dan Duggan of The Athletic , Dart will have his knee surgery on Friday. Dart will undergo a full meniscus repair and, if necessary, the surgeon will address his MCL and PCL. But the meniscus is Dart's primary injury. The procedure will take place at the Hospital for Special Surgery in Manhattan. Dart's recovery timeline is expected to be four-to-six months. That means if the Giants make it, he could possibly return for the postseason. But New York would have to make it there first. Dart completed 26-of-34 passes for 250 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions across his two games.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Work continues on field for Ravens-Cowboys
summary: On Sunday, the Ravens and the Cowboys will play in Brazil.
full_text: On Sunday, the Ravens and the Cowboys will play in Brazil. At Maracanã Stadium. Where the grass has raised concerns. But not enough concerns to spark any serious discussion about keeping the game in the U.S. At this point, it's too late to turn back. The only strategy is to move forward and hope the field holds up. The effort includes, as the venue's official account tweeted on Thursday, the addition of fiber stitching in order to increase " the field’s resistance and safety ." The machine, which looks like the grass version of a Zamboni, will reinforce the grass with synthetic material in the hopes of making it good enough to withstand the wear and tear of an NFL game. The game most likely will proceed, even if (as we've been told) the field will not look good on TV. As explained by Ben Fischer of Sports Business Journal , cancellation isn’t a viable option . When would the game be made up? (The Cowboys and Ravens have their byes on different weekends, so calling this week their bye and playing it later would require major surgery to the schedule.) It will be critical for the teams to get early access to the field, so that good decisions can be made about the proper cleats to wear. Because it's too late to bring the teams home and play in Dallas. The NFL continues to be the ultimate reality show, and the possible issues with the field will serve only to increase interest — and in turn boost the viewership at 4:25 p.m. ET on Sunday.
author: Mike Florio

title: Ronde Barber: "Mood is not great" at Buccaneers headquarters
summary: The Buccaneers are 0-2, capped by a 23-19 loss to the Browns in the Tampa Bay home opener.
full_text: The Buccaneers are 0-2, capped by a 23-19 loss to the Browns in the Tampa Bay home opener. And the sluggish start is having an impact. Via JoeBucsFan.com, Hall of Famer Ronde Barber said this week that the vibe in the building is not ideal. “ Look, the mood is not great ,” Barber said on his WFLA show. ”There’s too many mistakes. There’s a lack of urgency, if you will, in my mind when I look at them going onto the field. There’s got to be a little bit of a sense of a defining characteristic of your team through Week 2. I don’t know what that is. It’s mistakes. It’s busts. It’s lack of execution.” Barber believes the Bucs simply weren't ready for the games that count. “Week 2 can’t be the fifth preseason game,” Barber said. “At some point you have to start hitting your stride. And it doesn’t feel like they’re in their stride right now on either side of the ball.” “I feel like for much of the secondary, especially the coverage unit, they’re so focused on what they’re trying to do that they don’t know how to do it now.” Barber also singled out former Lions linebacker Alex Anzalone, who signed with the Bucs as a free agent. “There’s some dynamic going on, whether it’s not understanding what his role is in the defense, not understanding angles, maybe not having enough tackles in the preseason, I don’t know what it is,” Barber said. ”Something is hamstringing this defense in critical moments." It puts even more pressure on the Buccaneers for Week 3, the second of three straight home games. The official attendance last week was 61,391 — nearly 8,000 below capacity. (Often, the actual attendance is lower than the reported number.) By the time the game was over, the fans who stuck it out through the lengthy weather delay weren’t happy . Those who show up for the next game will be even saltier if the Bucs slip to 0-3. That makes it a dangerous game for the Vikings, who have overachieved to get to 2-0. This is exactly the kind of game in which the team that has done better than expected can step into a pothole against a team that has done worse than expected.
author: Mike Florio

title: The Packers' struggles could be the Jets' gain
summary: As the football-following world began to come to terms with the possibility that the Packers could be very bad this year, Cowboys fans began to perk up.
full_text: As the football-following world began to come to terms with the possibility that the Packers could be very bad this year, Cowboys fans began to perk up. Thanks to the Micah Parsons trade, the Cowboys hold Green Bay's first-round pick in 2027. So, the worse the Packers do, the higher the 2027 first-round pick climbs. But there's an important caveat, which works to the benefit of the New York Jets. The trade that sent defensive tackle Quinnen Williams to Dallas includes an important term as to the 2027 first-round pick the Jets received. It's not necessarily the Cowboys' pick. It's the higher of the two picks the Cowboys will have. Which means that, if the Packers bottom out (and the Cowboys don't), the Jets get the Green Bay first-round pick in 2027. The Jets, of course, failed to help themselves on Sunday, when they blew a 10-point lead to the Packers and mismanaged the late-game and overtime scenarios. Still, it's good news for the Jets. Especially since they also hold the Colts' first-round pick for 2027 — and the Colts are 0-2.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bijan Robinson and Drake London had a historic night, with 194 yards each
summary: Falcons running back Bijan Robinson and wide receiver Drake London ran wild at Lambeau Field on Thursday night.
full_text: Falcons running back Bijan Robinson and wide receiver Drake London ran wild at Lambeau Field on Thursday night. Robinson had 194 rushing yards and London had 194 receiving yards as the Falcons crushed the Packers 35-14. Via Josh Dubow of the Associated Press, London and Robinson are the first teammates each with more than 150 yards from scrimmage in a road game at Lambeau Field. They're also the fist teammates each with 190 or more yards from scrimmage in a road game in 50 years: It was last accomplished by Rams running back Lawrence McCutcheon and wide receiver Ron Jessie at Miami in 1976. Robinson and London have now played together in three games when they both had 150 or more yards from scrimmage. They're the first pair of teammates in NFL history to top 150 yards in the same game three times. Robinson, who also had two catches for 19 yards, totaled 213 yards from scrimmage. He's the first player to top 200 yards from scrimmage in a game this season, and he has an NFL-high 467 yards from scrimmage this season. He's averaging 155.7 yards from scrimmage through three games. In the first two weeks of the season, the Falcons' quarterback play was so bad with Cooper Rush getting benched for Jack Strand that it was easy to overlook what dynamic playmakers the Falcons have. If the now-healthy Michael Penix can just execute his job competently and get the ball to those playmakers consistently, the Falcons' offense is going to be a real threat for the rest of the season.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Christian Watson: We have to put a better product on the field if we want fans to have our back
summary: Things got ugly at Lambeau Field on Thursday night, with the Packers getting booed by the fans during their worst home loss of the Matt LaFleur era.
full_text: '' Things got ugly at Lambeau Field on Thursday night, with the Packers getting booed by the fans during their worst home loss of the Matt LaFleur era. Tucker Kraft had one response to the fans after the 35-14 loss to the Falcons. Christian Watson had another — one that will likely play better to the fanbase. "I mean, it’s tough. At the end of the day, it’s an entertainment business, so we’ve got to put a better product on the field if we want to have the fans have our back," Watson said, via Dominique Yates of the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel . "Obviously, we’d like to think that the fans will be there through the ups and downs. "But we’ve got to put out a better performance than that." Watson had seven catches for 96 yards with a touchdown on Thursday night. Now at 1-2, the Packers will be on the road in Week 4 to face the Buccaneers before home contests against the Bears and Cowboys in Weeks 5 and 6.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Brock Bowers remains limited on Thursday's injury report
summary: Raiders tight end Brock Bowers remained limited in Thursday's practice as he seeks to return to game action for the first time since Dec. 21.
full_text: ' Raiders tight end Brock Bowers remained limited in Thursday's practice as he seeks to return to game action for the first time since Dec. 21. Bowers is working his way back from a meniscus trim procedure earlier this month after injuring his left knee in training camp. It's the same knee that sidelined him with a PCL sprain and bone bruise during the 2025 season. He missed five games last season. The Raiders added defensive end Kwity Paye to the injury report with an illness. He did not practice. Four players returned to full participation: Linebacker Nakobe Dean (shoulder), defensive tackle Folorunso Fatukasi (shoulder), cornerback Darien Porter (foot) and wide receiver Dareke Young (hamstring) were limited Wednesday. The rest of the report was unchanged from Wednesday. Quarterback Aidan O'Connell (personal) and safety Treydan Stukes (concussion) did not practice. Linebacker Segun Olubi (knee) and defensive tackle JJ Pegues (back) were again full participants.
author: Charean Williams

title: Ed Policy may regret not waiting on Matt LaFleur, Brian Gutenkunst contracts
summary: After Ed Policy succeeded Mark Murphy as the president and CEO of the Packers, it quickly became clear that 2025 would be an up-or-out season for coach Matt LaFleur and G.M.
full_text: After Ed Policy succeeded Mark Murphy as the president and CEO of the Packers, it quickly became clear that 2025 would be an up-or-out season for coach Matt LaFleur and G.M. Brian Gutekunst. Both had contracts running through 2026. Policy made it clear that he's not a fan of lame-duck arrangements. So either they'd be extended or fired after the 2025 season. Ultimately, the Packers made it to the playoffs as the No. 7 seed in the NFC, before blowing a 21-3 halftime lead against the Bears in the wild-card round. That was enough, after a brief period of uncertainty, to get the Packers the give LaFleur and Gutekunst new contracts. Which, assuming that the deals guarantee one or more full seasons beyond 2026, complicates any consideration of firing either or both of them this year. So what was the rush to extend them? There was a time when having a lame-duck coach undermined him, because the players may not respond in the desired way to a coach who may be gone after the season ends. And it's possible that Ed Policy clings to that notion in part because his father, Carmen, firmly believed in that approach when he was running the 49ers and the Browns. Nowadays, there's a different reality in NFL locker rooms. Pro football has become a year-to-year reality, with continuity not guaranteed. The coach may be gone next year, and plenty of the players may be gone next year. All that matters is this year. For the Packers, their coach and G.M. have a layer of job security they wouldn't have enjoyed without the extensions. It takes off some of the pressure to perform at the highest possible level, especially because firing them — and buying out their contracts — becomes a challenge for a publicly-owned team that has been, through Policy, complaining about the financial realities of a league in which the other franchises can carve off slivers of equity for many millions in new revenue. That doesn't mean LaFleur and Gutekunst are safe. But, if they get fired, they'll get their buyouts. And the Packers will have to pay them while also paying their replacements. In hindsight, the right move would have been to press pause on the extensions. It's a lesson both for Policy and for other owners who may end up on the fence as to the question of whether a contract should be extended in order to avoid having the coach or the G.M. work through the last year of their deals. When in doubt, the best move may be to wait it out.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jordan Love: Packers' run game needs to improve
summary: Packers quarterback Jordan Love passed for 312 yards while the running game gained 17 yards in Thursday night's loss to the Falcons, and Love says that needs to change.
full_text: '' Packers quarterback Jordan Love passed for 312 yards while the running game gained 17 yards in Thursday night's loss to the Falcons, and Love says that needs to change. The Packers' two running backs, MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson, each got only four carries. Lloyd gained 11 yards and Johnson gained six yards. Love says that's not enough. "Our run game's got to improve. When you have a solid pass game and run game balancing each other, that always helps," Love said. "Obviously, our run game, I don't know how many rushes we had, but it's something we need to improve on right there. I think that'll help the pass game." The Packers took a 7-0 lead in the first quarter and were tied 7-7 for most of the second quarter, but once they fell behind Love said it was harder to commit to the run. "We got behind tonight and it didn't look good," Love said. The Packers are hoping that their starting running back, Josh Jacobs, will play eventually this season. Jacobs is currently on paid leave and is likely to be suspended without pay after pleading no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property stemming from an incident involving his ex-girlfriend. Getting Jacobs back might help, but the Packers' running woes appear to go deeper than the running back position. Green Bay's offense needs to get better, and the Packers can't afford to wait until Jacobs returns.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Matt LaFleur on ugly loss to Falcons: "It was a butt-whooping"
summary: The running game was MIA against ATL.
full_text: The Packers had won 13 straight home openers. They were unable to get to 14. The Falcons dominated at Lambeau Field on Thursday night, beating the Packers 35-14. After the game, Green Bay coach Matt LaFleur called it what it was. "It was a butt-whooping," LaFleur said. "That was at least three-quarter butt-whooping right there." His comments came in the context of the potential impact of a roughing the passer call that extended Atlanta's initial scoring drive on the flow of the game. Asked about that specific call, LaFleur said, "I'm not gonna answer that. I'm not gonna get fined." For now, no one is getting fired. Asked if the play of the offensive line will prompt changes to the coaching staff, LaFleur said, "I'm not even going to respond to that question." He also declined to hang the sluggish performance of the offense on the blockers. "I don't want to put all the blame on the offensive line," LaFleur said. "There's enough blame to go around to everybody." Still, the numbers say it all. The Packers couldn't run. They had nine rushing attempts for 17 yards, against 53 passes. And they clearly miss starting tailback Josh Jacobs. "I mean, I think we all saw a dynamic running back on the other side, and I think Josh is a dynamic running back," LaFleur said. "But it is the situation, it's the circumstance. And it is what it is right now. And we've got to find a way just to either — well, one, we've got to put them in a better position, and then those guys gotta go do it." They have extra time to figure out how to do it before a Week 4 game at Tampa Bay, for a renewal of the old NFC Central "Bay of Pigs" rivalry. With Green Bay at 1-2 and the Buccaneers at 0-2, it could be time for Chris Berman to dust off that name, for the first time in a long time.
author: Mike Florio

title: Tucker Kraft: Disappointing that fans booed us at Lambeau Field, won't help us win
summary: "It'd be much easier with the 70,000 people behind us rather than opposing us," Kraft said of the Packers fans who booed during the 35-14 loss.
full_text: '' The fans in Green Bay loudly booed during the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday night at Lambeau Field. Packers tight end Tucker Kraft did not appreciate that. "That's pretty tough," Kraft said of the booing. "Everyone pictures Lambeau Field and not boos. I don't picture boos when I picture my home stadium. That's tough. It's pretty disappointing. Especially for a home opener. It's pretty disappointing. It's not gonna help us win. I don't know what people think, that's gonna rally us or something like that. But we're grown men. We're mentally strong enough, capable enough to get back on the field and play ball. But it'd be much easier with the 70,000 people behind us rather than opposing us." Kraft, who caught four passes for 26 yards, admitted that he didn't play to his own standards, and that the Packers need to play better than they have during their 1-2 start. "Long season, we're three games in, we've dropped two to NFC opponents, though," Kraft said. Kraft said the Packers can't listen to boos, cheers or anything else. "We can't let external noise divide us," Kraft said. "Us guys in this locker room, we're really all we've got. We spend a lot of time together, so just continue to stay close and build off each other."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Thursday Night Football: Drake London, Bijan Robinson run by Packers 35-14
summary: London and Robinson combined for 407 yards and two touchdowns in Michael Penix's return to the lineup.
full_text: '' Drake London and Bijan Robinson combined for 407 yards and two touchdowns, leading the Falcons to a 35-14 rout of the Packers on Thursday night. It was the Packers' first home-opening loss since 2012. Both teams are 1-2. After their first two games, played without starting quarterback Michael Penix, the Falcons ranked 29th in total offense (262 yards per game) and last in scoring (16 total points). They did not have a single red zone snap. Penix's return changed everything. He had a slow start, throwing an interception on the team's first possession, but he went 13-of-15 with a touchdown in the second and third quarters. Penix finished 18-of-25 for 256 yards with a touchdown and an interception. London, who had six catches for 80 yards in the first two games, caught nine passes for 194 yards. Robinson, who had 37 carries for 80 yards in the first two games, had 29 carries for 194 yards and two touchdowns. He also caught two passes for 19 yards. They are the first teammates with at least 190 yards from scrimmage in a road game since Lawrence McCutcheon and Ron Jessie did it for the Rams against the Dolphins in 1976. The Falcons outgained the Packers 498 yards to 328, with two kneel downs in victory formation dropping them under 500 yards. They were 6-of-10 on third down. Green Bay led 7-0 on Christian Watson's fourth touchdown catch of the season, but it was short-lived. The Falcons went on a 27-0 run before Matthew Golden scored his first touchdown. The Packers managed only 17 yards rushing. Jordan Love was 28-of-53 for 312 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. Golden caught five passes for 100 yards, and Watson had seven receptions for 96 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Falcons rolling, taking a 24-7 lead on the Packers
summary: The Falcons are dominating the Packers at Lambeau Field.
full_text: The Falcons are dominating the Packers at Lambeau Field. Brian Robinson scored on a 7-yard run with 3:38 left in the third quarter, giving the Falcons a 24-7 lead. Atlanta went 92 yards in 10 plays after a fourth-and-1 stop of the Packers. Jordan Love threw incomplete in the end zone as Green Bay turned it over on downs at the Atlanta 7. The Falcons have outgained the Packers 340 yards to 171. In his 2026 debut, Michael Penix is 15-of-22 for 132 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Bijan Robinson has 20 carries for 158 yards and a touchdown and two receptions for 19 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Surgery not on table for Jayden Daniels, Commanders haven't discussed IR
summary: Daniels dislocated his left elbow in Week 2.
full_text: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said on Wednesday that he didn't have an update on quarterback Jayden Daniels's outlook for the coming weeks because he was still meeting with specialists about his dislocated left elbow, but General Manager Adam Peters had more to offer on Friday morning. Daniels will not play against the Seahawks this Sunday, but Peters indicated that the Commanders expect to have the quarterback in the lineup in the near future. “He met with doctors all over the country," Peters said, via 106.7 The Fan. "We got a lot of good opinions. As of right now, surgery is not on the table and we haven’t discussed IR.” An injured reserve stint would keep Daniels out for at least four games, so taking that out of the conversation suggests Daniels will be ready to return to action relatively soon. For now, though, the Commanders will have to hope Marcus Mariota will be able to lead them to their first victory of the season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cam Skattebo: Our crowd's gotta be lit, we have a really good shot at this
summary: The Giants learned this week that they will not have quarterback Jaxson Dart available for the rest of the 2026 season and that's dimmed their prospects for contending in the eyes of many people.
full_text: '' The Giants learned this week that they will not have quarterback Jaxson Dart available for the rest of the 2026 season and that's dimmed their prospects for contending in the eyes of many people. Running back Cam Skattebo is not part of that group. During a press conference on Thursday, Skattebo was reminded of the good vibes at MetLife Stadium from the team's Week 1 win over the Cowboys and was asked about how different things feel as they prepare to return to their home field against the Titans on Sunday. Skattebo replied with a plea for the crowd to show up with the same energy because he doesn't believe anything has changed for the team's outlook. "The crowd's got to be lit, just like it was the first week," Skattebo said, via a transcript from the team. "We have to have everybody's support, just like we did week one. I think the entire city of New York still knows we have a really good shot at this. And they love Jameis Winston. So, we're not going to take a step down. We're going to continue to push, continue to work. If we have our fan base with us, if they're giving everything they got towards us, I promise you they're going to get everything from us." At 0-2, the Titans provide about as soft a landing after a tough week as the Giants could hope to find on the other side of the field. A strong performance in a win will help keep some hope alive, but a dud with Winston playing as poorly as he did in relief of Dart last Monday will make it feel real late real early for the Giants.
author: Josh Alper

title: Kyler Murray: I've never had an issue protecting myself, concussion was an awkward play
summary: Kyler Murray will be back at quarterback for the Vikings when they take on the Buccaneers this Sunday and he won't be playing with fears of a repeat of what happened in Week 1.
full_text: Kyler Murray will be back at quarterback for the Vikings when they take on the Buccaneers this Sunday and he won't be playing with fears of a repeat of what happened in Week 1. Murray was knocked out of the Vikings' opener against the Packers after suffering a concussion while being hit by Lukas Van Ness and Javon Bullard at the end of a run. Murray said at a Thursday press conference that he felt back to himself "pretty quickly" and that the injury was a result of an unwieldy slide that put him in position to take a big shot to the head. "I've really never had an issue protecting myself ," Murray said. "I’d like to think I'm one of the least-hit quarterbacks in the league as far as just protecting myself, getting the ball out and stuff like that. That's new for me to have to go through that type of situation, because that's the last thing I ever expected is to get a concussion just because I am very careful with being in open field and I know that was kind of an awkward slide situation, but I'm always trying to protect myself. . . . Van Ness was behind me you're moving fast. You charge it to the game. I don't judge anybody over there for anything that happened. It’s part of the game." Murray has missed plenty of other games with injuries over the course of his career, but none have come in a similar fashion as the Week 1 concussion and the Vikings will be hoping that he'll be able to avoid a repeat in the weeks to come.
author: Josh Alper

title: Chiefs RB coach DeMarco Murray: It's hard to take Kenneth Walker out
summary: Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker is off to an impressive start to the season and the team has been giving him plenty of chances to show off his game.
full_text: Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker is off to an impressive start to the season and the team has been giving him plenty of chances to show off his game. Walker led the NFL in carries through the first two weeks of the season and he was tied with Jahmyr Gibbs for overall offensive touches, which led to questions for head coach Andy Reid earlier this week about whether the Chiefs should do more to manage his workload over the course of a long season. On Thursday, running backs coach DeMarco Murray fielded similar questions at a press conference. Murray said Walker "likes the ball a lot and I like giving it to him," but acknowledged that finding ways to get rookie Emmett Johnson into the mix more often is something that is on his mind heading into the Chiefs' Week 3 game against the Dolphins. "It’s more of a feel for me . Obviously, I want Kenneth to get into a groove and, as you guys have seen these first two games, it's hard to kind of take him out," Murray said. "But Emmett's done a great job and he's still learning. He'll continue to get more opportunities. I've just got to pull the trigger and get No. 9 out of there and put No. 10 in there." Johnson has 103 yards on 14 touches so far this season, which makes him an appealing backup option in any week and facing an overmatched Dolphins team this weekend might make giving Walker some extra time off an even easier call for Murray and the rest of the Chiefs staff.
author: Josh Alper

title: Drake London: Michael Penix is the definition of resiliency
summary: Michael Penix's return to the Falcons starting lineup didn't get off to a great start, but that just turned out to be one more chance for him to show his ability to bounce back from an adverse situation.
full_text: Michael Penix's return to the Falcons starting lineup didn't get off to a great start, but that just turned out to be one more chance for him to show his ability to bounce back from an adverse situation. Penix threw an interception on the fourth offensive play, which seemed like an omen that it would be a long night for the Falcons in the quarterback's first start since last season's torn ACL. It turned out far differently, however. Penix finished the night 18-of-25 for 256 yards and a touchdown to tight end Austin Hooper in a 35-14 rout of the Packers. "I knew we had a long game ahead of us, so I just continue to keep my head down, continue to keep working and doing what I can to help this team win a football game," Penix said of his response to the interception. Nine of Penix's passes went to wide receiver Drake London for 194 yards and the wideout had a succinct way of summing up Penix's return from both the injury and the early stumble. "He’s the definition of resiliency," London said. Penix noted that it is a "long season" and that the Falcons were "far from perfect" on Thursday night, but they were leaps and bounds better than they were in the first two weeks and Penix's play gives the team plenty of reason to believe that more good days are in their future.
author: Josh Alper

title: Zach Ertz: I never wanted to leave Philadelphia, glad to be back to my favorite place
summary: Veteran tight end Zach Ertz has returned to Philadelphia for his second stint with the Eagles, and he says he never wanted to leave.
full_text: Veteran tight end Zach Ertz has returned to Philadelphia for his second stint with the Eagles, and he says he never wanted to leave. Ertz, who was drafted by the Eagles in 2013 and traded to the Cardinals in 2021, said he never knew if the Eagles would welcome him back, but always hoped they would. "There was never a plan to come back," Ertz said. "I never wanted to leave in the first place, so let's just put that out there. The opportunity finally arose where I could come back. There's been times I asked in the past to come back and it didn't come to fruition for whatever reason. But for me, it's just a blessing to be back." Ertz played for the Commanders last year but suffered a season-ending knee injury, and he wasn't sure if he'd be back in Philadelphia or anywhere else. "If you told me when I got hurt that I'd be back here in nine and a half months practicing for the Philadelphia Eagles, you could have signed me up then," Ertz said. "For me, this is a place I always called home. When anyone asks my favorite place to play, everyone knows it's here" Ertz said there are still people in the Eagles' facility who mean a lot to him, from teammates to coaches to the cafeteria staff. "It's special," Ertz said. "It's great to see the people I've missed for a long time. It's special to be back, for sure." Ertz said he has spent the last nine and a months rehabbing his knee with the hopes to be ready to play as soon as he signs, but that he'll let the coaching staff decide when or if he's ready to be promoted from the practice squad to the active gameday roster. "It's up to the coaches. I'm not even on the active roster right now," Ertz said. "It's up to me to prove I can make a difference, whether it's Year 1 or Year 14." Ertz is just glad to be back in Year 14 where it all started in Year 1.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Ruling on key sealed document in Brian Flores case is also under seal, for now
summary: The Brian Flores case against the NFL and several teams (Dolphins, Texans, Giants, and Broncos) has recently focused on a document produced by Korn Ferry, in connection with a coaching search the company performed for the Ravens.
full_text: The Brian Flores case against the NFL and several teams (Dolphins, Texans, Giants, and Broncos) has recently focused on a document produced by Korn Ferry, in connection with a coaching search the company performed for the Ravens. Korn Ferry and the NFL want the document to remain under seal and, as a result, not available to the public. Flores has challenged the designation. In most federal civil cases, the presiding judge delegates disputes that arise during the discovery process to a magistrate judge. In this case, the magistrate judge has issued a ruling. The ruling, as reported by Daniel Kaplan, is also under seal . For now. The apparent reason for the decision is to give the party that lost the issue a chance to appeal to the presiding judge. And the fact that the decision is sealed doesn't necessarily mean Korn Ferry lost. In order to issue the preliminary ruling, the magistrate judge likely had to quote from or otherwise describe key aspects of the currently secret document. If the case goes to trial, the document undoubtedly will be presented and discussed in open court. But that's a long way away. Securing the publication of the document sooner rather than later could create a bad P.R. look for the league, which could not only spark meaningful settlement talks but also prompt the media, the fans, and those with oversight of the league to sit up and take notice of the manner in which the sausage gets made. For now, the question is whether the losing party on the issue of the sealed document will appeal within the 14-day time period for doing so. And whoever files the appeal necessarily will have been the losing party.
author: Mike Florio

title: Thursday Night Football: Falcons lead Packers 17-7 at halftime
summary: Michael Penix is back . . . and so are the Falcons.
full_text: Michael Penix is back . . . and so are the Falcons. The quarterback, who hadn't played since Nov. 16, got off to a slow start. His third pass was an interception and he was only 5-of-11 to start. Penix, though, found his groove, finishing the first half 13-of-20 for 114 yards with a touchdown and an interception. His 5-yard touchdown throw to tight end Austin Hooper on third-and-goal with 59 seconds left in the half has the Falcons in the locker room with a 17-7 lead at halftime. The Falcons, who did not have a red zone snap in the first two games, are 2-for-2 in the red zone tonight. They scored on three of their last four possessions in the first half. Falcons running back Bijan Robinson has 15 carries for 111 yards, including a 3-yard touchdown run. He also has one catch for 17 yards. Drake London has five catches for 54 yards. The Falcons have outgained the Packers 253 to 108. Green Bay went three-and-out on four of six possessions in the first half, going 1-for-6 on third down with four punts. Green Bay kicker Trey Smack had his 47-yard field goal try blocked by Falcons defensive lineman Zach Harrison. Jordan Love is 9-of-19 for 96 yards, including a 4-yard touchdown pass to Christian Watson. It is Watson's fourth touchdown of the season. Matthew Golden has two catches for 53 yards. The Green Bay run game is nonexistent with five carries for 12 yards from MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson. The Packers have won 13 consecutive home openers at Lambeau Field.
author: Charean Williams

title: On Thursday, Mike McCarthy didn't want to say much about Joey Porter Jr.'s status
summary: On Wednesday, Steelers coach Mike McCarthy wasn't asked about cornerback Joey Porter Jr.
full_text: On Wednesday, Steelers coach Mike McCarthy wasn’t asked about cornerback Joey Porter Jr. On Thursday, McCarthy was. He didn't seem to like it very much. After McCarthy said Porter, who was officially limited in practice on Wednesday, is scheduled “to do some more today, so we’ll see how that goes,” McCarthy was asked whose decision it was for Porter to be limited on Wednesday. “ We have a plan for every one of our players ," McCarthy said, via Brandon Contes of Awful Announcing. "So, he did the work that was planned on." McCarthy then was asked whether that means it was the team's plan for Porter to be limited. “We’re not gonna play this game anymore about every little question,” McCarthy said. "You can just see [P.R. director] Burt [Lauten] for the injury report." And here's where a strange situation becomes even more strange. On Wednesday, the team's website listed Porter as limited with this designation: "not injury related — conditioning." The NFL's official report, which is distributed via email, said on both Wednesday and Thursday that Porter was limited due to "not injury related — other." The team's website, as of this posting, contains no specific injury description for any of the injured Steelers players: Porter, Jamel Dean, Rico Dowdle, Gennings Dunker, Cole Holcomb, Michael Pittman Jr., Jalen Ramsey, or Jaylen Warren. While it's possible that the error is clerical (frankly, we can't recall ever seeing a team website omitting the specific source of the injury for its players), the deeper issue here is whether the Steelers' representations to the world regarding Porter's status will become relevant if/when the Steelers decide to play hardball with Porter. If they've been officially saying Porter is injured (for Week 1, it was "back" and for Week 2, it was "back" and "conditioning"), it becomes awkward for the Steelers to suddenly contend that he was fine all along, if they ever choose to do that. Either way, the tension seems to be increasing. As evidenced by McCarthy's reaction to fair and reasonable questions about Porter that were posed to the head coach on Thursday.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bijan Robinson's TD has Falcons tied 7-7 with Packers
summary: The Falcons became only the fourth team since 1978 without a red zone drive through two games.
full_text: The Falcons became only the fourth team since 1978 without a red zone drive through two games. The last time it happened was in 2008 by the Rams. It took the Falcons three drives to get inside the Packers' 20-yard line on Thursday night. Bijan Robinson's 55-yard run got the Falcons to the Green Bay 5, and two plays later, the running back had his team in the end zone. Robinson scored on a 3-yard run. He has seven carries for 73 yards. Michael Penix has struggled in his 2026 debut, completing only 2 of 7 passes for 22 yards with an interception. But the Falcons are tied with the Packers 7-7 at the end of the first quarter.
author: Charean Williams

title: Christian Watson scores his fourth TD of the season, giving Green Bay a 7-0 lead
summary: It is Week 3, and Christian Watson already has four touchdown receptions.
full_text: It is Week 3, and Christian Watson already has four touchdown receptions. His career-high for touchdowns is the seven he had as a rookie in 2022. Watson's latest touchdown came on a 4-yard throw by Jordan Love with 5:13 remaining in the first quarter on Thursday night. The Packers drove 87 yards in nine plays on their second series to take a 7-0 lead. Love was 5-of-6 for 76 yards and the touchdown. Matthew Golden had the big play, catching a 45-yard pass to the Atlanta 43 on third-and-11. On their first possession, the Packers failed to take advantage of safety Xavier McKinney's interception of Michael Penix. The Packers went three-and-out as Love was only 1-of-3 for 6 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Puka Nacua remains out of practice Thursday
summary: Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua sat out practice again Thursday.
full_text: Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua sat out practice again Thursday. He has missed the past four practices after injuring his hip in the Sept. 17 practice. It puts his availability for the Week 3 game in question. Nacua missed the Week 2 victory over the Giants, watching as Davante Adams caught eight passes for 195 yards and two touchdowns. Coach Sean McVay said Wednesday the Rams will be deliberate in Nacua's return given it's a soft-tissue. Wide receiver Jordan Whittington (quad) returned to practice Thursday with limited work. He did not play in Week 2. Offensive lineman Alaric Jackson (knee) and tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle) were full participants Thursday after being limited a day earlier. Tight end Colby Parkinson (knee) and safety Kam Kinchens (hamstring) were non-participants a second consecutive day. Inside linebacker Nate Landman (shoulder) remained limited.

title: NFL Week 3 picks: Our experts face off on Texans at Colts, Ravens vs. Cowboys and more
summary: CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games
full_text:
Week 3 of the NFL season is here, and some teams are already in trouble. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers , Los Angeles Chargers , Houston Texans and Indianapolis Colts are staring down the barrel of a 0-3 start, and a couple of those head coaches could be on the hot seat. The Texans and Colts face off this Sunday in Indy, so that will be one to watch!
Elsewhere in the NFL, Aaron Rodgers opens up division play against the Cincinnati Bengals , Kyler Murray returns to the lineup to face the Buccaneers, Lamar Jackson takes on Dak Prescott in Rio de Janeiro and the Los Angeles Rams will play the Denver Broncos on "Sunday Night Football." Which teams should you pick in Week 3, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Sept. 23 over at DraftKings Sportsbook.
Dajani (Bengals -3.5): A battle between two teams trending in opposite directions. The Pittsburgh Steelers are averaging the fewest points per game (11.5) and yards per game (249.5) through two games in Aaron Rodgers' career, while the Bengals defense is reborn and tied for eighth in scoring defense after ranking 30th last season. In Week 1, Cincinnati recovered four fumbles. In Week 2, it held C.J. Stroud and the Texans out of the end zone altogether. The Steelers, on the other hand, have been abysmal on the offensive side of the ball, ranking bottom three in not just total offense and scoring offense, but also yards per play (3.8) and third-down percentage (20%). Rodgers is 0-for-11 on deep balls this season, including 0-for-6 to droppin' DK Metcalf .
The Bengals haven't defeated the Steelers by at least four points since 2022, but I think it happens on Sunday.
Prediction: Bengals 23, Steelers 16
Dubin (Bengals -3.5): Pittsburgh's offense is just too broken for me to be comfortable taking the Steelers here. As Dajani mentioned, they are averaging just 11.5 points and 249.5 yards per game. Aaron Rodgers looks done. Both of their running backs are dealing with injuries. So is Michael Pittman Jr. The Steelers are still good defensively, as we've seen so far, but it's actually kind of hard to know how much stock to put into performances against the Cooper Rush-led Steelers and the A.J. Brown-less Patriots . Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are a different animal to deal with.
Prediction: Bengals 24, Steelers 10
Dajani ( Jaguars -3): Out of all the games on this list, Patriots at Jaguars may be the toughest one for me to pick. Let me explain...
If we were power-ranking all the teams in the NFL, the Jaguars are ahead of the Patriots right now. However, this game features a pretty interesting matchup, which I think could rule the day. Jacksonville suffered a close loss to the Broncos last week, in which Denver dominated the Jags' offensive line. The Patriots dominated the Steelers' offensive line last week in their victory, and this Mike Vrabel unit has been an underrated storyline through two weeks. New England actually ranks No. 1 in points per game allowed (8.0), third down (4/24) and red zone (0/3). I could take the points here and hope Drake Maye shows up, or I could trust in what appears to be the best team in the AFC South at home.
Prediction: Jaguars 24, Patriots 20
Dubin (Jaguars -3): Jacksonville looked for a while like it was going to take care of the Broncos fairly easily after blowing out the Browns in Week 1. Obviously, things changed following a Trevor Lawrence interception in the third quarter, and they ended up losing. But the Patriots haven't looked particularly good at any point so far this season. The Jaguars' offense has at least shown it has an ability to be efficient and explosive at times. I think they rediscover some of that here and take care of the Patriots at home.
Prediction: Jaguars 23, Patriots 17
Dajani (Texans -3): Am I worried that the Texans have started 0-2? Not really. They had to play Josh Allen and Joe Burrow. Plus, DeMeco Ryans has started 0-2 in three out of his four seasons as head coach! Par for the course. Now, I don't want to overlook the Texans' struggles on both sides of the ball. This supposedly elite defense has allowed 84 points over the past three games, including playoffs, which is the most in a three-game span under coach Ryans, and the offense didn't score a single touchdown last week vs. the Bengals. Not having Nico Collins or Tank Dell really hurts.
As for the Colts, they will be without a star wideout as well in Alec Pierce . I was impressed with how Daniel Jones , Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs kept up with the Kansas City Chiefs last Sunday night, but I couldn't get over how bad this defense was. The Colts are just the third team in NFL history to allow 500 yards of total offense in each of their first two games. Indy ranks dead last in total defense, passing defense and scoring defense. I'm taking the Texans to finally register that first win on Sunday. Houston is 13-1 SU and 10-3-1 ATS in its last 14 road divisional games.
Prediction: Texans 27, Colts 21
Dubin (Texans -3): I hate to keep parroting what Dajani says, but boy does this Indianapolis defense scare me -- and not at all in a good way. The Colts have gotten the ball run down their throats in each of the first two games of this season, and they also got lit up through the air by Lamar Jackson and Patrick Mahomes . The Texans don't have the same offensive talent as either the Ravens or Chiefs, especially if Nico Collins is out again, but they do have the defense to shut down Indy's offense and make this game a slog. I could see a low-scoring game where the Texans are just able to be more efficient than the Colts because the Indianapolis defense just doesn't have the horses (sorry) to compete.
Prediction: Texans 20, Colts 16
Dajani (Buccaneers +1.5): The Minnesota Vikings are riding high at 2-0 and are now favored to win the NFC North! They defeated an overrated Packers team in Week 1 with Carson Wentz , and then got some help from the football weather gods in Chicago. We were robbed of what could have been a really fun matchup between Caleb Williams and Brian Flores. Kyler Murray is expected to make his return to the lineup after suffering a concussion very early in his first start with the Vikings, and I'm not sure what to expect from him. Wentz had the benefit of working in Kevin O'Connell's system last year. Murray really hasn't played in this kind of offense before.
The Buccaneers have been one of the biggest disappointments of the season, and Baker Mayfield has accounted for as many touchdowns as turnovers in his past 13 starts dating back to last year. Todd Bowles' defense made Deshaun Watson look like a starting quarterback last week thanks to a lackluster pass rush paired with blown coverages, but I'm going to call the upset here in Week 3 that finally gets Tampa Bay into the win column. The Buccaneers have failed to cover the spread in 11 straight games, which is tied for the longest such streak since 1970. The streak is snapped this week.
Prediction: Buccaneers 21, Vikings 20
Dubin (Vikings -1.5): I am very worried about Tampa on both sides of the ball. The Buccaneers just got lit up by Deshaun Watson . That is next-level embarrassing. The Vikings should be able to move the ball with relative ease in Kyler Murray's return game, even with the questions about how he fits in Kevin O'Connell's offense. And then the idea that Baker Mayfield is going to bounce back against a Brian Flores defense just doesn't pass muster to me. We've seen what this defense has done to Jordan Love and Caleb Williams in the first two weeks. I expect a similar level of performance from Tampa.
Prediction: Vikings 23, Buccaneers 17
Dajani ( Cowboys +3.5): International games aren't everyone's favorite, but consider that South American NFL games are averaging 55.5 points and 782.5 total yards! I'm expecting some points in this one, but I want to know where those…
author: Jordan Dajani

title: NFL Week 3 best bets: Seahawks win big in Sam Darnold's return, plus three player props to target
summary: The Week 3 card features two receiver props, a low-scoring Panthers-Browns prediction and a Saints same-game combination
full_text:
After a tough Week 1, we got back on track in Week 2. That's good news. As I said at the start of the week, the more we find out about these teams, the better we get (hopefully).
Stefon Diggs hit his five receptions, Jordan Love threw a pair of touchdowns to cash that bet, and the Rams won on "Monday Night Football." I had tied that to an any-time Puka Nacua touchdown, but Nacua didn't play (this column comes out on Friday, and last Friday, his status was up in the air). Hopefully you tailed the Los Angeles pick at least.
Regarding the misses, the Eagles , as seven-point favorites, barely escaped the Titans . Saquon Barkley getting hurt and missing a significant amount of the game didn't help, but clearly I underestimated Tennessee, and I also underestimated how much the Philadelphia offensive line and running game is struggling. I also missed on Justin Jefferson 80+ receiving yards. The game was took place in an absolute downpour. Sometimes, that's just how it goes.
Again, more knowledge is good. Week 2 was better than Week 1. Let's make Week 3 better than Week 2. As always, odds are via DraftKings .
Let's do a quick rundown of what the Commanders are facing:
Need I say more? I'd be surprised if the Commanders keep this within single digits, so if you want an alternate line, be my guest. I'll stick with Seattle -7.5 here.
Jameson Williams has to get going at some point, right? He has just six catches for 78 yards through two weeks, and his longest catch is just 22 yards. That's not the Jameson Williams we've come to know. He's a big play waiting to happen, and we shouldn't have to wait much longer.
This week will be the week it happens. The Jets ' defense has impressed thus far, but it helped that they played the Titans and then faced the Packers in the pouring rain. In the safe confines of Ford Field, the Lions -- and especially Williams -- are set to have a big day. Plus, given the state of the Lions' defense, this could be a high-scoring game that forces both offenses to keep their foot on the gas pedal.
Williams is still seeing solid under-the-hood numbers. He has 13 targets, and he's playing 90% of Detroit's offensive snaps. Two drops early have hurt, but Jared Goff sung his praises this offseason. He averaged 67 receiving yards per game in 2024 and 66 last year. Coming off a mini-bye, the Lions will have some big opportunities dialed up for their speedster.
Bryce Young has been superb to start this season, but check these numbers out:
Guess who plays the most man coverage in the NFL by a wide margin? The Browns !
It's a small sample size, of course, but Young also struggled vs. man coverage last year. There are concerns about whether Jalen Coker can play, too, and the ground game is yet to get going.
Meanwhile, I'm not buying the Deshaun Watson one-game renaissance. If he plays poorly at home, the boo birds will come out quickly, and it could snowball in the wrong direction from there. Carolina's defense played much better in Week 2, and it should be able to do so again here.
The Chargers ' offense has been an absolute mess this year. If you want a breakdown of why it's bad and how it can be fixed , JP Acosta explained it earlier today.
But the defense has also been underwhelming, and it's facing the Bills ' excellent offense. You know what that means? The Chargers will be chasing points all day long.
Ladd McConkey has been one of the very, very few bright spots. Not only has he looked good, but the Chargers' offense has actually looked good when he's on the field. No, really!
Anyway, McConkey has been a full participant in practice this week after leaving Week 1 with a rib injury and being questionable entering Week 2. He should have a big day.
I love combining these two here for a solid payout. New Orleans is coming off a 24-17 win over the Raiders . In the fourth quarter this season, Tyler Shough is 24 for 31 (77.4% comp pct) for 271 yards, with two touchdowns and no interceptions.
Plus, I don't think we're giving this Saints defense enough credit. Maybe it's because of their history with previous teams, but former Chargers coach Brandon Staley has been terrific as New Orleans' defensive coordinator, and the same goes for former No. 2 overall pick Chase Young . Since the start of last season, the Saints are 11th in defensive EPA per play. Young had 10 sacks in just 12 games last year and is off to another terrific start. His 18% pressure rate is 10th among 94 players with at least 40 pass rush snaps.
And then there's Chris Olave , who is just so, so good. He's seen 23 targets through two weeks and has 18 catches. He can win all over the field, and his route running is superb. The Raiders' secondary has been one of the pleasant surprises early this year, but they've yet to see a player of this caliber. Olave should have another huge day.

title: NFL Week 3's most underrated games: Why you should watch these three under-the-radar contests
summary: A look at some of the less talked-about games you should be tuning into
full_text:
I know it's only Week 3 of the NFL regular season, but does anyone else already feel like it's flying by? We've already seen so many highs and lows this year, and there are sure to be more of each this week.
There have been numerous significant injuries so far, with backup quarterbacks in all corners of the league needing to step in and step up. One of those quarterbacks will be highlighted in this week's edition of underrated games.
Every week I look at some of the under-the-radar games I think are worth tuning into and why. Let's not waste any time and dive into this week's selections:
Sunday, Sept. 27 at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS and streaming on Paramount+
Are the Las Vegas Raiders this year's New England Patriots , going from one of the worst to one of the best? It's too early to tell, but just three weeks in, the Raiders have the chance to make history. Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins can join Kurt Warner as the only quarterback since 1950 with three-plus passing touchdowns in each of his first three starts.
If the Raiders defeat the New Orleans Saints , they would become just the third team in the past 20 years to start 3-0 after a season with three or fewer wins. The other two teams to do so were the 2006 Saints and 2013 Kansas City Chiefs , both with a new head coach and quarterback.
The Saints won't make it easy, however. They are coming off a 24-17 win over the Baltimore Ravens , consistently one of the top AFC teams in recent history. They narrowly lost to the Detroit Lions in Week 1 after coming back from three touchdowns down. It was an overtime battle that came down to a failed two-point conversion.
The Raiders haven't made the playoffs since 2021 and haven't advanced past one round since 2002. The Saints last made the playoffs in 2020. This could be the year one of these teams snaps that streak.
I think this game will be a big one in seeing whether these teams can keep improving their stock.
Sunday, Sept. 27 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS and streaming on Paramount+
The New York Giants suffered a significant loss to their offense last week, when quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending injury. The Giants started the season on a high, defeating the Dallas Cowboys in Week 1, but came back down after the injury.
The optimism around the Giants has diminished, but playing a team that is still ironing out issues could work in New York's favor. The Titans come in 0-2, losing to the New York Jets in Week 1 and the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 2. A win this week would be a big morale booster in the Giants locker room and a confidence boost for Jameis Winston , who is now at the helm.
Winston is famously a very up-and-down QB who struggles with turnovers. He has 156 touchdowns and 114 interceptions in his 12-year career, including one pick in last week's loss to the Los Angeles Rams . I am interested to see whether the Giants can take an easier opponent than their last two and use it for momentum, or if the Titans can get their first check in the win column.
Another thing that makes this matchup interesting is that former Giants head coach Brian Daboll is now with the Titans as the offensive coordinator.
Sunday, Sept. 27 at 1 p.m. ET on Fox Sports (Stream: Fubo , try for free)
The Cleveland Browns won last week, and for a team that historically doesn't do a lot of winning, you'd think that would be a good thing. However... the Browns winning last week could actually be the worst thing to happen to them, and if you want to read more on that, click here .
The team was set to evaluate the quarterback position after two weeks, and much of Cleveland's fanbase is ready for the Deshaun Watson experiment to be over. The win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and former Browns quarterback Baker Mayfield pushed back the end of that experiment.
The Carolina Panthers are also coming off a win, a 34-3 victory over the Atlanta Falcons . Quarterback Bryce Young is tied for the league lead in touchdowns with six and is second in passing yards with 648.
I want to see where the Browns quarterback situation goes, as a bad game for Watson will have the fans calling even louder for a change. It will be a storyline to closely watch. I'm also curious to see how Young continues his touchdown streak. The Browns defense has allowed the third-most touchdowns this year (five) and could be one the former first-rounder could take advantage of.

title: 49ers GM John Lynch addresses potential Mac Jones trade amid wave of NFL quarterback injuries
summary: Jones went 5-3 as a starter in Purdy's absence last season and will become a free agent after the 2026 campaign
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers have no interest in trading No. 2 quarterback Mac Jones this season, at least not yet.
General manager John Lynch received more questions about the potential availability of Jones given the flurry of early injuries to starting quarterbacks around the league, which includes Caleb Wiliams, Jaxson Dart and Jayden Daniels .
Jones agreed to terms this offseason on a contract restructuring with the 49ers , who gave him a bump in pay after he went 5-3 as a starter in Brock Purdy's absence last year while completing 69.6 percent of his passes with an average attempt distance of 7.4 YPA — both career bests.
The NFL 's trade deadline is Nov. 10.
"I got to leave that alone," Lynch said this week, via KNBR . "What I will tell you is, I think a lot of people see all that and say, OK, there's opportunity. It also tells you we're very fortunate to have a guy like Brock (Purdy), franchise quarterback, but then to have a guy like Mac in the event (of Purdy getting injured).
"There's no more important position in football — they're all important — but I think we know as your quarterback goes, so goes your team. So, I think it's a really special situation to have Brock here and to have Mac here. And to have a guy we're really excited about with Kurtis Rourke ."
Having two viable quarterbacks you can win with is vital to league success, a luxury most teams don't have. Over 11 games last season, Jones proved his value to the 49ers after throwing for 2,151 yards and 13 touchdowns with a 97.6 passer rating — the highest of his five-year career.
Jones will be a free agent at the end of the season after initially signing a two-year deal with San Francisco in 2025 .
"I think back to Bill Walsh, maybe he was on to something when he had Joe Montana but he also brought Steve Young in here," Lynch said. "It's a good position to be in, a position of strength, and it provides opportunities in a number of ways, the most important way being that you're well insulated in the event something ever were to happen.
"And then there also are opportunities you receive calls and then you make decisions accordingly. But we love our situation at quarterback."
Purdy battled a turf toe situation last fall, giving way to Jones. Through two starts in his return to the lineup, Purdy is completing 80.4% of his passes for 492 yards and five touchdowns.
After beating the Rams to open in Australia and cruising past the Dolphins last week, it's clear the 49ers have Super Bowl hopes this fall with Purdy as their No. 1. If the team fades over the next seven weeks before the trade deadline, however, perhaps Lynch and the front office would engage in discussions with the promise of a healthy return of draft picks.
Unlike many teams entering Week 3, the 49ers are in a healthy position under center.

title: Giants' Jaxson Dart to undergo knee surgery for a full meniscus tear that will end his 2026 season
summary: Dart's ACL is intact, but his season is over
full_text:
The New York Giants ' fears have been realized. Quarterback Jaxson Dart will undergo knee surgery to fully repair his meniscus on Friday, ending his 2026 season, according to The Athletic . With damage to his MCL and PCL as a result of the injury as well, the surgeons may repair those areas if needed, but the meniscus remains the major issue. Dart's ACL is intact and shouldn't require treatment, ESPN reports.
The recovery is expected to be four to six months, putting Dart at a timeline of January to March. Earlier this week, Giants head coach John Harbaugh left the door open for a potential postseason return. The 2026 playoffs begin on Jan. 16, just under four months from the surgery date.
"I think I said it. I said it. Regular season," Harbaugh said on Wednesday, discussing how long Dart would be sidelined for. "Other than that, how do you know? It depends on the recovery. You can't pinpoint it."
Dart suffered the injury on the first drive of the night in New York's Monday night matchup against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 2. The former first-round pick was hit by multiple defenders while in the air, and his knee bent awkwardly. Initially, it was thought Dart's injury was not as severe, with reports suggesting he sprained his MCL.
Upon further review of the injury, however, it was worse than initially diagnosed.
Harbaugh discussed how much of a loss this is for the team and the message he's delivering to the locker room as the team adjusts to a new quarterback.
"I think [Dart's] determined. He's bummed. It's hard," Harbaugh said. "The season is not over, but it is for him. We kind of talked about that [in the team meeting], too. That was part of it. That was part of the deal. With injuries, there is a certain mourning that takes place. ... But it's tough on the team. It's tough on all of us."
Starting 12 games as a rookie after being the No. 25 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft , Dart entered this season as the full-time starter, and New York was eyed as a potential breakout team with John Harbaugh as head coach. The club furthered that offseason hype when it defeated the Dallas Cowboys in the season opener. In that game, Dart completed 79.3% of his passes for 230 yards and three passing touchdowns. Now, the 2026 season is viewed through a much different lens.
With him on the shelf, the Giants will likely turn to Jameis Winston as their starter going forward. While coming in under duress on Monday night against the Rams, Winston completed 11 of 27 passes for 111 yards and an interception.
That sharpens the stark contrast in what the play under center has looked like for New York over the last two seasons, with and without Dart.
Over the next month-plus, the Giants will host the Tennessee Titans in Week 3, and then the Arizona Cardinals in Week 4 before heading to Washington to face the Commanders (who lost their starter in Jayden Daniels ) in Week 5. They'll return to MetLife Stadium for a Week 6 matchup against the Saints , then travel to Houston to face the Texans in Week 6 before their Week 7 bye.

title: Jayden Daniels injury update: Commanders QB will avoid injured reserve after dislocating elbow

Despite his second gruesome left elbow dislocation in 11 months, Jayden Daniels will not undergo surgery, and no IR stint has been discussed, Commanders GM Adam Peters said Friday on his weekly appearance on The Sports Junkies radio show . ESPN later reported Daniels will not go on IR and is considered week-to-week.
Daniels visited multiple specialists and underwent further imaging after suffering the injury when trying to brace an awkward fall on Sunday against the Cowboys . The 2024 Offensive Rookie of the Year took an under-center snap and got stepped on by left guard Chris Paul. He was eventually carted off with a towel over his head.
Daniels will miss Sunday's game against the Seahawks as the 0-2 Commanders look to get their season on track with Marcus Mariota under center, but Peters stating that an IR stint hasn't been discussed is an encouraging update.
When Daniels dislocated his elbow for the first time last year, he missed four weeks (three games plus a bye). When he returned, however, he re-aggravated the injury after falling hard on his left elbow while chasing down Andrew Van Ginkel following an interception. Daniels, who was wearing an elbow brace, didn't suffer any additional damage to the elbow, but he did not play again for the rest of the year; the Commanders were out of the playoff race. title: Packers desperately need Micah Parsons, Josh Jacobs back: When are they expected to return?
summary: Green Bay's streak of 13 straight wins in home openers came to an end against Atlanta
full_text:
This isn't how it was supposed to go early this season for the Green Bay Packers , especially after Thursday night's get-right opportunity against Atlanta in front of their home crowd.
What followed was a deflating 35-14 loss without two of their top players, pushing the Packers to 1-2 — their worst start in eight seasons under coach Matt LaFleur.
Punctuated by a chorus of boos in the second half , Green Bay had no answers defensively for the Falcons ' dominance at the line of scrimmage. It's all the more evidence the Packers are clearly struggling to fill production voids left by injured stalwarts Micah Parsons and Josh Jacobs .
The Packers desperately missed Parsons in run support after Bijan Robinson galloped his way to 194 yards rushing and two scores on 29 carries, going downhill for much of the second half against a gassed defense. Green Bay only managed one sack and rarely pressured Michael Penix Jr. , who was making his season debut after a season-ending injury in 2025's Week 11 last fall.
Parsons hasn't played this season after tearing the ACL and meniscus in his left knee last December. He's on the PUP list, meaning he will at least miss one more game before he's able to return.
The Packers have not opened Parsons' 21-day practice window, however, and LaFleur said on Sept. 17 that he felt the defensive end was still "a couple weeks away" from getting back out there.
After putting together a nine-play, 87-yard touchdown drive on their second possession against the Falcons, Green Bay's next six drives resulted in no points, including three 3-and-outs. Over that stretch, a one-possession lead turned into a 20-point home deficit, leading to disdain from the Lambeau Field faithful.
The Packers' 17 yards rushing was their lowest total in a game since 1999. Marshawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson each had four attempts, while quarterback Jordan Love had a single scramble.
"I think we've got to continue to work with these guys and try to figure out what we do well," LaFleur said. "Because right now I don't know what we're doing well offensively."
Without Jacobs, their leading rusher the past two seasons, the Packers' offense averaged a league-worst 64.5 rushing yards per game coming into Thursday's faceplant. Jacobs is currently on the commissioner's exempt list after an offseason arrest and groin injury during camp.
Previous reports indicate that the NFL may count his time on the exempt list as "time served" in the event of a suspension. Over 32 games in his first two seasons with the Packers, Jacobs has rushed for 2,258 yards and 28 touchdowns, giving Love more than enough firepower behind him to balance the offense.
Beyond the availability of Parsons and Jacobs, Green Bay has a lot to fix, and it signed LaFleur to a multi-year contract extension in January after the 2025 season ended with a wild-card round playoff loss to the Chicago Bears .
The agreement with LaFleur was reportedly a "real commitment" to him from Green Bay's power brass despite the franchise losing five consecutive games to end the 2025 campaign. It put an end to hot-seat talk coming out of his seventh season, but a surprising 1-2 start has raised questions again.
This was another stunning performance, which comes after the Packers lost by 17 points in the opener at Minnesota and needed overtime to beat the New York Jets last week after erasing a 10-point deficit in the fourth quarter.

title: Packers' Tucker Kraft responds to boos at Lambeau Field: 'It's not going to help us win'
summary: Kraft didn't appreciate the reception from the home crowd during the team's loss to the Falcons
full_text:
The Green Bay Packers got demolished on Thursday night, dropping their home opener to the previously 0-2 Atlanta Falcons , 35-14. The Packers struggled to do everything, essentially, on both sides of the ball, and their fans took notice, raining boos down on the team throughout the game and especially the second half.
Packers tight end Tucker Kraft did not appreciate the serenades.
"That's pretty tough. Like everyone pictures Lambeau Field and not boos," Kraft said, via NBC26 . "I don't picture boos when I picture my home stadium. That's tough. It's pretty disappointing, especially for a home opener. It's pretty disappointing. It's not going to help us win. Like, I don't know what people think that's going to rally us or something like that. But that's — we're grown men. We're mentally strong enough, capable enough to get back on the field and play ball. But it'd probably be much easier with the 70,000 people behind us rather than opposing us."
The thing about the boos in this situation is that they were well-earned.
The Packers were a disaster on Thursday night. They allowed the Falcons to pile up 498 yards and control the ball for 37:05 of game time. They repeatedly missed tackles and allowed Bijan Robinson and Drake London to run wild. The Packers also ran the ball for just 17 yards on nine carries, their fewest rush yards in a game since 1999. Jordan Love averaged 5.8 yards per pass attempt. There wasn't a single thing the Packers did well, and the fans let them know about it.
Packers wide receiver Christian Watson didn't necessarily appreciate the boos, either, but he acknowledged that they stemmed from the performance the Packers put out there.
"It's tough," Watson said, via ESPN . "But at the end of the day, it's an entertainment business, so we have to put a better product out on the field if we want to have the fans have our back. Obviously, we like to think that the fans will be there through the ups and downs, but we've got to put out a better performance than that."
The Packers are now 1-2 heading into their Week 4 game against the Buccaneers . They are decimated by injuries and have yet to truly play well on either side of the ball. They need to use this mini-bye to clean things up, or else the boos are going to be something they'll have to get used to this year.

title: Week 3 2026 bold predictions: Lackluster Steelers force multiple turnovers against Joe Burrow
