title: Strange coincidence ties Buffalo Bills pass rusher Greg Rousseau to Chargers rookie Akheem Mesidor
summary: Akheem Mesidor and Greg Rousseau are connected in a few ways. They both attended the University of Miami. They both were first-round picks. And they have the same birthday, April 5th. Earlier this week, I wrote about age-based draft analysis regarding Rousseau, and that now, at 26 years old, he’s starting to look like a […]
full_text: Akheem Mesidor and Greg Rousseau are connected in a few ways. They both attended the University of Miami. They both were first-round picks. And they have the same birthday, April 5th. Earlier this week, I wrote about age-based draft analysis regarding Rousseau , and that now, at 26 years old, he’s starting to look like a clear long-game win for those — like myself — who very much factor age into pre-draft analysis. On that note, check this tweet I sent back on April 5 (disregard me mis-spelling Mesidor’s first name): Greg Rousseau is exactly one year older than '26 draft prospect Ahkeem Mesidor (their birthday is today) — Chris Trapasso (@ChrisTrapasso) April 5, 2026 How insane is that? Rousseau is more than 3,500 NFL snaps into his career despite being exactly one year older than the Chargers rookie who’ll play in his third professional game in Orchard Park. Mind-blowing, really. Mesidor does have five pressures on 40 pass-rush snaps through two contests, which equates to a solid albeit unspectacular pressure rate of 12.5% — anything over 15% for an edge rusher is outstanding. He’s appeared on 66 snaps through two games, which means he’s the bookend to one Khalil Mack, a defender who many believe should be a future Hall of Famer. I am one of those many, by the way. At 6’3” and 260 pounds, Mesidor is decently compact, sizable outside rusher, and he thrived against the run in college. Here’s what I wrote about him before the draft: “Akheem Mesidor is a wide-framed, well-built EDGE with adequate length and a powerful, tenacious play style. He’s difficult to displace in the run game thanks to his mass and balance, and he delivers consistent pop on contact. While his first-step burst is above average, he won’t consistently win in the NFL purely on get-off. He’s a better overall mover than you might expect for his build — fluid enough changing directions, flexible enough to flatten occasionally, and relentless with his motor. As a pass rusher, Mesidor is advanced and versatile. He works half a man effectively, mixes outside speed with inside counters, and keeps tackles guessing with varied rush paths. His rip move carries real power, the swim is functional, and he’ll mix in bull rush attempts with good — though not overwhelming — point-of-attack strength. He’s close to being a true finesse technician, showing more polish than most EDGE prospects in this class. That said, when counters stall out, his pad level can rise and he can be driven off his track. He wins more with sequencing, balance, and controlled violence than rare explosiveness. Against the run, Mesidor aggressively works off blocks and shows strong awareness locating the football. He’s not fun to double due to his brawler mentality and sturdy base. The primary caveat is age — he’ll be 25 before the draft — and his game reflects that maturity in terms of nuance and refinement. While others in the class may be more explosive, few offer his blend of power, hustle, hand usage, and natural movement skills. He projects as a pro-ready rotational EDGE with three-down capability and a relatively high floor.” In short, Mesidor showed outstanding relentlessness on film that was every bit first-round caliber. Frankly, he looked exactly how you’d expect a 24 year old to appear facing offensive linemen younger than him. It was because of his age I couldn’t convince myself he should’ve been selected in Round 1. I gave Mesidor a late Round 2 – early Round 3 grade (and compared him to Michael Bennett). He ultimately was picked at No. 22 overall by the Chargers and will see his fellow Hurricane alum and birthday twin on Sunday as the Chargers take on the Bills. What a strange coincidence regarding Rousseau and Mesidor, one that provides immense perspective on how age factors into the pre-draft process.
author: Chris Trapasso

title: Buffalo Bills Week 3 rooting interests around the NFL
summary: Buffalo did its part last week. Asking the rest of the NFL to cooperate apparently was a little too much.  Still, the Bills head into Week 3 with two wins and a chance to add another against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday. That’s the assignment that matters most. Everything else is us being helpful — whether the teams involved appreciate […]
full_text: Buffalo did its part last week. Asking the rest of the NFL to cooperate apparently was a little too much. Still, the Bills head into Week 3 with two wins and a chance to add another against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday. That’s the assignment that matters most. Everything else is us being helpful — whether the teams involved appreciate our very temporary support or not. We’re three weeks into this, and our rooting interests already need a reminder: We don’t want every AFC team losing every week. Some of them need to win just enough to stay away from the best players in next year’s draft. The exception, of course, is the AFC East. The Patriots, Jets, and Dolphins can keep losing. We’ll live with the consequences. For everyone else, there’s an order to this. Buffalo wins first. Division rivals lose. Then we want wins from teams the Bills have beaten to help their strength of victory, followed by wins from other Buffalo opponents to build strength of schedule. When none of those apply, we want the AFC leaders coming back toward the middle of the standings and the struggling teams winning their way out of premium draft position. These are rooting interests, not predictions, and absolutely none of them require us to like the teams we’re choosing. Which is good, because you’ve probably already noticed who Miami plays this week. _____________________________________________________________________________ AFC EAST Buffalo Bills over Los Angeles Chargers We wanted the Chargers to win last week. This week, they’re visiting Buffalo, so that arrangement is over. The Bills have an opportunity to get to 3-0, and nothing happening elsewhere makes up for letting that opportunity get away. Go Bills! Jacksonville Jaguars over New England Patriots Before anyone brings up the fact that Buffalo plays New England twice, yes, we know. That’s why the division rule comes before strength of schedule. Jacksonville gets our support, and the Patriots get another week of us wishing them absolutely nothing good. Detroit Lions over New York Jets Detroit can help us twice here. Buffalo already beat the Lions, so a Detroit win adds to the Bills’ strength of victory while handing the Jets a loss. We spent last Thursday rooting against them, but this is a very good week to get back on Detroit’s side. Kansas City Chiefs over Miami Dolphins Yes, again. But this week, you don’t even have to listen to a lengthy explanation about Buffalo’s schedule. Kansas City is playing Miami, and our division rule settles it. You can spend the entire game complaining about the Chiefs and still want the Dolphins to lose. We’re capable of both. _____________________________________________________________________________ The rest of the AFC Houston Texans over Indianapolis Colts Houston, we need you to start holding up your end of this arrangement. Buffalo already has the win over the Texans. Now we need Houston to collect some wins of their own so that victory can help the Bills in a tiebreaker later. Pittsburgh Steelers over Cincinnati Bengals Neither team is on Buffalo’s schedule, so this one goes to the standings. Cincinnati has started 2-0, while Pittsburgh is 1-1. Give the Steelers the win and bring the Bengals back to the middle of the pack. We don’t need Cincinnati building an early cushion while we’re busy worrying about everybody else. Cleveland Browns over Carolina Panthers This is where our draft-position rule gets some work. Neither team is a Buffalo opponent, and Cleveland isn’t leading its division. Let the Browns collect a win that could eventually move them away from a premium pick, while the Panthers take the loss. If somebody is going to come out of this season with access to the best available talent in next year’s draft, we’d prefer that somebody live in the NFC. Tennessee Titans over New York Giants Same principle. The Titans are winless, and neither team is on Buffalo’s schedule. We don’t need Tennessee spending the entire season working toward the top of the draft. Give the Titans a win and leave the Giants a little closer to that particular prize. Las Vegas Raiders over New Orleans Saints Here’s where the order of our rules matters. We could make an argument for wanting an AFC loss, but Las Vegas is on Buffalo’s schedule, and New Orleans isn’t. For now, that strength-of-schedule benefit gets the Raiders our support. If the conference race gives us a more pressing reason to root against them later, we’ll adjust, but we aren’t there yet. Baltimore Ravens over Dallas Cowboys Baltimore is another Buffalo opponent, so we’re sticking with the schedule benefit here, too. There will probably be plenty of opportunities to root against the Ravens before this is over. This week, we want them beating Dallas. Nobody said following our own rules would always be pleasant. Los Angeles Rams over Denver Broncos Buffalo plays both teams, which means we get the same strength-of-schedule benefit either way. Denver won its division last season, so this is a chance to apply our rule about bringing those teams down a peg without giving up anything on the schedule side. _____________________________________________________________________________ NFC vs. NFC games Green Bay Packers over Atlanta Falcons The Packers are on Buffalo’s schedule, and the Falcons aren’t. That gives us a straightforward assignment for Thursday night without needing to consult the standings, think about the draft, or argue with ourselves. Go Pack Go. Minnesota Vikings over Tampa Bay Buccaneers Minnesota gets the same treatment. The Bills play the Vikings later this season, so we want them adding wins whenever Buffalo isn’t the opponent. Tampa Bay doesn’t give us that benefit. Go Vikings. Chicago Bears over Philadelphia Eagles Last week, I let my irritation with the Bears’ offense comparisons help settle a pick between two Buffalo opponents. This week, only Chicago is on the Bills’ schedule, so I have to put that aside. We’re rooting for the Bears. After all, having rules means being held to them. San Francisco 49ers over Arizona Cardinals San Francisco has opened 2-0, while Arizona is 1-1. With no direct Buffalo schedule benefit available, we’ll give the win to the 49ers and leave the Cardinals closer to the better pick. _____________________________________________________________________________ So, yes, we’re asking some AFC teams to win and others to lose while making a few exceptions for Buffalo’s schedule. We want help now, useful tiebreakers later, and fewer opportunities for struggling conference opponents to solve their problems next April. If that sounds a little selfish, you’ve understood the assignment. Go Bills!
author: Rachel Auberger

title: Brian Answers: Bryce Young & Brad Idzik evolution, Bobby Okereke surprise, and more!
summary: Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone! We got the Browns on deck on Sunday coming off a fantastic and complete win last week. The rose colored glasses are on, and hopefully don’t drop off any time soon. So I’m going to answer all of your […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - AUGUST 21: Offensive coordinator Brad Idzik of the Carolina Panthers takes the field prior to the preseason game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Field on August 21, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone! We got the Browns on deck on Sunday coming off a fantastic and complete win last week. The rose colored glasses are on, and hopefully don’t drop off any time soon. So I’m going to answer all of your questions from the week, let’s dive right in! Forager: Continuing with the optimism and believing the Panthers have their franchise quarterback (I’ll let you pick if it’s Bryce or Haynes :-)), and that they will be picking 32nd in next year’s draft, what position or positions would be on the table for that pick? Seeing the success Waller is having, maybe a pass-catching TE? Possibly an OG for salary cap concerns? Another edge rusher because injuries seem to love this position? Its hard to say at this point, but the Panthers definitely seem to prioritize the trenches on both sides of the ball. Depending on where they pick, a center or a guard would make a lot of sense. I can’t imagine they’ll hang on to both Robert Hunt and Damien Lewis as their cap hits get larger. They could again aim for another tackle since Taylor Moton, Ikem Ekwonu, and Rasheed Walker could all be out the door next off-season depending on circumstance. EDGE rusher is always a thought since this defense tends to rotate them in quite often. I could even see an interior linebacker as a longer term answer to pair with Devin Lloyd. Bobby Okereke has been playing well, but I think he’s more of a stop gap option for the team. Brice Guild: Brian, I know all the talk is about the play of Lloyd and he has been fun to watch but my biggest surprise has been Okereke. He seems faster and more versatile then I expected. He seems to already, in this new to him defense, playing quick and effective. Is it just a good scheme match that is allowing him to play faster then last year? What is your expectations for the development of the chemistry between Lloyd and him and their ceiling together as a interior LB pairing. I think Okereke is definitely a good scheme fit for what Carolina wants out of their interior linebackers, guys who can aggressively pursue the rush and maintain integrity in zone coverage schemes in the pass. I think they’ve developed relatively good chemistry but we’ve also seen both sides of the extremes as far as offenses they’ve faced are concerned. The Bears blew up this defense and the Falcons could barely move the ball without hurting themselves. Let’s see what it looks like in 4-5 weeks for a better answer. TXPanther: The Panthers hiring Darrell Bevell as associate HC/offensive specialist flew under the radar for most of us… could he be the answer to why the offense looks to have taken a step? I absolutely think it helped quite a bit. Between hiring the guy that Dave Canales and Brad Idzik cut their teeth under in Seattle, and Dave Canales handing the reigns off to Idzik with Bevell there to support him, I could totally see Bevell being a bigger reason than people realize in this offense being so effective all of a sudden. Both Canales and Idzik call plays that are likely largely based on what they learned during their time serving underneath him. WanderingJanusz: Is Nic Scourton the Kelvin Benjamin of 2026? I’m not ready to award this team with the energy of the 2015 Panthers just two weeks into the season. They are 1-1, so they’d have to win every game left in the regular season to match that energy. That said, it is interesting how Ejiro Evero is deploying his defense now that the pass rush isn’t going to passively generate pressure like they would have (in theory) with a fully healthy Scourton in the rotation. He blitzed a lot last week. @WTMealey: Amongst their peers who would rank higher BY vs QBs Canales vs HCs DM vs GMs Idzik vs OCs Meaning if Bryce is top 15 QB but DM is top 5 GM he ranks higher I would say Dan Morgan vs General Managers, basically because he has two whole offseasons under his belt where many pundits said it was some of the best drafting and maneuvering in free agency they had seen. Right now, Canales, Bryce Young, and Idzik are all kind of starting on new footing. So I’m going with Dan Morgan. Gunnercrf: How about that lead block by Moehrig on that pick six?! That was so hype he pancaked the guy so bad at the endzone he woke up in a Denny’s. Love seeing defensive players lead blocking for their teammates. While Tre’Von Moehrig isn’t a traditional safety by any means, he absolutely brings the physicality on just about every play he can. I very much enjoy watching him play. Kind of reminds me of Chris Harris with how he hits at times. SmoothC: How different would the ATL game be if they had a QB above the level of a moldy pumpkin? The defense still allowed 160 yards rushing. Taking your starters out in the 4th quarter during a blowout win doesn’t help the rushing numbers in a vacuum. They very much held the Falcons and especially Bijan Robinson in check when it mattered. SnarkyComet: Brian, curious on your take of a segment on Rich Eisen’s Overreaction Monday (On a Tuesday) this week where it was proposed that Bryce could wind up in the top 5 passers in the NFL this season. Eisen quickly said it wasn’t an overreaction and that he’s been playing great, but he wants to see how Bryce will do against this Browns defense. Crazy talk or is there something there? Based on two games worth of information to digest, no it isn’t crazy. Is it objectively an overreaction? Yes, I would say so. Carolina has a lot of good teams on their schedule this season and much better defenses ahead. Combine that with the general wear and tear of the long NFL season likely causing some important starters to miss at least some time, and teams getting more film on Brad Idzik’s tendencies as a play caller, and things could absolutely slow down. But Bryce has built a case so far that he could and should be in that conversation. JakeNCVA: At least twice this summer (once by me), you were asked if we expected the playcalling to be much different under Idzik than it was under Canales. And if I remember correctly the short answer was no, not really. We have seen the offense be better so far than it was most of the time last season. Well to be more precise, we have seen the passing game be better. Some people are attributing this to Idzik calling for more passes down the field. But that would mean that last season Canales called pass plays that were designed dump offs at the LOS at least half of the time while still sending receivers downfield. Through two games the Panthers offense is averaging almost 40 drop backs at game to around 20 running plays. Yes there have been increased targets to the tight ends in both games – something I imagine Canales and Idzik planned on doing in the offseason. As some of your CSR counterparts have said — it appears the game has slowed down for Bryce. Canales said “Bryce has taken advantage of the looks he has gotten”. Is it really the play calling or more like both Bryce Young and the receivers have both improved this season. I’ll be happy to get my receipts for not being correct necessarily in my prediction. However, I do think its a combination of Brad Idzik encouraging more aggression and Bryce Young simply being way more comfortable and confident. They were running similar down field concepts in 2025, and sometimes Bryce just didn’t throw them and elected to play it safe. But by the same token, I don’t know how much Canales was gearing him towards playing it more safe than letting it rip. We certainly saw Bryce let it rip at times in 2025, but he’s been really dealing the ball. I almost feel like we’re seeing an evolution of Canales’s game plans with some higher urgency to score…

title: Panthers vs Browns: Matchups to watch
summary: The Carolina Panthers bounced back from a big home loss to the Chicago Bears at home to notch a big win over the Atlanta Falcons on the road. They swept the matchups we highlighted in this space last week, particularly with the linebackers coming to play against Bijan Robinson (even though Robinson did manage a […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 29: Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns reacts in the third quarter against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on September 29, 2024 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers bounced back from a big home loss to the Chicago Bears at home to notch a big win over the Atlanta Falcons on the road. They swept the matchups we highlighted in this space last week, particularly with the linebackers coming to play against Bijan Robinson (even though Robinson did manage a decent amount of rushing yards). Winning all the key matchups like that is an easy way to beat your opponent be 31 points. The Panthers will try to get a similar result in another road game, this time against the Cleveland Browns. Jaelan Phillips vs Tytus Howard The Browns traded for Howard in the offseason to try to solidify a leaky offensive line. He hasn’t provided a great return on that investment yet. The Browns as a team have yielded seven sacks through two weeks, and all but one of them has come from an edge rusher (shoutout former Panther A’Shawn Robinson for the other). A fair amount of that is on DeShaun Watson for holding the ball too long, but still, it’s an opportunity for Phillips to make it three straight games with a sack to start his tenure in Carolina. Howard has had some struggles in pass protection, so it’s a matchup the Panthers will be looking for Phillips to win. Howard has been decent in the run game, but he’s been just about the only Browns lineman that can boast that, and if Phillips can hold up there, the front should be able to keep the Browns woeful run game in check. Jaycee Horn/Mike Jackson vs Denzel Boston The safeties may have a role to play here as well, but the corners will get the bulk of the responsibility for covering the Browns rookie wide receiver. Boston has caught touchdown passes of over 40 yards in each of the first two games of the season. The Browns have not been good from play to play and drive to drive, so it’s paramount that the Panthers don’t let them off the hook with any big plays over the top. Now that it’s worked a couple of times, Watson will surely be hunting more deep looks to Boston in this one. Panthers interior offensive line vs Mason Graham The Browns have four sacks through two games. Two are from Mason Graham, and the other two are from safeties Grant Delpit and Ronnie Hickman. The rest of the Browns pass rush has been underwhelming so far (though there’s always a chance that Jared Verse wakes up). Based on the first two weeks, if the interior can hold up against Graham any blitzers from the secondary, the offensive line should be able to give Bryce Young time to find his targets. Cleveland Browns fans vs DeShaun Watson Browns fans have made it no secret that they’re not happy about their controversial quarterback getting paid tens of millions dollars per year to barely play and then play poorly when he does play. And Watson has not been shy about his frustration with people who are unhappy that he’s been a terrible quarterback while also allegedly being a terrible person. Shame on them, right? Well this will be Watson’s first regular season game in front of the home crowd. The Browns are coming off a win, and Watson played reasonably well in that win. It’ll be interesting to see if Browns fans will send more vitriol his way or if one decent performance in a win is enough to call off the dogs for the time being. Either way, if the Panthers defense can jump on Watson early and cause some poor offensive possessions, it’s very likely the crowd is going to turn on the home team and create a lot of strife.

title: Panthers vs. Browns: Storylines to watch
summary: The Carolina Panthers are coming off their first win of the season, over the division rival Falcons. Their opponent this week is also coming off a win over an NFC South division rival, as the Browns defeated the Buccaneers 23-19. This put both teams’ 2026 seasons back on track at 1-1, and the Panthers will […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NC - AUGUST 08: Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young (9) directs a receiver before throwing a touchdown pass during a NFL preseason football game between the Cleveland Browns and the Carolina Panthers on August 8, 2025, at Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, N.C. (Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Carolina Panthers are coming off their first win of the season, over the division rival Falcons. Their opponent this week is also coming off a win over an NFC South division rival, as the Browns defeated the Buccaneers 23-19. This put both teams’ 2026 seasons back on track at 1-1, and the Panthers will now visit the Browns in Cleveland on Sunday. The Panthers are riding high off a strong offensive start to the season for QB Bryce Young, and that’s my first storyline to keep track of. Offense: Continue attacking down the field The most surprising storyline coming out of two weeks of the NFL season across the league is the Panthers’ crazy effectiveness with the deep ball. Jalen Coker is rated the highest at deep ball effectiveness at WR by Pro Football Focus so far, and Tetairoa McMillan has also been an effective down field weapon for the team. Combine that with an insane air yard throw from Bryce to Xavier Legette this past Sunday, and its clear this Panthers team is pushing to be aggressive in the passing game. The Browns defense as a whole hasn’t been the best so far, but on paper they quietly have a very solid defense. They have a very solid secondary and a front seven that could cause problems for the Panthers rushing attack. The Panthers need to see the continued momentum from Bryce Young attacking down the field with touch and confidence, as he’s put together some of his best consecutive deep passing games in his career. I would expect offensive coordinator Brad Idzik to continue to be aggressive on that front. Defense: Don’t sleep on Quinshon Judkins The Browns faced two very good rushing defenses against the Jaguars and Buccaneers in consecutive weeks, and those teams held down the Browns rushing attack for the most part. Judkins only averaged 2.8 yards per carry in week 1 and 1.8 yards per carry in week 2, both pretty miserable performances for the former 2nd round pick who likely would have been picked in the 1st had he not had some off field issues. This could be a bounce back game for Judkins if the Browns focus on the rushing attack to try and stabilize the offense for QB Deshaun Watson, who himself had a decent bounce back performance last week against the Browns. X Factor: Cleveland Browns young receiving core The Browns spent high picks on WRs KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston in 2026, and drafted promising young TE Harold Fannin in 2025. Any time you have a receiving group that unproven, teams tend to view it as a weakness. However, Denzel Boston has caught 7 receptions for 154 yards and 2 TDs this season, Fannin has 7 catches for 75 yards, and Concepcion has 10 catches for 71 yards in two games. This is with Deshaun Watson at QB who hasn’t really played football for several years now. I wouldn’t underestimate these guys, even if the Panthers secondary matches up extremely well against them in theory. The Bears lit up this defense in the passing game week 1, admittedly with an all-world performance from their QB Caleb Williams. Still, I wouldn’t be surprised if many of these guys eat well on Sunday and the game is much closer than many fans expect. What storylines are you watching this weekend, Panthers fans?

title: Do you trust Tyson Bagent or Case Keenum more against the Eagles?
summary: The Chicago Bears have a big matchup on Monday Night Football, taking on the Philadelphia Eagles. If the Bears lose, they’ll fall below .500 for the first time in a year. It’s only game three, but obviously, everyone would like to see the Bears get back on track after a tough loss in week two […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 29: Case Keenum #11 of the Chicago Bears drops back to pass during the second half of the Week 3 preseason game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on August 29, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears have a big matchup on Monday Night Football, taking on the Philadelphia Eagles. If the Bears lose, they’ll fall below .500 for the first time in a year. It’s only game three, but obviously, everyone would like to see the Bears get back on track after a tough loss in week two against the Minnesota Vikings. Caleb Williams was knocked out of the game, and Ben Johnson has said that he is week-to-week, but almost everyone is certain that he will miss the Eagles game. If he does, that means it will either be Tyson Bagent, if he can clear concussion protocol, or Case Keenum, the veteran QB who has been mostly considered an assistant QB coach in a Bears uniform. Bagent has the youth; Keenum has the veteran experience (but is it too much experience, if you know what I mean). Who do you trust more against the Eagles: Tyson Bagent or Case Keenum? I think the easy answer without thinking would be Tyson Bagent. But this Eagles defense is led by the great Vic Fangio, and we know that Vic has the ability to put inexperienced QBs in a blender. Would the Bears be better off with Keenum, who happens to be 3-0 career against Fangio (albeit when he was much younger), who can read a defense as well as anybody in the league and make snap decisions with the football? Answer: This one, for me, is really difficult to answer. I think the idea of Keenum makes a ton of sense to go up against the Eagles and Fangio. He is a statue back there, but he can stand and deliver. The question is, who is Case Keenum at this point? In the preseason, Keenum was outstanding (as he was in the 2025 preseason as well). Keenum was 25 of 40 for 354 yards, 2 TDs, and 0 INTs. That’s good enough for a 107.7 rating. However, we have to take into account that he was going up against 3rd-stringers. Keenum hasn’t thrown a ball in the regular season since 2023, and in his final four years where he played (2020-2023), the numbers were poor. He threw just 140 attempts over those 4 years and had a yards-per-attempt average under 6. He also had as many INTs as TDs (4 each). So we have to ask ourselves: with Keenum, are we getting the guy who can operate Ben Johnson’s system brilliantly in the preseason, or are we getting the washed QB that looked terrible in his last few regular-season games? While I’ve been leaning towards Keenum for most of this week, I think, in the end, Bagent, if he can play, makes more sense. Bagent also operates Johnson’s system well in the preseason, and his arrow is pointing up, not down. If it’s Keenum, I don’t think it’s a huge difference. If we ranked QBs on a scale of 1 to 10 to face Philly and Caleb is a 10, I think Bagent is a 6 and Keenum is a 5. I think the way Garrett Bradbury is playing with those Eagles DTs, I would rather have a more mobile QB in Bagent because I think the Bears will give up a little pressure. So while I will have almost as much confidence in Keenum as I would with Bagent, I think I lean just a little bit on the Bagent side. What do you say, Bears fans? Would you rather see Bagent or Keenum out there against the Eagles? Sound off in the comments section!

title: Chicago Bears Big Play Breakdowns from Week 2
summary: Week 2 brought 8 more explosive plays. Wait – eight?! That can’t be right; let me go back and…yeah, eight. It’s honestly unbelievable the Chicago Bears didn’t win this one, but a fumble at the goal line and the Williams injury, combined with the constant rain, conspired to leave the Bears with only three points […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Kyle Monangai #25 of the Chicago Bears runs with the ball during the third quarter of the game against the Minnesota Vikings at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 2 brought 8 more explosive plays. Wait – eight?! That can’t be right; let me go back and…yeah, eight. It’s honestly unbelievable the Chicago Bears didn’t win this one, but a fumble at the goal line and the Williams injury, combined with the constant rain, conspired to leave the Bears with only three points for their efforts. However, there was still some good stuff, particularly in the run game, as this 2026 Bears squad starts to figure out who they are going to be this year. Explosive Play 2.1 – Q1 10:26, 2nd and 3 from the Chicago 38. Caleb Williams aborted snap, recovered at Chicago 36 by Williams, run up the middle for 17 yards. Obviously an incredibly creative play call by Johnson to put the ball on the ground and just have Caleb run up the middle for an explosive play… Okay, maybe we should’ve known this one was going to be weird. Busted play, quarterback is talented enough to make it a chunk gain instead of a disaster. Caleb Williams drops the snap, recovers, and picks up 17 yards MINvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/awjnArPfjv — NFL (@NFL) September 20, 2026 Explosive Play 2.2 – Q3 14:50, 2nd and 10 from the Chicago 35. D’Andre Swift off left tackle for 12 yards. The Bears come out in 12 personnel with Kmet attached on the right and Loveland attached on the left side of the line. Rome and Kalif Raymond line up stacked to the left of Loveland. At the snap, Raymond drags across to the right in what looks like a potential play action pass dump off option for a future play. Braxton and Loveland do enough to stalemate their defender and Thuney works up to the second level to get a hat on his assignment. Swift finds the space off the left tackle (hat tip to Rome for hanging with his defender) and with a little stutter step makes the safety miss in the hole, gaining another 6-7 before running out of bounds. Well blocked but Swift’s missed tackle takes it from a nice run to set up a third and short to a fresh set of downs. Explosive Play 2.3 – Q3 14:10, 2nd and 10 from the Chicago 47. Caleb Williams scrambles up the middle for 11 yards. It goes down as an explosive play as it is a run play once Caleb decides to tuck it and go. This was his second of three explosive runs on the day and the first off a scramble. A good decision to go after working through his progression and he knew where the sticks were to keep this drive going early in the third by taking contact and pushing through for the first. It’s the second explosive run of the series. Explosive Play 2.4 – Q3 13:28, 1st and 10 from the Minnesota 42. Kyle Monangai off right end for 15 yard gain. The third explosive run of the drive and the first for Monangai. This is one of those runs where you look back and think…why did he not have 30 carries in this one? The Bears use 12 personnel here, with both Loveland and Kmet on the right hand side of the line with Odunze split out wide. Monangai runs through contact trying to poke out the ball around the line of scrimmage and bursts through the hole before dragging the corner for about six additional yards and another set of downs. Explosive Play 2.5 – Q3 12:14, 2nd and 6 from the Minnesota 23. Kyle Monangai off right guard for 12 yards. The fourth explosive run on the drive and the second for Monangai. Just two plays after the 15 yarder, the Bears use Cole Kmet as a full back and line up in the I-formation. Blocking action moves to the right with Kmet filling the edge defender on the left. Monangai starts the action to the right and makes a cut back to the middle of the field. He’s untouched for ten yards before falling forward for a couple extra. Well blocked here by the Bears. Unbelievably, the four explosive runs on the same drive would not lead to points as D’Andre Swift would fumble at the one a few plays later. Explosive Play 2.6 – Q3 5:19, 3rd and 6 from the Chicago 17. Caleb Williams scrambles off left end for 10 yards. It’s not worth spending a ton of time breaking down scrambles but again I think this is an aspect of Caleb’s game that we can appreciate him flexing when needed. The concern with the hamstring injury going forward is if he’ll feel comfortable running and if so, will he be able to shift into high gear. Anyway, love the spin move here and my mind automatically added a Chris Berman sound effect when he did it. First down with a spin 👀 MINvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/yL3Bljcwxk — NFL (@NFL) September 20, 2026 Explosive Play 2.7 – Q4 11:43, 3rd and 7 from the Chicago 36. Caleb Williams passes short left to D’Andre Swift for 32 yards. A well-timed screen on 3rd down here. It’s a nice play design with a WR screen set up on the right side, where Caleb gives a pump fake, before coming back to Swift on the left side. Swift has a couple of blockers who don’t really impact the play here. He is able to make the first defender miss at the sticks before breaking away from a second defender who goes for the strip. He’s not quite able to run away from the third defender before being taken down for a monster gain. The play design earned the first but Swift again took it from a nice play to an explosive. Big catch-and-run for D'Andre Swift! MINvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/2Pcqvzgkg3 — NFL (@NFL) September 20, 2026 Explosive Play 2.8 – Q4 0:38, 2nd and 10 from the Minnesota 41. Tyson Bagent completes pass deep right to Rome Odunze for 21 yards. This is a nice route from Rome in the waning seconds of the game. Bagent is a little late getting this one out and the velocity of the pass allows the defender to recover. Rome does a nice job bringing in the football against his body, fighting through the contact, and getting out of bounds to stop the clock. We know that Bagent’s arm strength isn’t going to be able to deliver a ball at pace in this situation so he’ll need to deliver that one in the future a touch quicker. Nice play overall from Rome knowing the situation and fighting to move forward to stop the clock. A running clock there would’ve shorted the Bears multiple shots to the end zone. 2026 Explosive Play Count: D’Andre Swift 4, Kyle Monangai 4, Caleb Williams 4, Rome Odunze 2, and one each for Kalif Raymond, Luther Burden, and Cole Kmet. What was your favorite explosive play from the opener? There’s something beautiful about Kyle Monangai dragging defenders – he’s got my vote for the week.

title: Week 3 NFL game preview: Chicago Bears vs. Philadelphia Eagles
summary: The first primetime game for the 2026 Chicago Bears has lost much of its luster since the team will most likely be starting its third quarterback on Monday night. The Bears welcome the Philadelphia Eagles to Soldier Field in what should have been a great matchup of historical franchises with young quarterbacks dueling it out. […]
full_text: Nov 28, 2025; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) scrambles with the ball defended by Chicago Bears defensive end Montez Sweat (98) during the first quarter of the game at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The first primetime game for the 2026 Chicago Bears has lost much of its luster since the team will most likely be starting its third quarterback on Monday night. The Bears welcome the Philadelphia Eagles to Soldier Field in what should have been a great matchup of historical franchises with young quarterbacks dueling it out. But the NFL is a fickle thing. Bears head coach Ben Johnson has to navigate his first game without his QB1 or QB2. And the Eagles, coming in 2-0 but not looking dominant, have a lot to prove. Beyond wanting to flush the memories of Black Friday last season, when the Bears completely dominated them. The Eagles want to make a statement that they’re back to being true contenders and that their new offense is working well. Even with a third QB, it should be an interesting game. Let’s get into the opponent then. Philadelphia Eagles SB Nation site: Bleeding Green Nation Record: 2-0, first in NFC East Last week: 24-20 win over the Tennessee Titans Game day, time, TV: Monday, 7:15 p.m. CT, ESPN and ABC Spread: Eagles -3.5 Bears all-time record against: 31-17-1, including postseason Historical meetings: Week 4, 2008. The Bears hosted the Eagles on Monday Night Football. Kyle Orton gave the Bears an early lead, hitting Greg Olsen for a 19-yard touchdown on Chicago’s first offensive drive. The Eagles answered back with a 74-yard touchdown drive, capped with a Dean Jackson 22-yard touchdown from Donovan McNabb. Chicago recovered an Eagles muffed punt by Jackson on Chicago’s 40-yard line. Two plays later, Orton hit Marty Booker for a 23-yard touchdown. Once again, the Eagles answered back with Cornell Buckhalter rushing for a touchdown. Chicago scored again before halftime on an Orton-to-Devin Hester 20-yard pass. Things got sloppy in the third quarter, with McNabb and Orton throwing picks on their teams’ drives back-to-back and Philadelphia missing a field goal. But the Eagles got the ball back right away when Trent Cole forced a fumble on a sack of Orton. That led to a David Akers field goal. Another Orton fumble set up another Eagles field goal, cutting the Bears lead to 21-20. But the Bears drove the field and tacked on a 41-yard field goal. The defense stuffed Buckhalter on a fourth-and-one rush. The Bears bled almost the entire clock and held on for a 24-20 win. Last meeting: Black Friday last season in week 13. The Bears put together their best rushing game of the season, outgaining Philly 281 to 87 on the ground. Chicago racked up 425 total yards and forced Jalen Hurts into two turnovers, including a fumble on the so-called unbeatable Tush Push. Chicago won 24-15. Injury report: Since it’s a Monday Night Football game, the injury report was unavailable at press time. Offense: The Eagles offense ranks 13th in points and yards. Their passing offense ranks 12th and their rushing offense ranks 14th. Jalen Hurts (64.5 pct. cmp./467 yds./5 TD/2 INT) is playing well in his seventh different NFL offense. There have been some struggles, as the Eagles haven’t been dominating, even against a bad team like the Titans. Saquon Barkley (19 att./92 yds./0 TD) is dealing with a stinger. Tank Bigsby (14/36/1) has taken on some work for him. Hurts (12/62/0) remains effective as a rusher, too. Will Shipley (9/28/0) is also getting carries. This year, it’s the DeVonta Smith (13 rec./170 yds./1 TD) show in the passing game. Dontayvion Wicks (7/147/1) is the number two. Dallas Goedert (5/81/2) is dealing with an injury. The Eagles brought in Zach Ertz this week, who is 35 and played for the Commanders last year. Rookie receiver Makai Lemon (4/9/0) is coming on slowly. Defense: The Eagles defense ranks 12th in points allowed and 11th in yards. Their passing defense ranks fifth, and their rushing defense ranks 24th. Vic Fangio remains a great defensive coordinator. Their pass rush is led by Jihaad Campbell (19 tkl/1 sk/1 TFL/1 QB hit/1 FF) Jalen Carter (1 sk/1 TFL/1 QB hit/1 FF), and Nolan Smith (1 sk/2 TFL/1 QB hit). Moro Ojomo (7 tkls/1 TFL) and Jordan Davis (9 tkl). LBs Zack Baun (16 tkls/2 TFL/2 PD), Jalyx Hunt (8 tkl/1 TFL/1 QB hit) are also playmakers. In the secondary, Cooper DeJean (13 tkls), Quinyon Mitchell (8 tkl) and Rig Woolen (4 tkl/1 PD) will be tasked with slowing down the Bears’ receivers. The Eagles have yet to snag an interception through the first two games of the season. Key matchups: Playing with the third quarterback is a disadvantage for any team, even if the third QB is as accomplished as Case Keenum is for Chicago. Ben Johnson will have to rely on his ground game to keep the Bears in the game. Keep the Eagles on the sideline with long, sustained drives and let Case take explosive shots when possible. Vic Fangio surely remembers Black Friday and will want to get back at his former team. On defense, slowing down the Eagles’ run game is key. If Saquon can go, don’t let him run wild. And always watch out for Jalen Hurts, too. On the outside, Smith is a very good receiver, and keeping him contained will be important, too. Key stats The Eagles are fourth in third-down conversions, moving the sticks 53.1 percent of the time. They’re ninth in red zone scoring, with 71.4 percent of their drives ending in touchdowns. Philly is allowing opponents to run for 4.2 yards per carry and has allowed three touchdowns on the ground. Philly has zero defensive takeaways so far this season. The Eagles rank 25th in blitz percentage and 21st in pressure percentage. Chicago enters week 3 tied for the third-most penalized team (20), while Philadelphia is tied for the third-fewest penalties (9).

title: Under-the-radar plays and hidden yards helped the Bengals dominate the Texans
summary: For every big play in a football game, there’s usually a play that sets it up. It’s like how in baseball, setup men “set up” the closer to come in and throw gas to get the final three outs of the game. In addition, football is also a game of hidden yards. It’s those yards […]
full_text: Sep 20, 2026; Houston, Texas, USA; Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud (7) passes the ball during the game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Reliant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect For every big play in a football game, there’s usually a play that sets it up. It’s like how in baseball, setup men “set up” the closer to come in and throw gas to get the final three outs of the game. In addition, football is also a game of hidden yards. It’s those yards that may not be talked about a whole lot, but they’re so important to the outcome of the game. The Bengals’ 20-6 win over the Houston Texans in Week 2 was about big-time defensive stops and two timely offensive touchdowns. Joe Burrow’s first touchdown pass to Ja’Marr Chase on Sunday was a timely kill shot. Their second touchdown connection was a backbreaker that broke the game open. But those two touchdowns were set up by under-the-radar plays, and there were other hidden yards that kept the Bengals in control of the game for all four quarters on Sunday. From the opening kickoff, they were in control. On the opening kickoff, Dohnte Meyers ran the ball back to the Bengals’ own 41-yard line. He came close to breaking it loose for a kick-return touchdown, but he still gave the Bengals excellent field position to start the game. Although the Bengals punted on their first three drives, all of them starting at least at their own 40-yard line, they forced the Texans to start at their own 13, 8, and 8-yard line on their first three drives. That’s winning the field position battle. The Bengals won that battle early because of Meyers’ opening kick return. Let’s go to the play before Chase’s ridiculous touchdown catch in the second quarter. The Bengals faced a 3rd&4 from their own 45-yard line, and Burrow converted by finding Tee Higgins for a 23-yard gain. It’s a play that may not have made the highlight shows, but it was important to set up the play that did make the highlights. Meyers struck again early in the third quarter. After the Bengals’ defense forced the Texans to a three-and-out to start the second half, Meyers returned a punt 15 yards to the Bengals’ own 44-yard line. It was a good return to give the Bengals already good field position, and it was made better by an unnecessary roughness penalty that moved the Bengals to the Texans’ 41-yard line. Although the Bengals only moved the ball eight yards, a 5-yard reception by Erick All Jr. and a seven-yard reception by Andrei Iosivas sandwiched a four-yard tackle for loss on a Chase Brown run. The eight yards moved the Bengals to the Texans’ 33-yard line, leading to a 51-yard field goal from Evan McPherson. Bengals 10 — Texans 3. Joe Burrow and Ja’Marr Chase executed a scramble drill to perfection on the Bengals’ second touchdown of the day. On that drive, though, Joe Burrow converted a much-needed 3rd&7 despite being grabbed around the legs by a Texans defender. Burrow kept his eyes downfield and found Samaje Perine for a 16-yard gain. The play kept the drive alive, and it led to a backbreaking touchdown for the Bengals to put them up 17-3. Tee Higgins came up clutch again on the Bengals’ first drive of the fourth quarter. Facing a 3rd&5 from the Bengals’ 33-yard line, Burrow threw a masterful back-shoulder throw to Higgins for a 23-yard gain to the Texans’ 44-yard line. Chase Brown racked up five yards on the Bengals’ next two plays, both of them for runs, which led to a 57-yard banger by Evan McPherson. It’s those under-the-radar plays by Tee Higgins and those hidden yards by Dohnte Meyers in the return game that led to the big plays the Bengals made on Sunday. The under-the-radar plays and hidden yards are why this Bengals team may be different than teams in the past. When the game got clunky on Sunday, the Bengals found other ways to impact the game and control it from start to finish. Cincinnati is a team known for its big-play ability, but this Bengals team is also capable of finding other ways to dent the stat sheet and the final box score.

title: Joe Flacco responds to Giants trade rumors: Bengals QB says it’s “not true”
summary: There was a brief bit of Joe Flacco-to-New York chatter on Thursday after Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered an injury, but don’t expect the Bengals quarterback to start packing his bags for the Big Apple just yet. Flacco addressed the trade speculation in an interview with Kelsey Conway of The Cincinnati Enquirer, making it pretty […]
full_text: There was a brief bit of Joe Flacco-to-New York chatter on Thursday after Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered an injury, but don’t expect the Bengals quarterback to start packing his bags for the Big Apple just yet. Flacco addressed the trade speculation in an interview with Kelsey Conway of The Cincinnati Enquirer , making it pretty clear that he has no reason to believe Cincinnati is looking to move him. “I have no reason to believe that,” Flacco said when asked if he expects to be traded. With the #Giants recent injury to QB Jaxson Dart, social media has swirled with rumors that Joe Flacco could be someone that NYG would be interested in trading for. Here's my convo with Joe Flacco on the subject. Full story to come over at the @Enquirer pic.twitter.com/3cuinS9mqa — Kelsey Conway (@KelseyLConway) September 24, 2026 The veteran quarterback even said some of his friends had already started joking with him about a potential reunion with Giants head coach John Harbaugh, who coached Flacco in Baltimore. “It’s obviously not real and not true, but it was good enough to get people, certain friends of mine, to text me, ‘Hey I’ll see you in New York,’” Flacco said. “I was like, ‘No, guys, you won’t, that’s not true.’” Of course, Flacco also knows better than most that things can change quickly in the NFL. He didn’t exactly see his move to Cincinnati coming last season, either. The Browns traded Flacco to the Bengals after Joe Burrow’s season-ending injury, putting the veteran in position to start four games for Cincinnati. “I had no idea I was going to get traded last year, so you never know,” Flacco said. That may be the most important caveat here. Flacco is currently the Bengals’ backup to Burrow, and he’s made it clear that he remains focused on Cincinnati. But if another quarterback-needy team comes calling, the Bengals will ultimately have the decision to make. For now, though, Flacco isn’t expecting anything to happen. “I’m a Cincinnati Bengal, and I’m doing everything I can to get ready for the Pittsburgh Steelers,” he said. And given what happened to him last year, he probably won’t be taking anything for granted.

title: Ja’Marr Chase calls out NFL for celebration fines after he and Tee Higgins get fined
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals have seen plenty of excitement through their 2-0 start. They have especially seen their duo of Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins making plays. What has come along with that is a celebration that may have caught your eye. They are referring to it as “the people’s elbow.” Whether they are making a […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals have seen plenty of excitement through their 2-0 start. They have especially seen their duo of Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins making plays. What has come along with that is a celebration that may have caught your eye. They are referring to it as “the people’s elbow.” Whether they are making a reference to the move done by Dwayne ‘the Rock’ Johnson during his time as a pro wrestler or not hasn’t been explained. I think most of us can judge for ourselves if they have anything to do with each other. In any case, Chase has also said that NFL players and the NFLPA should fight these celebrations getting fined. #Bengals WR Ja'Marr Chase says the NFL fined him this week for doing the "peoples elbow" after his TD on Sunday. "This is where the superstars have to get in with NFLPA and fight for our money. I'm getting fined for an elbow. … It's a wresting move." pic.twitter.com/KWdzPFgxUq — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) September 24, 2026 I think we all understand what these two are trying to get away with, but Chase and Higgins have a point. These are the kinds of things the NFL will highlight for traction and engagement on social media. Then they will turn around and fine the player. It is also worth noting that this isn’t the first time Chase has been hit with a fine by the league. His biggest hit was a fine and suspension that cost him over $500,000 when he spit on Jalen Ramsey and then was hit with a one-game suspension. Otherwise, his five other fines have added up to under $100,000. According to Jonathan Jones, Higgins and Chase were fined a combined $89,556. Update at @TheAthletic : BOING! The NFL fined Bengals receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins a total of $89,556 for their six phallic-like celebrations https://t.co/CY1BRC4jZ0 — Jonathan Jones (@jjones9) September 24, 2026 It may sound like small potatoes at the end of the day to a guy who signed the most lucrative non-quarterback contract in NFL history (when it was signed), but that is money they are earning getting taken away regardless. It will be interesting to watch how this unfolds since the NFL has gone back on strict celebration rules before. Prior to the 2017 season, the NFL rolled back a ton of needless acts that would get called for penalties or be fined. You can combine this with Joe Burrow’s argument to just not penalize taunting anymore either, because at the end of the day, these are adult men getting paid to play a game. As long as everything is PG-13, what are we even talking about, you know?

full_text: With New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart suffering a major injury, the team will likely be in the market for another quarterback to add to their locker room. They will be looking around the league to see which teams have an extra quarterback on their roster who they could potentially trade for, and the Cleveland Browns may be one of those teams. Dillon Gabriel would make sense for the Giants to bring in as a short-term fix. Gabriel has significant college experience and also played in several regular-season games for the Browns last year. He is someone they could bring in to run their offense while relying on their defense to win games. Gabriel is currently on injured reserve. Shedeur Sanders would be a more complicated option for them to pursue through a trade. There were rumors during the 2025 draft that New York was interested in drafting Sanders. If there is still interest, Sanders could be a player they want to bring in. With Sanders comes significant off-the-field chatter and a lot of eyeballs, which may deter them from wanting to make this trade. Sanders didn’t feel like he “hit it off” with the Giants in the NFL draft process , but John Harbaugh was not the coach at that time either. ESPN’s Stephen A. title: Nick Chubb officially retires as a Cleveland Browns legend
summary: Nick Chubb’s arrival in Cleveland was a quiet one, as captured by the camera of HBO’s Hard Knocks series.  Chubb was filmed at the baggage carousel of Cleveland Hopkins Airport, waiting for his luggage when someone asked him who he was. Chubb softly mentioned he was a newly drafted member of the Cleveland Browns, which […]
full_text: (Photo by Eric Espada/Getty Images) | Getty Images Nick Chubb’s arrival in Cleveland was a quiet one, as captured by the camera of HBO’s Hard Knocks series. Chubb was filmed at the baggage carousel of Cleveland Hopkins Airport, waiting for his luggage when someone asked him who he was. Chubb softly mentioned he was a newly drafted member of the Cleveland Browns, which elicited a basic “good luck” from the other person. But once he set foot on the field, there was nothing quiet about Chubb, who signed a one-day contract on Friday to officially retire from the NFL with the Cleveland Browns. It took until Week 4 of his rookie season for Chubb to get a carry, but he took that handoff and ripped off a 63-yard touchdown run that firmly established himself as one of the best running backs in the league and a fan favorite throughout his seven years in Cleveland. During his time with the Browns, Chubb: Set the franchise record for the longest rushing touchdown with a 92-yard run against the Atlanta Falcons in 2018. Posted 30 100-yard rushing games, the second most in franchise history. Rushed for 51 touchdowns, the third most in franchise history. Rushed for 6,843 yards, the third most in franchise history. Had four consecutive 1,000-yard rushing seasons, highlighted by a career-best 1,525 rushing yards in 2022, the most by a Cleveland running back not named Jim Brown. Earned four Pro Bowl trips to go along with countless memories for Browns fans. Chubb reflected on what he called his second home in a team-issued statement on Friday : “I love Cleveland. It’s a second home to me. Ever since I stepped foot into the city, I’ve felt nothing but love and positivity. The decision to retire a Brown was an easy one. To be able to officially retire as a Brown means a lot to my family and me. The Browns have the best fans in football. There were some memorable experiences with the Dawg Pound that I’ll never forget. “Jimmy and Dee Haslam, Whitney and JW Johnson, and Andrew Berry have done nothing but welcome me with open arms, and I’m appreciative of them as I make this life-changing decision. Cleveland has meant a lot to me over the past eight years, and I’m proud that I can always call it another home.” General manager Andrew Berry issued a statement highlighting Chubb’s legacy as one of the game’s best running backs : “For seven years, Nick Chubb was the gold standard for performance, professionalism and leadership within the Browns organization. Although he came in as a quiet, second-round pick, it didn’t take long for him to make an impact. While our fans mostly began to notice him after his 105 rushing yards on 3 (!!) carries and two touchdowns in an overtime game during his rookie year in Oakland, Nick had been garnering respect across the organization behind the scenes with his work ethic and team orientation. A perfect example of this is during that very same game in Oakland, Nick played 15 special teams snaps and recorded four tackles for us. He has always been about helping the team. “Although Nick ran his way into our fans’ hearts as the best RB in football during his prime, his story of perseverance resonates just as deeply,” Berry continued. “To welcome him back to the field at home against Cincinnati during the 2024 season is a memory that will be permanently etched in all of our minds. While we all feel that Nick’s career ended sooner than it should for factors beyond his control, we cherish all the special moments he brought to this franchise and how well he represented us. We are so excited for him to retire a Cleveland Brown because he embodies everything we value.” Chubb was never the same after suffering a devastating knee injury in Week 2 of the 2023 season, but he worked his way back to play eight games for the Browns in 2024, then 15 games with the Houston Texans in 2025. Chubb retires with 7,349 rushing yards, 54 rushing touchdowns, and an average of 5 yards per carry in his 100 games. The Browns will honor Chubb during Sunday’s home opener against the Carolina Panthers, and he will speak with the media later today. Stay tuned to Dawgs By Nature for full coverage. title: Browns Week 3: Scouting the Panthers, best team in the NFC South?
summary: As the Cleveland Browns prepare for their home opener after upsetting the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 2, the team will look to build some form of a winning streak as the team will host the Carolina Panthers. The Panthers, who were a playoff team last season, earned their first victory of the year after […]
full_text: As the Cleveland Browns prepare for their home opener after upsetting the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 2 , the team will look to build some form of a winning streak as the team will host the Carolina Panthers . The Panthers, who were a playoff team last season, earned their first victory of the year after thrashing the Atlanta Falcons last Sunday. On paper, the Panthers seemed to have marginally improved but are not a team that is primed to make a jump to contender status. How good are the Panthers? It’s hard to gauge how good Carolina is as a team. Last week, the Panthers made light work of the Atlanta Falcons, but the Falcons were starting a journeyman quarterback in Cooper Rush before benching Rush and playing undrafted rookie Jack Strand. The week prior, Carolina was in a shootout with the Chicago Bears as the defense gave up 59 points and over 500 yards of total offense. It’s hard to gauge how good this team actually is, but considering that the season just started, time will tell. If the team plays like they did last week with the offense and defense playing well, this team could win the division again. However, if they are relying on the offense to get into shootouts, it’s hard to imagine this team can win consistently like that. QB Bryce Young seems to be figuring it out When it comes to quarterbacks who have had unfortunate circumstances, quarterback Bryce Young is one of them. Whether it was a coach who originally didn’t want him or the team not putting him in the best position to succeed, it hasn’t been easy for him. However, it seems that he’s figuring it out. Bryce Young ranks this season Pass TD t-1st Pass Yards 2nd Pass Rating 5th Yards/Att 3rd ADOT t-3rd pic.twitter.com/8TrDybCRBk — PFF (@PFF) September 20, 2026 Not bad at all, right? Bryce Young this season: -6 passing touchdowns (tied for 1st) -648 passing yards (2nd) -8.9 yards per attempt (3rd) pic.twitter.com/sSLNVcbwjm — Ian Hartitz (@Ihartitz) September 21, 2026 Young has always had the talent despite the physical limitations, but the lack of a stable offensive infrastructure clearly had an impact on him. The stats say he’s improving, and the tape backs it up. Generating explosive plays, good footwork in the pocket, and you understand why Panthers fans believe that they have their franchise quarterback. Panthers LB Devin Lloyd has changed Carolina’s defense One of the biggest weaknesses that the Panthers have had defensively is a quality linebacker. Enter linebacker Devin Lloyd, who missed the first two practices so far this week . The Panthers signing Lloyd was one of the more underrated pickups of free agency. Lloyd made his presence known last week against Atlanta, and the film proves it. Devin Lloyd went OFF vs Falcons 😤 pic.twitter.com/UvBZcbtXKU — PFF (@PFF) September 20, 2026 Carolina’s defense has been a weak point for quite some time now, and the team invested their resources in making it better by signing guys like Lloyd and defensive end Jaelan Phillips. The unit looks improved on paper, but the weaknesses are still there. Consistency is the key for this Panthers defense, and it will determine the ceiling of this team.

title: Playoffs? The Browns?
summary: The Cleveland Browns entered the 2026 season with low expectations on both a local and national level. According to the script, the club would start quarterback Deshaun Watson for a handful of games, either until he played himself out of a job or was injured again. Then they would “see what they had” with Shedeur […]
full_text: (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns entered the 2026 season with low expectations on both a local and national level. According to the script, the club would start quarterback Deshaun Watson for a handful of games, either until he played himself out of a job or was injured again. Then they would “see what they had” with Shedeur Sanders, give Dillon Gabriel a couple of games, and then close out with rookie Taylen Green making the annual Week 18 meaningless start. From there, it would be on to draft season, where the Browns would make their latest attempt at solving the quarterback conundrum that has plagued the team for far too long. It is only two weeks into the season, but the Browns – especially Watson – are trying to rewrite that script. The Browns open the home portion of the season on Sunday when they host the Carolina Panthers, whom the Browns have beaten in the past two meetings, followed four days later by a visit from the Pittsburgh Steelers, who have lost four in a row and six of their last seven games against the Browns in Cleveland. Following the mini-bye after the Pittsburgh game, the Browns take on the Jets, where there are already calls for head coach Aaron Glenn’s job. Play well enough, and rather than spending time juggling through a quarterback room full of players who will not be on the roster in 2027, the Browns could be heading to Baltimore on October 18 to face the Ravens with a 4-1 record. This is putting the cart so far ahead of the horse that you can’t even see it, but that hasn’t stopped ESPN senior NFL reporter Jeremy Fowler from booking a seat on the Cleveland bandwagon. "I would say closer to a playoff spot," – @JFowlerESPN on if the Browns are closer to the playoffs or a top 5 pick. pic.twitter.com/jj94J30CAx — ESPN Cleveland (@ESPNCleveland) September 24, 2026 Fowler was on ESPN 850 radio on Thursday and provided a surprising answer when asked if the Browns are closer to a top pick in the 2027 NFL Draft or making the playoffs: “I would say closer to a playoff spot. That is kind of where I’m at. I’ve been on record that I think they are going to be better than last year but not quite a playoff team, probably somewhere in the middle. Winning is infectious; if you get a few that can carry you a little bit into winning games you have no business winning. “It can go the other way in a hurry, too; 17 games is a long way. But I do have them closer (to the playoffs) right now.” It is nice that anyone is using the Browns and playoffs in the same sentence, but as Fowler points out, there is still a long way to go. No matter how much they turn the roster over, this is a franchise that has consistently shown that it can’t handle even a little bit of success. Sunday against the Panthers is the first opportunity for this year’s squad to show that things are going to be different. Take care of business against the Panthers and Steelers next week, and Fowler won’t be the only one high on the Browns. Bring the Dawg Pound with you on the SB Nation app! This season, they have the same record as the Browns at 1-1. Although the consensus seems to still be leaning Carolina, the Browns have garnered some respect. Here is what the national media is saying about the Week 3 game between the Browns and Panthers: NFL.com (Various) Why Bobby picked the Panthers: Cleveland’s upset victory over the Buccaneers felt more like Tampa Bay continuing to be the team that fell on its face throughout the end of last season than a sign the Browns will stick it to another NFC South opponent. Lest that be misconstrued as a “Browns is the Browns” take, Cleveland played well and fought hard for its win. Deshaun Watson was as precise as he’s been in years, rookie Denzel Boston looks like a stud and the Browns defense was the far more composed side during the game’s final two minutes in the aftermath of a 132-minute weather delay. The Panthers just happen to be playing better ball than both the Bucs and the Browns. Bryce Young is off to the best start of his career, buoyed by the budding wide receiver duo of Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker. He’s averaged 324 passing yards through two games with three touchdown passes in each contest. It’s not out of the question he keeps it going against a Cleveland defense still navigating the early days of the post-Myles Garrett era. The wild card remains the Panthers’ defensive Jekyll and Hyde act to start the season. Are they the closer to the group that gave up 59 points to an explosive Bears team in the opener or the unit that dominated a woeful Falcons squad while allowing only 3 points? Even if it’s more the former, Dave Canales’ offense should be able to do enough for a victory. Deshaun Watson sparked the Browns to victory at Tampa but returning for the home opener can actually more hostile. title: 3 Browns who have disappointed so far and need to step up in Week 3
summary: The Cleveland Browns welcome the Carolina Panthers to town for their home opener in Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season. A victory heading into Week 4’s “Rock & Roll” showdown with the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football would be huge for the Browns. Wednesday’s injury report presented a lot of concerns for the […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns welcome the Carolina Panthers to town for their home opener in Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season. A victory heading into Week 4’s “Rock & Roll” showdown with the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football would be huge for the Browns. Wednesday’s injury report presented a lot of concerns for the Panthers defense, a potential positive for QB Deshaun Watson , while Carolina also lost RB Jonathan Brooks to injured reserve . For Cleveland to get a win on Sunday, the run game led by Quinshon Judkins will need to get rolling . Judkins needs help from his offensive line, which has not been great in run blocking so far . Judkins is among three Browns players who have been mostly disappointing so far this season and need to step up this week: Quinshon Judkins lacks production 54 yards rushing in two games. Just 24 carries, while playing 72 snaps (66% of the offense’s). A paltry 2.3 yards per attempt. Is it Judkins’ struggles to return from injury? The offensive line? Too much time in shotgun? All of the above? Hard to tell overall, but the Browns offense cannot sustain success without improvement from Judkins Tytus Howard has shown why the Texans traded him away When you combine these things: There are not a lot of good offensive linemen in the NFL, and the Houston Texans traded Howard away for a fifth-round pick; alarms should have been ringing about why. Through the first two games with Cleveland, Howard has shown why he was available for such a cheap trade price. Week 2 was especially bad : Howard was a liability for much of this game. The only thing the Browns have been able to count on him for through two weeks is jumping offsides in critical situations. He had a false start on third down for the second time in two games. Howard gave up another sack when he gave up a soft edge to David Walker. It’s becoming more apparent why the Texans played him at guard. The Browns need more from Howard than just a pretty good pregame speech: gonna want that volume up for this one 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LcwBWoDXzF — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) September 22, 2026 Jared Verse needs to dominate, show versatility Five tackles, two tackles for loss, one QB hit in two games. Playing 79 snaps (65% of the defense’s), Verse has not been able to make an impact after being the key piece of the Myles Garrett trade. Cleveland’s defense started to get pressure in Week 2, but Verse was rarely a part of that. A power player, mostly, Verse hasn’t learned to set up his moves and countermoves, something that is just necessary at the NFL level. As LeCharles Bentley noted : My concern is not that Verse failed to beat one of the best tackles of this generation. My concern is that I am not seeing him string his rushes together yet. Verse is a power player. He plays hard, attacks with force and can collapse space. But power cannot live in isolation. It must set up the next rush. As Bentley said, facing Tristan Wifs is rarely going to lead to impact stats, but failing to have a pass rush plan won’t work against even good tackles, much less elite ones: Good pass rushers have moves. Elite pass rushers tell a story throughout the game. One rush in the first quarter creates the conditions for the next one they’re planning in the fourth quarter. The Browns need more from Verse in Week 3 and beyond, or the defense will struggle to impact the game. Are these 3 the players that need to step up the most for Cleveland?
