full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer takes his team to Rio de Janeiro in his second season with a 1-1 record through two games. How can the Cowboys get an early statement win to string together two in a row after beating the Commanders, against a Ravens team coming off a home loss to the Saints? What is the biggest challenge the Ravens present to the Cowboys to right their ship under first-year HC Jesse Minter? Let’s take a closer look. The Dallas Cowboys will beat the Baltimore Ravens if… they win on early downs on both sides of the ball. So much of the buildup for this matchup between a Cowboys team that was second in the NFL in points scored in week two, and a Ravens team that was second in week one (behind only the Bears’ scoreboard-breaking 59 points) has been about the skill players and big-play potential from both quarterbacks. No matter how good these groups are, games are still won and lost at the line of scrimmage, and this is where the Cowboys will need to put together their most complete game of the season. Starting with the Dallas defense against the Baltimore offense, the Cowboys will be facing a mobile quarterback for the second week in a row in Lamar Jackson. They’ll also be depleted in the secondary without Cobie Durant and P.J. Locke against Rashod Bateman, Devontez Walker, Chris Moore, and Mark Andrews. This is a game where the Cowboys defensive front needs to make their money, particularly the interior tackles that have yet to make as big of a splash as expected through two games. The Ravens offensive line has graded out well in run blocking, but the matchups will be there for Kenny Clark, Quinnen Williams, and Otito Ogbonnia to win at the point of attack and try to limit Derrick Henry – especially on early downs. Doing so will be the key to earning pass rush opportunities in longer down and distances to allow Donovan Ezeiruaku, Rashan Gary, Malachi Lawrence, and even Von Miller, to assert themselves into this game. Both starting guards and the Ravens starting center are new to their lineup. Rookie first-round draft pick Vega Ioane will be making his third start at right guard. Jovaughn Gwyn has been in the league since 2023, but played his very first snaps on offense as a starter in week one for this year’s Ravens. John Simpson is a veteran left guard, but one the Cowboys saw last year when he was with the Jets, and won that matchup handily. In fact, Simpson was the Jets’ lowest PFF graded player for the whole offense in that game. It’s still no easy task, but if the Cowboys defensive front can have their best game of the season, Christian Parker’s scheme can commit enough bodies to the coverage umbrella to limit downfield shots, keep eyes on Jackson when scrambling, and keep the Cowboys own offense within striking distance of winning this game. Those strikes will have to be delivered by Prescott through the air for the most part, as confidence in Dallas running the ball well consistently right now is low. A hallmark of a Jesse Minter defense is not being moved off the ball at the point of attack easily, but the Cowboys will need to force themselves to try and find some balance in their approach offensively. Early down runs that actually keep the offense on schedule and don’t feel like wasted plays would help Dallas control this game with their best players on the field, the defense resting on the sideline, and the Ravens most dynamic players also on the sideline without the ball in their hands. The Dallas Cowboys will lose to the Baltimore Ravens if… they can’t contain Derrick Henry outside the tackles. Through two games, the ageless Derrick Henry is second in the NFL in rushing yards and tied for first in touchdowns. His best runs have come outside the tackles, as we see on these two charts via Next Gen Stats: While it’s true that the Cowboys defense saw some encouraging things from rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham at the MIKE position and Dee Winters against the Commanders, this Ravens game could easily be a fall back to reality for a group that’s still unproven. Barham is still a rookie starter at a somewhat new position, wearing the green dot and trying to get a lot of new players lined up properly. There will be even more new players in the Cowboys defensive lineup against the Ravens as they deal with injuries, and the tackling from this group against such a big, physical back like Henry is a major concern. Rookie Caleb Downs has performed well in this area, but Dallas is using him close to the line of scrimmage in a lot of assignments. When Henry is able to break contain and get on the edge, the Cowboys will need an answer for who can get the angle on him, and more importantly bring him to the ground. Henry has also caught all four of the passing attempts thrown his way this season, proving he’s still a one-man gameplan wrecker on any given Sunday. Turning and handing the ball off could also prove to be the safest plan for both teams on offense, as the footing and condition of the field surface has been a concern all week leading up to kickoff. The Ravens come into this matchup with a huge advantage on paper when it comes to Henry’s production compared to Javonte Williams as the lead back for the Cowboys.
author: Sean Martin

title: Cowboys roundtable discussion: BrandonAubrey, Jaishawn Barham, and Brazil
summary: Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jorge Guajardo, Dyllan Rivers, Tom Ryle and Sean Martin.  Do you have better faith in Brandon Aubrey after punching all seven kicks for points against the Commanders, which included a […]
full_text: Photo by Mauro PIMENTEL / AFP via Getty Images Every week, we gather to discuss the latest news about the Dallas Cowboys and seek our writer’s perspective on each headline. Welcome back to the roundtable. This week we have Jorge Guajardo , Dyllan Rivers , Tom Ryle and Sean Martin . Do you have better faith in Brandon Aubrey after punching all seven kicks for points against the Commanders, which included a 60-yard field goal? Mike – Honestly, the faith in Brandon Aubrey was already high, but games like that only make it stronger. Going perfect on all seven scoring kicks, including a 60-yarder, is not normal, that’s a weapon. Aubrey gives Dallas something most teams do not have, the ability to turn stalled drives near midfield into points and change how the coaching staff thinks about field position. The bigger issue is not whether Cowboys fans should trust Aubrey, it is whether the offense becomes too comfortable settling for him. Jorge – I think he calmed some of the nerves, for sure. He needed, and the fans needed, to see that 60-yarder go through, and he nailed it. As long as he doesn’t have a Brett Maher-like meltdown, he should still be considered among the best kickers in the NFL and a huge asset for this team. Tom – All he can do to calm our doubts is to nail his kicks, and he did. I feel pretty good about him going forward. Sean – He’s butter. What else is there to say? The kicks sure looked good to me. Dyllan – I was only about 3.6% worried after last week. Now I’m back to a solid 0.0% in the worried about Aubrey department. Butter is simply the best there is. What grade do you give Jaishawn Barham for his first game wearing the green-dot, and where does he need improvement? Mike – I’d give Barham a B+ for his first game wearing the green dot. For a young linebacker taking on that much responsibility, he looked ready for the moment. The forced fumble was the headline, but the bigger takeaway was that the defense did not look utterly overwhelmed with him communicating calls and helping get players aligned. The improvement still needs to come but it was a quality start. Jorge – If we’re going with a letter grade, I’d have to say he was a B. Some of the communication issues were cleaned up, but the defense still had issues and gave up some plays, particularly in containment of Jayden Daniels, who ran wild at times. Still, Dallas is asking a ton out of the rookie, and the defense’s slight improvement is a good sign. Barham was a big part of that improvement, and one would think he’s only going to get better. Tom – B sounds about right. That was a huge load to put on the rookie’s shoulders, and he bore it well. And he caused one of the biggest plays of the game, and the best highlight for the defense so far this year. Sean – I’ll go with a B as well. We want to have higher expectations for this defense, and then they go and start an unproven rookie day two pick smack dab in the middle of the defense, and it makes those expectations difficult. Like Jorge said it wasn’t perfect, but the Dallas defense put tangible things to build off on on tape with some of their alignments, coverages, hustle to the ball, and of course a takeaway which was caused directly by Barham lowering the “Bar-hammer”. Dyllan – I’ll give Barhammer a B+ this week. The defense looked much tighter in communication with the rookie LB wearing the green dot. He also made some great plays throughout, including the forced fumble to put the offense in great field position. He somehow morphs through blocks and is always around the ball. This kid is going to be special. This week sees the Cowboys travelling to Brazil to face the Baltimore Ravens. Their last international game was in London back in 2014 with a 31-14 victory, but how confident are you feeling for this international clash? Mike – Cautiously confident is how I put it, and I’ve seen first hand how the Cowboys handle international pressure watching them in London way back when. The Cowboys have momentum after the Washington win, and an international stage should not scare a franchise that has handled this kind of spotlight before. The concern is the opponent. Baltimore brings the type of physical, awkward matchup that can expose any lack of discipline, especially with the travel, different routine, and field-condition questions in Brazil. Jorge – I am worried. It’s a 10-plus-hour flight, over 4,000 miles across three time zones, to a country in spring while we’re in fall, which could affect the natural circadian rhythm, and that’s a big deal. As someone who has traveled from Japan to the U.S. several times, that is not a trip to take lightly. On top of that, the Ravens are coming off a tough loss against the Saints and are going to be locked in for the bounce-back win, and oh, by the way, they own us historically in the head-to-head matchup six wins to one. My worry scale would be at a 9 out of 10 in this case. Tom – I’m not too worried about that rhythm, because the day will be almost exactly the same length. What does worry me is that Dallas has been so vulnerable to running quarterbacks. Now here comes Lamar Jackson. If they can’t find a way to slow him down on the ground, this one will be rough. Oh, and the pass defense hasn’t exactly sparkled so far. The early spread had the Cowboys as a three point underdog, and I think that is a bit kind to them. I have some hope if the offense can continue to ball out, but that may be a tall order against Baltimore. Sean – The pregame thoughts on this game feel too chalk, as if something completely unexpected is going to happen. The Ravens seem to have this type of early season head-scratching loss where they implode every single year, and the Cowboys have a win that still leaves an uneasy feeling. Logic would say keep going down the chalk line and the Ravens own the Cowboys yet again. My worry about that being a possibility in Brazil is still at a firm 7/10, but things are rarely, rarely this easy to predict in pro football, so let’s just see what Rio de Janeiro has in store. Dyllan – I’m extremely worried. Dallas has struggled against two mobile QBs through the first two weeks. Now they have the opportunity to face the best mobile quarterback in the NFL. On top of that, the ageless wonder Derrick Henry adds an intensity that not many other backs possess. Mix in the traveling and the beat up field; this is going to be a sloppy, brutal game for both sides. RAPID FIRE Who scores first for Dallas? Jorge – CeeDee Lamb stays hot. Tom – I’m going to stick with Javonte Williams. Sean – Hunter Luepke. You gotta get weird for an international game. Dyllan – George Pickens gets the first TD of the game and his first TD of the season. Jake Ferguson receptions- 4.5, over or under? Jorge – Under; Ferg is still too erratic for me to buy consecutive weeks of big impact like 5 receptions. Tom – Under. I’d guess George Pickens is going to get a lot of balls. Sean – I’ll go over. Dyllan – Under. Dallas just has so many weapons. Javonte Williams rushing yards- 59.5, over or under? Jorge – Under; Ravens currently own the 6th-best run defense in the NFL, and the Cowboys are struggling to get the ground game going. Tom – Under. Same reasons. Sean – Under this time. Dyllan – Under. Dallas has struggled to run the ball. I don’t see that changing now. Lamar Jackson rushing yards- 59.5, over or under? Jorge – Over; Jayden Daniels just ran for 69 yards in one half. Lamar is going to feast. Tom – Unfortunately, over. The defense is helpless against running QBs. Sean – Under because he still wants to throw the ball first. Dyllan – Over. Dallas has struggled vs mobile QBs and now they face the king of mobile QBs. Sacks recorded by Dallas- 1.5, over or under? Jorge – Under; Although the Cowboys’ pressure looked good at times, they didn’t register a single sack against Daniels or Mariota, and they have been poor tacklers in the first two games. Tom – Under, sadly. Sean – Yeah, under. Dyllan – Under. Although I…

summary: After a much needed bounce back win in week two, the Dallas Cowboys are set to take on the Baltimore Ravens in Rio for their week three matchup against the 1-1 Ravens. Both teams are heading into Rio a bit banged up, with some questionable field conditions on the horizon. While the Cowboys await to […]
full_text: Photo by Mauro PIMENTEL / AFP via Getty Images After a much needed bounce back win in week two, the Dallas Cowboys are set to take on the Baltimore Ravens in Rio for their week three matchup against the 1-1 Ravens. Both teams are heading into Rio a bit banged up, with some questionable field conditions on the horizon. While the Cowboys await to see if Ravens star WR Zay Flowers will play in this matchup, the Cowboys have already ruled out four players on the defensive side, who are all expected to play a big role for the Cowboys defense in 2026. Updates: Cowboys rule out four players for Brazil – DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys secondary has been under to microscope so far this season, but through two weeks that have played relatively well. Unfortunately they are heading into Rio a bit banged up at both safety and cornerback. Second-year cornerback Shavon Revel is expected to get the start at cornerback. DeMarvion Overshown headlines a list of four players that will not make the trip with the Cowboys to Brazil to take on the Baltimore Ravens. Overshown continues to rehab his injured hamstring and has been officially ruled out, as is Cobie Durant with an injured hamstring. Like Durant, PJ Locke suffered injury against the Washington Commanders, though to his foot, and will not make the trip to Rio. Malik Hooker is still recovering from a fractured forearm that will hold him out as well until, at minimum, Week 4 against the Houston Texans, though that remains to-be-determined. It isn’t cliché when Cowboys players say they’re treating this weekend’s 10-hour trip to Brazil as a business trip. The Cowboys will land in Rio de Janeiro on Friday morning. They’ll have a walkthrough practice later that day at the practice facility for Flamengo, a professional soccer team in town. The next day, they’ll do a literal walkthrough at Maracanã Stadium , which carries an added importance after concerns arose from one Flamengo player about the field’s conditions . Shortly after Sunday’s game ends the Cowboys will be on their charter back to Texas. title: 2026 Week 3 rooting guide for Cowboys fans
summary: There was a fair bit of balancing in the NFC in Week 2, leaving the conference with nine 1-1 teams. One of them, thankfully, is your Dallas Cowboys. As America’s Team tries to get its second win this Sunday in Brazil, what else should Cowboys fans be rooting for from the Week 3 schedule? NFC […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images There was a fair bit of balancing in the NFC in Week 2, leaving the conference with nine 1-1 teams. One of them, thankfully, is your Dallas Cowboys. As America’s Team tries to get its second win this Sunday in Brazil, what else should Cowboys fans be rooting for from the Week 3 schedule? NFC East teams Bears d. Eagles Commanders d. Seahawks Titans d. Giants Two obvious picks here, wanting to see the Philly and New York go down. Unfortunately, the Bears are down to a fan in a Jim McMahon jersey at quarterback, so that may be asking too much. And while the Giants may no longer be a division threat without Jaxson Dart, we don’t need them restoring confidence with a win, even if it’s against the Titans. Why would we root for Washington this Sunday? They were potentially starting 0-2 even with Jayden Daniels, so his absence likely takes them out of any contention. Meanwhile, Seattle is 2-0 and much more likely to cause problems for the Cowboys in January. The Commanders are the lesser of evils this week. NFC vs. NFC Falcons d. Packers Cardinals d. 49ers Buccaneers d. Vikings A second-straight loss for Green Bay, and against the winless Falcons, would send the Cheeseheads into a spiral and put the Packers in a tough early-season hole. The 49ers and Vikings are both 2-0, so it’d be good to see them take losses. Neither the Cardinals nor the Bucs feel like down-the-road threats, so it’s a good week to keep possible NFC contenders within Dallas’ range. NFC vs. AFC Browns d. Panthers Jets d. Lions Raiders d. Saints Broncos d. Rams More easy picks in these inter-conference games. Outside of the Steelers and Texans, who we’ll get to next, Dallas has no vested interest in other AFC teams. So we’re happy to see them hang losses on our NFC rivals. The Lions, Panthers, Rams, and Saints are all 1-1 going into Week 3, so it’d be nice to have as many of them below .500 as possible. AFC vs. AFC Bengals d. Steelers Colts d. Texans As we’ve discussed before, Dallas owns the Steelers’ fourth-round pick and the Texans’ seventh-round pick in next year’s draft. So unless one of them is facing an NFC team whose record is more important to us than draft value, we’ll be rooting against them weekly.

For the Cowboys defense, it’ll be essential that they are able to limit […]
full_text: Photo by Elsa/Getty Images | Getty Images After only two weeks into the season, the NFL has seen many teams ravaged by key player injuries. For the Cowboys, who need to stack wins in short order, the next opportunity comes against a team who historically has had their number. For the Cowboys defense, it’ll be essential that they are able to limit explosive plays from a depleted Ravens team and keep their offense firing. Here’s the latest we know about the injuries ahead of the game. Cowboys-Ravens Thursday practice report: Cowboys CB Cobie Durant, S Malik Hooker, S P.J. Locke and LB DeMarvion Overshown are all ruled out and will not travel to Rio de Janeiro. Another day of DNP for Ravens WR Zay Flowers and OT Ronnie Stanley. pic.twitter.com/tjhzWsbdON — Tommy Yarrish (@tommy_yarrish) September 24, 2026 For the Cowboys, Cobie Durant (hamstring) did not practice. Also not practicing with the team were P.J. Locke (foot), DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring), and Malik Hooker (forearm). All seem unlikely to play with two DNPs to open the week. On Thursday, the Ravens were still without receiver Zay Flowers (hamstring) and offensive lineman Ronnie Stanley (toe). Flowers is a big part of the Baltimore offense and is a dynamic weapon the team relies upon at multiple levels in the field in a variety of offensive looks. Without him and Stanley, thats good news for a Dallas secondary who are also working through a spell of injuries. Defensively, Teddye Buchanan (knee) and Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) were full participants. Madubuike hasn’t played since last year, and despite practicing fully the last two days has been non-committal about whether he will make his season debut Sunday.

title: Digging into the numbers to predict Cowboys vs Ravens
summary: Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. We’ll look at historical data points as well as more recent numbers. At the end, we’ll add it all up to see what Dallas needs to do to secure a win and which team may have the edge. The history The Cowboys […]
full_text: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images | Getty Images Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. We’ll look at historical data points as well as more recent numbers. At the end, we’ll add it all up to see what Dallas needs to do to secure a win and which team may have the edge. The history The Cowboys and Ravens have met just seven times. The Ravens lead the series 6-1 . The Cowboys’ lone win came during Dak Prescott and Ezekiel Elliott’s rookie season, finishing the game 27-17 . The last time the two teams met was September 22, 2024. The Ravens fended off a late Cowboys rally in the fourth quarter, winning 28-25 . Arrow pointing up on defense? The Cowboys defense improved last week against the Commanders. They still weren’t good. Pressures increased between week one and week two. Dallas had just two pressures when rushing four against the Giants and nine when rushing four versus the Commanders. They couldn’t seal the deal and wound up as just one of four teams to not record a sack last week. But the fact that they are able to generate pressure without blitzing is a promising step in the right direction. Against the Commanders, the Cowboys jumped from 32nd in EPA/play to 17th . Surely Jayden Daniels being forced out with injury has something to do with that jump, but the team can only play whoever is placed in front of them. And with Marcus Mariota in, the defense stood firm – even if a bit lucky at times . Dallas also took advantage of turnovers when they presented themselves. Both rookies Jaishawn Barham and Caleb Downs popped the ball out, with one of the two fumbled being recovered. Dallas will need to continue to cash in on turnovers when possible. Cowboys key stats from last week Dak Prescott threw for 279 yards, four touchdowns and zero interceptions against the Commanders. CeeDee Lamb exploded with eight catches on nine targets for 153 yards and two touchdowns. Jake Ferguson was the other key receiving option for Dallas last week, going for 43 yards and two touchdowns. Defensively, Dallas is still a work in progress. They allowed 389 total yards, including 182 on the ground. Mobile quarterbacks have not been kind to this defense through the first two weeks, utilizing their legs to pick up huge chunks of yardage at a time. Ravens key stats from last week The Ravens were shocked at home by the Saints last week, losing 24-17 . Derrick Henry’s longest run went for just eight yards against that Saints defense. He rushed for 68 yards on 16 rushing attempts. Lamar Jackson was also bottled up on the day, rushing just four times for 34 yards, with a long of 13 yards. Saints quarterback Tyler Shough had a 79.4 completion percentage against the Ravens defense. He finished with a quarterback rating of 107.4 . Most of the Saint’s offensive damage came through the air, as they only rushed for 2.4 yards per carry on 27 attempts on the day. What do the numbers mean? Offensively, Dallas should look to a similar gameplan as last week when they take on the Ravens. If that defense can make Tyler Shough look like an NFL All-Pro, imagine what that could mean for Dak Prescott. Dallas should focus on lining up in 11 personnel as often as possible to take advantage of the matchup between the Cowboys receivers and Ravens defensive backs. It’s not that the Ravens secondary is bad; they are just extremely willing to give up underneath routes to prevent the explosive plays. Dallas must use that to their advantage as an extension of their running game instead of banging their head against a wall trying to establish Javonte Williams on the ground. On defense, Dallas must do everything in their power to avoid third-and-short situations. Last week, the Commanders converted 83% of their third-down attempts when they needed less than four yards. However, their conversion rate dipped to 37.5% when they needed four yards or more. That means winning on first and second down. That would require the defense to reign in that brutal Baltimore rushing attack. Containing Lamar Jackson and hitting Derrick Henry in the backfield before he gets a full head of steam are paramount. This week comes down to a pair of strength versus weakness matchups. Can the Cowboys high-powered passing game light up the Ravens secondary? Will Derrick Henry and Lamar Jackson run wild against a defense that’s struggled twice in two weeks when facing mobile quarterbacks? Both teams are looking to avoid 1-2 in Rio. Both teams have plenty of reasons to believe they could come out on top. Given their ability on the ground and the corresponding weakness of the Dallas defense, the numbers suggest the Ravens will likely be the team to enjoy their long victory flight home.

title: Dallas Cowboys offensive line matchup vs. Baltimore Ravens
summary: Every week, we’re digging into the trenches, because that’s where the real action happens. We shine the spotlight on the Dallas Cowboys offensive line, who’s holding it down, who’s opening holes for the running backs, and who’s keeping Dak Prescott clean. Let’s get to it. Trench Dashboard Here are the Cowboys offensive line metrics for […]
full_text: Photo by Matthew Pearce/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Every week, we’re digging into the trenches, because that’s where the real action happens. We shine the spotlight on the Dallas Cowboys offensive line, who’s holding it down, who’s opening holes for the running backs, and who’s keeping Dak Prescott clean. Let’s get to it. Trench Dashboard Here are the Cowboys offensive line metrics for the 2026 season so far. Pass Block Win Rate – 54% 10th Run Block Win Rate – 66% 32nd Pressure rate allowed – 25% 7th Sacks allowed – 2 (3rd) Last three-week trend: N/A The Pressure Point Every opponent will look at the Cowboys offensive line and ask, where can we break it? Here’s what to watch for. PRESSURE POINT: Baltimore can create pressure without dominating every individual matchup This is the biggest problem Dallas has to solve in Brazil. The Ravens have generated pressure on 43.8% of opposing quarterback dropbacks, fifth-highest in the NFL. They have five sacks through two games, tied for 11th in the league. Baltimore has players capable of beating blocks and Trey Hendrickson is the obvious name to watch. His 26% Pass Rush Win Rate ranks 12th among qualifying edge defenders, and PFF has already credited him with 10 pressures, sixth-most among edge defenders, despite playing only two games. He added his first sack as a Raven against New Orleans. But Hendrickson is not alone. Tavius Robinson already has seven pressures and two sacks, while Mike Green also registered a sack against New Orleans. That means Dallas cannot simply double-team Hendrickson on every passing play and assume the problem is solved. PRESSURE POINT: Terence Steele remains the obvious place to test Tyler Guyton’s start to the year has been extremely encouraging and the left tackle question looks close the being answered. The same cannot yet be said about the other tackle spot. Through two games, PFF has given Terence Steele a 54.2 pass-blocking grade and 46.6 run-blocking grade, ranking him 56th and 62nd respectively among 66 qualifying tackles. He has surrendered three pressures and Dallas’ only sack charged to an offensive tackle. Baltimore will see that on film. Whether it is Hendrickson moving across the formation or another Ravens edge defender attacking that side, Steele should expect attention. The danger does not always show up as a sack. If Steele loses quickly, Prescott may have to move before a route has developed and throw the ball away or check it down. A pass rusher can ruin a play without ever touching the quarterback. Where to Attack Every defensive line has a weakness, here are the Ravens’ soft spots and where the Cowboys offensive line should attack. GREEN LIGHT: Make Baltimore defend the run This might be the most important statistic in the entire matchup. Baltimore ranks 27th in Run Stop Win Rate at only 26%. Dallas ranks 32nd in Run Block Win Rate at 66%. So this is weakness against weakness. Baltimore’s traditional rushing numbers actually look much better. Opponents have rushed for only 167 yards at 3.6 yards per carry through two games. That is why the ESPN number is interesting. Baltimore has prevented huge rushing totals, but its defensive front is not consistently defeating its blocks according to the tracking data. Dallas has to test whether that weakness is real. Tyler Booker gives them a good place to start. PFF currently grades Booker at 81.7 as a run blocker, seventh among guards. T.J. Bass has also settled into Tyler Smith’s position much better than expected, earning a place on PFF’s Week 2 Team of the Week. Rather than putting everything on Prescott again, Dallas should make Booker, Bass and Cooper Beebe move Baltimore’s defensive front. GREEN LIGHT: Use quick passes to take the teeth out of the rush New Orleans provided Dallas with another blueprint. Baltimore sacked Tyler Shough three times against the Saints, but the pressure largely disappeared during New Orleans’ fourth-quarter comeback when Shough began getting the football out quickly. The Saints scored 15 unanswered fourth-quarter points, and Baltimore did not record a sack in the final period. Dallas has the personnel to copy that idea. CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Jake Ferguson can all give Prescott quick answers. Screens can also punish defenders who are racing toward the quarterback. The idea is simple. If Hendrickson is expecting three to four seconds to eventually reach Prescott, make sure the football is already gone after two. That can also help Steele. Dallas does not have to leave its right tackle in difficult pass sets repeatedly if the offense forces Baltimore to worry about quick throws, screens and the running game. The Chaos Report Here are the Baltimore Ravens’ defensive trends for this season at the defensive line. Sack Total – 5 (11th) Pass Rush Win Rate – 55% 10th Run Stop Win Rate – 26th% 27th QB Pressure Rate – 43% (5th) Last three week trend: N/A Matchup of the week Tyler Guyton vs. Trey Hendrickson This is Guyton’s biggest examination of the young season. The Cowboys left tackle has allowed four pressures and no sacks through 78 pass-blocking snaps, while his 81.8 PFF run-blocking grade ranks fourth among qualifying tackles. He has taken a significant step forward after all the questions surrounding him during the offseason. Now comes Hendrickson. The Ravens’ new edge rusher has already produced 10 pressures. His current 26% Pass Rush Win Rate means he is defeating roughly one out of every four qualifying pass-rush blocks within 2.5 seconds. Hendrickson is dangerous because he does not give an offensive tackle only one problem to solve. If Guyton worries too much about Hendrickson racing around the outside, he can leave space inside. If he sits too heavily inside, Hendrickson has enough speed to attack the edge. That is what makes this individual battle bigger than two players. Guyton winning by himself allows the entire Dallas offense to remain open. Best route to success: Run the football before Baltimore’s pass rush gets the chance to take over. Dallas cannot enter this game with the league’s worst Run Block Win Rate and simply expect Prescott to throw it 40 times against a defense producing pressure at a good rate. Test Baltimore’s 27th-ranked Run Stop Win Rate. Run behind Booker and the interior line. Use quick passes and screens. Stay ahead of the chains. Then, when Dallas does want to attack deeper, give Prescott situations where Baltimore still has to respect the run. Injury Updates: The coast is clear this week in terms of the Dallas offensive line, with nothing major report other than Tyler Smith still recovering. For Baltimore, Nnamdi Madubuike is the major name to monitor. The Pro Bowl defensive tackle missed the first two games with a neck injury. Baltimore deliberately kept him off injured reserve because it believed a return against Dallas in Rio or Tennessee in Week 4 was possible. Linebacker Teddye Buchanan is on a similar timetable. Both were able to practice on Wednesday.

title: Finding run game vs. Ravens would be timely for the Cowboys
summary: Lose to a division rival on the road, beat one at home, get exposed in week three. Lose to a division rival on the road, beat one at home, get exposed in week three. This is the pattern the 2026 Dallas Cowboys are looking to avoid for a second straight year, but doing so would […]
full_text: Photo by Matthew Pearce/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Lose to a division rival on the road, beat one at home, get exposed in week three. Lose to a division rival on the road, beat one at home, get exposed in week three. This is the pattern the 2026 Dallas Cowboys are looking to avoid for a second straight year, but doing so would take beating the Baltimore Ravens for the first time since 2016 and just second time in franchise history. Last year’s pattern went loss at the Eagles (also by one score), home win versus the Giants, and loss at the Chicago Bears which is really where the defense showed they’d keep this team far from a playoff spot until the end. The defense left plenty to clean up against the Washington Commanders in this year’s week two win, primarily containing a mobile quarterback when Jayden Daniels was in the game for the first half. Daniels exited down just 17-10, and in came Marcus Mariota who the Cowboys got close to but couldn’t bring to the ground. Now comes Lamar Jackson in an international game in Brazil, and it will take another step up, or likely a big ol’ leap, from Christian Parker’s defense in a hurry to slow down Jackson. Despite the location of this game being a wild card, the Ravens also come into it with a frighteningly similar pattern unfolding. The last time these teams met in 2024 was also in week three, and the Ravens were off an inexplicable home loss to the Gardner Minshew-led Raiders in week two. The Ravens took some of this frustration out on the Cowboys, racing out to a 21-3 lead that reached 28-6 in the third quarter. The Cowboys did make a rally to put a scare into the Ravens, cutting the lead to 28-25 in the final three minutes, but this is as close as they’d get to fall to 1-2. For this Sunday, the Ravens are also off a bit of a head-scratching home loss, this time to Kellen Moore and the Saints, and will go for win number three in a row against the Cowboys as a response. The Ravens are also 6-1 all time against the Cowboys. Ravens fans aren't imagining it – Since 2018, Baltimore has a top-5 defense over the whole game and the worst defense in football in the 4th quarter of a one-score game. The Ravens are in their own corner Those who thought it was Harbaugh – sorry pic.twitter.com/jYYp5BRJ6G — Stick to the Model (@StickToTheModel) September 21, 2026 Dallas has already lost to former Baltimore head coach John Harbaugh this season, and now they will match up against first-year HC Jesse Minter – still trying to find his own solution for how the Ravens have let so many close games slip away in similar fashion like they just did at home. The fans in Brazil should certainly get their money’s worth if this game remains undecided in the fourth quarter. The Cowboys seeing Dak Prescott pour on points against a NFC East team in week two was nothing new. In fact, he now has 24 touchdowns to zero interceptions in eight career home games against the Commanders, all wins. Doing so against the Ravens will be a taller task, but assuming both quarterbacks play well for their respective 1-1 teams is where breaking down the other factors of this matchup gets fun. ESPN offensive line run block win rates through Week 2: Ravens: 79% Bengals: 79% Bills: 78% Rams: 78% Vikings: 78% Broncos: 77% Chiefs: 76% Colts: 76% Buccaneers: 76% Seahawks: 76% Panthers: 75% Jets: 75% Saints: 74% Giants: 74% Chargers: 73% Jaguars: 73% Packers: 73% Dolphins:… — Ryan Paganetti (@RyanPaganetti) September 22, 2026 According to ESPN metrics, this game will feature the widest possible disparity in run blocking win rates, and that doesn’t bode well for the Cowboys. They come in, still without Tyler Smith at left guard, in last place here while the Ravens are tied with their divisional rival the Bengals for first place. The Cowboys can hope the Ravens make the same mistake they did against the Saints by forgetting about Derrick Henry on all of their crucial second half drives, but this feels unlikely for a few reasons. In the last meeting of these sides, with the Ravens also coming off a bad loss like we mentioned, they ran the ball 45 times compared to just 15 passing attempts for Jackson. The Cowboys, playing in come-from-behind mode most of the afternoon, ran it just 16 times while asking Prescott to throw 51 attempts. Rico Dowdle led the Cowboys in carries with eight for 32 yards. For this contest in Brazil, Declan Doyle is now the Ravens OC. Doyle was Ben Johnson’s OC last year, a game we also already mentioned as one where the Cowboys defense was shredded. The Cowboys do have the best third-down conversion rate in the league so far this season, but also the worst third-down defense. This game has the type of feel where one short-yardage stop, or really any third-down stop of any kind, could be massive for momentum. If the Cowboys can match some of the Ravens intent to run the ball physically by doing so themselves, it would go a long way in avoiding a third straight 1-2 start. The Saints managed to hold the ball for 5:30 more than the Ravens in last week’s game, while the Cowboys in their win actually lost time of possession by just under three minutes. If the Cowboys can combine these things and continue to make the splash plays that allow you to win while not possessing the ball as much, but also keep the Ravens offense off the field even a little bit, it would be impressive. The feeling from week one that this Cowboys team doesn’t look or feel any different from so many recent ones has not gone away even after a 17-point win in Dallas. Ravens fans are likely saying the same thing about their teams’ early season struggles, and now the two outfits go head to head in Rio de Janeiro. This is a huge spot to learn about both Jesse Minter and Brian Schottenheimer’s teams with the second month of the season approaching.
author: Sean Martin

title: Cowboys have reasons to believe they can beat Baltimore in Brazil
summary: After getting their first win of the season against the Washington Commanders, the Dallas Cowboys now head somewhere completely different. Sunday’s Week 3 game against the Baltimore Ravens will be played at the famous Maracanã Stadium in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Dallas is officially the home team, although there obviously won’t be the normal advantages […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After getting their first win of the season against the Washington Commanders, the Dallas Cowboys now head somewhere completely different. Sunday’s Week 3 game against the Baltimore Ravens will be played at the famous Maracanã Stadium in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Dallas is officially the home team, although there obviously won’t be the normal advantages that come with playing at AT&T Stadium. What the Cowboys will have instead is momentum. Dallas enters Brazil 1-1 after a convincing 37-20 victory over Washington, while Baltimore is also 1-1 after letting a second-half lead disappear in a 24-17 home loss to the New Orleans Saints. And there are plenty of reasons for Cowboys fans to believe Dallas can leave South America above .500. Let’s start with the most obvious one. Dak Prescott is coming to Brazil absolutely red hot. Prescott completed 26 of 31 passes for 279 yards and four touchdowns against Washington. He didn’t throw an interception and finished with a 143.8 passer rating. The performance also moved Prescott past Tony Romo for the most touchdown passes in Cowboys history. Prescott now has 249 career touchdown passes after one of the best games he has played in recent memory. That is exactly the sort of quarterback performance Dallas will need against Baltimore. Dak Prescott delivers a MASTERCLASS vs. Washington ⭐️ His 4-TD performance earns the Cowboys their first win of the season 🤠 pic.twitter.com/7oKOp6zGxR — Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) September 20, 2026 The good news is that the Ravens just showed that their pass defense can be attacked. Saints quarterback Tyler Shough completed 27 of 34 passes for 252 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions against Baltimore. New Orleans wasn’t relying on constant deep throws either. It consistently moved the chains with accurate passes underneath and in the middle of the field. That style suits what Dallas did extremely well against Washington. Prescott was accurate, decisive and spread the ball around. When the Commanders tried to take something away, another Cowboys weapon became available. None was more dangerous than CeeDee Lamb. Lamb caught eight passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns against Washington. It was his first 100-yard game of the season and another reminder of how difficult Dallas can be to defend when Prescott and Lamb are in rhythm. Dak Prescott to CeeDee Lamb for 6️⃣ WASvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Kk3G5Twly6 — NFL (@NFL) September 20, 2026 Baltimore has just watched another number one receiver cause problems. Chris Olave caught eight passes for 86 yards and a touchdown for New Orleans. The Saints also got 66 receiving yards from tight end Juwan Johnson and another 64 from Devaughn Vele. That should immediately catch Dallas’ attention. Because stopping Lamb isn’t the only problem Baltimore has to solve. Jake Ferguson is coming off a two-touchdown game. Ferguson caught all four passes thrown his way against Washington for 43 yards, with two of those receptions ending in touchdowns. TD No. 2 for Jake Ferguson 🤠 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/NKpsobgh9v — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) September 20, 2026 Through one afternoon, Dallas showed exactly why defending this passing game can become difficult. Lamb scored twice. Ferguson scored twice. Prescott barely put the ball in danger. If Baltimore decides it has to give Lamb extra attention, Ferguson should again find space underneath and through the middle. The Cowboys also have George Pickens available on the outside, meaning Baltimore cannot simply build its entire coverage around stopping Lamb. Baltimore’s defense struggled badly to get off the field against New Orleans. The Saints converted eight of their 15 third-down attempts and went a perfect two-for-two on fourth down. Baltimore’s pass coverage and pass rush failed to work together properly when New Orleans moved toward a quicker passing attack. That is something Schottenheimer and Prescott should be looking at closely this week. Get the ball out quickly. Make Baltimore defend the full width of the field. Let Lamb, Ferguson and Pickens create yards after the catch. And, most importantly, keep Prescott away from obvious passing situations where Baltimore’s rushers can attack. Then there is what happened to the Ravens after halftime. Baltimore led New Orleans 14-6 at the break. The Ravens then lost the second half conceding 18 and only scoring three. They were eventually shut out over the final 18 minutes and allowed New Orleans to drive for the winning touchdown late in the fourth quarter. That matters because Dallas showed the exact opposite quality last Sunday. NEW ORLEANS FONT TOMBER LES RAVENS À BALTIMORE ! @Saints #Saints pic.twitter.com/5XBTMDnAgf — NFL France (@NFLFrance) September 20, 2026 When Washington threatened to get back into the game, the Cowboys answered. Prescott kept making plays. Brandon Aubrey kept adding points. Jaishawn Barham forced an important fumble. And Dallas eventually turned a competitive divisional game into a comfortable 17-point victory. One team showed it could pull away. The other just showed it could be caught. Baltimore’s inability to finish the Saints game gives Dallas every reason to believe it can stay patient even if things don’t begin perfectly in Brazil. The Ravens are also dealing with several injuries worth monitoring. Their biggest concern is Zay Flowers. Flowers exploded for 150 receiving yards and a touchdown in Baltimore’s Week 1 win over Indianapolis but suffered a hamstring injury. He missed the Saints game completely. His status for Dallas remains something to follow throughout the week; he missed Wednesday’s practice. Baltimore is already without rookie receiver Ja’Kobi Lane, who was placed on injured reserve after undergoing wrist surgery. That means Baltimore could again enter a game without two important receivers if Flowers cannot return. Flowers’ absence clearly changed the Baltimore offense against New Orleans. The Ravens also have questions on their offensive line. Left tackle Ronnie Stanley entered Week 2 carrying a toe injury and then left the Saints game during the third quarter. He did not play in the fourth. That’s an important situation for Dallas to watch. Defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike has yet to play this season because of a neck injury, while linebacker Teddye Buchanan has also yet to make his 2026 debut. Both practiced on Wednesday. Cornerback T.J. Tampa has gone on injured reserve. Star pass rusher Trey Hendrickson is playing through a broken finger with heavy protection around his hand. Now let’s talk about the international series. This will be the first NFL regular-season game ever played in Rio de Janeiro, and Dallas is the designated home team. Talking to folks over in Brazil who cover the Cowboys, they’ve told us that the country has a massive Cowboys following and fan base, which will make this game feel like a home game away from home. And for the Cowboys, they don’t have much international regular-season history, but what they do have is perfect. Their previous regular-season game outside the United States came in London in 2014, when Dallas beat Jacksonville 31-17. So the Cowboys enter Brazil with a 1-0 record in international regular-season games. COWBOYS COUNTDOWN DAY 31 Cowboys beat the Jaguars 31-17 in 2014 at Wembley Stadium, London. The Cowboys largest win outside the United States. #DallasCowboys #Cowboys #NFL pic.twitter.com/IoCEjoCKlH — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 7, 2024
author: Mike Poland

title: Broncos vs Rams 5 questions: What does Aaron Donald’s return mean for LA?
summary: Aaron Donald is back. Unfortunately, or fortunately for the Denver Broncos, Myles Garrett is on IR. But bringing back one of the best defensive linemen in NFL history to a defense is obviously huge. That’s one of the reasons the Los Angeles Rams were heavy favorites to win the Super Bowl heading into the season […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Aaron Donald #99 of the Los Angeles Rams warms up prior to the game against the New York Giants at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images Aaron Donald is back. Unfortunately, or fortunately for the Denver Broncos, Myles Garrett is on IR. But bringing back one of the best defensive linemen in NFL history to a defense is obviously huge. That’s one of the reasons the Los Angeles Rams were heavy favorites to win the Super Bowl heading into the season and still are the favorites. Offensively, LA has the reigning MVP and an explosive offense. So what does the return of Donald mean? To get a feel for the Rams and how big it was to get their first win against the New York Giants, we go “behind enemy lines” with Evan Craig from Turf Show Times . MHR: How important was that win over the New York Giants on Monday night? What was different between the first two games Evan : The win was extremely important and exactly what the doctor ordered. Los Angeles looked all out of sorts in Week 1, and the 49ers took full advantage. New York really didn’t stand a chance, even if Jaxson Dart had never gotten injured. The Rams poured too many resources into improving this offseason, and they weren’t about to let the Giants ruin that by dropping them to 0-2. I will say, there are things to clean up, especially as LA was only up 11 at halftime. It should’ve been much worse, but back-to-back turnovers on a Matthew Stafford pick and a signature Kyren Williams fumble momentarily gave the G-Men hope. Still, it was a night-and-day difference. It helped that the Rams, as Sean McVay eloquently put it, didn’t have a “dumbass” travel plan ahead of the game. Much of their awful showing in Australia was due to the fact that they arrived a day before the game. Several new pieces needed to gel together, but it was mainly due to the travel plan MHR: What does the return of Aaron Donald mean for the Rams defense and the team? Evan : Aaron Donald’s return means a great deal to this team, and Monday night was a huge reminder of why. During the win over the Giants, AD didn’t put together much of a stat line, yet his presence was felt on every one of his 33 snaps. It was also as if he had never left, with his power and burst on full display. That was impressive to see in someone who was two years removed from the game. I guess that fitness regimen he was on during retirement certainly paid off. If he gets better as the season progresses, and it’s very likely he does, that should scare all opposing offensive coordinators. Now, imagine what will happen once Myles Garrett returns. Did anyone else get chills? At first, Donald’s return seemed like nothing more than a gimmick and an unnecessary distraction for a team aiming for another Super Bowl run. Gimmick might not be the correct word, as he seemed genuine about returning, even if a large percentage of the NFL world was doubting it. Clearly, Rams fans can see he’s committed to helping the team secure a ring. Maybe you can go home after all. MHR: How does LA get the win on Sunday night? What must the Rams do defensively and offensively? Evan : LA will get the win if they take a page out of the Chiefs’ Week 1 playbook. Kansas City rushed for 220 yards and ran the ball down the Broncos’ throats in the opener. Against the Giants, the Rams’ two-headed attack of Williams and Blake Corum combined for 164 rushing yards. They have a strong enough attack on the ground to keep Denver on its toes all game. Also, the Rams must have better pass distribution. Davante Adams and Terrance Ferguson combined for 19 targets when no other pass catcher had more than two targets. Spreading the ball out will help take the pressure off Adams, especially if Puka Nacua’s out. The Rams have a diverse array of playmakers to make this happen. Defensively, the Rams must make the Broncos one-dimensional. Denver doesn’t have the strongest running game, but if LA can take away that run game and put a ton of pressure on Bo Nix, they can secure the win. Nix is a very capable quarterback, yet assuming the Rams follow KC’s playbook, they can limit his effectiveness by taking away his new favorite target in Jaylen Waddle and security blankets Courtland Sutton and Troy Franklin. MHR: What do you make of the current spread? And what is your best bet for the game? Evan : I think 2.5 points is a fair spread, but I don’t like LA as the favorite. Denver is a really tough place to play, and the Broncos deserve more credit as a team, even if they haven’t had the smoothest start to begin the season. Yes, I believe the Rams are a better team on paper when they’re at full strength, yet they’re without Garrett and possibly Puka for this one. That, to me, feels like the sportsbooks are disrespecting Denver, at least this week, which wouldn’t be the first time for them. My best bet is Matthew Stafford under 200 passing yards. The Broncos have a far superior secondary than the Giants, meaning they won’t allow Davante Adams to run wild on them if, again, Nacua is out again this week. MHR: How does this game unfold, and what is your prediction? Evan : This is a tough game to predict, since the Rams are typically slow starters to begin the season. Last season was their best start in years, and it was only with a 3-2 record. The Broncos were in the same boat in 2025 because they began the year 1-2 before winning 13 of their next 14 games to finish the season and clinch the top seed. That said, I wouldn’t be surprised if the Rams drop this one, which would certainly spell trouble among the fan base right before they travel to Philly. I also expect this to be a low-scoring game due to the strength of both defenses. The first one to 20 should win this one, and I expect it to be Denver. Broncos 21, Rams 17
author: Ian St. Clair

title: Scouting the Enemy: Los Angeles Rams
summary: The Denver Broncos host the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday Night Football. Both teams are coming off impressive Week 2 wins after faltering in their season openers. Here is a deeper look at the Broncos’ Week 3 opponent. 2025 Los Angeles Rams Season Review The Rams finished their 2025 regular season with a 12-5 record […]
full_text: Inglewood, CA - November 02: Head coach Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams reqxcts with quarterback Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams after a touchdown against the New Orleans Saints in the first half of a NFL football game at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood on Sunday, November 2, 2025. (Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images The Denver Broncos host the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday Night Football. Both teams are coming off impressive Week 2 wins after faltering in their season openers. Here is a deeper look at the Broncos’ Week 3 opponent. 2025 Los Angeles Rams Season Review The Rams finished their 2025 regular season with a 12-5 record earning second place in the NFC West. They would go on to lose the NFC Championship game to the Seattle Seahawks 31-27. 2026 Los Angeles Rams Offseason Additions and Departures After failing to make the Super Bowl, General Manager Les Snead made a series of high-profile trades and moves this offseason. The big focus was on improving their defense. They made a gargantuan trade with the Cleveland Browns to acquire Myles Garrett. However, he suffered a knee injury in Week 1 and won’t be available for their matchup versus the Broncos on Sunday Night Football . They also made a trade with the Kansas City Chiefs for star cornerback Trent McDuffie to improve their secondary. Versatile defensive back Jaylen Watson was also added into the mix on a three-year deal. And the big surprise? Defensive lineman Aaron Donald came out of retirement to help the team’s pursuit of another Lombardi Trophy. Instead of getting a player to help them win now in the 2026 NFL Draft , the Rams picked Alabama quarterback Ty Simpson in the first round. With Matthew Stafford getting up there in age, it’s understandable, but a lot of their fan base was certainly hoping for a player that could have provided a year one impact for the team. In the second round, they took Ohio State tight end Max Klare—another curious decision since they brought back Tyler Higbee and had drafted Terrance Ferguson in the second round in the 2025 NFL Draft. Offensive X-Factor: Quarterback Matthew Stafford A handful of players could have earned this designation for the Rams. However, choosing last year’s MVP makes the most sense. That’s longtime quarterback Matthew Stafford who is in his eighteenth season in the NFL. Stafford’s productivity and longevity will certainly result in him eventually being enshrined in the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Last season, Stafford threw for 4,707 yards and 46 touchdowns with just 8 interceptions. It was arguably one of the best seasons by a signal caller in NFL history. The Rams touted the best offense in the NFL in 2025. His primary target last season was Puka Nacua, who reeled in 129 of 166 targets for 1,715 yards and 10 touchdowns. However, his availability for Sunday’s primetime matchup is uncertain and it seems unlikely he will be able to play. Even so, Davante Adams gives them a top-notch wide receiver. Adams was the Rams’ second leading receiver with 60 receptions on 114 targets for 789 yards and 14 touchdowns last year. He is coming off a huge game versus the New York Giants where he had nearly 200 receiving yards and two touchdowns. The longtime veteran could be a huge problem for Denver. There’s no doubt the Rams have a prolific passing attack with Stafford at the helm. He’s also been a hard quarterback to sack over the years. Dialing up the heat on Stafford and limiting Adams’ impact will be crucial for Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph. They can’t let their passing attack go wild on Sunday Night Football . Defensive X-Factor: Cornerback Trent McDuffie Myles Garrett certainly would have earned my designation here, but he won’t be playing. That’s good news for the Broncos. Aaron Donald earned some consideration, but I ultimately wound up going with two-time All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie. The Rams gave up a lot of draft capital to acquire McDuffie and gave him one of the biggest contracts at the position in NFL history. In his first two games for the Rams, so far so good for the fifth-year cornerback. McDuffie has been targeted six times and allowed four receptions for just 23 yards. Against the Giants, he was able to pick off Jameis Winston after starting quarterback Jaxson Dart left the game due to injury. Bo Nix already has a few bad decisions and turnovers this season. Denver can’t afford to have him get picked off by McDuffie in primetime. It’ll be interesting to see who McDuffie ends up trailing the most in coverage. Conventional wisdom says Courtland Sutton, but with the way the Broncos are trying to involve Jaylen Waddle in their aerial attack, it wouldn’t be surprising to see McDuffie matched up against Waddle on occasion. How the Broncos can secure a victory over the Rams ICYMI: I offered a blueprint for a Broncos’ victory yesterday. This is going to be a very tough game for Denver to win, but I do like the fact Denver will have homefield advantage. Some people will discount that, but the stadium was absolutely rocking due to fan noise against the Jaguars. The Broncos need to have a strong rushing attack and have time consuming drives. This also means better execution on third down. The Rams have an offense that can strike quick and score a lot of points. This isn’t a game where I want to see Nix have to throw forty times and try and outduel Stafford. I’d also like to see them do much better with starting field position. They did not do well in this regard against the Jaguars and were routinely inside their own fifteen-yard line to begin several drives. Hopefully Marvin Mims Jr. is able to return from injury and offer some impact as a returner on special teams. And as I say most weeks—no more penalties. This is absolutely crippling the offense’s ability to be efficient. Somehow, someway, I think the Broncos will squeak out a victory in primetime. Hart’s Prediction: Broncos 24, Rams 23.
author: Christopher Hart

title: Broncos embrace their prime-time moment against the Rams
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! A prime-time do-over. After an embarrassing performance on Monday Night Football to open the season, the Denver Broncos get a chance to settle the prime-time score on Sunday Night Football. The big difference is that this game is at home. Plus, the Broncos are coming off a good win over the […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos looks to pass during the first quarter of the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! A prime-time do-over. After an embarrassing performance on Monday Night Football to open the season, the Denver Broncos get a chance to settle the prime-time score on Sunday Night Football. The big difference is that this game is at home. Plus, the Broncos are coming off a good win over the Jacksonville Jaguars. The task in front of Denver doesn’t get any easier against the Los Angeles Rams, but playing at home doesn’t hurt. Midnight Navy on prime time 🔜 pic.twitter.com/iFIJo29oOP — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) September 24, 2026 “I think primetime games in general are awesome,” Broncos quarterback Bo Nix said to the media earlier this week. “Night-time games at our stadium are awesome. We have a great electric atmosphere. It’s always fun when you grow up, you watch these primetime games. It’s usually when everybody’s watching, when all the TVs are on. You just know it’s a big deal, you know it’s a big game, you know two good teams are playing against each other. For us, we say it all the time, we know we’ll play in bigger games, but right now this is the next biggest one. “We have to continue to have success in these so that we can have success as an organization. So this is the next challenge, and we’re excited to be on primetime. That’s always a really good thing. That means you have something good going, but you have to keep winning and keep staying on primetime, or ultimately, it doesn’t really matter.” There’s also something about playing on Sunday Night Football. As Carrie Underwood’s intro belts out, “Waiting all day for Sunday night.” “Playing primetime at home is just a different type of vibe, a different type of scenery,” Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain II said to the media. “Having that home crowd to our advantage is pretty beneficial on our end, especially defensively. Having that crowd noise to affect the offense, I think it’s going to be pretty huge, so we’re looking forward to it. It’s going to be another fun and exciting battle at Empower. So we have a great challenge ahead of us, so we just have to prepare and make sure we stay sharp.” When you get two legitimate Super Bowl contenders, that only makes the potential for a great game even higher. “I think each week is its own battle,” Broncos receiver Courtland Sutton said to the media earlier this week. “Each week is an opportunity to go out there and showcase our best. I think I might have mentioned this before last year, but it’s not easy to win in this league. I don’t care what a team’s record is; every team has aspirations to go out there and be successful. “It’s our job to go out there and put our best foot forward. The Rams are a really good team. They played really well last year, they did a lot of things really, really well, and watching the film, they’re continuing to do a lot of things really well. It’s on us to have a great week of preparation on the field, meeting rooms, recovery, the whole nine, to make sure that we can go out here and put our best foot forward going against these guys.” Broncos links

title: Pat Surtain ready to battle Davante Adams in Week 3
summary: The Denver Broncos have a big prime time matchup this Sunday against the Los Angeles Rams and while much of the discussion will be around the quarterbacks, there is one battle that is always a strong matchup to watch: Pat Surtain vs. Davante Adams. Early in Surtain’s career, he was cooked by Adams when he […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - SEPTEMBER 20: Pat Surtain II (2) of the Denver Broncos prepares for the Jacksonville Jaguars offense during the second quarter at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Sunday, September 20, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images The Denver Broncos have a big prime time matchup this Sunday against the Los Angeles Rams and while much of the discussion will be around the quarterbacks, there is one battle that is always a strong matchup to watch: Pat Surtain vs. Davante Adams. Early in Surtain’s career, he was cooked by Adams when he was a member of the Las Vegas Raiders. But the tide began to shift Surtain’s way in 2023 and beyond with Adams increasingly getting locked down. “It’s good battles, good competition,” Surtain said this week. “It’s going to be another battle on Sunday. [I’m] Looking forward to it. In his last two games against Denver (back in 2023), Adams had a combined 11 catches for 112 yards and one touchdowns. Decent for most wide receivers, but in 2022 he torched Surtain for 16 catches for a whooping 242 yards and two touchdowns. With Adams getting older, this could be a sport where Surtain dominates as Adams did in 2022. We shall see. Broncos daily recap Broncos vs. Rams: 3 Things to Watch for in Week 3 The Denver Broncos host the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday Night Football . Here are three storylines to keep your eyes on. Denver Broncos look to continue success vs. NFC opponents In the last nine games against NFC teams, the Broncos are 9-0. All streaks end. When will this one? How the Denver Broncos can beat the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday Night Football Here is what the Denver Broncos have to accomplish to defeat the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday Night Football . Potent quotables Bo Nix On the importance of building brotherhood within the team “Close teams play for one another and the tighter the team, usually the more you’re willing to give and [the] more passion, and effort and intensity you play with. So when you care about the guys you’re out there competing with, it means a lot. I think it helps in competition like that. It’s sometimes tough in a professional league to have a close team because you have so many different walks of life, but we have a close team. There are a lot of guys on our team that been here for a while, and then we’ve just welcomed in the new guys that have joined us and they just fall right in.” On why the offense performs better in the second half and how to sustain that for a full game “I think two plays in that first half, and it looks like we scored 14 points and it’s completely different, we’re not really talking about a slow start or anything. We had two really good drives that we just didn’t score points on. I think that in the second half, that translated to touchdowns and we got a good lead. So we just have to focus on those things to get the ball in the end zone. Then I think that is really what we could look like as a team. If we score points there, we’re in the 30s [points scored] and it’s a really good outing for us against a really good team. So we just have to find ways to finish the drive, score in the red zone, convert on a few more third downs so we can get to the red zone. It’s just complete football.” On what stands out from the Rams defense on film and the challenges they present “They have a veteran defense. They have a really good front. They really play through their front four, their front five, the guys that are the defensive line that are in there. They’ve done a good job of building on their back end this off season with some corner depth. But they’re going to be good, they’re going to provide a challenge for us. They’ve won a lot of games in the past couple years, and I feel like they’re similar to us. They had a very similar season last year where they could have gone all the way. So they’re loaded up front. They have a really good young core. They have some older veteran guys obviously with some guys coming back. It’s going to present us with a challenge, but our offensive line’s really good and we’re going to fall back on them and then just at skill, we have to be aggressive and go make plays.” On his reaction to Rams DE Aaron Donald coming out of retirement “For a guy like that who’s played so much football at a dominant level, if anything, he could be better because he’s got some good rest. It’s exciting to play the greats, it always is. I know he’s a really good football player, and he’s going to provide a challenge that we haven’t necessarily faced before. He’s literally one of the best at his position of all time, so you don’t play those many Sundays. He’s going to be a good player, he’s going to play more and more as the season goes with rep count. I’m sure he’s just getting back in the swing of things, but a dominant player for a long time. So I honestly don’t expect anything different, we just have to limit the time he’s dominant.” On facing veteran QB Matthew Stafford “It’ll be a really fun game because of that. I’ve always watched him, looked up to him and admired the way he plays the game. He’s just extremely smart. He has a really strong arm, he’s just always been fun to watch. As our quarterback room, since I’ve been here for the last couple years, we’ve enjoyed watching their offense and watching him play. So it’ll be fun to go against him. It’ll be fun to meet him for the first time, I haven’t ever met him. But at this point in the league, you feel like you play a great quarterback every Sunday. So for me, he’s another guy that I can cross off the list that I could say I watched in person, and I think it’ll be a fun battle between our two teams.” On if he has more freedom to make adjustments at the line of scrimmage “I think just that’s how we’ve been operating and that’s how he [Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb] wants really to get our offensive system going and let the quarterback play the game through his eyes and get us to the right plays and not… Ultimately as an offense, you just want to limit the times you run bad plays into bad looks. So for us, it’s all about getting to the right football play so that we give ourselves the best advantage. There’s a lot on our plate as a quarterback, but there’s also a lot on his plate and we do a good job. As I’m on the field seeing things, he’s on the sideline seeing things. We communicate, we get to the right look and I expect that to just continue to build as the season goes on.” On WR Jaylen Waddle’s route on the final third-down conversion “We ran that play because we really wanted man. We wanted him to get matched up on the nickel and sure enough, we see it and we’re champing at the bit just to get the play off. I didn’t realize he ran such a good route and had that outcome really until watching it. When he’s that open, you’re like, ‘I just don’t want to miss him.’ Don’t overthrow him, don’t miss him. So he caught it, and he got down and saved some time. That’s just the element that he provides. It was a really great route, really impressive. He’s going to be really difficult to guard in man-to-man situations as the game goes on because we have two of the other guys that are basically getting held as they’re running their routes because they’re tough to guard as well. So we just have a really good personnel grouping when those guys are out on the field, and it’s not easy to play man-to-man against them. They’re just difficult to guard, tough matchups.” On if there is a reason for the team’s success in its last nine games against NFC opponents “I don’t know. I think that’s just by schedule, by chance. We’ve competed against some really good teams. We’ve had some close NFC matchups. One that I remember is last year, the Eagles. They gave us a challenge, and we had to come back and same with the Giants. So we’ve had to play some complete football against these teams, and so I think it’s just by chance and by schedule. Obviously you play more AFC teams,…

title: Broncos vs. Rams: 3 Things to Watch for in Week 3
summary: Coming off an impressive comeback victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars, the Denver Broncos earned a much-needed confidence boost heading into their matchup versus the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday Night Football. Here are three storylines for Broncos Country to keep a close eye on in Denver’s Week 3 primetime game hosting the Rams. Will Jaylen […]
full_text: Sep 20, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton on the sidelines during the second half against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Coming off an impressive comeback victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars, the Denver Broncos earned a much-needed confidence boost heading into their matchup versus the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday Night Football . Here are three storylines for Broncos Country to keep a close eye on in Denver’s Week 3 primetime game hosting the Rams. Will Jaylen Waddle have another impact game and shine in primetime? One of the highlights in their victory over the Jaguars was how dominant wide receiver Jaylen Waddle was. After being virtually shut down in Week 1 against the Kansas City Chiefs, Waddle had a tremendous impact last Sunday and was the highlight player for the Broncos offensively. He reeled in eight receptions on ten targets for 138 yards. Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb did a great job utilizing Waddle in a variety of manners from the slot to ‘Z’. I felt Webb was fantastic isolating him in mismatch scenarios against a tough Jaguars defense. How the Broncos choose to deploy Waddle on a weekly basis will certainly be one of the most intriguing aspects of the season. The Rams spent a lot of money this offseason revamping their secondary via free agency additions or making big trades. It’ll be interesting to see how Denver comes up with a gameplan to attack that. For the second straight week, my money is on Waddle playing a big role for the Broncos’ offense. Can Bo Nix pick up where he left off against the Jaguars? Head Coach Sean Payton called the Broncos’ affair against the Jaguars a tale of two halves. The offense struggled in the first quarter of the game. Through fifteen minutes of play, all three of their drives resulted in punts. Denver didn’t achieve a second down until the second quarter and only netted three points in two redzone trips before halftime. In the second half, Nix seemed much more poised in the pocket. He put together another impressive fourth quarter rally which earned him yet another comeback victory. Webb’s half time adjustments played a big role in that. He helped set Nix up for success by getting him to throw on the move and having him get some more looks under center. It will be important for Nix and the Broncos’ offense to start off hot and forego their slow starts. Nobody wants to see Denver have to try and rally back against a well-coached team that scored the most points in the NFL last season. I’m optimistic Nix can deliver, but the offensive line will have to give him a chance to make plays. What’s the defensive plan to combat the Rams’ offense? The Rams had an uncharacteristically bad game in their season opener against the San Francisco 49ers. Though they looked much better and reverted to top form against the New York Giants on Monday Night Football . Stafford threw for over 300 yards and had four touchdowns. Keep in mind, that was without Puka Nacua—whose availability for Sunday Night Football is still up in the air. With Nacua out, Davante Adams went off and hauled in eight catches for 195 yards and 2 touchdowns. Even with Denver’s talented secondary, Adams could prove to be a problem depending on who is tasked with covering him. Additionally, their running back duo of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum combined for 164 yards rushing on just 24 carries. In addition to those players, the Rams also have a handful of intriguing players at tight end. Terrance Ferguson is an emerging player in their offense and looked good last week. Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph is going to have his hands full again this week coming up with another game plan to stop a talented and high-scoring Sean McVay offense. Even so, Broncos Country should be optimistic they can do that, especially given how well the group performed against the Jaguars last Sunday.

full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 19: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos in action against the New York Giants at Empower Field At Mile High on October 19, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos look to continue its success against NFC opponents in Week 3 when they host the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday Night Football . In the last nine games against NFC teams, the Broncos are 9-0. In fact, Bo Nix has only lost a single game against NFC teams and that was his first ever start in the league. That’s wild to think about. He is 9-1 all-time. Bo Nix career vs. NFC 2024, Week 1: Seattle Seahawks (20-26) L 2024, Week 3: Tampa Bay Buccaneers (26-7) W 2024, Week 7: New Orleans Saints (33-10) W 2024, Week 8: Carolina Panthers (28-14) W 2024, Week 11: Atlanta Falcons (38-6) W 2025, Week 5: Philadelphia Eagles (21-17) W 2025, Week 7: New York Giants (33-32) W 2025, Week 8: Dallas Cowboys (44-24) W 2025, Week 13: Washington Commanders (27-26) W 2025, Week 15: Green Bay Packers (34-26) W When asked about the streak, head coach Sean Payton smartly downplayed the whole thing noting the closeness of most of those games and how they just don’t play a whole lot of NFC teams. “We’ve competed against some really good teams,” Payton said. “We’ve had some close NFC matchups. One that I remember is last year, the Eagles. They gave us a challenge, and we had to come back and same with the Giants. So we’ve had to play some complete football against these teams, and so I think it’s just by chance and by schedule. Obviously you play more AFC teams, usually typically year-to-year, so the pool is smaller. I think we’re playing good football when we play out of the league, but obviously that doesn’t win us the next game. So we just have to keep at it, and work hard out here on the field, practice hard and just get ready for the next one.” I hate streaks and now that this one has been mentioned, I’ll be fretting every time they face an NFC opponent. To be fair, the NFC South was fairly bad in 2024 and the NFC East was not — which is why most of those games were wild and close comebacks wins for Denver. And it only got harder this season with the NFC West on the docket. All streaks must end. Where do you think this one against NFC teams ends? vs. Los Angeles Rams at San Francisco 49ers vs. Seattle Seahawks at Arizona Cardinals at Carolina Panthers The first three on this list are no gimmies, but if I had to pick where the streak ends I would have to say on the road against the 49ers.
