title: The Packers Have Won 13 Straight Home Openers. How Did Those Seasons Go?
summary: The Green Bay Packers have a chance to make history during Thursday night’s home opener against the Atlanta Falcons. The team is currently tied with the Miami Dolphins (1976-1988) for the longest streak of consecutive home opener wins in NFL history. With a win tonight, they could be the only team that’s won 14 home […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Robbins/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers have a chance to make history during Thursday night’s home opener against the Atlanta Falcons. The team is currently tied with the Miami Dolphins (1976-1988) for the longest streak of consecutive home opener wins in NFL history. With a win tonight, they could be the only team that’s won 14 home openers in a row, setting a new NFL record. Let’s take a look at the Packers’ last 13 home openers and how each season played out…buckle up and get those therapists on speed dial! 2025 Home Opener Opponent: Detroit Lions Score: 27-13 Notable Home Opener Moment: Micah Parsons chasing down Jared Goff for a sack 2025 Record: 9-7-1 Playoffs: Lost to Bears in Wild Card Spirits were at an all-time high to start the season after the Packers traded for Micah Parsons just before the season started. The team itself had its ups and downs to start, but after a brutal 10-7 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles at home, the Packers pulled it together and won 3 division games in a row, 1 against each team, bringing them to a 9-3-1 record. However, disaster struck in Denver when the Packers lost to the Broncos and, even worse, the team lost Micah Parsons for the rest of the season to an ACL tear. The team didn’t win another game last season, and ultimately lost in overtime to the Chicago Bears in the Wild Card round of the playoffs after leading 21-6 heading into the 4th quarter. 2024 Home Opener Opponent: Indianapolis Colts Score: 16-10 Notable Home Opener Moment: C Josh Myers puked on a ball right before snapping it to Malik Willis 2024 Record: 11-6 Playoffs: Lost to the Eagles in Wild Card This season started bumpy with the Packers taking on the Eagles in Brazil Week 1 and Jordan Love injuring his knee at the end of the game, causing him to miss the home opener. Despite their impressive 11-6 record, the Packers finished 3rd in a very competitive division and snuck into the playoffs as the 7th seed and clinched a playoff seed after their Week 16 34-0 shutout win vs. the Saints. However, disaster struck in their final game of the season when Christian Watson tore his ACL against the Chicago Bears. The disaster continued into their playoff game against the Eagles when the team lost several starters, including WR Romeo Doubs, WR Jayden Reed, RB Josh Jacobs, OL Elgton Jenkins, OL Josh Myers, LB Quay Walker, DT Devonte Wyatt. Between the injuries, bad luck, and ugly penalties, the Packers ended their season with a 22-10 loss. 2023 Home Opener Opponent: New Orleans Saints Score: 18-17 Notable Home Opener Moment: Jordan Love earning his “silly body” nickname 2023 Record: 9-8 Playoffs: Lost to the San Francisco 49ers in Divisional round The season got off to a promising start as the Packers went into Soldier Field and dominated the Bears in a 38-20 win in Jordan Love’s first game as Packers QB1 ( that gave us an iconic photo from David Bakhtiari ). However, it would take a bit for the Packers to find their footing with their new quarterback at the helm. The team started 2-5, but turned things around and stunned the world with an incredible performance on Thanksgiving in Detroit, followed by a big win over the Chiefs at home the next week. However, the Packers went 2-1 in their next 3 games against struggling teams including losses to the New York Giants and Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and a win over the Carolina Panthers thanks to poor clock management by Carolina in the final seconds. On New Year’s Eve, the team had a dominant win over the Minnesota Vikings and ended their season with a win over the Bears. The Packers faced a huge challenge against the Dallas Cowboys in the first round of the playoffs, a team that hadn’t lost at home all season. Jordan Love put up one of the greatest playoff performances in NFL history in his first playoff game ever and the Packers shocked the Cowboys in a 48-32 win that had the Packers up 34-10 at one point. Jordan Love was pulled from the game with a perfect stat line until the defense made things a little too close for comfort. Love came back in and had 1 incompletion, taking him out of a perfect passer rating. The Packers went on to face the San Francisco 49ers hoping to finally move on from the ugly history of Packers-49ers playoff games for Green Bay. Unfortunately, despite the Packers having a 21-14 lead heading into the 4th quarter, they couldn’t keep the momentum (sound familiar?), and they lost 24-21, ending their season. 2022 Home Opener Opponent: Chicago Bears Score: 27-10 Notable Home Opener Moment: Defense stuffing Justin Fields on 4th and goal late in the 4th quarter Record: 8-9 Playoffs: N/A This was QB Aaron Rodgers’ last season as a Green Bay Packer despite signing a new contract in the offseason, and unfortunately it was not exactly a good season to go out on. The Packers traded star WR Davante Adams to the Las Vegas Raiders in the offseason after being unable to agree on an extension and the team missed the playoffs for the first time since Mike McCarthy was fired. After starting the season 3-1, the team lost 7 of their next 8 with their one win coming in overtime against the Dallas Cowboys in Mike McCarthy’s return to Lambeau Field. The team made a push late, winning 4 of their next 6, including a win over the Bears that made them the winningest franchise in NFL history. All the team needed to do was beat the Detroit Lions in their final game in order to sneak into the playoffs. Despite it being at home, the team struggled, and like his predecessor before him, Aaron Rodgers’ last pass as a Green Bay Packer was a season-ending interception . Because as Packers fans we can’t just have normal moments. Things are either good or traumatizing and gutting. 2021 Home Opener Opponent: Detroit Lions Score: 35-17 Notable Home Opener Moment: Packers trainer finding Aaron Jones’ necklace in the end zone that contained his dad’s ashes Record: 13-4 Playoffs: Lost in Divisional to San Francisco 49ers The offseason was a little touch and go for the Packers after the team struggled to get a deal done with Davante Adams. However, both Rodgers and Adams posted a photo referencing “The Last Dance” indicating they’d both be returning for at least that season. The 2021 season gave us one of the best Aaron Rodgers moments when the team was playing the Chicago Bears in Soldier Field. After running in a touchdown in the 4th quarter, the QB put on his iconic belt and yelled “ I OWN YOU ” to Bears fans in the stands. Rodgers had one of the best seasons of his career in 2021, securing his 4th MVP win after throwing for over 4000 yards, 37 touchdowns, and only 4 interceptions. Both Rodgers and Adams also secured 1st team all-pro nods for the season. The Packers finally got their home playoff game against the 49ers after securing the 1 seed and faced the San Francisco 49ers in a snowy Lambeau Field. The Packers’ offense put up a disappointing 10 points. The defense held the team to 3 points through 3 quarters but ultimately Maurice Drayton’s special teams unit did what they do best…suck! Corey Bojorquez had a punt blocked late in the 4th that the 49ers returned for a touchdown to tie the game. The 49ers won the game on a field goal as time expired. Maurice Drayton lost his job and my therapist got a little more job security! Balance! 2020 Home Opener Opponent: Detroit Lions Score: 42-21 Notable Home Opener Moment: Chandon Sullivan (remember him?) pick 6 Record: 13-3 Playoffs: Lost in NFC Championship to Tampa Bay Buccaneers The offseason was a weird one after the Packers traded up in the draft to select QB Jordan Love in the first round. Between that little piece of drama and the league dealing with COVID-19, the season as a whole was a little odd. However, the Packers themselves were on a tear, specifically the offense. The Packers put up at least 30 points in 12 of their 16 games and scored a whopping 509 points, their 2nd highest scoring season of all time only behind the 2011 season (560).…

title: What a Packers game-day roster could look like: Week 3
summary: This week’s edition of playing out the Green Bay Packers’ game-day roster decisions will be much simpler than past ones, since there are fewer moving parts. The Packers have already ruled out four players for Thursday Night Football against the Atlanta Falcons, and they’re at positions where they were already “oversigned,” so their roster can […]
full_text: (Photo by Ross Harried/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images This week’s edition of playing out the Green Bay Packers’ game-day roster decisions will be much simpler than past ones, since there are fewer moving parts. The Packers have already ruled out four players for Thursday Night Football against the Atlanta Falcons , and they’re at positions where they were already “oversigned,” so their roster can withstand the numbers there. The only question is how the team will use their final inactive spot, or if both of their questionable players (DL Anthony Campbell and Javon Hargrave) will both miss the game. If that happens, the Packers will probably need to call up Eric Johnson II from the practice squad, despite him just arriving in Green Bay last week . That’s really it! Below is what the Packers’ roster will likely look like, unless they throw a curveball at us. Quarterback In: Jordan Love and Tyrod Taylor Out: None Running Back In: Chris Brooks, Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd Out: None Receiver In: Christian Watson (Z), Matthew Golden (X), Skyy Moore (slot), Bo Melton (X) and J. Michael Sturdivant (Z) Out: Jayden Reed (injury) The Packers’ receiver room has been very rigid dating back to the preseason, with players firmly locked into Z, X and slot positions. With Jayden Reed out, Skyy Moore is the backup slot on the team and is expected to fill in the snaps that Reed played. With that being said, though, now that push has come to shove, I wouldn’t be surprised to see Bo Melton, who is usually Matthew Golden’s direct backup at the X position, splitting some time with Moore and taking over some slot reps. Tight End In: Tucker Kraft, Mark Redman, Jonnu Smith and Josh Whyle Out: None Offensive Line In: Jorgan Morgan (LT), Donovan Jennings (LG), Sean Rhyan (C), Jacob Monk (RG), Anthony Belton (RT), Jager Burton (G/C), John Williams (T/G/C) and Travis Glover (T/G) Out: Zach Bako-Bewele (injury) and Aaron Banks (injury) This will likely be Travis Glover’s first active game of the 2026 season. John Williams was active in Week 1, when Aaron Banks was ruled out, but was a healthy scratch in Week 2 (along with Glover), as Banks was able to suit up for the game before eventually going down with a toe injury. Defensive Line In: Devonte Wyatt, Karl Brooks, Jonathan Ford and Chris McClellan Out: Warren Brinson (injury) One of three will play: Javon Hargrave (injury), Anthony Campbell (injury) or Eric Johnson II (practice squad) The only real decision this week is who the 48th man will be, and that player will almost certainly come down to a defensive lineman, as there are only four certain “goes” on the 53-man roster — leaving the Packers with just one sub at the position when they play base defense. Edge Defender In: Lukas Van Ness, Barryn Sorrell, Brenton Cox Jr. and Dani Dennis-Sutton Out: None Off-Ball Linebacker In: Zaire Franklin, Edgerrin Cooper, Isaiah McDuffie, Ty’Ron Hopper and Nick Niemann Out: None Cornerback In: Keisean Nixon, Brandon Cisse, Carrington Valentine, Benjamin St-Juste and Kamal Hadden Out: None Safety In: Xavier McKinney, Evan Williams, Javon Bullard and Kitan Oladapo Out: None Specialists In: K Trey Smack, P Daniel Whelan and LS Matt Orzech Out: None — Maybe the only benefit to the Packers’ injuries this year is that it’s made it easy to predict their Week 3 48-man game-day roster. It just comes down to who the fifth defensive lineman will be. — Update: The Packers didn’t elevate anyone from the practice squad today, so either Javon Hargrave or Anthony Campbell will be active for the game.

title: Judge denies permanent seal of Josh Jacobs video
summary: Judge Marc Hammer denied the motion to permanently seal evidence in the battery case of Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs, which includes a video from inside Jacobs’ garage, on Thursday. The evidence was previously under a temporary seal at the request of Jacobs, but Hammer denied the victim’s request to permanently seal the […]
full_text: (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images Judge Marc Hammer denied the motion to permanently seal evidence in the battery case of Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs, which includes a video from inside Jacobs’ garage, on Thursday. The evidence was previously under a temporary seal at the request of Jacobs, but Hammer denied the victim’s request to permanently seal the evidence. Evidence will now be in the hands of the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department, which will handle requests for the video moving forward. This is a notable shift in the Jacobs case, as it was previously reported that the NFL was attempting to acquire the video , but had not yet received it. Jacobs is currently on the commissioner exempt list, which prevents him from seeing the field or practice time — but he can still participate in meetings in the Packers’ building. The NFL has yet to make a suspension announcement on Jacobs because they wanted to talk to the back and see the video before they made a ruling. As the league learned during the Ray Rice case, the NFL is only allowed to punish a player for a single action once, and can’t punish a player further for the same infraction if the video eventually ended up in the public’s hands. Rice sued the league on the basis of that; the case went to arbitration and eventually ruled that the NFL’s initial suspension of Rice for two games stood, but their indefinite suspension must be dropped and that the back needed to be paid for the games beyond the two-game suspension. Jacobs pleaded no contest to battery and criminal damage to property earlier this month. According to the police report, the video shows “the altercation,” and at least shows the victim on the ground for 40 seconds before Jacobs returns to the garage and damages the victim’s cellphone. What’s uncertain, because of the wording of the police report, is whether the video includes what led to the victim hitting the ground. In the police report, it states that Jacobs grabbed and threw the anonymous woman to the ground, resulting in injury, but it doesn’t explicitly state whether or not that was caught on video, unlike the damaging of her cellphone. The anonymous woman was identified as Jacobs’ girlfriend, but because she did not live with Jacobs or have a child with Jacobs, the crime did not qualify for the domestic abuse enhancer in the state of Wisconsin. Both Jacobs and the victim have an opportunity to appeal a request to release evidence (including the video) moving forward, but only at the level of the police department, not the district court’s office. Officially, the district court’s order to deny the permanent seal will be active on Friday. Hobart-Lawrence Police Department has 10 days to fulfill public records requests for evidence, so we should get answers — one way or another — soon. title: Houston Texans Prediction at Colts Week Three
summary: The Texans unfortunately enter familiar territory. For the second straight year and third time in the DeMeco Ryans era, the Texans are 0-2 out of the gate. They face their AFC South rivals the Indianapolis Colts (0-2), who’ve also tripped coming out of the gate. Both teams are exceptionally desperate for a win, and neither […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - JANUARY 04: Running back Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts is tackled by a swarm of Houston Texans defenders during the NFL game between Houston Texans and Indianapolis Colts on January 4, 2026, at NRG Stadium in Houston, TX. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Texans unfortunately enter familiar territory. For the second straight year and third time in the DeMeco Ryans era, the Texans are 0-2 out of the gate. They face their AFC South rivals the Indianapolis Colts (0-2), who’ve also tripped coming out of the gate. Both teams are exceptionally desperate for a win, and neither are off to the start they hoped after losing two games to perennial favorites in the AFC. The Colts lost two high scoring affairs to the Baltimore Ravens and Kansas City Chiefs and are looking to right the ship against the Houston Texan. FanDuel’s odds currently favor the Texans by 1.5 points. Those odds are much lower than Houston fans would have hoped for and are indicative of the poor start the Texans have put together on both sides of the ball. Jonathan Taylor powers the Colts’ offense with 190 yards through two games. I predict he will have another productive and efficient day given the Texans difficulties stopping the run. No Henry To’oTo’o or Kayden McDonald means the Texans are vulnerable up the middle of the defense. QB Daniel Jones has been thoroughly mediocre in his return from Achilles injury suffered last season. He has thrown two touchdowns and two interceptions. He has struggled to sustain drives and has not looked efficient in the red zone. Newly minted $114M man Alec Pierce has landed on Injured Reserve. He crushed the Texans last year and racked up 210 yards and three touchdowns in two games. His absence will be an immense blessing for a Texans defense surely in need of a reprieve and get-right game. As for the Texans’ offense, they quickly shifted away from the run against the Bengals, opting to throw the ball a career high 55 times for C.J. Stroud. This was ineffective and certainly not the game script from Offensive Coordinator Nick Caley. Expect Houston to commit, heavily to the run game and incorporate the screen game to break up the issues they’ve faced on offense. PREDICTION: Colts 24, Texans 17 The Texans offense have yet to put it together. Without WR Nico Collins in the line up there is no indication of their ability to score points. Plus, the Texans’ defense has been unusually porous to start the 2026 season, not to mention unable to convert any turnovers. Houston has to find a way to get WR Kayshon Boutte incorporated into the offense. Boutte leads the league in go-routes, but that’s simply not enough for him to positively impact this offense. Slants and screens are two easy options for the wide receiver to take more ownership of the air attack and help move the ball down the field. What separates these two teams is the Colts’ run game. Jonathan Taylor is the most effective weapon for either offense and will allow the Colts to control the tempo. Houston has yet to counter a strong rushing attack. QB Daniel Jones is fairly immobile, which is ideal for the Texans pass rush. In Week One, Bills QB Josh Allen detonated the Texans pass rush duo with his scrambling ability. Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter won’t have to worry about that with Jones, who has already been sacked twice this season. I predict Tyler Warren to have a very productive game against the Texans defense. He leads their team with nine receptions, but only 39 yards. Houston gave up play after play to Buffalo’s tight end Dalton Kincaid. Expect Jones to find Warren early and often on play action plays to decrease the pressure on the run game. The Colts late addition of Keenan Allen has paid dividends as his seven receptions is third on the team behind Josh Downs and Tyler Warren. He is facing a potential three-game suspension due to driving over the legal limit in Indianapolis earlier this month. If he plays he should be the focal point of CB Kamari Lassiter, who is desperately in need of a good game. The Texans have not let Lassiter and Derek Stingley Jr. follow specific receivers, which has led to ill-advised mismatches in the secondary. The Colts game presents an opportunity for Stingley Jr. to follow the faster Downs and Lassiter to pursue Allen. One player on the Texans offense to watch for is Jaylin Noel. He was featured more often this game than in previous contests, mostly out of desperation, but it’s a good sign of his growth and incorporation in Houston’s plans. Fans saw Dalton Schultz shine in a big role last week, which should most certainly be the case again if Nico Collins is sidelined with a hamstring injury again. Going 0-3 again is not ideal. The criticism and disgruntled emotions will be at an all-time high under the Ryans era. This team was supposed to be better than the last across the board and haven’t shown any progression on any of the fronts they addressed this offseason. The offensive line can’t pass protect or move the ball. The run game is putrid. Whoever plays safety next to Calen Bullock forgets how to play football (C.J. Gardner Johnson, Reed Blankenship). Will it be different this game and can the Texans right the ship earlier than last year? We’ll find out on Sunday.

title: Five Good Texans Questions with Stampede Blue
summary: You stay in this game long enough and you start building relationships along the way. Chris Sheperd of Stampede Blue and I have been doing five questions for the last five years and it has been an enjoyable ride. Even though the Colts and Tecans are enemies on the field doesn’t mean we have to […]
full_text: You stay in this game long enough and you start building relationships along the way. Chris Sheperd of Stampede Blue and I have been doing five questions for the last five years and it has been an enjoyable ride. Even though the Colts and Tecans are enemies on the field doesn’t mean we have to be enemies in the proverbial press box. Yet again, the Texans and Colts stand in each other’s way for playoff contention. Two 0-2 teams are coming off of two tough weeks and that is where our conversation began. Battle Red Blog: Like the Texans, the Colts have started 0-2 but against quality opponents. Are you concerned or feel like the start is a function of the difficult competition? Chris Shepard: Most Colts fans believe the sky is falling and given the history of the last decade they may be right to believe that. I am less concerned than most but concerned all the same. The defense went through a big turnover this offseason. Colts fans were largely over linebacker Zaire Franklin on and off of the field, but he was a long tenured leader of the defense as was corner Kenny Moore. Indy was right to move on from them in an attempt to do a soft reset on a leadership group that had yet to find sustained success. Just because it was the right thing to do doesn’t mean it’s going to yield immediate positive results. The Colts added a lot of young players and lower level free agents and so far we’ve seen them struggle to get to speed. Week two was a large improvement for the defense but I expect this defense won’t hit it’s stride until week 8 or 9, if they ever come together at all. Facing Lamar Jackson and Patrick Mahomes back to back against a young defense with so many new pieces was always going to be difficult and while I don’t think CJ Stroud is in that tier of quarterbacks, it’s not like things are going to be significantly easier for them in week three. BRB: Injuries are a part of the game obviously. We all saw Alec Pierce leave the game on Sunday night. Are there any other injuries you are concerned about? CS: Sauce Gardner went out in the second half with an injury, he was able to return but he was in obvious pain. Sauce has been very good through two weeks so I’ll be monitoring his progress throughout the week. BRB: Who are some new faces we haven’t seen in this matchup that will play a key role on Sunday? CS: Rookie safety AJ Halucy has gotten every opportunity to contribute so far thus season. Halucy, a third round pick out of LSU, hasn’t been bad but he has made some rookie mistakes. I suspect they’ll continue to give him the majority of the snaps at strong safety and there is plenty of reason to believe he’ll make more of an impact as the season goes on. Rookie linebackers Bryce Boettcher (Oregon) and CJ Allen (Georgia) have been working their way into a linebacker rotation. Allen missed more than a month of training camp due to injury and is working his way back. Neither player has made much of an impact yet but week by week they should see more time on the field and week three should see another uptick of snaps for both. BRB: This is an annual question. Who are you most concerned about in the AFC South and how do you see the division shaking out? Which divisional opponent do Colts fans enjoy beating the most? CS: The Jaguars are my biggest concern followed closely by the Texans. Houston figured things out last season and while defensive success is more difficult to sustain year over year, DeMeco Ryans is a very good coach and I expect they’ll turn things around in short order. The Jaguars combination of Trevor Lawrence and Liam Coen has been solid. I’m less sold on Coen long term than I am on Ryans, I think that when things start to go bad for him he’s more likely to be unable to right the Jacksonville ship. But until that happens, the combo of Coen and Lawrence with that offense puts them at the top of the division. Ultimately, I think it’ll land on the Jaguars at the top and I hope Indy and Houston are in a battle for a wildcard spot headed into week 18 but given Houston’s recent history they absolutely have the advantage right now. BRB: Fanduel has the Texans favored by 2.5. How do you see the game going on Sunday? Are there any other bets you feel comfortable recommending? CS: I think that’s a fair line.Both teams are desperate and both are capable of winning. I see this one coming down to the wire, with both teams trading shots until the final moments. In games like this one anything can happen and while I hope the Colts pull it off, Houston being the favorite makes sense. We want to thank Chris for taking the time to answer our questions and for being such a joy to work with for all of these years. Remember, if you want to catch the best Colts coverage, please feel free to catch his site at Stampede Blue . We want to wish Chris the Colts the best of luck for the rest of the season. That is of course except for when they are playing the Texans.
author: Scott Barzilla

title: Nick Caley: yet another failed Texans OC
summary: Talent at the NFL level is exceptionally high. Rarely is a player added to a pro football roster who isn’t a physically capable, pro football caliber athlete. It happens, but not as often as unhappy fans might suggest. The player’s mindset, motivation and attitude are another matter. As is their mental ability to grasp the […]
full_text: Jul 24, 2025; Houston, TX, USA; Houston Texans offensive coordinator Nick Caley during training camp at Houston Methodist Training Center. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Talent at the NFL level is exceptionally high. Rarely is a player added to a pro football roster who isn’t a physically capable, pro football caliber athlete. It happens, but not as often as unhappy fans might suggest. The player’s mindset, motivation and attitude are another matter. As is their mental ability to grasp the scheme, concepts and plays, then remember them all in the heat of the moment. The first paragraph above falls on the general manager to gatekeep. Nick Caserio’s job is to add physically capable, pro caliber athletes to the Houston Texans roster. One can argue that Caserio needs to find players that fit the scheme, which is valid, but the EP system is very adaptable to the roster. The player’s mindset, motivation and attitude, plus their ability to understand the mental aspects of the game falls to the coaching staff. Coaches, after all, are first and foremost teachers and mentors. When we see an offensive line full of NFL caliber athletes unable to open holes for an NFL caliber running back, odds are it’s not due to the players. But, as fans watching a game, the easiest vent for frustration is the “tip of the spear”, i.e. the player involved in the failed play. When the Houston Texans fired former offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik, the presumption was they were making a major upgrade. The reality begs to differ: Well well well look at this .. CJ Stroud has his former and current offensive coordinator shown at the bottom half #HTownMade https://t.co/UpcWuU1nCu — Juan 🥇 (@JuansTweeter) September 23, 2026 Slowik is dead last, Caley is bottom 5. This is not a quarterback problem, a running back problem, an offensive line problem. This isn’t due to the Houston Texans wr depth chart, the injury report or the fact they haven’t yet pulled the trigger on a Marvin Harrison Jr. trade. This is a coaching issue. Unfortunately, most fans can’t easily see coaching issues. We do see quarterbacks taking sacks and committing turnovers, or tailbacks running right into defensive linemen. What often gets collectively missed is the coaching decision that put the player in a bad situation in the first place. But, here’s a snapshot of insight from someone who does see what the casual observer often misses: Before I start, for those who don't know who @JOEL9ONE is, here's a summary of his credentials: – 11-year NFL veteran (Rams, Patriots, Eagles) – 2x Super Bowl Champion (Patriots, Eagles) – NFL Walter Payton Man of the Year (2018) – NFL All-Rookie Team (2008) Now that we've… pic.twitter.com/1wiczi8ojP — Clayton Anderson | HTX Sports (@Clay_HTXSports) September 23, 2026 Want to keep blaming C.J. Stroud, or the o-line or receiving corps? Last weekend, Stroud earned a place in the NFL record books as the only quarterback to throw for over 350 yards in an offense that scored less than 10 points. Jacob Barzilla, an awesome voice for Texans Nation, recently X’d (tweeted?) a list of OC play calling hires in the last 2 seasons. Of them, all but 1 are doing better than Caley (with the exception of Chip Kelly who has an NCAA gig currently). Jacob Barzilla (via X) The OC hires for experienced guys that call plays over the last 2 offseasons: Drew Petzing Zac Robinson Brian Daboll Matt Nagy Frank Reich Chip Kelly Klint Kubiak DeMeco Ryans and the Texans brass hand the defense over to Matt Burke and it goes from really good to elite. They hand the offense to Caley and it goes from not so good to still not so good. Which brings us to this week’s poll: During a recent Masthead discussion, I posed the idea “what if Stroud didn’t sign the $50 mil extension offer a few weeks back because he doesn’t want to spend his career in a crap Slowik/Caley offense?” The narrative of Stroud betting on himself, being greedy, whatever is all out there. But what if he simply doesn’t want to play in H-Town due to the abysmal offensive coaching? Say what you will about his decision making under pressure, his demeanor when things go wrong, how his stats/production have fallen since his rookie season. The fact is, if he was a free agent today, some other team would back up a dump truck full of dollars to sign him. And, he’d likely have several teams to choose from, including several offensive coaching staffs. And, more pointed: drop him on a team with a quality OC and he might already have a ring. The next narrative, which is certainly valid: firing an OC mid-season tanks the year. But Houston already has Jerry Schuplinski on staff. He has 3 Super Bowl rings, is widely regarded as a key asset in Stroud’s 2026 offseason improvements and is very well versed in the Erhardt-Perkins offensive scheme. Could Schuplinski excel at play calling? Well, odds are he couldn’t be any worse than Caley. Nick Caley’s playbook pic.twitter.com/2f0NkbXdju — Bill (@Will_ace4) September 20, 2026
author: Mike Bullock

title: Value of Things: By the Numbers
summary: Sunday sees a matchup of two 0-2 football teams that have lost to two playoff bound teams in their first two weeks. In other words, neither fan base knows for sure whether the lack of success is a factor of difficult opponents or glaring roster holes. Obviously, it is likely it will be a combination. […]
full_text: Sunday sees a matchup of two 0-2 football teams that have lost to two playoff bound teams in their first two weeks. In other words, neither fan base knows for sure whether the lack of success is a factor of difficult opponents or glaring roster holes. Obviously, it is likely it will be a combination. So, the numbers we look at may not actually be indicative of the quality of the unit. That is a part of the peril of handicapping early season matchups, The Texans in particular showed glaring defensive holes in week one and glaring offensive holes in week two. It is almost a version of Dr. Heckyl and Mr. Jackass. The Colts have some of the same issues going on on both sides of the ball. It will be a battle to see who the real team is. One will walk away feeling some hope for the rest of the season. The other will be entering desperation mode. Of course, the Texans have been there on more than one occasion. Maybe they work best in desperation mode. The Numbers Texans Colts Rushing Yards 25th 16th Passing Yards 3rd 25th Rushing Yards allowed 6th 31st Passing yards allowed 26th 32nd I should point out that the Texans have a major identity crisis on their hands. They say they are a hard-nosed physical running team. Their numbers say they are a passing team. That’s a significant issue we will have to sink our teeth into as the season goes if those trends continue. Obviously, a part of that comes from playing from behind for much of the first two games. Numbers always have a context. The Colts numbers also have a context. The Chiefs and Ravens are two of the better offenses in the AFC, so either the Colts are bad or they just look bad. This Sunday will tell the tale on both accounts. So, let’s take a look at what each team will try to do to each other. What will the Colts offense do? Jonathan “Zachary” Taylor is one of the best five backs in football year in a year out. He doesn’t get the press that those other guys get primarily because he doesn’t show up in prime time nearly as much as those other backs. Plus, to call Daniel Jones a part of the middle class of quarterbacks is doing a whole lot of heavy lifting. Jones can be effective with his feet and when used in concert with Taylor gives the Colts one of the most dynamic rushing attacks in the NFL. Jones is facing the same issue this week that Stroud faced last week. He will not have Alex Pierce, so there will be limited targets. Ty Warren is a weapon to be sure and one to watch in the play action game and on run pass options. The Colts will be successful if they can stay ahead of the chains. If not, it could be a long day for Jones. What will the Colts defense do to the Texans? The Texans do not have a back the caliber of Derrick Henry or Kenneth Walker. David Montgomery has spent most of his career as a complimentary back. He has been one of the better ones, but he is not capable of carrying a team on his own. This is particularly true if that team struggles up front. So, if you shut down Montgomery and Woody Marks like the Bengals did and the Texans offense starts to look really ordinary really fast. Of course, they have also struggled against the pass, but Stroud is not Lamar Jackson or Patrick Mahomes. So, there is some hope on their end. What will the Texans offense do to the Colts? Here we go again. There is what they want to do and what they actually can do. The best thing a football team can do is lean into what they do well. Right now, the Texans have been effectively passing the football. At press time, Nico Collins’ status is still unknown. He has torched the Colts in the past, so we could probably start there if he is able to play. If he isn’t then Nick Caley will need to be creative. It might start by admitting that what is left over is not what we would call traditional playmakers. Again, the best teams are the teams that acknowledge what is and then lean into what is. We can hope for a hard-nosed rushing attack that takes pressure off of Stroud. Hope might be all we have at this point. One thing is for sure, if you can’t run on the Colts then you probably can’t run on anyone. What will the Texans defense do to the Colts? Like with the Colts, the Texans pass defense looks bad, but anyone can look bad against Josh Allen and Joe Burrow. What you are is made up of who you are in a majority of your data points. That is done over the course of 17 weeks and the playoffs. If Daniel Jones torches them then we know we have a problem. So, the key is slowing down Taylor. That will be easier said than done because he is likely the best back they have faced to this point in the season. If they can keep the Colts behind the sticks then they win the game. Period.

title: Colts just proved why the NFL stands for the “No Fun League”
summary: The NFL loves money. They do anything and everything to get as much of it as possible. Stream the season on 29 different platforms? No problem. Span the globe and play in 10 different countries? You bet. They love it so much that they are willing to fine players like Indianapolis Colts’ Matt Goncalves $9K […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - SEPTEMBER 20: Tyler Warren #84 of the Indianapolis Colts celebrates a touchdown with Matt Goncalves #71 in the first quarter of an NFL game between the Indianapolis Colts and Kansas City Chiefs on Sep 20, 2026 at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The NFL loves money. They do anything and everything to get as much of it as possible. Stream the season on 29 different platforms? No problem. Span the globe and play in 10 different countries? You bet. They love it so much that they are willing to fine players like Indianapolis Colts’ Matt Goncalves $9K for his celebration against the Chiefs. It’s a matter that is out of hand. What was Goncalves’ offense? Surely he must have gestured towards the other team in a crude manner, or maybe he inappropriately engaged fans on the sideline. Nope. After receiving the ball on a Tyler Warren touchdown, Goncalves acted like he was taking a drink. It was labeled as an “offensive demonstration”. More: Colts guard Matt Goncalves also was fined $8,847 for engaging Sunday night in what the NFL called an offensive demonstration. “Your imitation of chugging a beer constituted an offensive demonstration…in poor taste.” After Tyler Warren scored, he gave the football to… pic.twitter.com/7y50i79uXt — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) September 24, 2026 Mind you, this is the same league that promotes adult beverages every five seconds on their commercial breaks. The same league that has official tailgate and pregame areas sponsored by these brands. A league that sells a copious amount in the stadium and has designated areas in the stadium named after these companies has the gall to call this offensive. If the ad running on your television during an NFL game isn’t for an adult beverage, it’s for a betting site. If the ad isn’t for a betting site, it’s for an adult beverage. Taunting and lewd gestures towards other players and fans are acceptable as fineable offenses. Heck, even fining players $9K like the league did Goncalves is ok too, if the NFL is willing to uproot its current business model. This type of culture has permeated the NFL so much that I wouldn’t have been surprised to see that celebration officially sponsored by one of these companies. That’s how often fans are hit with it. The “No Fun League” strikes again. Young, impressionable children can’t see that type of celebration on television while their parent is building a can tower next to them on the table during the broadcast. They are blasted on repeat by ads and in person sponsorships, but when a player chugs a drink, which could have been literally anything, that is a step too far. Give me a break.

title: Colts Week 2 Film Analysis: Painful Performance in Primetime
summary: The Indianapolis Colts are 0-2. First and foremost, I’m not ready to write off the season just yet. But I also will do my best to avoid sugarcoating what we’ve seen so far. For a team that is this desperate to get over the hump and sneak into the playoffs, it’s never encouraging when you […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - SEPTEMBER 20: Indianapolis Colts defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo on the sidelines during an NFL game between the Indianapolis Colts and Kansas City Chiefs on Sep 20, 2026 at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts are 0-2. First and foremost, I’m not ready to write off the season just yet. But I also will do my best to avoid sugarcoating what we’ve seen so far. For a team that is this desperate to get over the hump and sneak into the playoffs, it’s never encouraging when you give up 1000 yards to two QBs that you will certainly see in the playoffs. But what I think is quietly encouraging is that the offense had a bounce back game and put up 30 points in one of the most vaunted stages in the sport: Primetime in Arrowhead. Let’s start with Daniel Jones because I thought outside of a brutal INT, he was tremendous. As great as Daniel Jones was in the 2H, this is a bad decision. Nice disguise, but looks like it could be Ring #14 2-Man with rolled safety help to Pierce Seems like a predetermined throw bc this route is dead vs. this look. Also fair to say Allen is soft at the catchpoint pic.twitter.com/t83Uiq6LZM — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) September 21, 2026 The Chiefs do a great job of rotating safeties here to disguise a version of 2-man. Ring is a coverage in the Vic Fangio system that is a way to roll coverage to a dangerous receiver while playing 2 man. Essentially it’s man coverage across the board, but with a Cover 6 shell on top of it. You can see them roll their coverage toward Alec Pierce. In 2-man, corners are going to play with heavy inside leverage, because that’s where the big play is waiting to happen. The corner here isn’t trying to disguise anything. Keenan is running an in-breaking route vs. heavy inside leverage. That route is dead unless you’re prime Davante Adams. Hot off a free runner in the A-Gap on 3rd & 4 Wow. pic.twitter.com/swMnFIWyRL — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) September 21, 2026 The Colts got to Tosser (two slants or double slants) to beat a lot of Spags third down pressure looks. It’s as simple as it gets on a chalkboard, but very difficult to execute. The golden rule of pass protection is to never let any free runners through the A and B gaps— and Spags gets it done all the time. Daniel Jones had to throw around free runners in the throwing window all night and he did it. The ball placement isn’t going to be perfect, but completing it all that matters on third down. Daniel Jones: The QB everyone says sucks and has no arm. A dime in OT when it mattered most. pic.twitter.com/QOjGjhoFxO — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) September 21, 2026 This was the play I was most impressed with. When the Colts got the ball in OT, Jones uncorked a big post route to Laquon Treadwell and completely flipped the field. A lot of people have said this ball is underthrown, and while I will concede that it is, only slightly. It’s a great ball that doesn’t give the DB a chance to make a play on it. 2nd & 11 Run in OT I don't like the decision, but the look is absolutely there to run Dart (Tackle Power) Right side of the line just completely whiffs and it kills the drive. pic.twitter.com/PhL4XIgf2x — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) September 21, 2026 I want to get to the defense but it’s only right that I talk about the end of the game here. I did not like the decision to run the ball at the end of the game, but the look is absolutely there. As for the 4th&8? I don’t hate the decision to kick it, though maybe I’m on an island on that. If they didn’t get the look they wanted, then why do it? I think it’s pretty delusional to assume that Treadwell or Keenan Allen were going to win a matchup on the outside with that down and distance. So would you rather lose the game there, or kick the FG and see what happens. I know it’s Mahomes. I know the defense was playing terrible. But if you go for it on 4th&8 you’re basically telling everyone on your defense you have zero faith in them. How is that supposed to help them ever turn this thing around? It never will. Tampa 2 and almost positive Cam Taylor-Britt has no idea what he's looking at and gives up a massive gain. Should be the deep half player here and be able to make a play on this post from Thorton pic.twitter.com/QULZZCRiNV — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) September 21, 2026 The Colts get to a Non Traditional Tampa from a mugged up alignment. This post route from Thorton should never be available. Never! But since Cam Taylor-Britt did not get to his zone on the other half, it’s a massive play. If anything Thorton could have walked right in if it wasn’t for Carlies forcing Mahomes to layer this throw over the top. The Colts will go nowhere with defense like this. Chiefs put Walker at 2-Weak in Empty and it's an easy pitch and catch with nobody with proper leverage to make a tackle. pic.twitter.com/OdsHsicYIe — Colts Film Room (@ColtsFilmRoom) September 21, 2026 The Colts are in Drop 8 coverage here vs. Empty. But nobody is aligned properly because nobody is outside leveraged on Walker. It’s an easy pitch and catch to setup a touchdown. This is bad defense! BOTTOM LINE The Colts still have time to turn their season around, but they are running out of time to fix their defense. The offense did their part after being punched in the mouth vs. Baltimore. The defense did not. 1000 yards in two weeks is simply unacceptable. My biggest takeaway is that Shane Steichen coached his ass off, until the final sequence. Without Alec Pierce it’s very difficult to go blow-for-blow with Mahomes and Walker (especially when your defense is playing that poorly). But how many games, and really seasons, in the NFL can you coach where you get outplayed in the 4th quarter? We’ll see how the loss of Pierce ultimately affects this offense long term, but I do think the Colts are going to have to be more creative in the run game. Teams should rightfully sell out vs. the run, and until the Colts punish them for doing that, it’s going to be tough sledding. Defensively, the pressure has to be at an all-time high. Under no circumstances can the Colts defense look that bad again. There’s never perfect comparison in the NFL, but in 2024 the Gus Bradley defense had a very rough start to the season, but even they eventually settled in during Week 3. I don’t think you can justify having an $100M secondary and look even worse than the defense that you eventually decided you had to replace.

title: Jaguars vs. Patriots: Matchup History Through the Decades
summary: After a crushing loss on the road, the Jaguars are back in Jacksonville this week hosting the New England Patriots. The two teams have faced off against each other 15 times, and the Patriots currently lead the series 12-3. The Jags’ only wins have happened at home, so let’s revisit the Jags defeating the Patriots […]
full_text: January 3 1999--JACKSONVILLE FLA. -- Fred Taylor scores a touchdown as the Pats fall into a hole before half time as Willie Clay chases him.Staff photo by Jim Mahoney (Photo by MediaNews Group/Boston Herald via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images After a crushing loss on the road, the Jaguars are back in Jacksonville this week hosting the New England Patriots. The two teams have faced off against each other 15 times, and the Patriots currently lead the series 12-3. The Jags’ only wins have happened at home, so let’s revisit the Jags defeating the Patriots through the decades. The 1990’s AFC Wild Card on January 3, 1999 Final score: Patriots 10 – Jaguars 25 Attendance: 71,139 Jacksonville recorded 17 first downs, 308 total net yards, and 32 minutes of possession, while New England managed 14 first downs, 206 net yards, and a 28 minute time of possession. Fred Taylor and Jimmy Smith scored touchdowns. Mark Brunell completed 14 out of 34 attempted passes for 161 yards and was sacked twice for a loss of 13 yards. Fred Taylor led the team with 162 rushing yards, and Keenan McCardell led with 72 receiving yards. Mike Hollis made the four attempted field goals. Chris Hudson had a 17-yard interception. Tony Brackens and Joel Smeenge recorded sacks on Scott Zolak for a loss of 19 yards. The 2000’s They tried. The 2010’s Week 2 on September 16, 2018 Final score: Patriots 20 – Jaguars 31 Attendance: 68,527 We all know what happened during the previous meeting between the two teams. Donte Moncrief, Keelan Cole, Austin Seferian-Jenkins, and Dede Westbrook scored touchdowns. Blake Bortles completed 29 out of 45 attempted passes for 376 yards. T.J. Yeldon led the team with 58 rushing yards, and Cole led the team with 116 receiving yards. Josh Lambo made the attempted field goal. D.J. Hayden and Dante Fowler Jr. recorded sacks on Tom Brady for a loss of 14 yards. Telvin Smith and Myles Jack both registered eight total tackles. The 2020’s Week 7 on Oct 20, 2024 Final score: Patriots 16 – Jaguars 32 Attendance: 86,651 I understand that this game was played in London, but the Jags were the designated home team, so I’m counting it. The first quarter was highlighted by Devin Lloyd sacking Drake Maye, and Jamycal Hasty scored a touchdown for the Patriots during the first drive, marking the team’s first time doing so for the season. The Pats had the lead 10-0, and despite Cam Robinson being evaluated for a concussion, the offense started heating up. First, Gabe Davis got a first down, Christian Kirk picked up twenty yards, D’Ernest Johnson got a first down, followed by Tank Bigsby with a first down. Lawrence connected with Brian Thomas Jr. in the end zone to put seven on the board. Lawrence found BTJ again for a gain of 58, then Bigsby ran it in to give the Jaguars the lead. Eight minutes later, Parker Washington returns the punt for 96 yards, and Lawrence hits BTJ for the two-point conversion. Cam Little brings the score to 25-10 during the third quarter. The Patriots score at the top of the fourth, but Bigsby strikes back with another touchdown with 1:45 left in the game. title: Will the Chiefs’ offense see the best of Xavier Worthy soon?
summary: I loved the pick. Unabashedly loved it. “He’s fast, he’s productive, and he’s going to add the element this offense has been missing.” That was my initial impression when the Kansas City Chiefs drafted wide receiver Xavier Worthy in the first round. That was not necessarily the consensus. Some national analysts panned the selection because […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images I loved the pick. Unabashedly loved it. “He’s fast, he’s productive, and he’s going to add the element this offense has been missing.” That was my initial impression when the Kansas City Chiefs drafted wide receiver Xavier Worthy in the first round. That was not necessarily the consensus. Some national analysts panned the selection because he was more of the same for the Chiefs’ receiver room, with too many small, gadget-type receivers. I rejected the notion. This would be different. Andy Reid selected him in the first round for a reason. He clearly had a plan. That appeared to be the case, at least in year one. After a slow start — 20 receptions in his first 9 games — Worthy was thrust into action in the second half of his rookie year. He became the team’s leading receiver in the second half of the season after Rashee Rice went down to injury. Worthy racked up nearly 400 yards in his final seven regular-season games. That seemed to offer a glimpse of what was to come. Xavier Worthy is not your typical Combine track star. He’s a real deal receiver with outlier speed. https://t.co/iHaM7FwmEp — Brandon Kiley (@BKSportsTalk) August 17, 2024 But then he ran into tight end Travis Kelce on a crossing route in the first game of the 2025 season, and everything changed. His shoulder became an issue. He missed a couple of games. An ankle injury also held him back. He finished the 2025 campaign with barely 500 receiving yards and only one touchdown. It was a frustrating season, marred by injury. The Chiefs spent the offseason telling anyone who would listen that this year would be different. Worthy would be healthy, and we would see a return to the player we watched in the second half of the 2024 campaign. I was optimistic. This would be the year he proved the doubters wrong, once and for all. I’m still waiting for that to happen. Worthy doesn’t look like the confident player he was in the second half of his rookie year. He’s shying away from contact. He’s not strong at the catch point. He’s not beating defenders to the corner. I’m struggling to understand how to use a player who doesn’t win deep, doesn’t play with the physicality needed to win across the middle, and can’t break tackles to win after the catch. What’s the proper usage for such a wide receiver? That seems to be the question the Chiefs are asking, too. I hope the Chiefs find that answer sooner rather than later. This offense looks like a legitimate contender. Running back Kenneth Walker has added an explosive element the Chiefs have been lacking for years. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes looks as confident as he has in his supporting cast since 2022. Kelce is rejuvenated. Wideout Tyquan Thornton is a legitimate deep threat. Receiver Rashee Rice is working his way back to prime form. If Worthy can return to his second-half 2024 form, this group is cooking with gas. Can he get back to that form, though? That remains to be seen. The history of first-round wide receivers who have produced like Worthy through two-plus seasons is less than ideal. 60 wide receivers were selected in the first round between 2011 & 2025. Worthy ranks 32nd among them in receptions, 38th in receiving yards and 33rd in receiving touchdowns through his first 33 games. By volume, none of those statistics are particularly alarming. The efficiency is where the trends are far more worrisome. Worthy is targeted at roughly the average rate among the 60 wide receivers selected in the first round over the past 15 years, but he’s produced fewer yards per target than nearly any other receiver on the list. His 6.6 yards per target is through his first 33 career regular season games ranks 51st among that group. The only other first-round wide receivers over that stretch to average fewer than 7 yards per reception through 33 career regular season games are Kevin White, Garrett Wilson, Josh Doctson, A.J. Jenkins, Nelson Agholor, John Ross, Kadarius Toney, Jalen Reagor, Xavier Leggette, Breshad Perriman, Cordarreelle Patterson, Tavon Austin, N’Keal Harry, Laquon Treadwell, Corey Coleman and Jonathan Baldwin. Uh oh. That’s not a group you want to be included in. It’s a who’s who of wide receiver busts over the past decade-plus. It’s especially worrisome that Worthy is producing like this with a future Hall of Fame coach and quarterback. Most receivers who overcame poor early-career efficiency (Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Malik Nabers, and Garrett Wilson) were dealing with a poorly designed offensive scheme, a below-average quarterback situation, or both. That excuse or explanation doesn’t apply to Worthy. The only reason I’m holding out hope my priors are correct on Worthy is the injuries. Maybe the first couple of weeks are a blip on the radar. Maybe he’ll have a second half similar to his rookie year. Maybe he’s still tentative after playing through so many ailments last season, and it’ll just take time to get himself right. Maybe. Hopefully. The Chiefs offense doesn’t need Worthy to step up the way it once did. But it sure would be nice if he could. I’m still holding out hope, but patience is running thin.
author: Brandon Kiley

title: Chiefs pass rush must improve after quiet Colts game
summary: A pair of seemingly contradictory defensive performances for the Kansas City Chiefs have left fans pondering how much trust to put in the unit. Kansas City opened the season with a dominant 31-10 beatdown of the Denver Broncos, sacking quarterback Bo Nix four times and holding the reigning AFC West champions to just 176 total […]
full_text: (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images A pair of seemingly contradictory defensive performances for the Kansas City Chiefs have left fans pondering how much trust to put in the unit. Kansas City opened the season with a dominant 31-10 beatdown of the Denver Broncos , sacking quarterback Bo Nix four times and holding the reigning AFC West champions to just 176 total yards. A week later, however, the Chiefs sweated 70 full minutes for a 33-30 overtime victory over the Indianapolis Colts . The Colts gained 329 yards against Kansas City. Despite multiple close calls, quarterback Daniel Jones played five quarters without being sacked. Speaking before Thursday’s practice, defensive line coach Joe Cullen credited the Indianapolis offensive line for thwarting the Chiefs’ pass rush. “They’re a physical offensive line,” observed Cullen. “They’ve always had a good offensive line. And one of the things we stressed is we got to get them in those down and distances like we had a third-and-16. [Defensive end George Karlaftis] made a great play on the screen… We had a third-and-11, and George jumped the gun, went offside. So now you’re down to third-and-6, and the ball gets out a little quicker. But they’ve always had a decent offensive line. And I think we saved the best rush for the last one when George put him on his back, but they’re a good offensive line.” On Thursday, defensive tackle Chris Jones reiterated the importance of wins and losses over all other stats while acknowledging the need for improvement. He does see an overtime victory as an indication of the Kansas City defense’s perseverance. “I think the most important thing that matters is wins and losses,” said Jones. “We were able to pull through, but we were also able to learn a lot about this team — the resiliency of the team and the core strength of the team. But there are still areas for improvement.” One area for improvement will be preventing quick passes — as Jones was able to seemingly get off for completions any time the Chiefs’ pass rush threatened him. Cullen knows it is a problem, but it will take the whole defense to prevent a repeat performance by opposing quarterbacks. “We’ve had some consistent pressure,” remarked the coach, “and it’s not always going to be a sack, but we’ve put pressure on the quarterback in a lot of different ways. But the coverage in the back end and the rush go hand in hand. Those are the things that when they’re tied in together, you’ve got to get home. [When] the quarterback’s patting that ball for over three seconds, you’ve got to get home. “Ball gets out quick —you may have to change your rush and get your hand up to knock a slant down. The slant’s getting out in 2.2 seconds. When you make the quarterback clutch it, you got to get home, and when he doesn’t, and he’s getting it out quick, we got to get our hands up and helping the slant game.” The Chiefs’ defense will next be tested on Sunday in South Florida against the Miami Dolphins . Cullen expects a well-prepared squad from new head coach Jeff Hafley. The Chiefs also have respect for possibly the league’s fastest running back, De’Von Achane, and quarterback Malik Willis — who took Kansas City to overtime in 2022 while with the Tennessee Titans . “We’re excited,” Cullen declared. “A great opportunity going on the road for the first time down to Miami, and Coach Hafley’s building that program, and they’ve got some really skilled athletes on offense. [Achane] — No. 28 —is as good a back as there is. He’s had 5.7 [yards] to carry last year. We played Malik Willis when he was at Tennessee in the game here. So great athletes, and we’ll have our hands full, but we’re excited and looking forward to the challenge.”
author: Jared Sapp

title: It wasn’t lost on Chiefs’ defense that they didn’t play well in Week 2
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs are 2-0. That’s all that really matters as the team looks ahead to three straight games against AFC opponents, two of them division rivals. That said, Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo isn’t ignorant of the team allowing 30 points, 329 total yards, and 24 first downs in the overtime victory. In […]
full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs are 2-0. That’s all that really matters as the team looks ahead to three straight games against AFC opponents, two of them division rivals. That said, Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo isn’t ignorant of the team allowing 30 points, 329 total yards, and 24 first downs in the overtime victory. In Week 1, Kansas City allowed just 10 points, 176 total yards and nine first downs. He talked about his unit’s performance during Thursday’s press conference. “We’re probably not as good as we were in the first week,” Spagnuolo said. “And hopefully not as bad as we were in the second. We didn’t reaffirm; we didn’t do a good job there.” The Chiefs’ defense played on a thin margin Sunday night, coming up with a red-zone stop in overtime that preserved the team’s ability to come back and claim victory. That red-zone stop came immediately after a wild, long completion that ended in a negated turnover. “I was really proud of the way they responded after the big play; that was huge,” Spags said. “That said a lot about this group and certainly (linebackers) Nick [Bolton] and Drue [Tranquill] on the inside, but it was hard not to think about all the other stuff; the reasons we were in overtime were because we kind of let the team down in certain areas.” Through two weeks, the Chiefs rank 11th in points allowed and third in total yards allowed. The unit, with inexperience and injuries to play through, already looks promising, but Week 2 represented a humbling experience. “I don’t think its lost on our guys in the defensive room that we didn’t play well,” Spags told reporters. “I don’t think we’re going to get clouded by the fact that we ended up winning it. It’s hard to win in this league. I said to them in the locker room, it wasn’t pretty as a defense, but enjoy it, because they’re really hard to come by. “When we got together on Tuesday,” Spags continued. “I think there was a feeling in there that ‘no, that’s not what we’re looking for.‘” #Chiefs DC Steve Spagnuolo assesses the play between their first two games. He adds that he was disappointed with how he called the second half of the Colts game. pic.twitter.com/7t9aBSxbH0 — Sports Radio 810 WHB (@SportsRadio810) September 24, 2026 After allowing just two third-down conversions of 12 attempts against Denver in Week 1, the Chiefs’ defense wasn’t as reliable getting off the field on those crucial snaps. The Colts converted five third downs on 12 attempts, but two failed third downs were followed by successful fourth-down conversions. “Eight out of 12 were third and six or third and five,” Spagnuolo reflected. “I would have liked to have another red-zone stop. The two runs that spit out were things that we worked on. We thought that he would try to get to the edge, and he did.” “I did a terrible job at the end of the half,” Spagnuolo went off on a tangent. “I told the guys that. I was fully disappointed in myself in what we called at the end of the half, and it led to a score. Otherwise, we might not have even been in that overtime situation.” The Chiefs have high standards for themselves in the bounceback campaign. The team is off to a good start with two wins, but coaches like Spagnuolo will not be satisfied anytime soon.
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: Rashee Rice’s big play for Chiefs in Week 2 was set up in Week 1
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs’ offense looks explosive again. After the ground game produced the big plays in Week 1, the passing game got in on the long gashes, with multiple completions for 20-plus yards. The first of the game came from wide receiver Rashee Rice, who caught a well-timed throw from quarterback Patrick Mahomes off […]
full_text: (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs ’ offense looks explosive again. After the ground game produced the big plays in Week 1, the passing game got in on the long gashes, with multiple completions for 20-plus yards. The first of the game came from wide receiver Rashee Rice, who caught a well-timed throw from quarterback Patrick Mahomes off an under-center play-action fake. The gravity of a potential handoff to running back Kenneth Walker opened up the middle of the field, and that wasn’t by accident. At the podium on Wednesday, Rice said the big play was set up by what Kansas City put on tape in Week 1. “[I] had a lot of plays where I would motion down into the line of scrimmage and block for the run game,” Rice said about the Week 1 win. “So it’s just based off that play in the following week, knowing that the team that we played last week would watch film and expect for me to go in that position and block for a running back.” A play from Week 1 and a play from Week 2 Rashee Rice talked about how the first setup the second yesteday, "knowing that the team that we played last week would watch film and expect for me to go in that position and block for a running back.” pic.twitter.com/5qjJFTaJ0o — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) September 24, 2026 This clip shows two plays: a Week 1 handoff to Walker and a Week 2 completion to Rice. Both plays present similarly, but on the second, Rice fakes the block and takes off across the field. The Indianapolis Colts defender he sets up to block is clearly fooled by the action, as are the linebackers who stepped all the way up to the line of scrimmage. It’s the result of the Chiefs’ willingness to run down the throats of a Denver Broncos defense that invited it throughout the season opener. The Colts felt more prepared to stifle Walker schematically, but Kansas City responded by turning up the dial on play-action concepts. “Our run game has been tremendous this year so far,” Rice said. “It’s going to continue to grow. I feel like, based off how we’ve been running the ball so aggressively, that it’s going to allow for defenses to have to come down and play inside the box as well as even when we have play-action plays, they’re going to have to play the run before our quarterback rolls out to throw the ball and make a play downfield.” Rice is in an especially unique position to fool defenders with the run game. Based on his listed size of 6 feet 1 inch tall and 204 pounds, he is the team’s biggest wideout and has been effective blocking defensive backs for Walker and others so far this season. It’s not the ideal skill set of the de facto No. 1 receiver on the team, but that doesn’t bother Rice. If anything, it sounds like he’s gaining an appreciation for what makes football so great: it’s the ultimate team sport. “It’s very rewarding,” Rice shared. “I kind of feel like not necessarily an O-lineman, but now I understand what it feels like to make a great block and not necessarily hear your name get called on the touchdown or anything like that, but it’s just knowing that you did your job to help the team and to progress down the field or even score a touchdown, it feels real good.”

title: Is Week 3 in Miami a trap game for the Chiefs?
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs and the Miami Dolphins appear headed in opposite directions through two weeks of the 2026 NFL season. However, don’t expect the 2-0 Chiefs to take the winless Dolphins lightly, even though Sunday’s road opponent is widely considered the NFL’s worst team. After previously taking over two losing programs in his career, […]
full_text: (Photo by Mark Brown/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs and the Miami Dolphins appear headed in opposite directions through two weeks of the 2026 NFL season. However, don’t expect the 2-0 Chiefs to take the winless Dolphins lightly, even though Sunday’s road opponent is widely considered the NFL’s worst team. After previously taking over two losing programs in his career, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid has respect for the job first-year Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley is doing. “You can see he’s doing it the right way,” observed Reid before Wednesday’s practice. “He’s got a really good staff all the way through. They’re very sound in what they do. I know that’s what he’s drilling home right now. He’s doing a nice job with that.” Quarterback Patrick Mahomes has started the season facing a pair of coaching staffs he knows well. He recognizes the challenge of facing the unknown in the first-year Dolphins staff and a roster stocked with young players. “We’ve played two great defensive coordinators these first two weeks,” the face of the league added on Wednesday. “They’re veteran coaches that have seen it all. There were definitely some changes that they’ve made from Week 1 to Week 2. We’ll continue to do that. I’m excited to see what we get this week against a young team — a hungry team — that wants to go out there and prove themselves. They’ll be flying around trying to make plays — and it’s our job to go out there and have continued success and get better and better.” For Reid’s part, he sees too many areas for improvement in what the Chiefs have done through two games to worry about the Dolphins being a trap game for his Chiefs. “I think you’ve got to focus on getting better,” the coach explained. “We have too much to worry about just getting better. There’s plenty of room for that. That’s what I focus on. I don’t worry about all the outside noise. I’ve got to get better, and the rest of the guys need to get better. That’s where we’re at.” Mahomes challenges his teammates not to forget the skepticism Kansas City faced entering the season and to keep being fueled by proving the doubters wrong. “I think more than who we’re playing,” said the star, “it’s just staying hungry. In this league, it’s week to week. One week, they’re patting you on the back. One week, they’re telling you [that] you’re terrible. I think all offseason we heard about how bad we were, and guys were super hungry and came in with that mentality. I think that’s why we’ve had the success we have these first two weeks. “How can you keep that hunger? Now that everybody is saying that we’re amazing and that we’re great — we’ve got to keep the hunger that we’ve had this entire offseason. That’s what we’re preaching. We’re nowhere near where we want to be at. We’re still so early in the season, and there’s still so much for us to learn from and so much for us to get better at. We’ve got to have that mentality week in and week out if we want to go out there and have success.” One of Reid’s areas for improvement hits home for Mahomes — scoring touchdowns instead of attempting field goals to cap off long drives. “I think as an offense,” he recalled, “we had more opportunities to score touchdowns. We kicked some field goals in the red zone, and it came down to little things like miscommunications or route depth or me not making the right read and getting to the right guy at the right time. Those are the little things you’ve got to continue to get better and better at.” “You don’t know how many of those opportunities you’re going to get when you’re in the red zone. I love kicking field goals — they’re three points — but touchdowns are so big in this league, and you want to make sure you can actually get those. So, we have to get better at that. Executing in the red zone and getting those touchdowns — that’s what wins you football games.” Mahomes is also unconcerned about falling into a trap game. The quarterback knows that some of Miami’s fellow Texas Tech alumni — including rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez — will be ready to prove themselves against the college’s most famous product. “I haven’t talked to [my teammates] about it,” Mahomes declared. “I think we’ve been so focused on just getting better and going to this next opponent and playing against a team that’s hungry and ready to play. There’re a lot of Texas Tech guys too. It gives me some more motivation to go out there and compete because I was going to watch these guys play and talking to them in the locker room. Now, they’ll be playing against me, so I know they’ll be hungry to go up against me as well.”
author: Jared Sapp

A stalled red-and-yellow passenger van — owned by a husband and wife, two Chiefs fans — was blocking the road. “Obviously, they’ve got a big van, so I was feeling bad. He was trying to push it by himself,” Gillotte told The Athletic in the locker room Wednesday. “So I was like, ‘I’ll just pull over.’” Gillotte said once he got out, he began talking to the couple. The husband’s efforts to push the van by himself had been futile, so Gillotte offered to help. He got behind the vehicle to help roll it forward. Soon after, Gillotte’s family friends joined in to get it moving faster. Two years into NFL career, receiver Jalen Royals is making his mark with Chiefs | The Kansas City Star “When he scored the touchdown, we saw the passion come out,” fellow Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice said. “He was able to scream and everybody was super excited for him.” Rice said the upbeat feeling has continued this week. “He’s talking in the meetings, smiling,” Rice said. “So, I think that’s all he needed to open up.” Kansas City Chiefs’ Most Surprising Players Through the First Two Games | Athlon Sports LT Kahlil Benson The Chiefs signed Benson as an undrafted free agent this offseason, and he’s made them look like geniuses. The former Indiana Hoosier has started at left tackle the first two weeks with Josh Simmons hurt. He’s looked like a natural at the position. No one expected Benson to even make the roster, much less protect Mahomes’ blind side in Week 1. He’s been a revelation through the first two weeks. Even when Simmons gets healthy, Benson should keep his starting left tackle job. George Karlaftis warns younger teammates before matchup with Dolphins | Chiefs Wire “They (Dolphins) haven’t gotten a win yet, so it’s their home opener,” said Karlaftis. “They’re going to be hungry. They’re motivated. They’re a young team. They got a new head coach. They’re going to be as motivated as ever to get their first win of the season, and it’s going to be on us to try to make sure that doesn’t happen.” Miami has revamped its roster and coaching staff this season, entering a rebuilding phase. As a veteran in the Chiefs locker room, Karlaftis understands the potential of a young team trying for an early-season upset. Chiefs’ 2025 2nd-Round Pick Could Make Season Debut After Bye Week | Heavy Sports While speaking to the media on Wednesday, coach Andy Reid was asked about the possibility of defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott making his season debut after the Chiefs’ Week 5 bye week. “Potentially, yeah,” Reid said about Norman-Lott returning after the bye week. “We’ll see where he’s at. He’s doing more right now, which is a positive.” Chiefs Backing Xavier Worthy Despite Early Struggles: ‘He’ll Be Fine’ | Sports Illustrated Is that presenting Kansas City with cause for concern that Worthy can’t be the player it planned for? Speaking to the media on Wednesday, head coach Andy Reid turned the volume down several notches by implying that Worthy is close to breaking through. “You know, he had an opportunity for that big catch — it was close, man,” Reid said. “You’re probably not asking that one [if he catches it]. He’s fine. He’s just got to keep rolling here. He’s coming off the shoulder part of it and working through all that. He’ll be fine as we go.” Around the NFL Seahawks’ Macdonald apologizes to Broncos’ Payton for comments | ESPN “It’s something that I didn’t intend for public use,” Macdonald said. “But I felt like it was the most appropriate thing to reach out to Sean and really just apologize to him for having that end up be public where it wasn’t meant to. It’s something that they have to deal with in real time. It wasn’t really on their end. So, that’s where you’re really like, ‘Crap.’ But it’s a lesson learned, honestly.” Payton said Macdonald called him Tuesday night. “He and I are good,” Payton said after Wednesday’s practice. “Lord knows I’ve been in his position, you know, you’re talking about something. The story is about three years ago.” Giants QB Jaxson Dart to undergo season-ending knee surgery | NFL.com However, that will not prevent the QB from needing surgery. ESPN added that Dart suffered damage to his left MCL, PCL and meniscus, with the latter being the main issue. Giants head coach John Harbaugh confirmed on Wednesday afternoon Dart will undergo season-ending surgery. Harbaugh, who did not specify when the surgery would take place, did leave the door open for Dart to return in the postseason. The timeline for a meniscus repair is four to six months, Garafolo noted. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride The Chiefs are chasing a significant mark of 3-0 to start this season RotoWire.com has a 10-year study (since 2016) of NFL teams starting 3-0; 73% of teams make the postseason and one in five reach the Super Bowl. The 45-team sample of 3-0 starts also shows that 38% of such teams reach the Divisional Round and 31% play in that year’s conference championship game.
