title: 5Qs, 5As with Mile High Report: Rams urged to test Broncos’ iffy run defense
summary: The Los Angeles Rams look to continue building momentum as they hit the road again, this time against the Denver Broncos on Sunday night. According to FanDuel Sportsbook, the Rams are a 2.5-point favorite in the Mile High City against the reigning AFC runner-up. Including the playoffs, the Broncos have gone 26-13 under veteran head […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Bhayshul Tuten #33 of the Jacksonville Jaguars runs the ball during the third quarter of a game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams look to continue building momentum as they hit the road again, this time against the Denver Broncos on Sunday night. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Rams are a 2.5-point favorite in the Mile High City against the reigning AFC runner-up. Including the playoffs, the Broncos have gone 26-13 under veteran head coach Sean Payton. Denver, like LA, is a Super Bowl hopeful. Ahead of this weekend’s primetime showdown, I spoke with Ian St. Clair of Mile High Report to get more intel on the Broncos. Q – The Broncos have struggled mightily on offense in the first two games. Denver scored 10 points against the Chiefs in Week 1 and started slowly versus the Jaguars before scoring 17 unanswered points to secure the win. What is your initial impression of offensive coordinator Davis Webb, and what areas must the unit improve on moving forward? A – Through the first six quarters, Bo Nix and the offense did struggle. However, it finally clicked in the second half. “Finally,” like it’s been half of the season. But what the Broncos offense showed against a good team and defense is an appetizer of what the unit can become. If Denver converts the two first-half trips to the red zone into touchdowns, the discussion changes. That’s where the focus should be – on finishing drives. That also takes care of the other issue – starting faster offensively. Dating back to last season, the Broncos offense doesn’t get going until the second half. That must change, and finishing drives is the first step. Denver also must stick with the running game. We saw it in the second half against the Jaguars, but consistently and effectively running the ball sets up the rest of the offense. As for Webb, he got into a rhythm in the second half and called a great game. Take that to Sunday night, build off it, and find ways to improve the offense even more. Webb is a bright young mind and he had some struggles to start. Some of it was execution, but just like life, he’ll need to take the failures and successes together. He has another big test this Sunday. Q – Speaking of offense, new wide receiver Jaylen Waddle had a great game against Jacksonville, catching eight passes for 138 yards. How are you enjoying the Waddle-Bo Nix connection two games in? A – What will make me enjoy it even more is if that type of playmaking becomes consistent, thus making the offense harder to defend. It’ll force defenses to shift coverages to ensure Waddle is the focal point. That then opens the ability to utilize Courtland Sutton, Marvin Mims (when healthy), Pat Bryant, Troy Franklin and Evan Engram. After Sunday, I’m enjoying the Nix-Waddle connection quite a bit, but I want to see how Denver expands it. Q – The Broncos have had one of the NFL’s best defenses in the last two seasons under defensive coordinator Vance Joseph. If you’re Sean McVay, what types of plays should you be calling to keep Joseph’s unit on its toes on Sunday night? A – Test the Denver rush defense. Even dating back to the playoffs last year, the Broncos struggled to stop the run. The biggest issue against Kenneth Walker III and the Chiefs is that Denver couldn’t tackle. The tackling was much better for the Broncos against Jacksonville, but run Kyren Williams and Blake Corum on Sunday night. That allows McVay to use the heavy offensive sets that he typically likes to run, especially the plays with three tight ends. Then he can have Matthew Stafford use those tight ends in the passing game. That’s the other thing Denver struggles with – covering tight ends. Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad, in a word, are not very good. So force the two linebackers into coverage and the Rams will likely have success. Q – Denver advanced to the AFC Championship last season and likely would’ve advanced to the Super Bowl had Nix stayed healthy. The team has certainly come a long way from the Nathaniel Hackett and Russell Wilson days, so what are your realistic expectations for the Broncos this season? A – Payton, Nix and this Denver team should compete for the Super Bowl again. To be honest, this could be the Super Bowl matchup. It is just Week 3, but these two teams could meet again on Valentine’s Day in LA. And both teams have that expectation. There’s no doubt the opener on Monday Night Football in KC was startling, but similar to the Rams, the Broncos struggle in September. The team we saw in Denver in the second half against a good Jaguars team is the team that will make it a contender. Q – What is one question that you have for Rams fans? A – How do fans feel about the “Super Team” moniker and all that comes with it?

title: Are Matthew Stafford and Rams’ passing game Super Bowl ready?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams’ passing game has been buck average so far in 2026. They are middle of the pack in several key metrics from Pro Football Focus (PFF): There are some silver linings. LA is still explosive through the air. They need to become more efficient on a play-by-play basis. The Rams aren’t allowing […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams blows a kiss after defeating the New York Giants in the game at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams’ passing game has been buck average so far in 2026. They are middle of the pack in several key metrics from Pro Football Focus (PFF): Success rate: 48.4% (17th) Completion rate: 66.1% (17th) Passer rating: 100.60 (12th) There are some silver linings. LA is still explosive through the air. They need to become more efficient on a play-by-play basis. Yards per attempt: 8.4 (7th) Explosive pass rate: 18.6% (8th) Pressure rate over expectation: -3.2% (9th) Pressure rate: 30.6% (8th) The Rams aren’t allowing much in the way of pressure. They’re top 10 in the two key metrics. Stafford is getting rid of the ball quickly on average—that helps. Somehow LA is still towards the top in average depth of target. Those two metrics usually correlate inversely. It’s impressive to have it both ways. In terms of the Rams’ leading man, Matthew Stafford individually ranks as PFF’s 22nd quarterback in offensive grade. The veteran has earned a positive grade on 12.4% of his plays, which puts him 30th of the 41 quarterbacks to drop back so far this season. Negative plays comprise 8.8% of his total and that is good for 20th of 41. Matthew Stafford with a dart to Davante Adams for 64-yard 🎯 📺 @ESPNNFL | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/i5zW3ehUU1 — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) September 22, 2026 In defense of Stafford, both he and the Rams offense overall were inept in Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers. LA was able to bounce back in a big way in their encore performance against the New York Giants. The real test comes in the next three weeks versus the Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles, and Buffalo Bills. The Denver and Philly defenses are formidable. The Rams will need to outscore the Bills in Week 5. There is no sense in prematurely saying this offense is in trouble or not as good as last year. It’s still early. A rough opening performance is skewing numbers and a larger sample size is required. Still, there are some concerning passing game trends for the Rams that cannot be ignored. We must continue to check in and track these metrics in order to gauge whether improvement exists or is being sustained. Stafford INT 🚨 Giants get the ball right back (via: @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/wZ3EuQyQP2 — B/R Gridiron (@brgridiron) September 22, 2026 These are the parts of Stafford’s game I would be concerned about moving forward: Turnover-worthy play rate: 4.8% (3.3% in 2025) Big-time throw rate: 3.3% (7.7% in 2025) Big-time throw to turnover-worthy ratio: 0.67 (2.23 in 2025) Attempts 20+ yards: 3/7 for 114 yards, 0 TD, 2 INT, 2 BTT, 2 TWP, 55.2 pass grade Attempts 10-19 yards: 10/16 for 184 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT, 0 BTT, 1 TWP, 73.8 pass grade Attempts 0-9 yards: 19/24 for 144 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT, 0 BTT, 0 TWP, 59.7 pass grade Sean McVay and Stafford are going to live and die by the deep ball. So far they have mostly died when targeting this area of the field. This is an area of the offense that needs immediate improvement, although it could in part be a defect of the receiving group. LA’s pass catchers lack long speed in the aggregate. They could struggle in this facet all season unless someone like Terrance Ferguson steps up consistently. LA’s bread and butter will always be over the middle of the field. It’s encouraging to see positive and consistent production in this area. The offense won’t function without it. But more concerning is Stafford’s performance in the short area of the field. Defenses in 2026 will prioritize taking away the explosive play. They want to force opposing quarterbacks to remain patient and take the underneath pass. Whether the Rams and Stafford can remain disciplined remains to be seen—sometimes their aggressiveness gets the best of them. Matthew Stafford connects with Kyren Williams for the TD Rams lead 14-0 (via: @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/k0NSIeQNLs — B/R Gridiron (@brgridiron) September 22, 2026 Out of 24 throws inside ten yards, the Rams have only gained six first downs. This also underscores their recent struggles on third and fourth down. Their best bet is to pick up a new set of downs on the ground, and that makes them one dimensional. Of course, LA played their second game without star receiver Puka Nacua. It’s uncertain whether Nacua will return in Week 3 . He’s battling a unique injury that could threaten his longer term health if not properly managed. We will continue to check in on these metrics for Stafford and the Rams in the season’s early going. The offense hasn’t been good enough through two weeks in order to offset the loss of Myles Garrett and a slower start on defense. Can Stafford and the Rams rise to the occasion to keep pace with the Broncos, Eagles, and Bills in the coming weeks?

title: Puka Nacua might miss Week 3 for Rams
summary: Puka Nacua was hurt throughout the offseason, and he played in Week 1, but missed Week 2 and now he might miss Week 3. Sean McVay says the injury shouldn’t be long-term, but it sure seems long-term. It’s been nagging the player for at least a month. I didn’t want to put this in the […]
full_text: Puka Nacua was hurt throughout the offseason, and he played in Week 1, but missed Week 2 and now he might miss Week 3. Sean McVay says the injury shouldn’t be long-term, but it sure seems long-term. It’s been nagging the player for at least a month. I didn’t want to put this in the headline, but any chance the Rams trade Nacua? Or, when will he suit up again for the Rams? This injury is likely hurting his shot at the big extension with L.A. that he is looking for. The Nacua situation is something to monitor. The team will also see if Myles Garrett can make his return by Week 5. The Rams are 1-1, which is better than 0-2, but they’ve got some problems. 15 games to go. McVay says Nacua’s injury not ‘long-term’ concern, but Rams being cautious (espn.com) “LOS ANGELES — Rams coach Sean McVay said he’s not sure whether Puka Nacua will play in Week 3, but the team is not worried that the wide receiver’s injury will be “any sort of long-term threat.” Nacua did not play Monday night with what was listed as a hip injury on the injury report, but McVay later clarified that Nacua was dealing with “a little bit of soreness” in his groin. McVay said Nacua does not have a hernia, but the team is being cautious with the injury. “When you’re a skill player and you’re really trying to hit high-speed yards and really open up and you feel just … it’s like some of the things that can almost be like pre-hernia is kind of what he’s feeling,” McVay said. “And so you err on the side of caution. Usually time is the best thing that allows that thing to heal. And then once you get to a certain point, then I think you feel pretty good moving forward.” Rams House, make some room for the SB Nation app! They want to make sure they are cautious with him, so [I’d] be surprised if he goes.” Highest-graded player of the Week: CB Trent McDuffie, Los Angeles Rams (pff.com) “The pregame focus on Monday Night Football was understandably on Aaron Donald ’s return to the Los Angeles Rams , but by the end of the night, it was one of the team’s newest additions who had delivered the best performance of any NFL defender in Week 2. The Rams traded for cornerback Trent McDuffie from the Kansas City Chiefs to get performances exactly like this one, and the 2022 first-round pick delivered, earning a 94.0 PFF coverage grade. McDuffie was targeted five times against the New York Giants and didn’t allow a single reception, coming away with three pass breakups and an interception. Let’s take a look at each target.“ Rams vs. Broncos Fantasy Football Worksheet, Week 3 (sharpfootballanalysis) “After a down Week 1, Stafford bounced back on Monday night, completing 22 of 31 passes (71%) for 327 yards (10.5 Y/A), 4 touchdowns, and an interception. After the Rams threw 12.3% below expectations in Week 1 (31st), they threw 8.8% over expectations (7th) against a depleted Giants defense. On throws of 10 or more yards downfield, Stafford was 10 for 13 for 224 yards (17.2 Y/A) with 3 touchdowns. That was also without Puka Nacua available. Stafford will look to keep things rolling against a strong Denver defense.“ Rams’ disappointing start on special teams isn’t cause for alarm just yet (ramblinfan) “Los Angeles Rams fans have little patience for poor special teams play. And so far, that patience has worn thin. Coverage continues to struggle. Ethan Evans’ punts have been nothing to brag about. And sure-footed kicker Harrison Mevis has missed his only field goal attempt. And fans are starting to sound off: They have a point. While data from two games is hardly conclusive, past disappointing trends are not turning in a positive direction. Coverage units have shown little to no improvement. The return game has been suspect. Mevis missed his kick.“ Rams star trolls Giants with savage meme after injuring Jaxson Dart (nypost) “Los Angeles Rams star linebacker Byron Young was one half of the tandem that injured New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart on Monday night. Young was initially apologetic about hurting Dart, saying in an Instagram post that he would, “Never play to hurt anybody. I pray for a healthy recovery 🙏🏾”. But that didn’t stop Young from trolling the Giants on social media soon after his apology to Dart. The Rams’ Instagram account posted a photo of Young doing his sack celebration, where he pretends to hang up a phone with his hand. The account added a meme of a scared-looking dog pretending to answer a phone while wearing a Giants hat.“ LA Rams Get Bad News on Super Bowl Champion Quarterback (sports.yahoo) “Rams Pro Bowler Byron Young and bookend outside linebacker Josaiah Stewart combined on a hit that left New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart out for the 2026 season. In need of veteran depth, the Giants are expect to at least explore Garoppolo as an option. “Jimmy Garropolo is still out there,” NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo said on “Big Day with Peter Schrager” on September 23. “The Rams wanted him back, by the way. He did consider retirement at one point. He has been working out. Retirement’s not the way he’d want to go. He would go for the right situation. My feel is that this would be one of the right situations for Jimmy Garopppolo here. So, would not be surprised if there’s some discussion regarding him.” NFL QB rankings, Week 3: Patrick Mahomes, Dak Prescott, Matthew Stafford heating up (nfl.com) “ 2026 stats: 2 games | 66.1 pct | 482 pass yds | 8.6 ypa | 4 pass TDs | 2 INTs | -2 rush yds | 0 rush TDs | 0 fumbles” Giants’ Jameis Winston returns to starting QB role after Jaxson Dart injury: ‘This is what I dream of’ (nfl.com) “It’s a product of unfortunate circumstances — usual starter Jaxson Dart suffered a knee injury that will require surgery — but there’s little time to waste on acknowledging misfortune. After being called into emergency action on Monday night in Los Angeles, Winston has a game to prepare for. “This is what I’ve always dreamed of, to be a starting quarterback,” Winston told reporters Wednesday ahead of New York’s Week 3 matchup with Tennessee. “Obviously, my respects and gratitude is just going to be with Jaxson, but at the same time, this is what I dream of. I dream of being what I am right now and executing at a high level.” Winston certainly didn’t execute at a high level when he replaced the injured Dart on Monday night, completing 11 of 27 passes for 111 yards and an interception in the 28-6 defeat. He’s been here before, though, starting in place of Dart for two games last season that both ended in one-score losses.“ NFC West Roundup Week 2: 49ers and Seahawks Set the Pace at 2-0 (sports.yahoo) “Two weeks into the 2026 NFL season, a clear top tier is already beginning to form in the NFC West. The San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks both wrapped up commanding Week 2 victories to preserve undefeated records, while the Los Angeles Rams bounced back in a major way and the Arizona Cardinals stumbled on their home turf. Here is how the NFC West stacks up following an action-packed Week 2: NFC West Standings After Week 2” Comment of the Day: “Falcons @ Packers : 27-10 Chargers @ Bills :…

title: Rams vs. Broncos: Matthew Stafford is far superior to Bo Nix
summary: OFFENSE: RAMS The Rams offense finally showed its potential in a 28-6 win over the Giants on MNF in Week 2. Matthew Stafford thew 4 touchdowns, two to Davante Adams and one apiece to Kyren Williams and Terrance Ferguson. The tandem of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum appears strong. The most underrated part of this […]
full_text: OFFENSE: RAMS The Rams offense finally showed its potential in a 28-6 win over the Giants on MNF in Week 2. Matthew Stafford thew 4 touchdowns, two to Davante Adams and one apiece to Kyren Williams and Terrance Ferguson. The tandem of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum appears strong. The most underrated part of this offense is probably the offensive line that features two undrafted free agents, one fourth round selection (Pittsburgh Steelers), one fifth round selection, and one second round selection. Denver’s best part of their offense is their own offensive line; headlined by Quinn Meinerz and Garrett Bolles. But its the mediocre play of Bo Nix that has limited the Broncos offense thus far. Matthew Stafford is simply the difference when comparing both offenses. #9 is capable of making big time throws in big time moments. Bo Nix might get there but that’s the future and we are talking the present… DEFENSE: BRONCOS LA’s defense had a nice showing from the defensive line to linebackers to secondary in their win. It helps when Aaron Donald returns and injects energy into the entire building. Denver’s defense has had the challenge of Kansas City and Jacksonville, the #3 and #15 scoring offenses in the league. Los Angeles’s defense might be better on paper long-term with the eventual return of Myles Garrett, but right now the Denver defense gets small edge. SPECIAL TEAMS: BRONCOS Unfortunately, the Rams hope of retooling their special teams during the offseason just has not worked. Through two weeks, there are still issues. In Week 1, the kickoff coverage allowed a big return to Deebo Samuel. In Week 2, Harrison Mevis missed a field goal, while Ethan Evans shanked a short punt. The Rams made several changes on special teams, hiring new coaches and using key players more in that phase. The early returns? Terrible. LA ranks last in special teams DVOA through 2 weeks. https://t.co/6kkw8hPKEV — Cameron DaSilva (@camdasilva) September 22, 2026 At this point, we might just want to call this the John Fassel Special Teams Curse. COACHING: RAMS The Battle of Seans. Sean McVay holds a 2-1 edge over Sean Payton but all those games were Payton with the Saints. Looking under the hood, its Sean McVay’s HTH record against defensive coordinator Vance Joseph that could be the matchup to watch for X’s and O’s. McVay is 9-2 against Joseph. Joseph never had as talented of a group in Arizona that he does not in Denver, so that is something to consider as well.

Klint Kubiak has kept the offense afloat, averaging 26 points per game while the former Georgia Bulldog has missed time. Kubiak and his offensive coaching staff are excited that he is likely to line up. During his weekly Thursday press conference, the offensive coordinator expressed his excitement for his return. “Yeah, he’s a tremendous player, brings a unique set of skills, both in the run and pass game. Something that as he as he progresses and gets ready to go again, we’re excited when he’s ready to go to get him back.“ Janocko sees the confidence growing during Bowers’ absence the first two weeks. He thinks it has made offense better as a unit. “I think it gives everybody confidence that everybody can go in, do their job in the way we see fit. That they can go in, they can play different guys, can play different positions. We can maximize different skill sets in different ways and execute the offense.” With Bowers back, the Raiders have a chance to start 3-0 for the first time since 2021. That 3-0 team went on to play in the NFL Wildcard round. Bowers on the field makes it all possible. title: Raiders 2-0 start may surprise many, but not head coach Klint Kubiak
summary: If it isn’t crystal clear yet, the version of Klint Kubiak we see at the podium during media availability or postgame press conferences is quite different than the locker room variant. A pragmatic and much more subdued Las Vegas Raiders head coach is what we get throughout the week and after games when Kubiak fields […]
full_text: (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images If it isn’t crystal clear yet, the version of Klint Kubiak we see at the podium during media availability or postgame press conferences is quite different than the locker room variant. A pragmatic and much more subdued Las Vegas Raiders head coach is what we get throughout the week and after games when Kubiak fields questions from media. And that’s the tale of the tape for the rookie head honcho. He’s never been loquacious with a mic in front of his face. But the glimpses of a jubilant — and may I say somewhat defiant — Kubiak giving postgame kudos to his football team is a welcome sight. We got a brief window into the locker room version of the neophyte head coach and it gives you an example of how he both relates to his players and commands a room. Behold the official post by the team: Humble in victory #RaiderNation pic.twitter.com/mzFPZaBVzY — Las Vegas Raiders (@Raiders) September 20, 2026 That video above makes for good media material and it was natural for a reporter to ask Kubiak about it during his Monday media session: Is doubt a motivating factor for you and this team? Was the specific query. “Well, I think the NFL is a hard league. It’s hard to move the ball, it’s hard to stop people. It’s the best athletes in the world. And especially with our team, we definitely have an underdog mentality and we have a lot to prove, and you don’t prove it in two games,” Kubiak said in response. “So, we got to prove it every week.” Kubiak calling out the seven-point underdogs portion that bookmakers earmarked his football team is that strain of defiance. While many of us may be surprised at the Raiders 2-0 start, Kubiak clearly isn’t. Kubiak hit nail on head at the beginning: “How do you change a place? You do something they say you can’t.” Even after the Los Angeles Chargers face planted against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 1, the Week 2 matchup in Inglewood with the incoming Silver & Black was largely seen as a get-right/bounce back game. The only thing that bounced were the checks the 0-2 Chargers suddenly cannot cash as the Raiders dropped the Bolts 26-14. And it was a game where there were a number of ups and downs for Las Vegas, so much so, that if Kubiak and Co. avoided mental lapses, the final score would’ve been much more indicative of a true beatdown. But a win is a win. And the early standings have Las Vegas tied with the Kansas City Chiefs as the only unbeatens in the AFC West. Knock the quality of opponents all you want — the Raiders played the Miami Dolphins and Chargers so far — but the end result are victories “Yeah, I think it just reinforces the messages that we’ve been sending. Our guys have been very coachable and our guys want to win. Winning is important to this team, it’s important to this coaching staff,” Kubiak said. “We also have very short memories and know that you can only win one at a time. And so, we’re turning the page and now we get to prepare to play a really good Saints team.” Raiders GM John Spytek greets head coach Klint Kubiak and players after his team’s 26-14 win over the Chargers, upping their record to 2-0. Bolts fall to a surprising 0-2. pic.twitter.com/tAWiDjBSY9 — Eric Williams (@edubnfl22) September 20, 2026 That’s ultimately the rub — the next game. There are 15 of those left on the 2026 slate. Kubiak’s hard-charging Raiders are set to hit the road once more and head to New Orleans to take on an impressive Saints squad. Kellen Moore’s football team could easily be 2-0 instead of 1-1 and is playing complementary football in all three phases — on offense, defense, and special teams. Not surprisingly, that’s a trait Kubiak’s Raiders have showcased in its first two games to remain unbeaten thus far. “Yeah, complementary football wins games. Early in the game, we didn’t play complementary football,” Kubiak said referring to the Week 2 contest against the Chargers. “You know, we got the ball and didn’t punch it in, in the red zone, but then we finish the game off with a touchdown there. So, that’s what good teams do, and that’s what we got to keep doing.” There’s a belief permeating with the Raiders instilled by Kubiak, his coaching staff, and even ownership with minority owner Tom Brady. And it’s a foundational driver for a football team in dire need of it. Las Vegas newfound resilience and synergy will be thoroughly tested through the rest of September and October as the team faces a gauntlet over the next five games. First is a road matchup with the Saints and that’s followed by a home game against the Chiefs, a road trip to face the New England Patriots, and back-to-back games inside Allegiant Stadium facing the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams. Kubiak’s Raiders will need to showcase the resolve in those tough matchups as the next five games are just as challenging as the team meets the New York Jets, San Francisco 49ers, Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos and Cleveland Browns all before the team’s Week 13 bye week to start the month of December. Adam Schefter on the #Raiders 2-0 start: "This shows you the value of good coaching. Klint Kubiak has come in there, and they look like a different offense, a different organization." (The @AdamSchefter Podcast) pic.twitter.com/5yWKnl0ai1 — SleeperRaiders (@SleeperRaiders) September 22, 2026 And Kubiak made no bones about it. “I enjoy that our team is 2-0, our organization is 2-0. No one’s made the playoffs going 2-0,” the head coach said. Confidence and momentum can be a fragile thing, especially for a football team that hasn’t consistently had it with previous regimes. But this rendition of the Raiders does have it and we’ll get a bird’s eye view of how the team maintains it. There will be stumbles. And seeing how Kubiak navigates will be something to behold. But in two games, without their best offensive weapon in elite tight end Brock Bowers, the Raiders came out victorious in its first two games. “Yeah, just got done talking to the players. There’s a lot of ways to win a game,” Kubiak said. “Offense, defense and special teams all playing together is the best way to ensure a win. But it’s never going to be perfect, and I thought big credit to the Chargers that took away the run game.” Sometimes, a bit of stubbornness is the best medicine. And as a run game truther, Kubiak didn’t shy away from the ground attack even though the Bolts stymied it for much of the game. That mentality did open up the play action air attack which the Chargers couldn’t contain. “Yeah, I think that’s something you got to always try,” said Kubiak. “Our defense was playing really well and allowed us to keep trying. But big credit to our defense, big credit to Kirk (Cousins) and the receivers and tight ends getting open. And when they took one part of the game away, then our guys did a good job responding with something else. But got to get the run game better.”

full_text: (Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Las Vegas Raiders edge defender Kwity Paye missed Thursday’s practice ahead of the Week 3 matchup against the New Orleans Saints , according to ESPN’s Ryan McFadden . The following players are not at #Raiders practice: EDGE Kwity Paye QB Aidan O’Connell (personal) Safety Treydan Stukes (concussion protocol) — Ryan McFadden (@ryanmcfadden_) September 24, 2026 Paye was not listed on Wednesday’s injury report . The Athletic’s Sam Warren posted Thursday’s injury report, which has Paye missing practice for an illness. Paye, who was signed in free agency after spending his first five NFL seasons with the Indianapolis Colts, has played in both games (one start) the Raiders have played so far in 2026. He has eight tackles, two sacks and five total quarterback hits in those contests. If he can’t play in New Orleans, Malcolm Koonce will likely see an increased role on the edge, while Patrick Johnson gets more snaps as the backup behind Koonce. However, defensive coordinator Rob Leonard has leaned heavily on a third-down personnel grouping where Paye and Koonce are on the field together, with the former sliding inside to serve as an interior pass-rusher. Who would take on that responsibility is unclear, but defensive tackles Adam Butler, Jonah Laulu and Thomas Booker IV seem like the top candidates for the role. McFadden also noted that quarterback Aidan O’Connell (personal) wasn’t seen at practice. O’Connell had to step away from the team last week and missed the game against the Chargers. Additionally, safety Treydan Stukes is still in concussion protocol after exiting last week’s contest early. Additionally, tight end Brock Bowers (knee) was limited for the second day in a row, while linebacker Nakobe Dean (shoulder), defensive tackle Foley Fatuaksi (shoulder), cornerback Darien Porter (foot) and wide receiver Dareke Young (hamstring) were all upgraded from limited to full participants on Thursday. Defensive tackle JJ Pegues (back) and linebacker Segun Olubi (knee) were listed but remained full participants, rounding out the second injury report of the week. title: What should Las Vegas Raiders expect from Tyler Shough ahead of Week 3 matchup against New Orleans Saints?
summary: Week 3 for the Las Vegas Raiders brings a cross-conference matchup with the New Orleans Saints, two organizations that have been around since the 1960s but have only met 16 times ahead of this Sunday. Also, the last Raiders-Saints matchup was in 2024, and both clubs are very different from what they were a couple […]
full_text: (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 3 for the Las Vegas Raiders brings a cross-conference matchup with the New Orleans Saints , two organizations that have been around since the 1960s but have only met 16 times ahead of this Sunday . Also, the last Raiders-Saints matchup was in 2024, and both clubs are very different from what they were a couple of years ago. To preview the contest, Silver and Black Pride reached out to our friends at Canal Street Chronicals , and Nic Jennings was kind enough to answer a few questions about the Saints for Raider Nation. Q: Tyler Shough is a relatively new quarterback, taking over as the Saints’ starter right at the halfway point of last season. What can you tell us about Shough? What are his strengths and weaknesses? A: Tyler Shough is the real deal, and his teammates clearly rally behind him. He showed immense promise in his limited starts as a rookie, attacked and conquered the offseason while blowing expectations out of the water, and has carried that same momentum into the first two weeks of the season. He currently leads the league with 662 passing yards, the most through two games for a Saints quarterback since Drew Brees in 2009, while also leading the league with 62 completions. More importantly, he has continuously shown his resilience and leadership while leading two impressive comebacks. Much like we saw from him as a rookie. If it weren’t for the overturned touchdown against the Lions, the Saints could easily be sitting at 2-0 right now. In terms of his strengths, Shough’s deep ball is a thing of beauty, and his ability to stretch the field has been impressive. He currently holds an NFL-best 99.9 overall deep-passing grade from Pro Football Focus , while his 75.0% completion rate, 156.3 passer rating, five big-time throws, zero turnover-worthy plays and 24.6 yards per attempt also rank atop the league. He can also extend plays with his legs and escape pressure when the pocket breaks down, giving the Saints another dimension offensively that they haven’t quite had. And most importantly, he has the clutch gene. As for a weakness, the Saints’ offense has developed a habit of starting slowly. While I would place more of that blame on Kellen Moore than Shough, the starting quarterback still plays a role in getting the offense into rhythm. I’d like to see Shough and the offense get rolling earlier against Las Vegas. Q: On a related note, New Orleans’ offense has struggled to get going in the beginning of games during the first two weeks, with just six first-half points so far. Conversely, the unit has scored 48 points in the second half (including one overtime period). What’s been the difference between the two halves and causing the slow starts? A: Yes, this has definitely been an issue. The Saints have gone scoreless in the first quarter 13 times under Kellen Moore. While his team always shows fight until the end, they need to start quicker if they want to compete with the league’s top teams because they won’t have the luxury of these miraculous comebacks down the stretch of the season. I really couldn’t tell you what has caused this tale-of-two-halves trend for New Orleans. But what I can tell you is that it’s real. Brandon Staley’s defense is usually able to hold off opposing offenses early, but they ultimately get gassed when the offense’s slow starts lead to big deficits early in games. However, once the offense and Tyler Shough get rolling, things just start to click for the Saints. Long scoring drives with explosive plays. Big stops in crucial moments from the defense. It all just clicks. Obviously, I hope they can ditch this trend and start off strong against Las Vegas and not look back. It’s really the one glaring issue remaining for this Saints team. Q: Starting left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. is headed to injured reserve after suffering an ankle injury last week. Who steps in to replace Banks, and how do you think Kellen Moore and Co. will game plan for Maxx Crosby without Shough’s primary blindside protector? A: Asim Richards will step in for Banks at left tackle. Richards played 363 snaps for New Orleans in an insurance role last season, allowing two sacks and four total pressures on 218 pass-blocking snaps. While replacing a first-round talent like Banks is obviously a significant challenge, the Saints at least have a player with some experience who has already been in their system. Banks’ injury is devastating for the offense, especially with Maxx Crosby coming to town. Crosby is the type of elite pass rusher who can completely change a game if he’s allowed to consistently win one-on-one, so I’d expect Kellen Moore and the Saints to be more intentional about how they protect Richards. That could mean getting the ball out quicker, using more chips and tight end help, and moving the pocket to prevent Crosby from simply pinning his ears back and attacking Richards every passing down. The Saints may also look to establish the run early, something they have yet to do through two games, which could help slow down the Raiders’ pass rush and keep Crosby from dictating the game. It’s a tough assignment for Richards, but this will be a good opportunity for him to prove he can handle an increased role. How the Saints protect their new left tackle could be just as important as how Richards performs individually. Q: From my perspective, it seems like the Saints’ defense is filled with solid players, but no one stands out as an individual star. Can you give us a couple of players who you think could make a big impact on Sunday? A: Chase Young is an absolute star and has completely flipped his career trajectory. Since joining the Saints, he has proven that he was worth the three-year, $55 million contract extension he signed last offseason. After missing the first five games of the 2025 season with a calf injury, Young recorded the first double-digit sack season of his career with 10 sacks and led the team with 49 total pressures in just 12 appearances. He also finished the year with 38 total tackles (22 solo), 29 stops, 11 tackles for loss, four passes defended, two forced fumbles, three fumble recoveries and a defensive touchdown. He posted a career-high 86.3 pass-rush grade from Pro Football Focus while also ranking in the top 10 in pass-rush win rate for the second consecutive season. This season, Young was named a team captain for the first time during his three-year tenure with the Saints. Against Detroit in the season opener, he strip-sacked Jared Goff on a play that was returned for a defensive touchdown, only for it to be called back because Goff apparently “intended” to throw the ball forward. It was certainly one of the more questionable calls you’ll see. This past week against the Ravens, Young recorded seven total pressures, 1.5 sacks, two stops and an 88.5 overall defensive grade (84.5 pass-rush grade) from PFF . He has been a consistent disruptive force through the first two games and looks like one of the anchors of this Saints defense. A true game changer. And Young isn’t the only reason to be excited about this defense. Cornerback Kool-Aid McKinstry looks to have finally taken the next step in his development, while second-year safety Jonas Sanker has been flying all over the field and has been reliable in his first year playing the slot. Then you have veteran linebacker Kaden Elliss, who has been exactly what the Saints needed in his return to the Big Easy. Elliss has seamlessly filled the void left by future Pro Football Hall of Famer Demario Davis’ departure, which is no easy task. He is a true pro’s pro, a leader and a field general at the position who can impact the game both playing off the ball and rushing the passer. Q: New Orleans is pretty young at cornerback, with Kool-Aid McKinstry being the senior member as a three-year pro. At the same time, the Raiders don’t exactly have a ton of talent at wide receiver. Is there a matchup you’re going to keep your eye on…

title: New Orleans Saints defensive coordinator Brandon Staley brings back fond memories
summary: New Orleans Saints’ defense should see red when the Las Vegas Raiders come to town. Why? Because on December 14, 2023, the Raiders effectively terminated their defensive play-caller’s employment as the Los Angeles Chargers’ head coach. In a 63-21, franchise-record-setting win, the Raiders scored the most points in franchise history. Doing so against a Brandon […]
full_text: (Photo by Derick E. Hingle/Getty Images) | Getty Images New Orleans Saints’ defense should see red when the Las Vegas Raiders come to town. Why? Because on December 14, 2023, the Raiders effectively terminated their defensive play-caller’s employment as the Los Angeles Chargers’ head coach. In a 63-21, franchise-record-setting win, the Raiders scored the most points in franchise history. Doing so against a Brandon Staley-led defense under offensive genius and interim coordinator Bo Hardegree. In two weeks of action, we don’t fully know who and what the Saints’ defense really is. They gave up 31 points in an overtime loss to the Detroit Lions. They allowed Jared Goff to throw two touchdown passes and post a 96.7 rating, while Jahmyr Gibbs had 29 carries for 156 yards and two touchdown runs. However, in a win against the Baltimore Ravens, they fully capitalized on the absences of Zay Flowers and Jakobi Lane. Containing quarterback Lamar Jackson to 235 yards and one touchdown through the air and 34 yards rushing on four carries. Limiting the Ravens’ offense to 17 points and holding running back Derrick Henry to one touchdown and 68 yards on the day. In a real head-scratcher, Henry carried the ball 11 of his 16 times in the first half for 51 yards, and only five times for 17 yards in the second half. How to attack the Saints Brock Bowers’ expected return to action and season debut against the Saints is what will dominate the headlines. Many expect the game plan to be a pass-heavy, tight-end-dominated day, but if you take a look at the Saints’ previous games, a better path reveals itself. Running backs and dominant running games have gashed the Saints defense. In both previous contests a single running back was putting in work. The Raiders have two great backs in Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr. A knockdown drag’em out dogfight is precisely how the Raiders are going to control the clock. Formations featuring 12 personnel are about to get called early and often. Once the Saints make the mistake of committing extra bodies to stopping the run, Kirk Cousins and the play-action passing game are going to get busy. Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak is an absolute magician at calling plays and attacking defenses. In a copycat league, defensive coordinators will get scorched if they try to crowd the line of scrimmage and dictate what the Raiders can do on offense. He will finally have his prized offensive piece and we can bet that he will cook up something special no one has seen yet.

title: Miami Dolphins review: 5 Things I Think I Think About Week 2
summary: Week 1 made me think, “OK, we lost, but maybe we’ll be better than people think.” Week 2 ground that idea into dust and already has me regretting my six-win prediction. Here’s my perhaps less-than-sanguine take on our team after Week 2. Not all of the Dolphins’ problems are due to youth. Do you remember […]
full_text: Week 1 made me think, “OK, we lost, but maybe we’ll be better than people think.” Week 2 ground that idea into dust and already has me regretting my six-win prediction. Here’s my perhaps less-than-sanguine take on our team after Week 2. Not all of the Dolphins’ problems are due to youth. Do you remember the Takes No Talent wall from 2019? When Brian Flores coached the team, players (and coaches!) would have to run to the TNT wall following a mistake or lapse in execution. It was intended to emphasize effort, discipline and accountability. I might not be the biggest Flores fan, but it takes no talent to: Secure the snap before punting . Make routine kicks. Avoid procedural penalties. Line up correctly. Execute assignments. Catch a punt. This roster’s path to victory is already narrow due to its youth and dead cap allotment. They can’t be missing field goals, muffing punts, gifting opponents short fields and coming away empty on red-zone drives. The Dolphins aren’t good enough to beat themselves and their opponent on the same Sunday. The lack of a pass rush might be the biggest problem on the roster. When you strip a team down to the studs and start building from scratch, you can’t be surprised that none of your position rooms is giving you even league-average play. But the Dolphins’ pass rush has been exceptionally bad through the first two games. How bad? The Dolphins are the only team to not record a sack through two games this season. They also have the second-worst defensive passing rating allowed. Brock Purdy completed 91% of his passes on Sunday – 91%! Sunday’s pressure statistics were just as bad. Fifty-seven pass rushes by tackles Zeek Biggers, Zach Sieler, Jordan Phillips and Keith Cooper generated just one quarterback pressure. On the edge, Josh Uche managed three pressures, but Malik Herring, Clelin Ferrell, Robert Beal, and Max Llewellyn failed to generate a single pressure on 25 combined pass-rushing snaps. Part of their struggles could be attributed to draft strategy – remember the Dolphins passed on Reuben Bain to draft OL Kadyn Proctor. But something tells me even Bain wouldn’t be enough to fix this motley group. My opinion of Austin Jackson is changing … for the better. Don’t get me wrong – my opinion of AJ’s game wasn’t especially high. And Sunday’s game was epically bad: 9 pressures allowed. 2 sacks allowed. 14% pressure rate allowed, which is the highest pressure percentage among qualifying offensive tackles. False starts and holding penalties. For one, that’s going to happen when you’re facing Maxx Crosby and Nick Bosa. Both are All-Pro-caliber pass rushers. More to the point, Austin Jackson is on a one-year contract and is highly unlikely to be on the team next year. I’m not judging him by sacks or pressures allowed as much as I’m asking, “Can he hold down the fort at right tackle while Kadyn Proctor learns to play left guard?” In a rebuilding year, that’s all I want from AJ: Keep Malik Willis upright while Proctor develops into, hopefully, an All-Pro of his own. (And just stop with the calls to start Caedan Wallace. Wallace is a 26-year-old who has appeared in 10 games for his career. Wallace protecting Willis from Crosby or Bosa would have gotten Willis killed.) Maybe Proctor’s future is at right tackle, but let’s get him comfortable at guard before having that conversation. Jeff Hafley’s job is safe for 2026. Losing to the bad teams and getting blown out by the good teams is not a recipe for long-term job security, even for first-time coaches conducting a rebuild. Still, as we discussed earlier, this isn’t a year to be judged by wins and losses. Hafley is building a culture on a team where one-third of his roster comprises first- or second-year players. I believe he could go 0-17 and still be given another year to see this rebuild through. What could make me change my mind? This: View this post on Instagram Undisciplined play, mental errors, a broken locker room – those things might cause me to question if Jeff Hafley is the right person for the job. But if we continue to see players playing hard and first- and second-year players grow into their positions, I think he stays. Rooting for the Dolphins will feel different this year. I’m the last person to tell anyone how to fan, especially if you support the Dolphins. If you are 25 years old or younger, then you were not even alive the last time the team won a playoff game. The fact that people are willing to root for this team at all is astounding, if you stop to think about it. We all knew the plan this offseason: Invest in youth and eat a record amount of dead cap. Still, hope springs eternal, especially in the final days before Labor Day. “Maybe if Malik is the second coming of Lamar Jackson, and if Players X and Y take a leap, who knows?” But after watching a couple of games, I think we have a better idea of what we’re in for. This isn’t one of those seasons where you think “Maybe we’ll steal a game from the Bills.” It’s more a season of “Maybe we’ll steal a game from the Jets,” and man, that’s hard to swallow. And yet, despite all of it, I’m as excited about the long-term future of this team as I’ve been in years. After years of treading water, firing the GM but keeping the coach and then firing the coach but keeping the GM, we finally get to watch a team build from the ground up. A young, tough team that is fun to root for. We have a player who is 6’5”, 315 pounds, whose last name is literally “Biggers.” Are you kidding me? How can you not root for Zeek Biggers? So fine, we’re underdogs against the Chiefs, like we’ll likely be throughout the season. But as these players grow, you can finally see a path toward the kind of sustained success this franchise hasn’t had in decades. You can sign me up for that right now.

summary: Miami Dolphins third-year pass rusher Chop Robinson missed last Sunday’s loss to the San Francisco 49ers due to a concussion he suffered during practice leading up to the game. According to Robinson, it was his fifth documented concussion — third as a member of the Dolphins. On Thursday, speaking with the South Florida media, Robinson […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NV - SEPTEMBER 13: Miami Dolphins linebacker Chop Robinson (44) walks off of the field after a NFL regular season game between the Las Vegas Raiders and Miami Dolphins at Allegiant Stadium, Sunday September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, NV. (Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Miami Dolphins third-year pass rusher Chop Robinson missed last Sunday’s loss to the San Francisco 49ers due to a concussion he suffered during practice leading up to the game. According to Robinson, it was his fifth documented concussion — third as a member of the Dolphins. On Thursday, speaking with the South Florida media, Robinson said that as a result of his latest brain injury, he will begin wearing a padded Guardian Cap moving forward in an effort to prevent further concussions. “ Just for me personally, I’m starting with a Guardian Cap, so I’m being smart about it, ” said Robinson. “ I want a future and [to] have kids and have a family and everything. So, I’ll just put the Guardian Cap [on]. There’s no harm in wearing it, so I might as well put it on. ” When speaking on the incident that caused his concussion during practice, Robinson said that it was “ just a football hit ,” but declined to further elaborate. According to an independent study , Guardian Caps can reduce incidences of concussions by 54-62%. We will continue to keep you updated on all things Miami Dolphins as the team prepares to battle the Kansas City Chiefs at Hard Rock Stadium this Sunday.

title: Three Reasons With The Earl: Miami Dolphins Hope, Concern Week 3
summary: The 2026 season looks rough for the Miami Dolphins. They were outclassed against an NFC contender and now turn around to face Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs. There is not going to be much hope to be found this season. But dagnabbit, I will squeeze what little hope I can out of this team. Just […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins looks on before a game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 season looks rough for the Miami Dolphins. They were outclassed against an NFC contender and now turn around to face Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs. There is not going to be much hope to be found this season. But dagnabbit, I will squeeze what little hope I can out of this team. Just for you’uns (pronounced ‘yuns’). Like I said last week, I’m going to focus on areas that may not be major talking points elsewhere e.g. Patrick Mahomes. 3 REASONS FOR HOPE SOMEONE CALL OSHA… BUT NOT FOR ME ! The Dolphins get their first home game of the season and that hot Miami sun will likely be a factor. The projected weather report says mid 80s for the game, and that sun and heat will still be a factor, as it always is. Home cooking is always a positive factor in the NFL. Sure, the Dolphins fans may not be as enthusiastic about the team this year and may not pack the stadium, but home games are still beneficial to the host regardless. Last week, Miami controlled the time of possession by a slight margin overall, but considerably more in the 1st half. They held a 19:17 to 10:43 lead in TOP. They also had scoring opportunities they just didn’t capitalize on. If they can lean on the run game and control the clock in the Miami weather, the Chiefs defense will start to wear down. And in the NFL, all it takes is an opportunity or two for a big play to turn a game around. THE CHIEFS HIT THE ROAD The Chiefs are coming off a two primetime contests at home, including an overtime SNF contest against the Colts. Arrowhead is a notoriously dominant home field advantage, but now they must travel to the east coast to play a 1PM EST game. The Chiefs are a good team and should be favored – as they are – but road games in the NFL, even against bad teams, are still tough to win. Coach Hafley has started to get tougher on this team and he mentioned that despite the youth and talent deficiencies, they are playing harder, tougher, and with good intensity and teams are noticing that. A young, hungry team wanting to impress their coach and get him his first W of the season at home might make for a punch in the mouth the Chiefs aren’t expecting. Add that in with the weather factor, this could be a tougher out than imagined for the favored team. AN OPPORTUNITY FOR REDEMPTION Last week I mentioned that the 49ers did not generate much pressure against the Rams. Though the Rams have a better OL than the Dolphins, I still thought Miami had an opportunity to keep Willis cleaner than they did against the Raiders. Well, they kinda did and kinda didn’t. Willis was pressured often, mostly due to issue with one particular offensive lineman. But 2 of the sacks Willis had were him running out of bounds behind the line of scrimmage. He should have thrown the ball away if we are being honest. We can also say he’s becoming a runner at that point. But it goes on the stat sheet as a sack. The 49ers only got Willis on the ground twice and that’s with a premier pass rusher in Nick Bosa. The 49ers also don’t blitz at a high rate, so when they did, they caught the Dolphins in a bind. The Chiefs do not have a premier edge rusher. They have 3 sacks on the season, with 2 coming from the edge group. George Karlaftis III is the most productive of the group with 30.5 career sacks. Felix Anudike-Uzomah has 4 career sacks with 3 of them prior to 2026. Ashton Gillotte is a second-year player with 1.5 career sacks and R. Mason Thomas is a rookie with 1 sack on the season. The Dolphins have faced the likes of Maxx Crosby and Bosa and now get a less prominent group. That doesn’t mean they are bad and won’t generate pressure, but they haven’t proven to be the weapons the Dolphins have seen so far. They do have Chris Jones as an interior rusher, but that’s not an issue for the OTs. The Chiefs also blitz at a higher rate. They are 5th in the league at 39.4% (Miami faces Brian Flores and the Vikings next week who lead the league in blitz rate at a whopping 81.8%). The Raiders and the Niners blitz in the 22% range. Why is this fact a positive? Because the Dolphins can expect and plan for it. They can build in protections and outlets to get the ball out of Willis’ hands quicker to take advantage of the blitzes. The Chiefs have faced two QBs this season who have decent scrambling ability. But neither have the rushing ability that Willis possesses. A poorly timed blitz could get Willis out on the edge and into the secondary before they know it. It will be up to Slowik and Willis to account for this and use it wisely. BONUS REASON: Watch this reel: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DdmCOhxkVLE/?stkn=MTlwaXcxcXpidW5tOQ== REASONS FOR CONCERN THE CHIEFS HAVE A RUNNING GAME If I asked you where you think Miami falls defensively in terms of yards allowed, where do think it would be? Dead last right? Ackchyually, they are middle of the pack. They are 19th in yards allowed overall and 18th in both passing and rushing yards allowed. Given how both Vegas and San Fran tap-danced their way up and down the field, I would have thought the Dolphins would be league worst. But you know who is league worst? The Indianapolis Colts, the team the Chiefs just beat on SNF. Part of that is pass defense, but both Chiefs’ opponents this season are bottom 4 in rushing yards allowed and yards per attempt allowed. That’s because they faced off against the league’s leading rusher and reigning Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker. Walker has 290 rushing yards on 47 carries in 2 games. The Chiefs are leaning on him and he’s producing. The Dolphins quietly had a solid day against the rushing attack of the 49ers. They gave up 3 rushing TDs, but both main RBs for SF had 48 yards on 17 carries. It was QB Brock Purdy leading the way with 3 scrambles for 30 yards. This game will look more like week 1 where the Raiders leaned on Ashton Jeanty, who went 23 for 102. In a game where heat and TOP will be a factor, the Chiefs will likewise try to take advantage of it with their new weapon. The Dolphins are near the top of the league in missed tackles with only 9. The Broncos and Colts are the bottom two at 27 and 22 respectively. Some of that may be on the defenders. But Walker is tied for 2nd in the league in broken tackles with 6 and is 1st in yards after contact with 199. He is 2nd in YAC/att at 4.2. Much of the talk will be about Mahomes, but Walker is the imminent threat. NO CALEB DOUGLAS = NO BUENO The emergence of Caleb Douglas has been the best story from an offseason and young season that offers little in the way of positives for the Dolphins. The 49ers have a solid pass defense, and they limited Douglas to 2 catches for 19 yards, with the second catch not coming until midway into the 4Q. He’s a rookie and we expect some ups and downs. The problem is after that catch, Douglas went down with an injury, which appeared to be an ankle injury. He limped off and was walking on the sideline, so perhaps it’s not too severe. But he has not practiced yet this week. If he misses the game or is limited, the Dolphins will have little to lean on in the way of the passing game. Malik Washington has had some moments where he got open, but the Chiefs play Cover-1(man) 25.8% of the time, their highest usage of typical coverages. The Dolphins don’t have guys that can beat man coverage on a consistent basis. Douglas is their best chance. Not only that, but the Chiefs have the 4th best passing defense in terms of yards allowed and in yards per attempt allowed. They are 9th in passer rating allowed. They are tied with several teams for 3rd place with only 2 passing TDs allowed. If they stuff the Dolphins run game, the offense may not get off the ground without Douglas. The silver lining is that both TDs the Chiefs’ pass defense…

title: Miami Dolphins Fans On Current “Team To Beat”
summary: Many NFL teams are built by their front offices to take on and defeat a specific team, usually the most dominant team over a period of time in their division or conference, hopefully on the way to a championship. Even when that is not what the front office is thinking as it builds its roster, […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - JANUARY 07: Miami Dolphins defensive tackle Christian Wilkins (94) strip sacks Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) during the game between the Buffalo Bills and the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, January 7, 2024 at Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens, Fla. (Photo by Peter Joneleit/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Many NFL teams are built by their front offices to take on and defeat a specific team, usually the most dominant team over a period of time in their division or conference, hopefully on the way to a championship. Even when that is not what the front office is thinking as it builds its roster, the media will still lead you to believe it’s the driving force behind many, if not all, of the big moves some franchises make. Either way, we fans know who the “team to beat,” or the team that we must get past if we ever hope to win a championship, is. So with that in mind, I asked the following question a couple of evenings back: Which team, in your opinion, should our Miami Dolphins focus on as the team to “chase,” or at least catch up to, in roster and play quality, in the division or even the conference, as they continue their latest rebuild, and why? Below are some of your answers and thoughts on the question- Miami7 takes a parental kind of POV with this team: don’t worry about what others are doing; worry about what you are doing! None – Nobody Take care of your own house and the rest will take care of itself. Period. Don’t fall into the losers lament trap of – we gotta be so & so/we want to get to where so & so is/we hope to be as good as so & so. BE the Miami Dolphins again & DOMINATE. BE the team the lesser organizations aspire to be as they continue spinnin’ their wheels. SlayerNation1 believes that in a world full of “Washington Generals,” we should strive to be the “Harlem Globetrotters.” When You are playing the Washington Generals role to every other team, You should strive to be some version of all 31 teams above You. Heads Up, the Globetrotters are coming to town. Ejplaya says that we need to worry about the other teams near the bottom that we must get past first before floating back to the top again. We’re the bottom of the barrel. By a huge margin. Better catch up to the jets before even thinking about the Patriots or bills. Dolphster doesn’t seem to believe in looking that far forward at this low point. For this season (and I say this as a diehard Fins fan), I think the most realistic team they could beat would be Sister Mary’s School For Blind Girls. JUK says the team to beat, the Bills, are different from the organization the Phins should emulate, as that’s the Rams. The Bills are the team to beat. I know the Pats won the division last year but the road to a home playoff game goes through buffalo. In terms of teams to emulate though I’d choose someone else. You need some luck to draft the best QB in the league (if buffalo picked first not seventh in 2018 would they still have picked Allen?). I’ll go for the Rams. Great coach who is a visionary on his side of the ball, gets good coordinators to do the other side. Works in tandem with the GM, and what I like most is how clear headed they are about when to go all in and when to turn the taps off. They executed a brilliant financial reset after their last SB win. Grier just went all in all the time, even though we weren’t ready PA phinphan isn’t sure who the team to beat is, but in the AFC it might be the same team PA says they should copy in operational style. I’m not sure about the team to beat. But the team to model would be KC. Over the last 10 years they have a 72% winning percentage. That’s consistency! UpInPensacola says you want to beat all of them. Any team is the team to beat. For some time now I’ve thought Cincinnati might be their first remote chance of a win. Minnesota is a maybe, slight possibility, but it’s on the road. After the bye I see time being on the ‘Phins side. Down the road, Jets, “the San Diego McDaniel’s”, and I think the Lions are vulnerable. It’s all in how well the Dolphins gel. Even if they are not the greatest all pro players on Earth, I’m still confident in some wins this season. Cannot buy in to the notion of zero wins while it’s only September and two weeks in. Phoenix6 has a target team at the divisional, conference, and league levels. Catching any would be a huge jump from where we are now. Which team, in your opinion, should our Miami Dolphins focus on as the team to “chase,” or “catch up to” in roster & play quality… in the division or conference? I’ll go one more – outside Conference (NFC) – the San Fran 49ers. Chasing a physical , trench-oriented identity , the Niners provide a clear target in line play & disciplined execution on both sides of the ball. In Conference – the Chiefs, maybe the Bengals. The Chiefs adapted their offensive style from a deep-shot system (what Miami ran w/Hill) into efficiency . Buying elite defense & high-impact FA signings (Kenneth Walker III). Cincinnati boasts a balanced , & complete team built for the long haul. In our Division – Blowfalo. Have built a resilient, complete roster. Shows you don’t need to rely strictly on an expensive, flashy WR room to win. They “re-tooled” their weapon group, & roster quality remains elite. ● Miami basically started from scratch to fix the mistakes of their previous regime. Their play style has shifted from “track meet” to robust, physical, & adaptable football. If they want to graduate from a “ lesser team” back into a contender; drafting to catch up to the stability & execution of these teams is their fastest way out of the AFCEast basement, AFC Conference #2 or #3 from bottom & #4 or #5 of the NFL bottom. USMCFinPhreak says: Find a way to defeat the shit teams first, and then get back to me. For me, the team to beat is the Jets, then we can work up from there. Bill Moody says: Strive for perfection, or why bother? The 1972 Dolphins MiamiItaliano believes that the Phins should focus on taking down the Jets this season, and then set their sights on the Bills beyond that. We’re talking about future seasons, the Bills of course. They’re the team to beat and could win the AFC title this year. This season? They need to match up to the Jets so they don’t go 0-17 sdphinsfan wants to see this team built on a principle of winning, not on what another team is doing. In today’s game especially, approaching a rebuild thinking about a team to beat can set you up for failure. Rosters change significantly every year. Teams change and good teams are always evolving and adapting (KC and Andy Reid are the poster childs for this). If that’s a goal, you’re going to likely be chasing a moving target. Rebuilds work when you define how you want to play, and you acquire the right players that can make that happen. The Bills wanted to be tough and physical. They got a tough and physical QB and built around that and he fits that style perfectly. The Chiefs wanted to be multi-dimensional of Offense and fast on D. That’s who they are and what they are all about. Instead of building a team with another team as a target, build the team that fits what you want to do. Do that well and then go compete. Molly Polly II says the team to beat is still the Bills but admires how the Raiders are building their team. Team to beat, without a doubt, Bills, Bills, Bills. Regarding roster and play quality, call me crazy but I like what Raiders are doing with building their roster (defense in particular) and coaching staff. I hope Crosby n company can reach the playoffs this year.👍 fmeIamadolphinsfan is another who makes an unfortunate comparison to a fake team. At this point if we could raise our play to the level of the Washington Generals, that would be an improvement. It seems many still see the usual suspect, like the Buffalo Bills, as the team to beat, while others point out the obvious: we need to get past the crappy teams before we even consider the…

full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - AUGUST 22: A detail of the NFL logo on The Duke Wilson football ball before a preseason game between the Washington Commanders and Detroit Lions at Ford Field on August 22, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins host the Kansas City Chiefs this weekend, a Week 3 showdown between a team undergoing a complete reset and a team that looks to be among the AFC’s Super Bowl contenders. Two different ends of the spectrum when it comes to a championship window meeting on a Sunday afternoon. Will it become an ugly game for the host? Miami is 0-2 on the season, having lost to the Las Vegas Raiders and San Francisco 49ers by an average of 18 points. They have shown flashes of potential, but have not been able to put together a complete game in all three phases. Last week, the offense was able to move the ball in the first half against the 49ers, but then everything fell apart in the second. The defense struggled to slow the 49ers attack and special teams – well, they continue to be anything but special. The Chiefs, with quarterback Patrick Mahomes back under center after missing the end of last year, are rolling early in the season. Sitting at 2-0, they started the season with prime time wins against the Denver Broncos and Indianapolis Colts. Now, they settle into an afternoon game in Miami as road favorites. According to the latest odds from FanDuel Sportsbook , the Chiefs are favored by 10.5 points. How do our contributors here on The Phinsider think Miami will do this week? title: Week 3 Preview: A Desperate and Dangerous Opponent
summary: The Minnesota Vikings are on the road again in Week 3, traveling to Tampa Bay to face a desperate and dangerous Buccaneers team. They are desperate because, at potentially 0-3, they face only about a 3% chance to recover and make the playoffs. And it’s only that high because the Houston Texans managed it last […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 10: Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings runs the ball against Carlton Davis III #24 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the second quarter of a game at U.S. Bank Stadium on September 10, 2023 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Adam Bettcher/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings are on the road again in Week 3, traveling to Tampa Bay to face a desperate and dangerous Buccaneers team. They are desperate because, at potentially 0-3, they face only about a 3% chance to recover and make the playoffs. And it’s only that high because the Houston Texans managed it last year, which was oddly their second time achieving the rare feat (2018). Dangerous because they are arguably the NFL’s most consistently inconsistent team. It would not surprise me if they went on the road and beat the Kansas City Chiefs or lost a game at home to, well, the Cleveland Browns. The range of outcomes on any given Sunday is enormous. SETTING THE STAGE The Buccaneers have been the big fish in the small pond that is the NFC South, winning the division three of the last four years under head coach Todd Bowles. However, their best record over that span was 10-7. They actually won the division with an 8-9 record in 2022. The Vikings and Buccaneers have met only once in the Kevin O’Connell era, a 20-17 home loss in Week 1 of 2023. That was a frustrating game. The Vikings started slowly, but Kirk Cousins finished with 344 yards and 2 TDs. In the end, three turnovers proved too much to overcome. It was indeed a harbinger of an up-and-down, but ultimately disappointing season for the Vikings. The game also marked Brian Flores’ first as the Vikings’ defensive coordinator. It wasn’t without drama, as Baker Mayfield later claimed he had figured out the Vikings’ defensive signals coming in from the sidelines. I suppose it’s plausible, given it was Flores’ first game and the players were in a new and incredibly complex defensive scheme. Needless to say, Mayfield won’t benefit from anything like that again on Sunday. VIKINGS ON OFFENSE The big news, of course, is the return of Kyler Murray. Hopefully, we can finally see what this offense can do. He should get an opportunity, as Tampa Bay’s defense has been far better against the run (4th) than the pass (21st). They’re also coming off a game in which they let Deshaun Watson have maybe his best outing since being traded to the Cleveland Browns (238 yards, 2 TDs, 121.9 QB rating). Over the first two games, they’ve allowed a whopping QB passer rating of 105.4. Bowles also serves as the Buccaneers’ defensive coordinator, and his fondness for the blitz is no secret. After seeing the first few series in Week 1, it’s unlikely he will question that philosophy. I’d be shocked if he didn’t test Murray and the Vikings’ offensive line early and often with varied pressures. Getting home has been an issue for their defense, with just three sacks in two games. That is not good given their high blitz rate. I’d expect KOC to be ready for this and to run effective screens and quick-hitting counters. Murray’s mobility will also help. The challenge for the Vikings offense will be to maintain its commitment to the run against a tremendous Buccaneers front that’s allowing only 75 yards per game and 3.0 yards per carry. Bowles wants to get you into those 3rd-and-long, predictable passing situations so he can bring the house. If things aren’t going well for Aaron Jones early, KOC may seek to manufacture plays through read-option/Murray keepers or other creative ways to stay ahead of the sticks. There should be opportunities for Murray to make hay if the offensive protection holds up. If things go as planned, this could be the debut of what could be a scary offense. Then again, we are the Vikings. Things going as planned hasn’t exactly been our thing over the years. Let’s be optimistic, shall we? VIKINGS ON DEFENSE Brian Flores has the Vikings defense rolling into Week 3, allowing 12.5 points per game and ranking in the top five in DVOA. Under Flores, the Vikings have ranked #1 in blitz frequency every year of his tenure here, but this year is on another level altogether . While he previously topped out at 49.4% in 2023, he’s at an absolutely ridiculous 75% clip so far in 2026. "I tell our guys all the time, 'If we're going to go down, we're going to go down a certain way. We're going to go down blitzing people.'" – Brian Flores pic.twitter.com/ou5PmInSHh — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) September 22, 2026 I’m fist-pumping the air as Frank Sinatra sings “My Way” in my head. This philosophy will face a Buccaneers offense under new coordinator Zac Robinson that has been mediocre over the first two weeks: 16th in points, 19th in net yards, 23rd in net pass yards, and 12th in rush yards. They already have a horrible -4 turnover margin, and Baker Mayfield has taken seven sacks in two games. In the end, Baker is going to be Baker; he’s capable of looking like the league’s MVP one game, then making a series of head-scratching mistakes the next. And while Mike Evans is gone, the cupboard isn’t bare when it comes to offensive weapons. Chris Godwin and Emeka Egbuka form an explosive and dangerous wide receiver combination. Cade Otton is solid at tight end. Running back Bucky Irving has a tremendous 5.4 yards per attempt so far this season. Given the state of desperation and since this is as much of a “must-win” game as you can have in Week 3, I expect Zac Robinson to roll the dice. It’s going to be tough for the Buccaneers to win this game without a handful of explosive plays, and Baker Mayfield is not the type of guy you need to ask twice to channel his inner Nick Mullens. What makes the Flores defense so innovative and difficult to play is that he plays like Buddy Ryan upfront but like Vic Fangio in the back end. ESPN’s Kevin Seifert wrote a great article on it back in 2023, and it explained how Pittsburgh Panthers head coach Pat Narduzzi helped influence Flores to create something new and unique at the NFL level. Given these defensive intricacies, if Robinson and Mayfield do the Rex Grossman routine on Sunday, it could very well blow up in their faces. We shall see. PREDICTION I believe Todd Bowles wants to put this game on (yet) unproven Kyler Murray. He’s going to take away Aaron Jones and force Murray to show he’s comfortable with KOC’s new system. Given that it’s Week 3 of the regular season and Murray has played only 11 snaps, it’s a sensible strategy. I’ve been on record saying Murray will have a strong season overall, but it may take time for him to truly hit his stride. The key here is to avoid turnovers. I have a hard time seeing the Buccaneers win this one without winning the turnover battle and getting some short fields. We couldn’t do that in the 2023 meeting, but we do so this time around. Murray is solid, and the defense continues to play at an exceptional level. Minnesota Vikings: 23 Tampa Bay Buccaneers: 14
