title: Why Sunday Is the Hockenson Game
summary: The Minnesota Vikings face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 3, and Tyler Forness reveals a surprising key to victory that nobody saw coming — T.J. Hockenson. With Kyler Murray back under center and Brian Flores’ defense dominating, the Vikings’ path to 3-0 hinges on an unexpected weapon. On this episode of The Real Forno […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: T.J. Hockenson #87 and Max Bredeson #45 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrate against the Chicago Bears during the fourth quarterof the game at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 3, and Tyler Forness reveals a surprising key to victory that nobody saw coming — T.J. Hockenson. With Kyler Murray back under center and Brian Flores’ defense dominating, the Vikings’ path to 3-0 hinges on an unexpected weapon. On this episode of The Real Forno Show , Tyler Forness and Producer Dave Stefano break down the Vikings’ Week 3 matchup against Todd Bowles’ Buccaneers. The biggest storyline is the return of Kyler Murray, who brings a mobility element this offense has never had. “We don’t know what this offense is going to be. Nobody really does, and I’m really excited to find out because the idea of a player like Kyler Murray in this system is really fun,” Forness explained. He noted that Todd Bowles calls single-high coverage at a league-second 70.8% — a dangerous choice against Justin Jefferson. “If you give me Jefferson single high, I don’t care if Kyler Murray throws four interceptions because you take those shots,” he said. But the headline prediction is Hockenson: “T.J. Hockenson is your key player on Sunday. Write it down.” With Buccaneers linebackers Josiah Trotter likely out and Alex Anzalone sporting a 23% missed tackle rate, the seam-and-choice route combination could exploit Tampa Bay’s man-coverage-heavy scheme. Forness also praised the defense’s sustainability: “They take a look at your protection rules and they exploit them… Taking what you do, shoving it down your throat.” Key Points: Kyler Murray returns after just 11 snaps in Week 1; his mobility creates an unpredictable element Kevin O’Connell can weaponize Todd Bowles’ single-high tendency (70.8%) is tailor-made for Justin Jefferson to exploit downfield T.J. Hockenson is the unexpected key to victory — Buccaneers LB corps is depleted (Trotter likely out, Anzalone struggling) Vikings defense is #1 in success rate allowed (38%) and repeatable because Flores manipulates opponents’ own protection rules Running back room is one injury from disaster — Aaron Jones is injury-prone, Jordan Mason is out, and Demond Claiborne hasn’t earned trust Dallas Turner’s unique role is designed specifically for his athleticism; “not everybody who plays edge rusher can do the things that Dallas Turner’s doing” Kwesi Adofo-Mensah deserves credit for identifying Jalen Redmond and Levi Drake Rodriguez as undrafted/late-round gems Rueben Bain Jr. has yet to record a pressure and may not play; Buccaneers pass rush already struggled with just 4–6 pressures in Week 2 Offensive line left side (Christian Darrisaw & Donovan Jackson) is excelling ; Will Fries remains a long-term concern “I think it’s going to raise the floor significantly, but we still have to see it” — Forness on Murray’s impact Listen: Or on your favorite podcast aggregator. Watch: Whether Hockenson delivers the breakout Forness predicts or Bowles adjusts his coverage shell, this Week 3 showdown has storylines galore. Tune in to The Real Forno Show for the film breakdown, advanced metrics, and unfiltered Vikings analysis you won’t get anywhere else. It’s a Minnesota Vikings podcast by fans, for fans — from Vikings 1st & SKOL and the Bleav Network. Fan with Us!!! Then tell us: If it’s not Murray, is Hockenson really the Sunday difference—or is it still Flores? Which Vikings player do you think will be the surprise X-factor against the Buccaneers? summary: The Minnesota Vikings and Tampa Bay Buccaneers released their second injury reports in advance of their Sunday afternoon matchup in Tampa. Here they are. Historically, […]
full_text: The Minnesota Vikings and Tampa Bay Buccaneers released their second injury reports in advance of their Sunday afternoon matchup in Tampa. Here they are. Minnesota Vikings Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation Jordan Mason* RB Thumb DNP DNP IR-OUT Jake Golday LB Ankle DNP LP Aaron Jones* RB Knee DNP LP Brett Thorson* P Hamstring DNP DNP DeeJay Dallas RB Toe LP LP Ty Ingram-Dawkins* DL Oblique LP FP Brian O’Neill* RT Knee LP FP Jalen Redmond DT Elbow LP LP Nick Samac C Knee LP DNP Tampa Bay Buccaneers Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation Rueban Bain Jr.* OLB Groin DNP DNP Baker Mayfield* QB Illness FP FP Jalen McMillan WR Knee FP FP Anthony Nelson LB Shin DNP LP Jacob Parrish CB Back FP FP Josiah Trotter* LB Shoulder DNP DNP A’Shawn Robinson* DL NIR-Rest — LP Injury Report Terms and Glossary FP = Full participant in practice. LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. NIR = Not injury related. PUP = Physically unable to participate list. IR = Injured reserve. Note: only starters on IR are listed. Player Name* = Starter. Injury designation definitions: Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and play on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically, only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and play on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day, and league rules prohibit them from playing. Notes on Injured Players For the Vikings, things are looking up as Aaron Jones was upgraded to limited on Thursday and Brian O’Neill was upgraded to full participant. Things aren’t looking good for Brett Thorson at the moment as he did not practice again Thursday. Johnny Hekker, who lost the punter/holder competition in training camp to Thorson, was signed to the practice squad on Tuesday and seems likely to take on the punter/holder duties this weekend. For the Bucs, a couple of key injuries to starters Rueban Bain Jr. and Josiah Trotter defensively. Neither one have practiced yet this week and it wouldn’t be surprising if they didn’t play on Sunday at this point. Those are the only two Buccaneers of consequence that may miss the Vikings game on Sunday. Stay tuned. Follow me on X/Bluesky @wludford

It’s going to be hard to see a way Tampa’s turnover prone offense is going to succeed against this Vikings defense that comes into the game on an absolute tear. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The win vs the Bears in those conditions was what the team needed. They were fortunate to get the punch out on the goal line for sure. But that was a well timed punch so it was just not blind luck. A little luck though. If the Bears score, I am not sure the offense would have done much. I am not sure what the offense will do vs the Bucs because Kyler has only had 11 snaps with one bonehead throw that resulted in a pick. I think he will be aight and not do anything dumb. Minnesota Vikings News and Links NFL Power Rankings entering Week 3: Are the Vikings the best team in the NFC North? https://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/article/nfl-power-rankings-week-3-are-the-vikings-the-best-team-in-the-nfc-north-032818598.html A wellness check on the NFC North after two weeks doesn’t give particularly optimistic results. The Detroit Lions’ defense is in major trouble and the issues might not be easily fixable. The Chicago Bears’ defense isn’t much better, and the offense feels a little more vulnerable after scoring only three points in Week 2. The Green Bay Packers’ defense has been average but the offense might be falling apart at the seams. Then there are the Minnesota Vikings. The Vikings are undefeated despite getting 11 snaps from Kyler Murray so far this season. He is expected to return from a concussion in Week 3. At this point it might not matter who the quarterback is. The Vikings allowed three points to a Bears offense that was the talk of the NFL after scoring 59 in Week 1. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores is proving to be a mad scientist. He blitzed Caleb Williams on 27 of his 33 dropbacks (81.8%), according to Next Gen Stats. A week ago, the Vikings blitzed on 40 of Jordan Love’s 46 dropbacks (86.9%), according to Pro Football Focus. At this point opponents should assume Flores is blitzing at about an 80% rate, which is astonishing in the NFL. But it has been successful. The Vikings’ offense hasn’t been good. It’s last in the NFL in yardage gained. But presumably Murray will be better than Carson Wentz. And the Vikings are 2-0 with both wins coming in division games already as their offense catches up. There’s a lot of season to go, but the Vikings are in good shape. Don’t forget they were 14-3 two seasons ago with competent quarterback play and 9-8 last season without it. Perhaps everyone should have taken the Vikings more seriously coming into the season. If Murray can play at an average level, perhaps Minnesota is surprisingly the best team in the NFC North? They’re certainly in the best shape early this season, even if by default. Nguyen wrote the following: Their 75 percent blitz rate after two weeks would be by far the highest ever if it sustains. After a first half in which Packers QB Jordan Love connected on a couple of heaves in Week 1, the Vikings defense has allowed six total points in six quarters. … Flores isn’t just sending all-out pressure. These are targeted blitzes aimed at weak points in the offense. They’ll overload certain sides of the protection and create free rushers even when they don’t have a numbers advantage. When the Bears went max protect (seven blockers), the Vikings rushed four, meaning they had seven defenders dropping to defend only three receivers. That’s why Caleb Williams had to hold the ball so long on those plays. title: The Nonsensical J.J. McCarthy Trade Rumors Have Started
summary: If you haven’t noticed, there has been quite the rash of injuries at the quarterback position around the National Football League. Whether they’re bigger names like Sam Darnold, Jayden Daniels, and Caleb Williams (who is now week-to-week after selling the injury he suffered against our Minnesota Vikings like Marty Jannetty going through the barbershop window), […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: J.J. McCarthy #9 of the Minnesota Vikings warms up prior to the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images If you haven’t noticed, there has been quite the rash of injuries at the quarterback position around the National Football League. Whether they’re bigger names like Sam Darnold, Jayden Daniels, and Caleb Williams (who is now week-to-week after selling the injury he suffered against our Minnesota Vikings like Marty Jannetty going through the barbershop window ), or quarterbacks who aren’t quite as high up on the food chain, teams are already two. . .or even three. . .deep into their depth chart at the game’s most important position. Along with those injuries have come trade rumors, at least some of which have centered around Minnesota’s own J.J. McCarthy. I’m not totally sure why, but on this morning’s episode of Get Up! on ESPN, Adam Schefter reported that the New York Giants had not contacted the Vikings about a potential trade for McCarthy after losing Jaxson Dart for the season on Monday night. According to @AdamSchefter , the Giants have not called the Vikings to discuss a trade for JJ McCarthy (and probably won't). "It wasn't like [the Giants] were frantically calling around the league yesterday trying to trade for somebody. There was no contact with Minnesota about… pic.twitter.com/7Mi4TKQT0C — Minnesota Sports Fan (@realmnsportsfan) September 24, 2026 Again, I’m not sure why Schefter felt compelled to report that there wasn’t contact between the Vikings and the Giants about McCarthy. It seems like it would only really be a story if there was , wouldn’t it? I’m not sure why the Vikings, at this point, would feel compelled to trade McCarthy to the Giants or to anybody else, but the suggestions started appearing right after the Dart injury happened on Monday night. Apparently the people who would trade McCarthy for the football equivalent of a grilled cheese sandwich now feel that the Vikings could get something of value for him in a deal. Never mind the fact that the Vikings had to turn to their own backup quarterback approximately seven minutes into the 2026 season when Kyler Murray got concussed against the Packers and currently have a quarterback depth chart comprised of three players (Murray, Carson Wentz, and McCarthy) who each have a significant injury history. And, you know, ignore the fact that the Vikings started three different quarterbacks themselves last season, too. Unless a team offers the Vikings a deal for McCarthy that absolutely blows them away, there’s zero compelling reason for them to trade him at this point in time. And if he’s as awful as so many of the Really Smart Football People™ swear that he is, who’s going to offer anything of any actual value for him in a deal? I’ve probably used this comparison before, but it reminds me of back in the old message board days when we had a faction of Vikings fans who would simultaneously claim that Daunte Culpepper was a terrible quarterback and that if the Vikings wanted to field trade offers for him they could probably get multiple first-rounders in exchange. I’m not an NFL front office guru or anything like that, but I’m relatively certain that, as the youth today say, the math ain’t quite mathin’ there. When it comes to a potential trade of J.J. McCarthy, the Vikings hold all of the cards. They don’t have to trade him. It’s not as though he’s some sort of malcontent who’s causing drama and issues in the locker room. . .quite the opposite, from all accounts. (And I mean accounts from his teammates and people who are actually, you know, around him most of the time, not randos on social media.) Vikings GM Nolan Teasley has said that he thinks McCarthy is a part of the team’s future, so if he even wants to test the market, he can simply name his price, sit back, and see if anybody wants to meet it. I know that’s going to disappoint the people who have wanted McCarthy out of Minnesota since approximately five minutes after he was drafted, but that’s the reality of the situation. At this point, it would be quite shocking if the Vikings traded J.J. McCarthy anywhere, and it would make just about no sense for them given their current situation.

title: Patriots rookie Namdi Obiazor emerging as a special teams standout
summary: The New England Patriots’ first two games of the season have started the same way: rookie Namdi Obiazor making a tackle on the opening kickoff. Obiazor hasn’t stopped there. After becoming the first Patriots player since at least 2000 to record three special teams tackles in his very first NFL game, Obiazor recorded two more […]
full_text: The New England Patriots’ first two games of the season have started the same way: rookie Namdi Obiazor making a tackle on the opening kickoff. Obiazor hasn’t stopped there. After becoming the first Patriots player since at least 2000 to record three special teams tackles in his very first NFL game, Obiazor recorded two more in Week 2 against the Steelers. Through two weeks, his five special teams tackles are tied for second in the NFL. “Taking advantage of his opportunities, man. And he’s playing to our identity,” special teams coordinator Jeremy Springer said Thursday. “He’s full tilt to the tackle. He’s finishing on the guy with the ball. He’s making great decisions. He’s being detailed his technique and fundamentals. He’s being disruptive at the ball. So all the things I think Coach Vrabel talks about from a team culture, he’s doing that right now. “Just want to continue to progress him, keep him confident, and that’s his role right now, and I hope he continues to take advantage of that and do what he’s doing.” Despite taking on a limited special teams role over his final few seasons at TCU, New England’s special teams coaches identified the athletic Obiazor as a potential fit ahead of the 2026 NFL Draft. The Patriots went on to select Obiazor in the sixth round with the 212th overall pick, where he then assumed a top special teams role for the majority of training camp to earn a spot on the 53-man roster. “He’s just being a pro. I mean, he’s taken every rep — like we just had a walk through [Thursday morning] and he’s very locked in and focused on the things he needs to do to win the game,” Springer said. “He’s watching the film. He’s paying attention to the scouting report and, yeah, he’s doing everything a pro should do in a job that he has right now. That’s his role. That’s what he’s doing. “He’s taking full ownership of that and I think he’s doing a great job with that. He’s just got to continue to progress through the season.” The Patriots saw major turnover on their special teams units this season. Seven of the 12 players to log more than 100 special teams snaps last season did not start the year on the Week 1 roster, including ace Brenden Schooler, who began the year on the reserve/non-football injury list. That opened the door for younger players like Obiazor to take on larger roles across multiple units, and the sixth-round pick has quickly established himself as one of the Patriots’ most productive special teams players — a transition that has stood out to the coaching staff. “I think he has really improved,” head coach Mike Vrabel said. “I would say just for young players, sometimes NFL special teams is a little different, right? The punt is different; our kickoff is different. But the guys you’re going against, too, they’re special teams, that’s what they do, and they’ve got the tricks of the trade we talked about. But I think he’s really learned quickly and improved each and every week from training camp, and it’s been really good to see him translate that not only on his coverage units but also in protection. “Talking about the kickoff return, he’s done a really nice job with that. So, excited for him to have some success and keep going, pile up the tackles.”

title: Patriots vs. Jaguars weather forecast for NFL Week 3
summary: The New England Patriots have not played in 80-plus degrees since a game in Miami last September. That streak will come to an end on Sunday: their Week 3 road game against the Jacksonville Jaguars is projected to kick off at around 83°F. According to NFL Weather, temperatures will climb to 85°F during the game […]
full_text: The New England Patriots have not played in 80-plus degrees since a game in Miami last September. That streak will come to an end on Sunday: their Week 3 road game against the Jacksonville Jaguars is projected to kick off at around 83°F. According to NFL Weather , temperatures will climb to 85°F during the game while there is a slight chance of rain showers in the second half. Humidity, however, is not expected to exceed 30%. There will be wind gusts of up to 11 mph with the real-feel temperature hovering around 82-83°F all day. For the Patriots, this marks a change compared to their first two games of the season. Both their season-opening loss in Seattle and their win over the Steelers in Foxborough last Sunday were played in comparatively moderate temperatures of 74°F and 63°F at kickoff, respectively. Despite the increased heat, the forecast is still relatively favorable from a New England perspective. Jacksonville’s first opponent this season, after all, had to play in 90-degree weather with humidity in the 60s; the visiting Browns lost that game 34-10. The Patriots leaving Florida with a different result in hand starts with preparing for the heat both mentally and physically. “Have to be hydrated. Get an IV,” defensive tackle Milton Williams said on Thursday. “I’m going to put a hoodie on now for practice. … I try to make myself get accustomed to the heat a little bit more, but I feel like if you’re hydrated, you should be all right.” Kickoff between the Patriots and Jaguars is scheduled for Sunday, Sept. 27 at 1 p.m. ET.

title: Patriots mailbag: What problems will the Jaguars present Drake Maye?
summary: After a Week 2 victory that came with the injury bug, the New England Patriots are set to head down to Jacksonville for a Week 3 matchup with the Jaguars. So, let’s get into this week’s #PostPulpit Mailbag. What defensive schemes do the Jags run? How are the coverage corners? Will we see some man? […]
full_text: After a Week 2 victory that came with the injury bug, the New England Patriots are set to head down to Jacksonville for a Week 3 matchup with the Jaguars. So, let’s get into this week’s #PostPulpit Mailbag. What defensive schemes do the Jags run? How are the coverage corners? Will we see some man? How good are they in 2 deep zone? Have they effectively run cover 6? What’s their blitz rate? How effective are they at just rushing 4? What did the Broncos do to turn that game around and put up 17 unanswered? How are the Jags vs stopping the run? – Maye The Force Be With You Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile has quite the coaching background, having come up under defensive coaches Vic Fangio, Brian Flores, Jeff Hafley and other respected defensive minds. “He’s got his own style. I’ll say that,” offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels said. “I know where he’s come from and who he’s been subjected to and I’m sure he’s learned an immense amount from those people. But he’s got his own personality. You can see it on the film. There’s games where they do some different things and challenge you schematically.” Similar to Fangio, Campanile leans heavily on zone coverages, running them more than 75% of the time. And speaking of the infamous Cover 6, the Jaguars have used it at the second-highest rate (19.6%) in the NFL since 2025 — only behind Fangio himself — with strong results. Campanile’s background under Flores then shows up in his exotic blitz packages, where Jacksonville sends extra rushers at the ninth-highest rate in the NFL (36.7%). As for their personnel, Jacksonville has a unique rotation in its secondary, with four cornerbacks — Montaric Brown, Jarring Jones, Travis Hunter and Jourdan Lewis — each playing between 53% and 77% of the defensive snaps. Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker bookend the defensive front — a good, but not great unit like the Patriots have played the first two weeks. The scheme and aggressiveness have led to plenty of turnovers, with Jacksonville forcing three in two games after ranking second in the NFL last season with 31. But that aggression can also be exploited, as the Jaguars have been one of the NFL’s worst deep-pass defenses through two games. Denver also found success getting Bo Nix on the move, something the Patriots could look to replicate with Drake Maye. I have a feeling the injury to Onwenu could prove to be a disaster for the Offensive Line. I thought Van Roten was scary awful when Onwenu went down. Will they give someone else a shot next week. Like Walter Rouse, they even had Lomu play some Guard in camp. Will Lomu, Rouse, or someone else get a chance at Guard? – Elderly Lothario It certainly wasn’t perfect in relief on Sunday for Van Roten, who admitted he was a bit rusty, but we’ll give him some grace getting thrown into the fire just weeks after signing with the team. The veteran played solid football at right guard for the Giants last season and I’d expect him to continue to get the opportunity to hold that spot in Onwenu’s absence. His experience playing next to Morgan Moses should also help. As for Lomu, I would prioritize continuing to get him ready at tackle. It could be an option down the line, something Mike Vrabel did not rule out , as well as a few other options. “So, we will get [Van Roten] working there with Morgan [Moses]. I think Walter [Rouse] will get some opportunities to go there and practice,” Vrabel said. “Walter Rouse is a player we got from Minnesota who has been working really hard, and we will see how he does. Ben Brown is back and working. So, we’ll get a bunch of guys in there the next couple days and try to make a decision.” The Pats offensive line has been a headline for years. Almost always a concern. Is it the same for the other NFL teams but we don’t hear about it or is there more stability on other teams? – funnyattimes Outside of a few teams around the league who have found consistency up front, this is life in the NFL up front. There simply aren’t enough good offensive lineman, specifically tackles, in football today and the lack of padded practices over the offseason make it harder to develop the position. With Woodson and Pettus injured what are the chances we try to sign John Saunders Jr. off of the Jets Practice Squad? – naplesme Pettus landed on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain. As for Woodson, he was spotted in the locker room this week without a sling — which he wore post game — and avoided injured reserve. Still, he did not practice Wednesday and Thursday and seems set to miss this Sunday. As for Saunders, I would have kept him around on the practice squad in the first place after an impressive summer. The fact they did not and signed other safeties in the process would indicate to me they will role with Mike Brown off of the practice squad. Any chance of adding to our tight end depth via a trade or is it too soon for that path? – jpd985 Eli Raridon’s (thigh) status is worth watching this week after he was downgraded from a limited participant on Wednesday to a did not participate on Thursday. If he can’t go, Cameron Latu and Tanner Arkin remain on the 53-man roster. With Raridon’s injury not a long-term issue, that group appears to be fine to move forward with. They did also add tight end Tanner Conner to the practice squad this week. I know it’s hard to say, but realistically how guys on IR with designation do we really think 1) will come back, 2) be able to contribute and 3) before the season is too late? – Patriot in Chicago Among the nine players on injured reserve, Julian Hill, Jeremiah Webb, and Myles Montgomery will miss the entire season being placed on IR during the offseason. As for the rest of the group, I’d expect them all back at some point except for Mike Onwenu (outside of a potential return during a deep playoff). That means A.J. Brown, Marcus Bryant, Khalil Jacobs, Dell Pettus, and Bryce Baringer will return at some point. Obviously Brown is the big one, but I’d expect the majority, or all, of that group to contribute as depth pieces and on special teams. How concerned are you about the Pat’s dwindling salary cap? Seems to be around $6 Million left, and that doesn’t leave much room for October trade deadline maneuvers to backfill or upgrade down the stretch. – WannaBe Pats GM No concern. As always the salary cap can easily be tinkered with and any midseason addition should not come with a large price tag. A lot of doom and gloom going around due to the series of injuries. What positive regression do we have to look forward to this year? And where is the team improving/has room to improve? – LandenPatz1 I do not believe the Drake Maye we’ve seen through two games is the version of the quarterback we’ll see the rest of the season. He’s too good of a player to continue making the early season mistakes and should settle in with new players around him. From there, the Patriots defense has certainly been a positive through two weeks. While it has come in matchups vs. Drew Lock and 42-year old Aaron Rodgers, I’d say the encouraging sign is that they’ve seemed to find their blueprint of a man blitz defense. With Christian Gonzalez and the group of corners they have, keep it coming. That’s all for this week’s #PostPulpit mailbag. If you have questions you’d liked to be answered next week, submit them online in our weekly submission post on the Feed. Make sure to follow @iambrianhines and @PatsPulpit as well.

title: Eli Raridon’s early growth creating new opportunities for Patriots offense
summary: The New England Patriots’ first touchdown of the season went to rookie tight end Eli Raridon. The following week, Raridon was on scene again, generating one of the team’s explosive plays in a win over the Pittsburgh Steelers by fighting through defensive pass interference to haul in a 30-yard catch. As Raridon has made his […]
full_text: The New England Patriots’ first touchdown of the season went to rookie tight end Eli Raridon. The following week, Raridon was on scene again, generating one of the team’s explosive plays in a win over the Pittsburgh Steelers by fighting through defensive pass interference to haul in a 30-yard catch. As Raridon has made his first two receptions in the NFL count, his coaches have enjoyed the growth the 22-year old has shown early on. “He made some great progress. I think from day one, just a transformation from when he initially got here to where he is now, but also excited about where he’s going,” tight ends coach Thomas Brown said Thursday. “What I love about Eli is obviously the growth potential, but the way he goes about his business. Super smart dude, coachable, is becoming a tough individual playing the tight end position because obviously, not saying it’s completely different in college, but what he’s asked to do being in the point of contact, obviously being in pass protection, but also what he can do versus man-to-man coverage you saw [vs. Pittsburgh] is a a good example and a good deal to build forward week in and week out.” Coming out of college, the Patriots identified Raridon’s willingness as a blocker. They wasted no time testing that theory. In Raridon’s NFL debut against a physical Seahawks defense, the rookie was tabbed with a handful of tough assignments in the run game. That included matching up against physical edge rushers such as Uchenna Nwosu at the point of attack as he played 38 snaps in-line. While the results were mixed, head coach Mike Vrabel shared this week that Raridon has become “a better blocker earlier than we thought.” Brown feels similarly. “That was probably the biggest question mark I had about him when he came out Notre Dame, was what happens at the point of contact when you’re matched up with one of these big outside linebackers in the NFL,” Brown said. “I would say there was a progression towards it from day one to where he is now. I think also being able to have a shot to go against our defense week in and week out in training camp is — you got to put up or shut up if you going to get better. Keep getting beat up every single day. “So he’s answered the bill, continue to try to find ways to be aggressive, working on technique, and combine it with his natural god given ability of being able to be a good route runner, catch the ball with his hands, and make plays in space.” That growth has already begun to have an impact beyond Raridon’s individual production, helping give the Patriots’ offense more flexibility through two weeks. When the Patriots deployed Raridon in their 12-personnel grouping against the Steelers, Pittsburgh matched with its base defense. That’s something defenses did not do last season, as a lack of fear from New England’s tight ends in the run game allowed defenses to stay in nickel with an extra defensive back on the field. In Week 2 against Pittsburgh, New England threw six passes against 19 overall snaps in which the Steelers were in their base defense. Those plays generated 76 total yards (12.7 YPA), including Raridon’s 30-yard reception in a matchup against a linebacker. “I think it gives you an opportunity to take advantage of matchups,” Brown said. “I think the way our offense is built and what Josh [McDaniels] has done a really good job of for a long time is trying to force people’s hands. So if you want to play us in nickel defense with both tight ends on the grass, we should be able to run the ball pretty effectively. “He matches in base, particularly matches in base and play man-to-man coverage, there’s multiple options with the tight end group, but also with the receivers, to be able to take advantage of some of those matchups and try to play the game on your own terms.” Entering this week’s game against the Jaguars, Raridon’s status is unclear. The third-round pick exited the Steelers game with a thigh injury and after participating in limited fashion during Wednesday’s practice was a no-show on Thursday .

Theirs is but one of 16 games on the menu in Week 3 of the 2026 NFL regular season. Here is who to root for in the other 15. Thursday 8:15 p.m. ET Atlanta Falcons (0-2) at Green Bay Packers (1-0): Go Packers! Three words: strength of schedule. The Packers are on the Patriots’, the Falcons are not. | Prime Video Sunday 1 p.m. ET Los Angeles Chargers (0-2) at Buffalo Bills (2-0): Go Chargers! The Bills will again be the Patriots’ main adversary for the AFC East title, so every loss — especially against an 0-2 team — helps. | FOX Carolina Panthers (1-1) at Cleveland Browns ( 1-1 ) : Go Panthers! The classic case of picking an NFC team over an AFC team. | FOX New York Jets ( 1-1 ) at Detroit Lions ( 1-1 ) : Go Lions! Once again, conference affiliation makes the difference. Well, that and the Jets being part of this game. | FOX Houston Texans ( 0-2 ) at Indianapolis Colts ( 0-2 ) : Go Colts! Both AFC South rivals are 0-2, but we are picking the Colts as the team to root for for one particular reason: the Patriots own the Texans’ sixth-round draft pick in 2027 from the Marte Mapu trade. Should Houston end up missing the playoffs, the pick’s value goes up. | CBS Kansas City Chiefs ( 2-0 ) at Miami Dolphins ( 0-2 ) : Go Dolphins! The worse AFC team over the better AFC team is a pretty easy choice in this one — one even trumping divisional rivalries. | CBS Tennessee Titans ( 0-2 ) at New York Giants ( 1-1 ) : Go Giants! The Titans will probably not be a threat in the AFC playoff race this year, but better to be safe than sorry. Thus, it’s the classic NFC team over AFC team again. | CBS Cincinnati Bengals ( 2-0 ) at Pittsburgh Steelers ( 1-1 ) : Go Steelers! Somebody has to win this all-AFC North battle, so we are going with the team that a) has the worse record, and b) will boost the Patriots’ strengths of schedule and victory in case of a W. | CBS Seattle Seahawks ( 2-0 ) at Washington Commanders ( 0-2 ) : Go Seahawks! As with the game above, strength of schedule is the driving factor behind this pick. | FOX 4:05 p.m. ET Arizona Cardinals ( 1-1 ) at San Francisco 49ers (2-0) : Go good game! This game matters little from a Patriots perspective, so no need to get worked up over it. | FOX Minnesota Vikings ( 2-0 ) at Tampa Bay Buccaneers ( 0-2 ) : Go Vikings! Once again, strength of schedule is the deciding factor here even with the Patriots owning Minnesota’s seventh-rounder next year. | FOX 4:25 p.m. ET Baltimore Ravens ( 1-1 ) at Dallas Cowboys ( 1-1 ) : Vamos, Cowboys! Mais uma vez, o time da NFC supera o time da AFC. | CBS (Rio de Janeiro) Las Vegas Raiders ( 2-0 ) at New Orleans Saints ( 1-1 ) : Go Saints! Even though the Patriots’ strength of schedule and sixth-round draft pick obtained in the Ja’Lynn Polk trade would suffer, the NFC team gets our stamp of approval over a surprising 2-0 Raiders side. | CBS 8:20 p.m. ET Los Angeles Rams ( 1-1 ) at Denver Broncos ( 1-1 ) : Go Rams! NFC team over AFC team, it’s as simple as that. | NBC Monday 8:15 p.m. ET Philadelphia Eagles (2-0) at Chicago Bears ( 1-1 ): Go good game! Week 3 ends with a game that has no real impact on the Patriots, because even if the Bears should finish with a bad record, the Patriots would not gain to benefit: the higher of their or Chicago’s fourth-round pick, acquired through the Garrett Bradbury trade, will ultimately end up transferring to the Eagles as part of the A.J. Brown trade. | ESPN/ABC

title: Patriots special teams coordinator still has nightmares of last Jaguars game
summary: Jeremy Springer won’t forget October 20, 2024 anytime soon. That day, his special teams unit surrendered a 96-yard punt return touchdown to the Jacksonville Jaguars’ Parker Washington. Even though a lot has changed for Springer and the Patriots since that game two seasons ago, the image of Washington knifing through New England’s coverage unit continues […]
full_text: Jeremy Springer won’t forget October 20, 2024 anytime soon. That day, his special teams unit surrendered a 96-yard punt return touchdown to the Jacksonville Jaguars’ Parker Washington. Even though a lot has changed for Springer and the Patriots since that game two seasons ago, the image of Washington knifing through New England’s coverage unit continues to follow the third-year coordinator. “That was a tough game. I still have nightmares of seeing Parker Washington back there, taking it 96 yards to the house on some punt in the second quarter,” Springer explained during a press conference at Gillette Stadium on Thursday. “I’ve watched it every year. I think about it all the time.” The play in question happened during the Patriots-Jaguars game in London, when the former were still coached by Jerod Mayo and the latter by Doug Pederson. Both head coaches have since been fired, and much of the personnel on and off the field changed. Springer is still around, though, as is Washington. On Sunday, the two are set to face off again. The Patriots assistant knows about the challenge his team is set to face yet again. “Parker Washington is elite,” he said. “He’s a top three guy, in my opinion, in the NFL. He’s unbelievable on offense, but he’s also unbelievable on special teams. And he’s not scared. He’s out there for a reason. He’s a starting receiver, he doesn’t have to be out there, but you can tell that mentality that he has for the team — he’s a team guy. I have so much respect for him what he does on the punt return unit, and the guys blocking for him as well. They’re blocking their tails off for him, because they know how dynamic he is.” This season, Washington’s impact has primarily come on offense. In two games, Jacksonville’s leading receiver has been targeted 18 times with 12 receptions, 181 yards and a touchdown. As a returner, meanwhile, he has been limited to three runbacks for 7 combined yards. Just don’t tell Springer about it. “He’s extremely quick and elusive,” Springer said. “He just has a good feel for making guys miss in space. If you’re on an island with this guy, it’s really hard to bring him down. So, you have to be very disciplined in your coverage, because he can take it to the big field, he can stretch and cut, he can go down the sideline. There’s really nothing — like I said, he’s an elite guy in this league and the elite guys can do anything.” While Springer will be confronted with Washington again on Sunday, he is not necessarily focused on what was but rather what awaits him and his team. Namely, how the Patriots can prevent a similar big play from happening again. “It’s just another opportunity for us to go out there against a very well-coached team,” he said. “And the past is the past. I don’t really think about the past on that team anymore. I just think about what do we have now? What does this team have in Jacksonville? And what do we need to do to help fuel our offense and help fuel our defense to win the game?”
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Josh McDaniels preaches patience with Patriots offense
summary: As the New England Patriots’ offense has gotten off to a slow start through two games, quarterback Drake Maye noted that the unit is still “finding themselves.” For offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels, that’s a typical part of the process at this point in the season. “I think it’s normal,” McDaniels said Thursday. “This time of […]
full_text: As the New England Patriots’ offense has gotten off to a slow start through two games, quarterback Drake Maye noted that the unit is still “ finding themselves .” For offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels, that’s a typical part of the process at this point in the season. “I think it’s normal,” McDaniels said Thursday. “This time of the year is generally an extension of the work you’ve done in training camp and, you know, whether it’s one aspect of the game in terms of situational play or last year I thought we made progress in a running game as we got along. And there’s been many years, I know I’ve lived through a bunch of them, where you start, we all have high expectations and hopes for starting this season looking a certain way and what it requires is just a lot of hard work and improvement. “I don’t know that anybody’s where they want to be at this point in time, but the progress you make going forward is really the most important part of our journey.” Maye noted the Patriots found themselves in a similar spot last season, sitting at 1-2 before scoring 42 points in Week 4 against the Panthers to kick-start an 11-game winning streak. McDaniels has seen similar slow starts unfold plenty of times during his career calling plays, dating beyond 2025. He knows a slow start to the season does not mean the Patriots should completely change directions. “We could sit here and talk about this all day. ’14, ’18, ’21, ’25, every one of those years in my career. And then there’s probably another two or three, four that I could tack on of those,” McDaniels said. “The first month of the season is about growth and improvement. Progress is a big word. And if you jerk the wheel and turn the car into the wall, you’re going to have a problem. “So, I think our guys are really working hard at it. Squeezing harder to try to get a result that you are looking for is often times a bad formula.” Part of that growth will come from better play from Maye himself. Through two games, the quarterback has thrown four interceptions and taken six sacks as the 24-year old has tried to find the balance between aggressiveness and patience. For McDaniels, however, the offense’s performance ultimately comes back to all 11 players on the field. “I mean a mistake is a mistake. But there was a lot of good plays. I’d say too for us offensively, it’s always about the group. It’s always about the group,” McDaniels said. “It’s always about the group. It takes 11 people on offense to make a good play go. That’s what it takes. It always has required that. So, he has to do his part. We have to do our part around him. We have to do a good job as coaches of putting our group in the right position… “Drake made some really good plays the other day and certainly want to try to clean up some of the things that are — putting the ball in harm’s way is obviously something we want to try to do away with.”
author: Brian Hines

title: Week 3 Film Preview: Highlights from the All 22
summary: Raiders 26 – Chargers 14 The Raiders thus far have played two of the worst teams in the NFL over the first two weeks in the Chargers and the Dolphins. While I think the Chargers are likely a better team than the Raiders overall, this past week they made too many mistakes to come away […]
full_text: Raiders 26 – Chargers 14 The Raiders thus far have played two of the worst teams in the NFL over the first two weeks in the Chargers and the Dolphins. While I think the Chargers are likely a better team than the Raiders overall, this past week they made too many mistakes to come away with the divisional win and sent the Jim Harbaugh’s home winless heading into the toughest stretch of schedule in football (yikes LAC). I mention the Raiders schedule to explain the reason they are 2-0 and point to another statistic of theirs that is misleading, a league leading 8 total team sacks. Maxx Crosby and his buddies will need to be grounded if the Saints hope to win, but I firmly believe the Saints are the best OLine and team the Silver and Black have faced yet. Pressure the Passer Timing and Anticipation is crucial to Kirk Cousins's game. The Saints must affect Cousins comfortability with constant pressure to throw him off this weekend and force turnovers. Small errors by the Raiders offense can lead to big results for the defense. pic.twitter.com/MlTuZVoFz3 — Andrew Lotz (@andrewlot3) September 24, 2026 Brandon Staley schemed up some brilliant and effective ways to pressure Lamar Jackson last week and I expect him to do the same this week to attack the limited mobility of Kirk Cousins. The 38 year old with a repaired Achilles tendon will not be able to escape a serious pass rush and will become uncomfortable if Chase Young and the other Saints pass rushers can get home on Sunday. The video above is a good example of how easily mistakes can be made by Cousins if there are any issues in the timing of routes as zone defenders lurk. While the example shows the Raiders keeping a clean pocket and a mistake by the receiver, the Raiders have yet to face a defensive line with the talent that the Saints possess at that position group. The Saints must pit Cousins’s high level of football awareness against him to force him into sacks and turnovers. When a quarterback is using his brain to make up for the lack of arm talent that currently plagues the aging Cousins, added pressure can speed the clock up in his head just enough to throw passes before necessary and lead to crucial errors. To do this, if I were the Saints, I would consistently attack right tackle D.J. Glaze (below) by giving him a full rotation of Chase, Cam and Carl (did I just discover the killer C’s??) with stunts a nickel blitzes sprinkled in. There's an obvious weak link on the Raiders offensive line that the Saints need to exploit this weekend. pic.twitter.com/5thqO9Roxt — Andrew Lotz (@andrewlot3) September 24, 2026 Win the Rushing Battle The Chargers have the cutest running plays (not a complement) in the NFL pic.twitter.com/iNpkaP7Auq — Andrew Lotz (@andrewlot3) September 24, 2026 The Chargers have what I would define as the “Cutest rushing attack in the NFL” with all their cool Mike McDaniel trademark gadget plays that some (me) would call highly unnecessary and were still able to rush for 127 yards. Jim Harbaugh’s squad were able to be successful on the ground by out scheming the Raiders in the run game for most of last Sunday’s matchup. Below you can see that in the box (what is pictured), the Chargers have 7 blockers for 7 defenders (commonly referred to as the offensive having numbers or a hat on a hat) which means that if the Bolts can execute their blocking scheme in the play below, they will be able to run until someone outside the box can make the tackle. This is a problem for the Raiders that I expect the Saints to try to exploit and have their best rushing output of the season in doing so. In their nickel package shown below, the Chargers chose to go away from the triangle which includes the Raiders best run defender and their worst as they use Crosby to hide Taron Johnson (their nickel corner) and run a man blocking scheme I call double insert or double ISO. While this was successful, this would never work running at Maxx Crosby (he immediately beat Joe Alt on this play). When the Saints are able to outnumber the Raiders similar to this look, I expect their zone heavy rushing attack to give the Raiders fits as the Saints have a much better OLine than the Chargers and (although they haven’t produced many yards yet this season) better backs in Eitienne and Kamara which theoretically will have plenty of space to cut into the running lanes. Mistake Free Football The Kellen Moore version of the Saints have yet to play a game without any pre-snap penalties or turnovers to my recollection. The Saints need to take their opportunity Sunday to fine tune their discipline and overcome this final hurdle of becoming a seriously good team. Now that Tyler Shough seems to have settled in completely, I do not foresee the Raiders zone blitz scheme to be an issue for him if he can continue to identify blitzers properly (we saw this vs the Ravens) as the Chargers had countless wide open receivers on Sunday thanks to blown coverages by the Silver and Black. LAC was not able to take advantage of these as Justin Herbert was running for his life most of the game and his receiving corps (if you know you know) did him no favors by dropping multiple could be explosive plays and even (David Njoku) bobbling a pass straight into a defender’s hands after being wide open 20 yards down field. Thankfully, the Saints receiving corps has been one of the better units in the NFL so far this year and unless there is a cataclysmic event in the Dome on Sunday, I have faith that will not happen if Olave, Juwan, Vele, and the rest of the bunch are left open the way some Chargers were. Bonus: Were you aware that Tyler Shough is possibly the funniest quarterback in the NFL. How could you not like this guy? The turns have certainty tabled for the Black and Gold since the Derek Carr days. “This is why Tyler Shough is the best” -Big Cat pic.twitter.com/dOc5rgR3Jb — Barstool Sports (@barstoolsports) September 22, 2026 Keys to Victory Pressure Kirk Cousins to throw off timing Win the rushing yards battle Emphasize discipline and play mistake free

title: Saints vs. Raiders predictions: Bring the noise
summary: After opening the season with back-to-back road games, the New Orleans Saints finally return to Caesars Superdome on Sunday, looking to build on their first win of the season. New Orleans enters Week 3 with a 1-1 record following a 24-17 victory over the Baltimore Ravens. Meanwhile, the Las Vegas Raiders arrive in New Orleans […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - DECEMBER 29: Ameer Abdullah #8 of the Las Vegas Raiders tackled by Pete Werner #20 and Willie Gay #6 of the New Orleans Saints during the first quarter at Caesars Superdome on December 29, 2024 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Sean Gardner/Getty Images) | Getty Images After opening the season with back-to-back road games, the New Orleans Saints finally return to Caesars Superdome on Sunday, looking to build on their first win of the season. New Orleans enters Week 3 with a 1-1 record following a 24-17 victory over the Baltimore Ravens. Meanwhile, the Las Vegas Raiders arrive in New Orleans undefeated at 2-0 under first-year head coach and former Saints offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak. Sunday’s matchup presents an opportunity for the Saints to build some early-season momentum, but it won’t come easy against a Raiders team that has gotten off to a strong start. Through the first two weeks, Tyler Shough has given Saints fans plenty of reasons to be optimistic. After throwing for 410 yards and three touchdowns in the season-opening overtime loss to Detroit, Shough followed up with another solid performance against Baltimore, completing 27 of 34 passes and scoring the go-ahead touchdown on the ground. His connection with wide receiver Chris Olave has already proven to be one of New Orleans’ biggest offensive weapons, and the Saints will need that chemistry again Sunday. However, protecting Shough could be a major concern. With left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. out indefinitely with an ankle injury, New Orleans must find a way to contain Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby, who is capable of disrupting an offense on his own. One of the biggest storylines surrounding Sunday’s matchup is the return of Klint Kubiak, who served as the Saints’ offensive coordinator in 2024. Kubiak has led Las Vegas to a 2-0 start, with veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins leading an offense that has shown it can make big plays. Cousins threw three touchdown passes in the Raiders’ 26-14 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 2, while wide receiver Tre Tucker racked up 119 receiving yards. New Orleans showed improvement defensively against Baltimore, particularly in the second half. The Saints will need another strong performance, especially when it comes to pressuring Cousins and preventing explosive plays. The biggest difference this week is that New Orleans will have a very loud and proud home crowd behind them. Prediction: Saints 34 – Raiders 27 You can expect this one to be another entertaining matchup, with both offenses finding ways to put points on the board. But finally playing in the dome for the first time this season will give the Saints an extra spark, and I think they will make enough plays in the fourth quarter to hand the Raiders their first loss of the season. title: By the Numbers: Saints vs. Raiders
summary: Both the New Orleans Saints and Las Vegas Raiders are coming off road victories ahead of their week three matchup in the Big Easy. Las Vegas defeated the Los Angeles Chargers 26-14 for their second win in as many weeks, while New Orleans upset the Baltimore Ravens 24-17, picking up their first win and improving […]
full_text: Both the New Orleans Saints and Las Vegas Raiders are coming off road victories ahead of their week three matchup in the Big Easy. Las Vegas defeated the Los Angeles Chargers 26-14 for their second win in as many weeks, while New Orleans upset the Baltimore Ravens 24-17, picking up their first win and improving to 1-1. Let’s check out the breakdown of numbers for this week’s contest. 8 : Las Vegas is tied for 1st in the NFL with eight sacks as a team through two games. The Raiders already have five players with at least one sack, so you never know who will wind up getting after the QB. This could be bad news for a Saints team with a struggling offensive line that has already given up eight sacks this year and will now be without starting LT Kelvin Banks Jr. for an extended period after landing on IR with a high ankle sprain. 35 : Las Vegas’ fifth-round selection CB Hezekiah Masses, who rocks jersey number 35, has looked every bit the part of an NFL talent through the Raiders’ first two games. The rookie from California (Cal) is already making his mark in the defensive backfield with two interceptions (tied 1st in the league) and three passes defensed (tied 7th in the league). 55.6 : Kirk Cousins has faced the New Orleans Saints nine times in his career and has a near even split of 5-4 in those games, or a .556 record. Most recently, Cousins swept the division series in 2025 against New Orleans as a member of the Atlanta Falcons, but the veteran QB will now return to the Superdome at the helm of Klint Kubiak’s offense with the Raiders. 60 : New Orleans is celebrating its 60th season as an NFL franchise this year, and Sunday will mark the home opener inside the Caesars Superdome for the celebratory year. 136.5 : After facing two of the top running backs in the NFL in Jahmyr Gibbs and Derrick Henry, the Saints have given up an average of 136.5 yards on the ground per game. Things will not get much easier for New Orleans as they will now hope to slow down agile RB Ashton Jeanty whose managed 210 all-purpose yards thus far. 662 : The Saints have found themselves a QB of the future (and current) in Louisville product Tyler Shough. The second-year QB currently has a league-leading 662 passing yards and will now attempt to throw the first TD pass against the Raiders’ defense this season. 2021 : The Raiders have not begun a season with a 3-0 record since 2021. Las Vegas, then led by QB Derek Carr, had two overtime victories in the first three weeks of the regular season. This is also the last time that the team made the postseason. 2023 : Meanwhile, New Orleans has not gotten out of September with a winning record since 2023, when they beat the Tennessee Titans and Carolina Panthers to open the season. Sunday’s game will have a huge effect on the trajectory of the rest of both squads’ seasons.

title: Domecoming 20 Years Later: The Night the Saints and New Orleans Came Home
summary: On Nov. 1, 1966, the National Football League awarded the city of New Orleans a professional football franchise. At exactly 11:11 a.m., then-NFL commissioner Pete Rozelle delivered the words that would forever change the city: “Professional football has voted a franchise to the state of Louisiana, the city of New Orleans.” The team would later […]
full_text: On Nov. 1, 1966, the National Football League awarded the city of New Orleans a professional football franchise. At exactly 11:11 a.m., then-NFL commissioner Pete Rozelle delivered the words that would forever change the city: “Professional football has voted a franchise to the state of Louisiana, the city of New Orleans.” The team would later be named the Saints, a fitting choice given that the franchise was awarded on All Saints’ Day during a news conference at the Pontchartrain Hotel on St. Charles Avenue. That December, oil and real estate businessman John W. Mecom Jr. purchased the franchise for $8.5 million. At 26, Mecom became the youngest owner in NFL history. On Sept. 17, 1967, the Saints played their first regular-season game at Tulane Stadium. Eight years later, in August 1975, the Superdome became their permanent home. For the next three decades, the Superdome became an integral part of Saints football and the culture surrounding the team. Then came Hurricane Katrina. In August 2005, Katrina devastated New Orleans and the Gulf Coast, flooding most of the city and severely damaging the Superdome. The disaster displaced hundreds of thousands of residents and forced the Saints from their home for the entire 2005 season. With the Superdome unavailable, the Saints played their home games in San Antonio and Baton Rouge. Uncertainty surrounding the future of both the franchise and the city only compounded the challenges facing a community just beginning the long road to recovery. One year later, the Saints finally returned home. On Sept. 25, 2006, the Saints played their first game back in the Superdome, facing the Atlanta Falcons on Monday Night Football before a sold-out crowd of more than 70,000 fans. Appropriately nicknamed “Domecoming,” the game became much more than a football game. It was a symbol of recovery and resilience. Today marks 20 years since that unforgettable night inside the Superdome, when the Saints’ return reminded the world that New Orleans was still standing, still fighting and determined to come back stronger than ever. The emotion inside the Superdome reached another level early in the first quarter when Steve Gleason blocked an Atlanta punt and Curtis Deloatch recovered in the end zone for the Saints’ first touchdown. The moment became one of the most iconic plays in franchise history. That night, the Saints defeated the Falcons 23-3. They went on to finish the season 10-6 and advance to the NFC championship game for the first time in franchise history. The Saints’ remarkable run ended with a loss to the Chicago Bears, but the 2006 season marked the beginning of a new era in New Orleans. More importantly, it reinforced a bond between a football team and its hometown that had been developing for nearly four decades. As New Orleans rebuilt, so did the Saints. Under new head coach Sean Payton and quarterback Drew Brees, a franchise that had spent much of its history searching for sustained success gave a community something to rally around each Sunday. The Saints became more than a source of entertainment. For many, they became a source of hope during one of the most difficult periods in the city’s history. The journey that began with that emotional return to the Superdome in 2006 reached its defining moment three seasons later. On Feb. 7, 2010, the Saints defeated the Indianapolis Colts 31-17 in Super Bowl XLIV, capturing the first championship in franchise history. For generations of Saints fans who had endured losing seasons, heartbreak and years when simply reaching the playoffs seemed impossible, the victory represented far more than a Lombardi Trophy. New Orleans was finally a Super Bowl champion. When the team returned home from Miami, thousands of fans filled the streets near the airport for an impromptu championship celebration that looked and felt like something only New Orleans could produce. Over six decades, players, coaches and owners have changed. Tulane Stadium gave way to the Superdome. The paper bags of the “Aints” era were eventually replaced by division championships, playoff victories and a Super Bowl title. But the connection between the Saints and New Orleans has remained. It can be heard in the chants of “Who Dat?” and seen in the black and gold that fills the city on game days. It lives through generations of families who have passed down their Saints fandom and, in some cases, their season tickets from parents to children and grandchildren. There have been unforgettable victories, devastating losses, seasons of hope and seasons fans would rather forget. Through it all, New Orleans has continued to embrace its football team. Perhaps that is because the Saints and their city share something much deeper than geography. Both know heartbreak. Both know the joy of celebration and the devastation of tragedy. And both have always found a way to come back. Twenty years after the Saints came home to the Superdome and 60 years after Pete Rozelle announced that professional football was coming to New Orleans, that bond remains as much a part of the franchise as the fleur-de-lis on its helmet. The Saints are part of New Orleans, and New Orleans is part of them.

summary: Another week, another draft position, but this time, it’s happening after a win! Interestingly enough, due to the strength of the schedule and the Carolina Panthers winning, the Saints are now projected to select 14th, eventhough they were projected 19th last week. Here are two prospects that the Saints could select at pick 14: LSU […]
full_text: BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA - SEPTEMBER 12: Jordan Seaton #77 of the LSU Tigers in action against the Louisiana Tech Bulldogs at the Tiger Stadium on September 12, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Gus Stark/LSU/University Images via Getty Images) Another week, another draft position, but this time, it’s happening after a win! Interestingly enough, due to the strength of the schedule and the Carolina Panthers winning, the Saints are now projected to select 14th, eventhough they were projected 19th last week. Here are two prospects that the Saints could select at pick 14: LSU OT Jordan Seaton Let’s start with something crazy. So Kelvin Banks Jr., the Saints starting LT, is likely out for the season with an injury. In his limited time, he showed enough to feel comfortable moving forward, but Taliese Fuaga on the other side has been… an interesting experience. Fuaga is getting beat much more than usual, and he’s playing like when he was injured last year. So, with that in mind, taking a tackle may still be in the cards, even if it’s a bit frustrating. Both of the Saints’ tackles can be moved to guard, so although Jeremiah Wright is learning behind Cesar Ruiz, the Saints can try Fuaga at LG in this move. The best tackle available at this spot in the draft is LSU tackle Jordan Seaton, and he has been really good this year. Florida RB Jadan Baugh Sticking with the offense, the Saints have struggled to run the ball to start the season. Blame could, and should, be put on Kellen Moore, but the RB room is also in a weird spot. Kendre Miller was decent in Week 1 but didn’t even play in Week 2; Travis Etienne has been disappointing in his Saints career, and Alvin Kamara isn’t the RB he used to be. Etienne will likely be the only RB left next season, so adding another highly talented player to that room could really improve the rushing attack. He’s such a talented RB who can speed right past defenders, break their ankles, or run right through them.

title: Saints Rookie Report: Week 3 preview
summary: The New Orleans Saints got a win, and even with some injuries in the rookie class, there were still some strong performances. In Week 3, those performances can hopefully continue. DT Christen Miller Miller missed the Ravens game, and it’s a shame because I think he would have had a big game. Hopefully, Miller can […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Barion Brown #19 of the New Orleans Saints looks on against the Baltimore Ravens during an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints got a win, and even with some injuries in the rookie class, there were still some strong performances. In Week 3, those performances can hopefully continue. DT Christen Miller Miller missed the Ravens game, and it’s a shame because I think he would have had a big game. Hopefully, Miller can be back against the Las Vegas Raiders, because if he can, the defensive line could have an even better game. TE Oscar Delp Delp had limited play against the Baltimore Ravens, but he was really impressive. As a blocker, Delp did really well and helped the Saints deal with the pressure the Ravens were sending. One of his best plays of the day happened after Tyler Shough ran out of the pocket and threw it to Delp. It was a simple catch, but his first of his career. After this game, I would say the Saints may view Delp as TE2 right now, and he did outplay Noah Fant. Fant also had a nearly catastrophic false start on the Saints’ final scoring drive, before the Juwan Johnson catch. OG Jeremiah Wright Wright, once again, did not play, and as of now, it does not seem a change will be made. WR Bryce Lance Lance was quieter in the passing game, but as a blocker, he had one of the best plays of the day on Johnson’s catch, where the TE converted a long third down after catching it near the line of scrimmage. His blocking once again shows up as such a difference maker in the offense, and that may continue to keep Brown off the field. With Tyson still being out, Lance will be WR3 once again. WR Barion Brown Speaking of Brown, this was a better week for the young WR. He was not involved in the offense, but he had one of the most important plays of the day. Before the half, after the Saints just gave up a momentum-killing touchdown, Brown had a great return that put the Saints in field goal range. That play made it 14-6 going into halftime, setting up the Saints’ comeback. Hopefully, he can do the same agianst the Raiders. OT Mason Murphy This may be finally Murphy’s time to play. Kelvin Banks Jr. is out moving forward, and the two players likely fighting for his spot are Asim Richards and Murphy. Richards is still the likely choice, but Murphy could be in the running. Injured players: WR Jordyn Tyson DB Lorenzo Styles Jr.

title: NFL Picks Week 3: Coming home
summary: After two weeks, the New Orleans Saints find themselves with a 1-1 record that feels a lot like a 2-0 record. Two difficult road challenges stood in front of the Saints to start the 2026 season and they faced them better than most expected, now they finally come home to the Superdome to face the Las Vegas […]
full_text: Sep 21, 2020; Paradise, Nevada, USA; New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara (41) runs the ball against Las Vegas Raiders cornerback Damon Arnette (20) during the first quarter of a NFL game at Allegiant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports After two weeks, the New Orleans Saints find themselves with a 1-1 record that feels a lot like a 2-0 record. Two difficult road challenges stood in front of the Saints to start the 2026 season and they faced them better than most expected, now they finally come home to the Superdome to face the Las Vegas Raiders. The excitement for the Saints in New Orleans is at a level we haven’t seen in over half a decade, and the atmosphere in the Dome will be absolutely electric. Finally, the Saints are home, and there’s no place like it. Last week, I went 13-3 I told you so: Bills over Lions! What do I know: Ravens over Saints?! *** WEEK 3 Thursday, September 24th – Thursday Night Football Falcons(0-2) at Packers(1-1) Green Bay makes their home debut following a bad loss in Minnesota and an overtime win at the Jets, now they get just what they need in the Atlanta Falcons, the worst team in the NFC. Green Bay wins 34-16. Pick: Packers *** Sunday, September 27th – Early Games Chargers(0-2) at Bills(2-0) Josh Allen and the Buffalo offense has been on an absolute tear to start the season, and now their defense gets just the break they need in the Los Angeles Chargers, the worst team in the AFC. Buffalo wins 30-7. Pick: Bills *** Panthers(1-1) at Browns(1-1) Carolina’s offense has been looking as good as it has in a very long time to start this season, and they will continue that against a Cleveland team fresh off victory in Tampa last week. Carolina wins 26-21. Pick: Panthers *** Jets(1-1) at Lions(1-1) Detroit has faced a difficult slate to open the season, but now their defense will get a bit of a break against the Jets. Detroit wins 28-17. Pick: Lions *** Texans(0-2) at Colts(0-2) No team in the NFL has suffered a more disappointing start than the Texans, but Houston will finally get themselves in the win column this week against their division rivals in Indy. Houston wins 29-23. Pick: Texans *** Patriots(1-1) at Jaguars(1-1) The New England defense has impressed so far this season, but this week their offense finally steps up against a very good opponent. New England wins 33-21. Pick: Patriots *** Chiefs(2-0) at Dolphins(0-2) This mismatch will go just about how everyone expects it will. Kansas City wins 24-10. Pick: Chiefs *** Titans(0-2) at Giants(1-1) It may already be crisis time for the Giants, with Jaxson Dart out for the season, but their defense will carry the day against Tennessee this week. New York wins 19-10. Pick: Giants *** Bengals(2-0) at Steelers(1-1) Joe Burrow and the Bengals will make short work of Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers in this one. Cincinnati wins 33-12. Pick: Bengals *** Seahawks(2-0) at Commanders(1-1) Whether Sam Darnold returns this week or not, the Seattle offense will dominate this game. Seattle wins 34-20. Pick: Seahawks *** Sunday, September 21st – Late Games Cardinals(1-1) at 49ers(2-0) Unsurprisingly, San Francisco will handle Arizona with relative ease in this one. San Francisco 29-19. Pick: 49ers *** Vikings(2-0) at Buccaneers(0-2) The undefeated Vikings will beat the winless Bucs on a game-winning kick in the closing moments in Tampa. Minnesota wins 23-20. Pick: Vikings *** Ravens(1-1) at* Cowboys(1-1) – Rio de Janeiro, Brazil Baltimore will rebound from their Week 2 loss at home with a brilliant offensive performance against Dallas in Rio. Baltimore wins 31-21. Pick: Ravens *** Raiders(2-0) at Saints(1-1) The Raiders come into this game undefeated, under new head coach Klint Kubiak, but those wins came against the two worst teams in the AFC, and both were at home (yes folks, Los Angeles is Raiders Country). Now the Silver and Black gets their first road game in a hostile environment against the Black and Gold in New Orleans. Rob Leonard’s defense will face their toughest competition in Kellen Moore’s never-say-die Saints. Tyler Shough and the Saints’ offense has gotten a lot of credit early this season for their second-half heroics, and deservedly so, but it has been the Saints defense that has made these heroic comebacks possible over the last two weeks. Ultimately it will be the chess match of Kubiak’s offense against Brandon Staley’s defense that will tell the tale of this matchup, and Staley’s defense will rise to the occasion once again. Saints win 27-21. Pick: Saints *** Sunday Night Football Rams(1-1) at Broncos(1-1) – Game of the Week This game could easily be a Game of the Year candidate or a Super Bowl preview. Expect some fireworks in this one, as the atmosphere will be electric. This is certainly a premier matchup of two of the NFL’s very best head coaches, but unfortunately Sean McVay has always had Sean Payton’s number. Los Angeles wins 37-34. Pick: Rams *** Monday, September 28th – Monday Night Football Eagles(2-0) at Bears(1-1) A litany of injuries at the quarterback position for Chicago truly takes the steam out of this primetime matchup. Philadelphia wins 24-13. Pick: Eagles *** That’s how I see it, tell us how you see Week 3 playing out. Leave your comments and insight below!
