title: Eagles Injury Report: DeVonta Smith misses practice, Saquon Barkley limited
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles issued their first official injury report of the week on Thursday in advance of their Week 3 game against the Chicago Bears on Monday Night Football. The Eagles listed four players under DID NOT PARTICIPATE: DeVonta Smith, Tank Bigsby, Will Shipley, and Dallas Goedert. Smith was seen warming up with the team […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 20: DeVonta Smith #6 of the Philadelphia Eagles warms up prior to the game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles issued their first official injury report of the week on Thursday in advance of their Week 3 game against the Chicago Bears on Monday Night Football. The Eagles listed four players under DID NOT PARTICIPATE : DeVonta Smith, Tank Bigsby, Will Shipley, and Dallas Goedert. Smith was seen warming up with the team early in practice but he did not actually participate. He’s listed with a hamstring injury, which is never comforting. As of me typing this sentence, there’s no been reporting on the severity of the issue. Maybe the Eagles are just trying to manage him to get him to Monday. Both Bigsby AND Shipley missing practice doesn’t seem ideal when Saquon Barkley (more on him below) is less than 100%. Those are the only three running backs on the Eagles’ roster. Of course, the team does have Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele, and Jaydon Blue on the practice squad. From that trio, Pierce is probably the top candidate to be temporarily elevated to the roster if the Eagles need an extra running back. Goedert is set to miss multiple games but ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that he’s expected to avoid going on injured reserve. If that’s the case, the Eagles seem to be hoping Goedert can return for the team’s Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers. Otherwise they could’ve just put him on IR, where he would’ve missed at least four games. With Goedert out, one would expect the recently re-signed Zach Ertz to be the Eagles’ top tight end. They have Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins on the roster behind Ertz. The Eagles listed four players under LIMITED PARTICIPATION: Saquon Barkley, Jalen Carter, Jonathan Greenard, and Andrew Mukuba. Barkley reportedly expects to play on Monday night but his limited participation suggest he’s less than 100%. We’ll have to see if he can actually make it through the game. Carter is playing with a cast on his hand due to a wrist injury, so, he’s clearly not 100%. Guessing he’ll suit up against the Bears. Greenard is still not fully participating in practice. It seemed like Week 3 made sense for his debut since there’s an extra day prior to the Monday game. Maybe the Eagles want to be extra cautious with him now that Case Keenum is likely to start against them? Just a guess. If Greenard doesn’t ramp up to full participation over the next two days, it’s hard to see him playing. Mukuba suited up in Week 2 despite being ruled questionable to play with a knee injury. Guessing he’ll be able to play on Monday and the Eagles are managing his practice reps. The Eagles listed one player under FULL PARTICIPATION: Tyler Steen. Steen is a new addition to the report with a shoulder injury. He’s on track to start. PHILADELPHIA EAGLES INJURY REPORT (THURSDAY) DID NOT PARTICIPATE RB Tank Bigsby (abdomen) TE Dallas Goedert (knee) RB Will Shipley (foot) WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) LIMITED PARTICIPATION RB Saquon Barkley (stinger) DT Jalen Carter (wrist) EDGE Jonathan Greenard (pectoral) S Andrew Mukuba (knee) FULL PARTICIPATION OG Tyler Steen (shoulder) CHICAGO BEARS INJURY REPORT (THURSDAY) The Bears’ injury report is an estimation since they did not actually practice on Thursday. Their first session of the week was on Wednesday … but the first injury report of the week ahead of a Monday game always comes out on Thursday. The Bears listed six players under DID NOT PARTICIPATE: starting quarterback Caleb Williams, top backup quarterback Tyson Bagent, 1B running back Kyle Monangai, starting cornerback Tyrique Stevenson, kicker Cairos Santos, and starting defensive tackle Grady Jarrett. Bears head coach Ben Johnson previously said Williams will not practice leading up to Monday’s game. He also described Williams as “week-to-week” as opposed to the comparatively less ominous “day-to-day.” Sure seems like Williams will not suit up for this game while he recovers from the hamstring injury he suffered in Week 2. Bagent was in line to start for Williams until it was revealed that he’s in the concussion protocol. While there’s still time for him to be cleared ahead of Monday’s game, it’s not a good sign for his availability that he was listed under DNP today. The Bears’ vaunted rushing attack is powered by the duo of former Eagle/Philly native D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai. The latter is dealing with a knee injury that caused the Bears to list him under DNP. Something to monitor. The Bears are already missing slot defender Kyler Gordon to the reserve/PUP list. If Stevenson can’t play, Jaylon Johnson will be the only Bears starting cornerback available for this game. And while Johnson is a two-time Pro Bowler, he’s allowing a 118.7 passer rating when targeted in coverage this season. Santos’ status bears watching (no pun intended, I swear). Kicker issues against the Eagles? That would be a new one for Chicago. Jarrett is listed with a rest designation. He’ll be able to play, though the 33-year-old isn’t the same player he used to be earlier in his career. The Bears listed two players under LIMITED PARTICIPATION: Shemar Turner and Noah Sewell. They are ineligible to play on Monday since they need to miss four games before returning from IR. DID NOT PARTICIPATE QB Tyson Bagent (concussion) DL Grady Jarrett (not injury related – rest) RB Kyle Monangai (knee) K Cairos Santos (right hip) DB Tyrique Stevenson (hamstring) QB Caleb Williams (hamstring) LIMITED PARTICIPATION LB Noah Sewell (achilles) DL Shemar Turner (knee)

title: Eagles vs. Bears Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 3 enemy
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are on the road for the second week in a row, this time to take on the Chicago Bears. In order to preview this Week 3 Monday Night Football matchup, I reached out to our enemies over at Windy City Gridrion. The bright Bill Zimmerman kindly took the time took the time […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 28: Darnell Wright #58 of the Chicago Bears blocks Jalen Carter #98 of the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on November 28, 2025 in Philadelphia, United States. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are on the road for the second week in a row, this time to take on the Chicago Bears. In order to preview this Week 3 Monday Night Football matchup, I reached out to our enemies over at Windy City Gridrion . The bright Bill Zimmerman kindly took the time took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let’s take a look at the answers. [For my answers to Bill’s questions about the Eagles, stay tuned to WCG.] 1 – Although the Bears have yet to rule him out as of me typing this sentence, it doesn’t seem like Caleb Williams will be able to play on Monday night. What’s the confidence level in Tyson Bagent if he has to start? To what extent do you expect the game plan to look different with him starting instead of Williams? UPDATE: Or if Case Keenum has to start since Bagent is dealing with a concussion? Alright, let’s dive into the QB situation. We can start briefly with Caleb Williams, who Ben Johnson has called week-to-week. In my experience, week-to-week is Johnson-speak for “he won’t play.” Once he upgrades Caleb Williams to day-to-day, that’s when he has a chance to play. So I agree, it’s not going to be Caleb Williams on Monday. As for Tyson Bagent, he remains in concussion protocol at the time of my answering this question, so I don’t think he will play on Monday, but you can’t say he is definitely out, especially with the extra day of rest. Bagent is what you want in a QB2. He has some mobility to get out of issues; he can operate an offense efficiently, and he doesn’t make a ton of mistakes. But make no mistake, he isn’t a starter. He doesn’t have a strong arm and doesn’t have a lot of dynamic attributes. There is a pretty large percentage of Bears fans that adore Bagent and think he can step in and the offense will barely miss a beat. I am not of that school. The offense takes a significant hit without Caleb Williams, but it shouldn’t be inoperable with Bagent. As for Case Keenum, that’s one hell of a wild card. Keenum has only thrown 140 regular-season passes this decade and has a yards-per-attempt under 6 in that time. That would tell you that Keenum would be awful if he has to play, especially when you consider the last pass he threw was in 2023. However, I think there’s a decent chance that Keenum can operate well in Ben Johnson’s system. I understand they are exhibition games against 3rd-stringers, but he looks like an All-Pro when he plays in the preseason. This past preseason, he was 25 for 40 for 354 yards with 2 TDs and 0 INTs. That’s a passer rating of 107.7. He had similar preseason success last year as well. Does it matter? Probably not, but I just bring it up that he does look far better with Ben Johnson than he did previously in Houston and Cleveland. Will Keenum look like a solid veteran QB in Ben Johnson’s system or the player that looked cooked three years ago and show why he’s basically an assistant QB coach as the team’s QB3? Your guess is as good as mine. 2 – The Bears lead the NFL in yards per rush attempt. What makes their run game so hard to stop? It’s a combination of talent and scheme, but it starts up front. The Bears offensive line is what makes this run game go. The right side of the offensive line can dominate in the run game with Darnell Wright and Jonah Jackson. Garrett Bradbury is probably the weakest link right now at center, but Joe Thuney still is an elite guard on the right, and the left tackle continues to be “good enough” whether it’s been Braxton Jones or Theo Benedet. But it’s not just the talent of the offensive line; it’s how Ben Johnson puts his linemen in positions to succeed. The scheme works in such a way that when linemen need to scrape and get to the second level, they are in a great position to wall off the linebacker rather than chase them. They did a great job neutralizing Derrick Brown in week one, and you saw what they did against the Eagles’ front last November. But it’s not invincible. Brian Flores did a great job scheming up defensive fronts that gave the Vikings the advantage, and I’m sure Vic Fangio has learned some things from last year, and I’m sure he’s been watching the Flores tape from last week and getting some ideas as well. But I don’t want to discredit D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai. They are both quality running backs. A lot of Bears fans, myself included, were mostly out on Swift, but he’s been a different player since Johnson has arrived. He’s not the same guy in Detroit that seemed to avoid contact. He runs downhill and runs hard when he does it. Monangai is the perfect RB2 in this system. He doesn’t have elite speed, but he takes great angles and has the ability to break tackles when need be. With Caleb Williams out, the running game is going to be crucial. 3 – Through two games, the Bears have allowed the third-most yards per play in the NFL. What are the issues on defense? The issues are a lack of talent. I hate to just make it that simple, but that’s what it comes down to. I know the Vikings only had 9 points, but the field was insanely wet, and it rained hard for the entire game. So I’m not ready to say the defense figured anything out, especially when it’s an offense led by Carson Wentz. In the secondary, Kyler Gordon and Coby Bryant were two key pieces, and they are both injured. Jaylon Johnson does not look like the same player he was a couple of years ago, and Tyrique Stevenson can make plays, but he also gets torched multiple times per game. Rookies Dillon Thieneman and Malik Muhammad have both been bright spots for the team so far. The linebacking group was supposed to be a strength, but Devin Bush has been a non-factor. He’s been getting lost in traffic and hasn’t been able to utilize his speed to make plays. TJ Edwards is slow and can still be effective in the run game, but he’s not good in coverage. The defensive line is also a major concern. Last offseason, they signed Grady Jarrett and Dayo Odeyingbo, and both of them have been hugely disappointing. [Former Eagle] Kentavius Street, who was on a practice squad last year, is starting as their other defensive tackle. That’s never good. Austin Booker continues to improve as an edge player but still isn’t a game changer. Montez Sweat is easily the team’s best defensive lineman, but he just doesn’t have much help around him. I expect the Bears to massively overhaul this defense in 2027 when they can get out of a few of these contracts, but for 2026, it is what it is. 4 – What’s the biggest matchup in the Bears’ favor and the biggest matchup against their favor? Well, I think the easiest one is the biggest disadvantage, and that will be the Eagles offensive line vs. the Bears defensive line. I understand Landon Dickerson is out, and the Eagles offensive line isn’t quite what it used to be, but it’s still a strong unit, and the Bears defensive line just isn’t. If the Philly OL can’t control the line of scrimmage, that would be rather surprising. I think the biggest advantage for them is the fact that the Eagles are struggling to stop the run right now, and the Bears block it extremely well. Maybe it’s a cliché, but I think this game is going to come down to controlling the line of scrimmage. Both teams have strong offensive lines and have a chance to control the line when they have the ball. I think the Bears need to really have long drives and keep their defense off the field. Can they do it without Caleb Williams? We will see on Monday night. 5 – Who wins this game and why? With the Eagles currently listed as 3.5-point road favorites, what’s your score prediction? This comes down to Caleb Williams. If he were healthy, I would be picking the Bears, but he isn’t, so that makes it difficult to do so. I think the…

title: Eagles News: Sean Mannion says “the screen game’s going to be a big part of what we do”
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Maybe it’ll eventually get better but it’s hard to feel good about the Eagles running a successful screen at this point in time. Probably shouldn’t try to lean heavily into them! Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 01: Philadelphia Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion is shown during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 1st, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Complex in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Maybe it’ll eventually get better but it’s hard to feel good about the Eagles running a successful screen at this point in time. Probably shouldn’t try to lean heavily into them! Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Eagles refuse to stop running play that hits a brick wall every time: ‘We’re close’ – NJ.com For the second consecutive week, the Eagles did not make any positive plays on screens. But that won’t stop Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion from calling more of them. “I think we’re close on a few of them,” Mannion told reporters on Wednesday. “I think there’s some fundamental things to clean up a little bit. I think we had a couple that were fundamental based, a couple that were just execution based, but the screen game’s going to be a big part of what we do and called a couple of them that were close and a couple that I think will across the season be more productive plays moving forward.” During the Eagles’ Week 1 victory over the Washington Commanders on Sept. 13, Lemon lost three and five yards on two screens. Lemon was tackled instantly on both attempts because they weren’t blocked well. Until the Eagles improve their timing and blocking on these plays, they won’t work. Go Birds! Join Eagles fans on the SB Nation app! Share every touchdown celebration, big defensive stop and passionate game-day opinion with fellow Eagles fans. Join our live game chat Browse with fewer ads Jump easily between communities and conversations Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . The Eagles Have Thrown Seven Screen Passes This Season for -15 Yards – Crossing Broad With that caveat, the Eagles have now run seven screen this year for a total of -15 yards. They’ve completed 5 of these 7 passes and the other two were blown up by defensive linemen. They’re averaging -2.1 yards per screen attempt. […] In conclusion – yes. The Eagles are horrific in the screen game. Abhorrent and ghastly. The numbers confirm what you have witnessed with your own eyeballs. 6 thoughts on Zach Ertz’s return to the Eagles – BGN So, how does Ertz factor in here? The Eagles need to be honest with themselves about where their running game is at right now. Maybe it’ll improve down the line. For now, though, their strength is throwing the ball. Hurts looks great. The wide receivers are inspiring confidence. The offense should be leaning into their passing attack. Ertz can be one of the targets to help contribute to this approach. Also, if Nick Sirianni and Sean Mannion are truly as insistent on “staying on schedule” by getting to third-and-manageable as they purport to be, they can sub out ineffective running plays with short targets to Ertz that are likely to be more fruitful. Can the Eagles’ Jordan Davis keep the Bears’ 2 running backs in check? – Windy City Gridiron While the Bears no longer have Dalman, and Garrett Bradbury has not yet proven to be a perfect replacement, the duo of Jackson and Thuney in the middle should go a long way to help open up holes in the middle of the line. In looking at Davis’ snap count last season, he found himself on about 66% of snaps in most games, including the Bears. So far this season he is hovering around 50%, so I would expect the Bears to test his conditioning in the middle early and often with a power running attack. If the Bears can wear down Davis in the middle, we could see another big day from the rushing attack. If Monangai and Swift are unable to break loose — it’s going to be a long day at the office for Keenum. Eagles-Bears preview: 5 things to watch – PhillyVoice 5) Can the interior of the Eagles’ offensive line start playing better? In Week 1, an obviously not-right Landon Dickerson gave up pressure all day to a bad Commanders defensive line. In Week 2, after Dickerson was placed on IR, Cam Jurgens moved from C to LG, and Drew Kendall filled in at C. The interior of the line struggled yet again, with Jurgens having an alarming game. Of course, part of the reason for Jurgens’ poor performance was because he was trying to block the best interior defensive lineman in the game in Jeffery Simmons. The Bears don’t have any players along their defensive line anywhere remotely as good as Simmons, which presents an opportunity for improvement. And certainly, if the Eagles are going to contend for a Super Bowl this year, the offensive line has to be a lot better. Coming and Going – Iggles Blitz Kenny Moore has spent most of his career playing in the slot. He was with the Colts when Nick Sirianni was there so they have experience together. Vic Fangio was asked about Moore in his PC today and said he knew nothing about him and hadn’t watched Moore. This is a Howie move, not something the defensive coaches pushed for. The addition of Moore could mean Michael Carter will focus on playing safety. He’s been the top backup at slot and safety to this point. We’ll find out more about the plan for Moore and the other DBs in time. We can only speculate for now. Welcome to the Jalyx Hunt Show, right on schedule for the Eagles – The Athletic Jordan Mailata practiced against Hunt every day this summer. He saw the strides Hunt made — and when asked what’s different with Hunt this year, he referenced the exact lesson that Hunt took from top pass rushers. “Baby Jalyx and Jalyx now?” Mailata said. “One, I think he’s bigger, faster. He’s stronger. But then two, the confidence he plays with, and I think that attributes to his hard work, the coaching, and the style of player that they ordered him to be. …Now we have this product — now we’re still chipping away at that — but his confidence is probably the biggest game-changer, knowing that he can play with the best of them.” It’s unlike Hunt’s first training camp. Put him against a young tackle, and he’s the one hard to block. Hunt isn’t near Johnson’s status, but it’s said that rookie linemen might one day call home marveling going against Jalyx Hunt. “I don’t know when that will be,” Hunt said. “I don’t know what that will look like. But the day someone’s like, ‘Oh, snap, you’re Jalyx Hunt,’ you’re excited to be in the room with me? That’ll be pretty cool. And I’ll flash back to this moment when somebody asked me in my third year.” Fantasy playbook: NFL Week 3 Shadow Reports, lineup locks and projected scores – ESPN Fantasy scoop: Caleb Williams (hamstring) is likely to miss this game, which positions Tyson Bagent (who is in the league’s concussion protocol) or Case Keenum to start. It would be the first start for either quarterback since the 2023 season. Bagent played four full games that season (the only four of his career) and failed to impress, throwing three touchdowns and averaging 11.9 fantasy PPG. full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - DECEMBER 21: DK Metcalf #4 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks on during the game against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field on December 21, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s been a tough start to the season for the Pittsburgh Steelers both on and off the field. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr has yet to take the field this season after a summer full of contract negotiations that ended without a long-term deal, and they’ve scored just 23 points through two games. While trade rumors have been swirling regarding Porter over the last number of weeks due to his lack of long-term deal, nothing has taken place at the time of writing. Bryan DeArdo of CBS Sports , though, put forward an idea that would see Pittsburgh move on from not just Porter, but DK Metcalf, as well. DeArdo pitches a trade that would send the pair of Steelers and a 2027 fourth-round pick to the Detroit Lions in exchange for a first-round pick and wide receiver Jameson Williams. “Let’s start with the Steelers getting their coveted first-round pick and the Lions getting Porter,” DeArdo writes. “There’s also the layer of the Lions getting draft compensation from Pittsburgh after giving them a first-round pick (the Steelers would probably offer a lower draft pick since they are trading the better receiver, at least on paper)… If Metcalf and the offense continue to struggle in the coming weeks, however, the Steelers should consider making such a move. While it’s only been two games, it’s clear that the Steelers’ offense is way away from being a top-tier unit. If that continues to be the case, the Steelers should be willing to sacrifice some potential success this year, as it puts them in a better position down the road.“ While the idea of a trade of this magnitude coming to fruition is rare, it would be one that many Steelers fans would sprint to submit to the league office. Landing the speedster Williams would give the offense a bit more juice, while landing a first-round pick could help a potential trade up in the draft for a quarterback. title: Steelers’ offensive line decisions continue to plague struggling offense
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers’ offensive line decisions continue to be puzzling. Like a simplified 24-piece puzzle that’s scrambled into 1,000. They just can’t get it right. 42-year-old Aaron Rodgers was constantly under pressure when the Steelers lost 20-3 to the New England Patriots. Better defenses await in the following weeks. The problems didn’t begin when the […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - SEPTEMBER 20: Troy Fautanu #76 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks to block during the first half of the NFL game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers’ offensive line decisions continue to be puzzling. Like a simplified 24-piece puzzle that’s scrambled into 1,000. They just can’t get it right. 42-year-old Aaron Rodgers was constantly under pressure when the Steelers lost 20-3 to the New England Patriots. Better defenses await in the following weeks. The problems didn’t begin when the first snap hit Rodgers’ hands against the Falcons two weeks ago, but date back to the first day Mike McCarthy was hired. McCarthy and Omar Khan’s plan for the offensive line didn’t make sense from the start. Pittsburgh decided to move starting right guard Mason McCormick and right tackle Troy Fautanu to the left side of the line at the start of offseason workouts. What seemed like a confusing move has resulted in someone falling asleep on their keyboard, pressing the “Q” button with the number of questions that ensued. Why? Was it necessary? Did it make sense? In theory, the decision made sense… on paper. Fautanu played left tackle at Washington, and McCormick played left guard at South Dakota State. You’d think a former first-round pick in Fautanu would adapt back to the position he’s comfortable with, but this isn’t Kansas anymore, Toto. Life in the NFL at the tackle spots is different from college, ask Broderick Jones. How’d that one turn out? Dan Moore was seemingly incapable of playing the right side and forced Jones to a position he wasn’t comfortable with. Has the new staff made better choices with the line than Mike Tomlin’s? It seems like the decisions are coming from inside the front office – hello, Khan and Andy Weidl. Keeping the cohesion with Fautanu and McCormick made sense, but if it’s not broken, why try to fix it? The Steelers had a stable right side of the offensive line intact for years to come, but made a non-problem a glaring weakness. Former seventh-round pick and swing tackle Spencer Anderson has been tasked with holding down the fort at right guard. The fort was ransacked and overtaken by the Patriots on Sunday. Anderson allowed seven pressures against New England in Foxboro, the most of any right guard in football last week. The Patriots sacked Rodgers four times and forced two fumbles, one resulting in a scoop-and-score. He’s been sacked six times and pressured on 29 drop-backs through two games. Right tackle Dylan Cook did a decent job replacing Jones last season on the left side and became the leader in the clubhouse to start at right. He’s allowed more defenders to easily move past him than a PNC Park turnstile on bobblehead night. It’s not just the 29th-ranked passing game (175 yards per game) that’s struggled. The Steelers are only averaging 74.5 yards per game on the ground, also 29th in the league, and are 30th in total yards. Mike McCarthy’s offense has scored 16 points through his first two games. Matt Canada’s unit scored 33. Arthur Smith’s offense scored 31. Not a good look for the Steelers’ first offensive head coach in over 50 years. Center Zach Frazier is the only holdover from the 2025 offensive line. First-round pick Max Iheanachor dealt with an injury in training camp that hampered his development, but it’s beyond time we see what the rookie out of Arizona State has to offer the team. The Steelers placed themselves in a difficult position by picking Iheanachor and only committing him to the right side, partly resulting in the shift in dynamics. Wouldn’t it have been easier to change one thing (Iheanachor at left) than two? The lack of cohesion during camp was startling and is likely playing a factor for offensive line coach James Campen. Pittsburgh rotated Anderson and Brock Hoffman at right guard, plus Cook, Jones, and Iheanachor at right tackle before training Jones at the end of preseason. If you want everyone on the same page, why not keep them together for every rep and workout? The game of musical chairs continued with the Steelers rotating Anderson and Cook between the left and right sides during the media viewing window of practice on Wednesday. Hoffman and Iheanachor both worked exclusively on the right. They are trying to clean up their own mess and fix gaps in pre-snap communication deeper than Pittsburgh potholes in December. Time is ticking on how long Rodgers can hold up and prevent getting hurt behind this unit after taking nasty hits against the Patriots. Can it possibly get worse? I’m afraid to even ask.

title: Seahawks All-22 review: How Beau Stephens performed in his NFL debut
summary: Last week, we talked about how Jadarian Price was essentially the only rookie worth focusing on in this series. Somehow, that changed pretty quickly. Against the Arizona Cardinals, the Seattle Seahawks went from 24 rookie snaps in Week 1 to 53 in Week 2, with Price continuing to see a significant role while fifth-round guard […]
full_text: Last week, we talked about how Jadarian Price was essentially the only rookie worth focusing on in this series. Somehow, that changed pretty quickly. Against the Arizona Cardinals, the Seattle Seahawks went from 24 rookie snaps in Week 1 to 53 in Week 2, with Price continuing to see a significant role while fifth-round guard Beau Stephens made his NFL debut. Julian Neal also saw a couple of defensive snaps late in the game, while Avery Smith continued to contribute on special teams. Let’s analyze some of the key plays from this game! All data used in this article was taken from PFF. Jadarian Price, Running Back (24 snaps) Price left the game with a chest injury that, at least initially, did not appear to be serious. Had he stayed healthy, there’s a good chance he would have surpassed his career-high on Notre Dame of 15 touches. Instead, he finished with 14: 13 carries for 52 yards and one reception for eight yards. The numbers were solid, especially considering he also had a 25-yard run, but the tape showed both why Seattle was willing to give him a significant workload and why there is still plenty for him to clean up. Price’s ball-security concerns weren’t just pre-draft noise at Notre Dame. He had a tendency to carry the ball high through contact, leaving it exposed.That shows up here. Watch the previous snap, too—the same issue is visible. This is something Seattle needs to keep emphasizing. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-24T20:17:11.659Z Let’s start with the obvious one. A lot of the pre-draft discussion around Price’s fumbles seemed to downplay the issue, but it was a real concern during his time at Notre Dame. Price has a tendency to carry the ball relatively high when he enters contact, leaving it exposed and giving defenders an opportunity to attack it. That’s exactly what happens here. And if you watch the snap immediately before the fumble, you can see a similar issue with ball security. The technique hasn’t disappeared just because he got to the NFL. This is something Seattle will need to continue emphasizing with him, particularly as his workload increases. I really liked this snap coming right after the fumble.Price responded with confidence. He makes his cut, lowers his shoulder, takes the contact and squeezes out extra yards.For a rookie coming off his first NFL fumble, that immediate response says a lot about his confidence. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-24T20:18:51.937Z I really liked this snap coming immediately after the fumble. Price wasn’t put in the doghouse after the mistake. Instead, Seattle went right back to him, and he immediately showed that the turnover wasn’t going to change how he approached the game. He makes his cut, doesn’t try to avoid contact, lowers his shoulder and still manages to squeeze out a few extra yards. For a rookie coming directly off his first NFL fumble, there is something to be said about responding this way. Here’s another area where Price can improve.Seattle runs a long trap with Grey Zabel pulling. Price’s aiming point should be the guard’s left shoulder, but he hesitates when the path isn’t clean and briefly considers bouncing outside before cutting back in.Those extra steps cost him some burst. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-24T20:19:44.318Z Here’s another area where Price has room to improve. Seattle runs a long trap here, with Grey Zabel pulling. I believe Price’s aiming point should be the left shoulder of the guard. Instead, Price sees that the initial path isn’t completely clean, hesitates and briefly considers bouncing the run outside before cutting back inside. Those extra steps cost him some of his initial burst. Price takes an extra lateral step before cutting. His acceleration still gets him positive yardage, but that wasted movement matters.At the NFL level, hesitation can turn a 4-yard gain into a much bigger run. He’s still learning to trust his reads and get north faster. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-24T20:21:12.121Z This snap makes the issue even clearer. Price takes one additional lateral step before making his cut. He still gets positive yardage because of his acceleration, but the wasted movement is noticeable. This is the kind of thing that can be easy to overlook because the play still gains positive yardage, but at the NFL level, those hesitation steps can be the difference between a four-yard gain and a much bigger run. And, again, this is not unusual for a rookie. Price is still learning how quickly he needs to commit to his reads at this level. Once he becomes more decisive with his initial read and gets north faster, there’s a good chance these runs start producing significantly more yardage. Here, Price is much more decisive. He doesn’t waste any steps, makes a clean cut and immediately attacks the edge with his explosiveness. This probably ends in a touchdown if he doesn’t slip. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-24T20:22:07.818Z Here, Price is much more decisive. He makes his read, cuts outside with clean tech and immediately puts his speed and explosiveness on display as he attacks the edge. This probably ends up as a touchdown if he doesn’t slip. Price’s best play so far.He patiently lets the FB and RT blocks develop, sees the RT lose inside, then explodes through the opening and attacks the edge for 25 yards. Great balance after contact, too.And excellent block by JSN here. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-24T20:23:50.282Z This was probably Price’s best play until now. It’s a 25-yard run, but what stands out isn’t simply the final result. Price does a good job reading the development of the blocks from the fullback and right tackle, allowing the blocks to develop instead of immediately committing to the first available gap. He waits for the right moment, see that RT is losing inside then explodes through the opening and attacks the edge. He also shows good balance after the first tackle attempt, keeping himself upright and continuing to gain yards staying on the field. This is the version of Price Seattle wants to see more consistently. The explosiveness is already there. The next step is making the reads and decisions that allow him to access that explosiveness more often. And, as a quick aside: excellent block by JSN here. Bud Clark, Defensive Back (0 snaps) IR. Julian Neal, Cornerback (2 snaps) Neal finally got onto the field, although only during garbage time on Arizona’s final drive. Julian Neal first NFL tackle — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-24T20:28:28.877Z He played two defensive snaps and recorded his first defensive tackle as a Seahawk. There isn’t much to evaluate from such a small sample, but getting those first regular-season snaps out of the way is still part of the process for a rookie who has spent most of his time only on special teams. Beau Stephens, Guard (27 snaps) This was the surprise of the rookie class from a playing-time perspective. Stephens played 27 snaps in his NFL debut, while Christian Haynes handled 43. Mike Macdonald clarified that this wasn’t necessarily a planned rotation between the two guards, but Seattle still found a way to get Stephens meaningful playing time. With Anthony Bradford now on injured reserve , those 27 snaps could prove especially important as the Seahawks figure out what they have in the rookie. With Anthony Bradford now on injured reserve and expected to miss at least four games, those snaps could become extremely important for Stephens. Beau loses the initial hand battle against Josh Sweat and never establishes himself in the rep. His feet also need to be quicker here.The positive: Stephens keeps fighting after losing early, helping Lock escape the pressure.Also, good lord, what a terrible drop by Shaheed. — (@alexcastrofilho.bsky.social) 2026-09-24T20:24:58.937Z This was a pressure allowed by Beau. He lines up against EDGE Josh Sweat and loses the initial hand battle, failing to establish himself in the rep. His feet also need to move…

title: Seahawks vs. Commanders predictions: Expect another big game from Seattle’s rushing attack
summary: The Seattle Seahawks enters Week 3 with a 2-0 record and will travel to Maryland to take on the Washington Commanders and try and extend their winning streak to 13 games. The Seahawks are currently 7.5-point favorites at FanDuel Sportsbook, with the total set at 40.5 points. This matchup looks considerably different than it did […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 20: Jadarian Price #8 of the Seattle Seahawks rushes the football against the Arizona Cardinals during the NFL game at State Farm Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. The Seahawks defeated the Cardinals 31-7. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks enters Week 3 with a 2-0 record and will travel to Maryland to take on the Washington Commanders and try and extend their winning streak to 13 games. The Seahawks are currently 7.5-point favorites at FanDuel Sportsbook , with the total set at 40.5 points. This matchup looks considerably different than it did when the lines first opened. Washington is 0-2 after losing 37-20 to Dallas and will be without Jayden Daniels, while Seattle is still waiting to determine whether Sam Darnold will return from his injury. That uncertainty makes quarterback-specific bets less appealing for now. Instead, there are several other markets that stand out, particularly with Seattle’s rushing attack and its defense. Here are four predictions for Seahawks-Commanders. 1. Jadarian Price scores a touchdown Jadarian Price’s status is one of the things to monitor before kickoff, but if the rookie is active, I like his chances of finding the end zone. Price left Seattle’s 31-7 victory over Arizona with a chest injury, although his initial X-rays were negative. He was limited in practice, keeping the door open for him to play against Washington. Price has already shown why Seattle invested a first-round pick in him. Price had 52 rushing yards on 10 carries against New England in Week 1 before adding 52 yards on 13 carries against Arizona, including a 25-yard run. Prediction: Jadarian Price anytime touchdown scorer 2. Jaxon Smith-Njigba goes over 90 receiving yards At this point, there isn’t much reason to stop expecting big numbers from Jaxon Smith-Njigba. JSN has 17 receptions for 277 yards and four touchdowns through two games, including a three-touchdown performance against Arizona. He has quickly become the focal point of Seattle’s passing game, regardless of who is playing quarterback. The bigger question is whether Washington can find a way to slow him down. The Commanders enter this game after allowing 37 points to Dallas, while Seattle’s offense has already shown it can generate explosive plays through multiple areas of the field. Seattle could also have opportunities to attack through the air if Washington commits extra defenders to stopping the run. The one concern is game script. If Seattle controls the game early, there may not be enough passing volume for JSN to approach another 150-yard performance. Still, his role makes 90 yards a reasonable target. Prediction: Jaxon Smith-Njigba over 90 receiving yards 3. Seahawks cover -7.5 The current FanDuel line has Seattle favored by 7.5 points. That is a larger number than the Seahawks have had to cover in either of their first two games, but there are reasons to believe Seattle can create enough separation. The Seahawks have outscored their opponents 44-17 through two games. The defense has been the team’s biggest constant, while the offense has found ways to produce despite the uncertainty at quarterback. Washington, meanwhile, is 0-2 and will have to adjust to playing without Daniels. Marcus Mariota will take over at quarterback, changing the way the Commanders can attack Seattle’s defense. The biggest concern with laying 7.5 points is Seattle’s offensive ceiling if the quarterback situation remains unsettled. But the Seahawks don’t necessarily need another 30-point performance to cover. If Seattle establishes its rushing attack and controls the clock, a two-score victory is within reach. Prediction: Seahawks -7.5 4. Under 40.5 total points The total is currently set at 40.5 points at FanDuel. This might seem strange after Seattle scored 31 points last week, but the Seahawks have yet to play a game that went over this number. Their defense has also allowed just 17 points through the first two weeks. Washington has gone in the opposite direction, with both of its games going over the closing total. But the Commanders will now have to play without Daniels, potentially changing the way they approach the game offensively. Without their starting quarterback, Washington could lean more heavily on the running game and shorter throws rather than asking Mariota to consistently attack downfield against Seattle’s defense. Seattle could also become more run-heavy if it builds a lead, which would help shorten the game and reduce the number of possessions available to both teams. A game finishing somewhere in the 20s for Seattle and the 10s for Washington would comfortably stay below the current number. Prediction: Under 40.5 points Final score prediction The biggest variable remains Seattle’s quarterback situation, but the Seahawks have enough talent around the position to make that uncertainty less important than it might appear. Seattle should be able to establish its rushing attack against Washington, while its defense has the matchup to make life difficult for a Commanders offense without Daniels. I expect Washington to keep things competitive early, but Seattle should pull away in the second half. Seahawks 24, Commanders 13 That gives Seattle an 11-point victory, enough to cover the current 7.5-point spread while keeping the game below the 40.5-point total. 12s, make your voices heard on the SB Nation app! title: Seahawks will continue Christian Haynes, Beau Stephens right guard rotation
summary: Seattle Seahawks starting right guard Anthony Bradford was a (kind of) surprising scratch last week against the Arizona Cardinals after picking up a hip injury in practice. Christian Haynes started at right guard in his place, but he wasn’t the only one seeing time on the line as rookie Beau Stephens got some snaps as […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - AUGUST 28: Beau Stephens #60 of the Seattle Seahawks leaves the field after an NFL preseason game between the Seattle Seahawks and Kansas City Chiefs on Aug 28, 2026 at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Seattle Seahawks starting right guard Anthony Bradford was a (kind of) surprising scratch last week against the Arizona Cardinals after picking up a hip injury in practice. Christian Haynes started at right guard in his place, but he wasn’t the only one seeing time on the line as rookie Beau Stephens got some snaps as well. This week, Bradford was placed in injured reserve and will miss at least the next four games. Offensive coordinator Brian Fleury confirmed that Haynes and Stephens will rotate at RG again this week on the road against the Washington Commanders. “Yeah, I think that those two will continue to rotate in a similar situation. It’ll just be determined by the state of the game,” Fleury said in Thursday’s press conference. Considering the fact that the Seahawks rushed for over 150 yards against the Cardinals on the way to putting 31 points on the scoreboard, both of those players acquitted themselves well. Fleury agreed with that sentiment, and was pleased by their performance. “I thought Beau handled his first actual NFL snaps pretty well,” Fleury said. “We were deliberate in how we were going to sub him in. It wasn’t a set rotation. We just knew that there were going to be times in the game where we could just say, ‘Hey, this is going to be your series and see how he functioned, and I thought he did well. I was happy with how Christian played as well with the amount of snaps that he had. That’s quite a bit of volume compared to what he’s normally gotten.” It remains to be seen whether this rotation will continue for the entirety of Bradford’s absence or if either Haynes or Stephens will take hold of the position. Ideally, it would be Stephens since he’s under contract for multiple years, but in reality it will almost surely be Bradford’s job when he comes off IR. Still, this is a good chance for Haynes and Stephens to try and secure themselves a spot on the burgeoning Seahawks offensive line.

summary: The Seattle Seahawks may very well have Sam Darnold ready to return to action after just one game missed. In Darnold’s case, he injured his […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks may very well have Sam Darnold ready to return to action after just one game missed. Seattle’s starting quarterback was a full participant in Thursday’s practice, plus he had media availability, which is typically a positive sign toward playing for anyone who’s iffy due to injury. In Darnold’s case, he injured his glute just five plays into the opening game against the New England Patriots, and while the initial timeline ranged from a couple of weeks to over a month , there has been more consistently positive messaging in the lead-up to this week regarding Darnold’s health. “Feeling good,” Darnold said on Thursday prior to practice. “For me, especially during this week, taking it day-by-day. Continuing to balance the reps and do everything I need to get ready.” “I’m striving for [playing on Sunday],” he added. “I’m taking it day-by-day. Also, don’t want to jinx anything.” Drew Lock deputized extremely well for Darnold in Seattle’s 31-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals, throwing three touchdown passes to Jaxon Smith-Njigba while only suffering one sack and zero turnovers. It seems as if he won’t be needed to start as often as originally thought, but we’ll see how Friday goes. While Darnold looks like he’s another practice away from coming back, there is one concerning name who’s been added to the injury report. Safety Julian Love, who practiced on Wednesday, was a DNP for Thursday with a calf injury. That is worth monitoring for Friday’s game designations, especially as Ty Okada is still a DNP with his hamstring issue. Seattle has Rodney Thomas II and A.J. Finley as available backups, and now it’s possible both could be pressed into starting duties. Maxen Hook and D’Anthony Bell are also available off the practice/ready squad. Here’s the full Seahawks injury report for Thursday. All things considered, only Love, Brandon Pili, and Jadarian Price are clear question marks for Sunday.

title: Why Anthony Bradford’s injury is an early 2027 audition for Christian Haynes, Beau Stephens
summary: The Seattle Seahawks enjoyed a mostly healthy offensive line throughout 2025, with only Charles Cross and Jalen Sundell missing regular season action. For at least the next month of the 2026 season, the reigning Super Bowl champions will be without their starting right guard. Anthony Bradford was placed on injured reserve ahead of the team’s […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks enjoyed a mostly healthy offensive line throughout 2025, with only Charles Cross and Jalen Sundell missing regular season action. For at least the next month of the 2026 season, the reigning Super Bowl champions will be without their starting right guard. Anthony Bradford was placed on injured reserve ahead of the team’s Week 3 road game against the Washington Commanders. Bradford missed the Week 2 win over the Arizona Cardinals with knee and hip injuries, but Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald indicated that Bradford should be back sooner (after the minimum four games missed) than later. For however long Bradford is out, the right guard duties will go to Christian Haynes and/or rookie Beau Stephens. In the Cardinals game, Haynes took 43 snaps to Stephens’ 27, or roughly a 60-40 split. The bigger picture at right guard is what happens next season. Bradford is set to become an unrestricted free agent, and while he’s coming off his best (and healthiest) season, the odds of an extension don’t seem particularly high. Extending Jalen Sundell (who’s a restricted free agent this offseason) is arguably a higher priority than keeping Bradford. So who’s going to be the likely Bradford replacement in 2027? That could’ve been Haynes as far back as 2024, when he was a third-round pick from UConn. He had an opportunity to earn a starting spot over Bradford when Anthony was in his second season, but Haynes only mustered up sporadic snap-splitting before the Seahawks pulled the plug on that idea. When Bradford went down with a season-ending ankle injury against the Arizona Cardinals, Haynes played the remainder of the game, but the coaching staff preferred Sataoa Laumea to Haynes. Laumea is currently not on an NFL roster. Okay, throw out the Ryan Grubb/Scott Huff year because they were just boiling poo in a kettle . Under John Benton, surely Haynes would be poised for greater things in a more familiar blocking scheme? Well, he was tested out at center during training camp, and there wasn’t the slightest hint of Bradford’s spot being threatened. In his limited regular season playing time, he did replace an injured Grey Zabel against the Los Angeles Rams, then an injured/resting Anthony Bradford versus the Minnesota Vikings, but 10 of his 32 snaps came at center. Enter Beau Stephens, Seattle’s prized Day 3 pick after giving up 2027 draft capital to trade back into the fifth round. That level of investment suggested that Haynes was on the roster bubble or even a trade piece during camp and preseason. Haynes responded with an impressive July and August, comfortably cementing himself as the main backup guard on both sides. Stephens was mostly with the third-team before Mason Richman’s injury bumped him up the depth chart. And yet, he hasn’t yet cemented himself as someone who gets 100% of the snaps when called upon. Both Haynes and Stephens had encouraging reps on film last Sunday. Cardinals had nine players in the box against this George Holani outside zone run. Did not matter. Christian Haynes did a great job sealing Roy Lopez back inside, then throws him to ground. Zabel getting good push, Sundell gets to linebacker. Bully ball. #Seahawks pic.twitter.com/T5NvnEgotu — Corbin K. Smith (@CorbinSmithNFL) September 22, 2026 Christian Haynes played well on Sunday, but it's getting harder to ignore Beau Stephens. Check out the finish by #70 on this 10-yard run by Emanuel Wilson… #Seahawks pic.twitter.com/mE8zpWXKHY — Corbin K. Smith (@CorbinSmithNFL) September 22, 2026 #Seahawks didn't get this fourth and goal run, but it wasn't because of Beau Stephens. Rookie gets the pancake on former first round pick L.J. Collier. pic.twitter.com/sFVoQjueBd — Corbin K. Smith (@CorbinSmithNFL) September 22, 2026 For what it’s worth, neither Haynes nor Stephens had a sparkling PFF grade, but I’ve reached the point where I think PFF post-sale should be met with even greater skepticism than before it was sold. Christian Haynes had a 58.6 PFF grade vs. Arizona (76.6 pass block grade, 54.0 run block grade). Beau Stephens had a 52.3 PFF grade (54.1 pass block, 52.5 run block). — Cameron Van Til (@CameronVanTil) September 23, 2026 If nothing else, Bradford’s best asset is his run blocking, and it’ll be important for the Seahawks offense to have Haynes and/or Stephens adequately fill that role. They will be facing more talented defensive lines than Arizona’s during Bradford’s absence, including potentially Week 7 when Chris Jones and Peter Woods are in the Kansas City Chiefs lineup, so we’ll get a clearer picture of the differences between Bradford and his backups very soon. In the immediate, Haynes and Stephens will be tasked with making sure there isn’t a massive drop-0ff in performance when they’re in the lineup. Longer term, while nothing will be decided for next season based on these upcoming weeks, consider this the start of the 2027 starting right guard competition.

title: Week 3 Score Prediction: Seahawks vs Commanders
summary: Two weeks in, and another victory in the books, the Seahawks are getting ready to hit the road one more time to face off against the Washington Commanders. Without Sam Darnold, the reigning and defending Super Bowl Champions are 2-0 with the best backup quarterback in the league, Drew Lock. With Jayden Daniels dislocating his […]
full_text: Two weeks in, and another victory in the books, the Seahawks are getting ready to hit the road one more time to face off against the Washington Commanders. Without Sam Darnold, the reigning and defending Super Bowl Champions are 2-0 with the best backup quarterback in the league, Drew Lock. With Jayden Daniels dislocating his elbow, the Commanders will be trotting out their own veteran backup quarterback, Marcus Mariota. How well will the Seahawks do versus the other Washington? Let’s take a look. Seattle Seahawks The Seahawks are ranked fifth in total DVOA , 15th in offensive DVOA, second in defensive DVOA, and 15th special teams DVOA. Last week, they were ranked ninth overall, fifth in defense, 10th in offense, and fourth in special teams. Overall, they got better except for special teams. I expect that to be adjusted and fixed. Per Sumer Sports , they are 10th in offensive EPA per play and offensive total EPA, and fourth in defensive EPA per play and defensive total EPA. Last week, the Seahawks were ranked 14th in offensive total EPA and EPA per play and 11th in defensive total EPA and 12th in defensive EPA per play. Another jump up in ranking. Through two weeks, the Seahawks are averaging 22 points a game , and are holding opponents to a second-best 8.5 points per game. They are second in the league in point differential at +27 , with the margin of victory averaging 13.5 points. Washington Commanders The Commanders are the 28th ranked team in total DVOA, 22nd in offensive DVOA, 30th in defensive DVOA, and 28th in special teams DVOA. There is no doubt that the Commanders are struggling, and with now losing Daniels and having to start Mariota, the teams struggles will likely continue. On the EPA side of things, the Commanders rank 11th in offensive EPA per play and total offensive EPA and are 26th in defensive EPA per play and total defensive EPA. While close to the Seahawks on offensive efficiency, their defense is what is letting them down. The last two weeks, the Commanders are averaging 21 points per game and allowing opponents an average of 30.5 points per game. They are 27th in the league in point differential at -19, with an average margin of defeat at 9.5 points. Calculating the Score Seahawks 22 + Commanders opponents 30.5 (lets round that up to 31 for a whole number) = 53/2= 26.5, which we will round up to 27 points . Commanders 21 + Sea opponents 8.5 (which we will round up to 9) = 30 / 2 = 15 Points. Initial score prediction: 27 – 15, Seahawks win But, the margin of victory for the Seahawks is 13.5 points, so if we round that to 14 points, 15-2= 13 Final Score Prediction: 27-13 I go more into detail about the statistical predictions for players in this weeks episode of Eye On The Numbers on The Hawks Eye Podcast here: What do you think will be the final score? summary: Another 49ers season, another potentially season-ending injury for Nick Bosa. Or at least that is the scenario according to a report from NBC Sports Bay Area’s Jennifer Lee Chan, per 95.7 The Game. Bosa popped up on the injury report on Thursday with a calf problem, and Chan reported that there’s concern that Bosa has […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Nick Bosa #97 of the San Francisco 49ers warms up before a game against the Miami Dolphins at Levi's Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images Another 49ers season, another potentially season-ending injury for Nick Bosa. Or at least that is the scenario according to a report from NBC Sports Bay Area’s Jennifer Lee Chan, per 95.7 The Game . Bosa popped up on the injury report on Thursday with a calf problem, and Chan reported that there’s concern that Bosa has suffered a “serious calf injury” and, if he’s not out for the season, he’ll be out for multiple weeks. The 2022 Defensive Player of the Year missed most of last season due to a torn ACL he suffered in the Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals, whom the 49ers will face in their third game of the season this Sunday. San Francisco’s pass rush was non-existent without him in 2025, and any kind of prolonged absence would be a hammer blow to a defensive line that already has very thin depth. After consistently pressuring Matthew Stafford in the season-opening win over the Los Angeles Rams, the 49ers registered four sacks of Malik Willis in their blowout victory against the Miami Dolphins in Week 2. Bosa’s ability to collapse the pocket was a huge part of the latter performance and, if he is out, it will be substantial pressure on a young group to excel without him. Head coach Kyle Shanahan is due to hold his final press conference ahead of the Cardinals at 1:35 PT, about an hour after the 49ers practice. Bosa’s status will be the main talking point as San Francisco gears up for a difficult division game.
